MCU backend: C11, no_std-equivalent, no heap; SoC TBD until deploy authoring
Wire-interoperability with upstream zenohd for the sec 2 documented subset
caveats_bullets: Not a rewrite of zenoh/zenoh-pico; demonstration that SCE synthesizes industrial wire protocols.

10/10.2.intent: QoS config codegen — AP emits Rust const QosConfig (data section); MCU emits C const struct in .rodata (Flash, no RAM cost).

11.intent: Multi-layer testing strategy: byte-equivalence parity, wire replay, upstream interop, no-alloc guard, drift detection, fuzz.

11/11.1.intent: Cross-backend parity gate — every algorithm/codec with sce:test-vector runs on both backends and is byte-diffed; gate on merge.

11/11.2.intent: Wire replay tests — pcap captures from upstream zenoh peers replayed into generated stack with declared expected event sequence.

11/11.3.intent: Upstream interop CI — dockerized zenohd + AP node + MCU host-mode build (lwIP shim, renode/QEMU later) asserting full handshake + pub/sub roundtrip.

11/11.4.intent: MCU heap prohibition enforced as five layers — direct trap, linker wrap, libc pin, call-graph reachability, exception ban — not runtime trap alone.
rationale_bullets: Layer 1 direct trap: malloc/calloc/realloc/free stubs emit __builtin_trap on call.
Layer 2 linker --wrap: -Wl,--wrap on alloc symbols routes libc-internal indirect calls to traps.
Layer 3 libc pin: newlib-nano or picolibc tiny stdio prevents allocating printf path.
Layer 4 call-graph: post-link analyzer rejects any reach from out/mcu to deny-listed allocator.
Layer 5 exception ban: -fno-exceptions/-fno-rtti/-fno-unwind-tables blocks libstdc++ machinery.

11/11.5.intent: Drift gate: every emitted file carries source-hash + template-hash; sce-build verify recomputes and fails on mismatch; manual edits to out/ forbidden.
rationale_bullets: Per-file header carries source-hash + template-hash (sha256 over inputs and sce-build binary).
sce-build verify recomputes both hashes and fails the gate on mismatch (CI + pre-commit).
Fixed artifact set: out/{ap,mcu}, Cargo.toml, CMakeLists.txt, linker fragments, sce_sourcemap.json.
Manual edits to out/ forbidden: path is RFC or sce:extern; exceptions tracked with expiry date.
sce_sourcemap.json hash mismatch surfaces as traceability/sourcemap-source-hash-mismatch.

11/11.6.intent: Adversarial input fuzz testing on generated codec/parsers; deferred Phase D+ work; complements §11.1 cross-backend parity.

2/2.4.intent: Six extensibility invariants: static-first, link-extensible, kinds-additive, library-not-monolith, platform gating, out/ SSoT.

Link drivers extensible: open set via target plugin, not closed enum.
Kinds additive: ForgeKind set grows; existing kinds remain stable across versions.
Generated code exports as library, not monolith: out/ap and out/mcu are library targets.
Platform gating only when physically necessary; keep pool/link/worker kinds platform-neutral.
out/ is SSoT-downstream: manual edits forbidden; new features land via SCE extensions.

3.intent: Four design invariants: zero-runtime abstraction, location transparency, strict SSoT, hardware-aware codegen.

3/3.1.intent: Zero-Runtime Abstraction — no vtables, no dynamic dispatch in the hot path; all bindings resolve at build time to direct calls (SCE AOT philosophy carried through).

3/3.2.intent: Location Transparency — SCXML uses logical identities; physical transport realization and addressing live in deploy.yaml; same SCXML deploys to AP or MCU.

3/3.3.intent: Strict SSoT — wire format / algorithms / FSMs defined once in SCXML+Forge; AP and MCU are descendants; cross-backend drift is a generator bug, not expected.

3/3.4.intent: Hardware-Aware Codegen — MCU code integrates with target SoC capabilities (SRAM placement, DMA pairing, alignment) declared via deploy.yaml; AP/MCU share no memory.

7/7.1.intent: AP backend stack — generated code on top of sce_core + sce_link_runtime_tokio + Rust std/bytes/tokio; tokio::spawn workers, mpsc channels, BytesMut pools.

7/7.2.intent: MCU stack — generated code over sce_forge_runtime_c + sce_link_runtime_lwip; cooperative tick scheduler with WCET budget; static pools + DMA descriptors.

8.intent: Wire format layering: scouting/transport/network/zenoh/extensions; FSM, codec, link layers.

8/8.1.intent: Wire format stack layer diagram — Application -> Session FSM -> Network FSM -> Codec -> Link -> OS/HAL; bottom-up data flow on RX, top-down on TX.

8/8.2.intent: Session FSM sketch — Init/Scouting/Opening/Established/Closing path authored as session_unicast/multicast.scxml; full model lives in docs/session-fsm.md.

8/8.3.intent: Codec layer — one SCXML file per message type using RFC §5.B extensions (flags/vle/present-if/len-prefix/TLV); test vectors drive cross-backend parity.

8/8.4.intent: Link layer — kind=link SCXML files (UDP unicast/multicast/TCP/Serial/WS) with framer + RX-pool + backpressure declared; driver and address bound via deploy.yaml.

9.intent: Zero-copy: TX always zero-copy; RX happy path zero-copy; oversized/fragment stage-copy; pool placement; platform-aware link.

9/9.1.intent: TX path zero-copy — Codec encodes directly into pool slot, link send-from-slot, DMA reads via prebuilt descriptor; pool slot in DMA-coherent SRAM.

9/9.2.intent: RX happy path zero-copy — DMA writes pre-programmed RX slot; codec parses in place; event emitted with slot borrow; slot returned to freelist.

9/9.3.intent: Stage-copy RX path for oversized/multi-DMA — one copy DMA-slot to stage; build-time fragmentation analysis; stage_copy_policy warn/error/forbid per machine.

9/9.4.intent: Pool placement across .dtcm/.sram1/.flash regions; per-pool placement declared in kind source; memory regions in deploy.yaml; linker fragment ties them.

9/9.5.intent: Platform-aware link substrate: 5-row matrix (MCU bare_metal, linux+epoll, linux+io_uring, QNX, etc) sharing pool FSM.

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-1-unic.intent: Unicast session FSM has eight states plus Closed terminal; splits Opening (initiator) and Accepting (acceptor) explicitly.
inputs_bullets: Init: created, link not yet open; entry from outbound or inbound
LinkOpening: outbound link driver attempting open (TCP connect / WS upgrade)
Scouting: active scout loop pre-target (mode=active deploys only)
Opening: initiator driving 4-way Init/Open handshake
Accepting: acceptor responding to remote-driven handshake
Established: handshake done, RX/TX regions enabled (sub-region container)
Closing: graceful close in progress; sends Close with reason
Closed: terminal, link released, pool slots freed

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-2-unic.intent: Unicast transitions — outbound (LinkOpening → Opening.SentInitSyn → GotInitAck → Established) + inbound (Accepting.AwaitingInitSyn → SentInitAck → SentOpenAck → Established).
outputs_bullets: Outbound: Init → LinkOpening → Opening.SentInitSyn → GotInitAck → Established
Inbound: Init → Accepting.AwaitingInitSyn → SentInitAck → SentOpenAck → Established
Inbound entry guarded by half_open_cap_available + accept_rate_token (silent drop if denied)
Cookie validation guard: Accepting.SentInitAck → SentOpenAck rejects invalid/expired cookie
stateless_accept mode: AwaitingInitSyn→SentInitAck does not allocate FSM instance (cookie-only)
Framing errors → Closing(reason=INVALID); peer Close → Closed(peer-rejected)

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-3-esta.intent: Established is parallel SCXML region with 4 concurrent sub-machines: RxDispatch / TxSchedule / Keepalive / LeaseMonitor.
inputs_bullets: RxDispatch: Frame→NetworkMessage / Fragment→reassembly / KeepAlive→reset / Close→parent / OAM→diag
TxSchedule: Idle / Batching / Flushing per (reliability, priority) band
Keepalive: Armed / Sending; timer = lease × keepalive_ratio (default 1/3)
LeaseMonitor: Healthy / Warning / Expired; warning at lease×2/3

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-4-clos.intent: Close paths from Established by trigger; six trigger types; Closing state has 100ms default timeout for Close-frame flush before link teardown.
outputs_bullets: RxDispatch peer Close → Closed (no reciprocal Close)
TX congestion budget exhaust on RELIABLE batch → Closing(UNRESPONSIVE) → Closed

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-5-time.intent: 12 named timers (link / handshake / scout / lease / keepalive / closing / batch / reassembly / accept-rate / cookie). R61b: Hal time-mock for delayed-send coverage carry.
inputs_bullets: link.open_timeout (5s) / init_ack_timeout / open_ack_timeout (2s) / scout_timeout (1s)
lease (10s, negotiated) / keepalive_interval (lease/3) / closing_timeout (100ms)
batch_timer (1ms AP / 5ms MCU) / reassembly_timeout (500ms per peer-priority-reliability-sn_base)
accept_rate_window (1s) / accepting_inactivity_timeout (1s)
cookie_hmac_lifetime (30s) / cookie_hmac_key_rotation (1h, old key honored one extra lifetime)

session_arming: hosts Accepting cluster; quota + accept_rate required (hard error)
established_session: post-handshake Frame/Fragment, no Accepting attachment

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/2-7-acce.intent: 3-cap hardening (half-open / accept-rate / cookie HMAC) + silent-drop on denial. R62: cookie HMAC-SHA256 helper landed; R63b inbound parser populates Initiator-side cookie from peer InitAck.
inputs_bullets: Half-open capacity: session_arming_quota bounds concurrent Accepting.* instances per listener
Per-source token bucket: accept_rate_per_sec / accept_rate_burst per (link, src_addr)
Stateless accept (optional): cookie_hmac_sha256 defers FSM allocation until cookie validated
Three caps chain in series; silent drop on cap denial (no Close frame, anti-amplification)

caveats_bullets: R311fb: accepting.inactivity_timeout armed 1s (AwaitingInitSyn onentry); whole-accept silent drop.

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/3-1-mult.intent: Multicast session-level FSM: Idle → LinkOpening → Running (parallel: JoinEmit / RxDispatch / PeerSweep) → Stopped.

RxDispatch: classify Join/Frame/Fragment/KeepAlive/Close/OAM on TransportMessageLowLatency
PeerSweep: timer lease/3, evict PeerTable entries with last_seen > lease
Idle→LinkOpening on create(multicast_link); LinkOpening→Running on link.ready

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/3-2-mult.intent: Per-peer FSM (one per zid in multicast_peer_table bounded-collection): Discovered → Active → Expired.
inputs_bullets: Discovered: first Join validated (version/resolution/batch/qos); init RX seq table
Active: any msg refresh last_seen; Close{zid} or lease expiry → Expired
Expired: emit peer-lost event; PeerTable removes at next sweep
Rejection: version/max_sessions/SN-res/QoS mismatch → ignored + diag (not a transition)

A validated Join drives Discovered->Active together; Discovered is the init-rx-seq transient.
Impl (R311jk): peer keyed by src ADDRESS (Frame/KeepAlive carry no zid); zid stored from JOIN.
Found via _z_find_peer_entry(addr) (zenoh-pico parity); table is one-per-peer, addr-indexed.

session-fsm--prose-level-sketch/6-link-l.intent: 6 inbound link events + 3 outbound invocations. R52.1-R63 prototype: encode_init/encode_open/encode_close emit base body; transport-message header prepended by wz session_glue.
rationale_bullets: Inbound 6: ready / lost(cause) / rx(bytes) / tx_drained / backpressure(on|off) / framing_error
Outbound 3: link.open() / link.send(bytes, reliability) / link.close()
FSM never touches raw bytes — wz-codecs::init_body / open_body / close emit per-message body
Transport header prepended by session_glue::encode_init/open/close: (flags | T_MID-low-5-bits)
InitSyn flags=T_INIT_S (0x40); InitAck adds T_INIT_A (0x20); T_MID_INIT (0x01)
OpenSyn flags=T_OPEN_T per lease unit; OpenAck adds T_OPEN_A (0x20); T_MID_OPEN (0x02)
Close flags=T_CLOSE_S (graceful session close, 0x20); T_MID_CLOSE (0x03)

inputs_bullets: link.ready: TCP/WS open → LinkOpening→Opening.SentInitSyn or attach Accepting

link.rx(bytes): pass to codec, codec emits recv(MsgType) events
link.tx_drained: TX pool slot freed → wake TxSchedule
link.backpressure(on|off): TX queue watermark crossed → TxSchedule pause/resume
link.framing_error: codec decode failed → Closing(INVALID)
outputs_bullets: link.close(): tear down byte channel after Close flushed
caveats_bullets: link.rx parser pass (R63b carry): peer InitAck → SessionInitParams.cookie populate
Reliability::BestEffort path lands when wz UdpDriver session FSM wiring closes (R52)

Round 100.decision_summary: R100 promotes SubscriberRegistry from literal-only to zenoh chunk-wildcard matching (`*` single-chunk, `**` zero-or-more chunks) — production-realistic keyexpr semantics that closes R98 carry #3 and matches what real zenoh-pico subscribers use (`home/**`, `sensors/*/temp`).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs: `Subscriber.keyexpr_literal: String` replaced with `pattern_chunks: Vec<String>` pre-split on `/`. Registration eagerly splits the pattern so the hot dispatch path only re-borrows the slice as `&[&str]` per Push rather than reparsing per match.

New free function `keyexpr_pattern_matches(pattern_chunks: &[&str], target: &str) -> bool` implements the matcher as a two-cursor walk with a single `**` backtrack frame (mirrors standard glob-match algorithms; worst-case `O(|pattern| * |target|)` for single `**`, linear for the productive `home/**` / `sensors/*/temp` patterns).

`SubscriberRegistry::register` accepts `impl Into<String>` (unchanged signature) but reinterprets the argument as a zenoh chunk-wildcard pattern. Backward compatibility: a literal keyexpr like `"topic/a"` still matches itself because all chunks are literals — the existing R98/R99 tests continue to pass without modification.

`SubscriberRegistry::dispatch` walks subscribers and runs `keyexpr_pattern_matches(&chunks, suffix)` per registered pattern; non-zero `keyexpr.id` filtering preserved (DECLARE mapping still deferred).

Module-level doc updated to declare R100 scope: chunks split on `/`, `*` matches exactly one chunk, `**` matches zero or more chunks (incl. empty), literal chunks compare byte-for-byte, `$*` intra-chunk substring deferred until a consumer surfaces.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib pubsub: 12 passed — 6 pre-R100 tests stay green (literal patterns still match themselves) + 6 new wildcard tests cover literal-equality, single-chunk `*` (including the negative case where `*` does NOT collapse to zero), and `**` at prefix / middle / trailing positions plus the zero-chunks case.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --test session_fsm_drive_session r99_subscriber: still 1 passed — R99 integration test uses a literal pattern `"demo/topic"` so it stays unchanged.

The next user-visible deliverable is a runnable Linux + tokio binary that opens a real TCP session against a zenoh-pico peer (or two wz peers), subscribes via the registry, and exercises the demo. Estimate 2-3 rounds for scaffolding + real-peer fixture + golden-path assertion.

`$*` intra-chunk substring wildcard — zenoh full keyexpr language includes patterns like `home/temp$*` matching `home/temperature`. Per-chunk pattern compilation needed (chunk-internal `$*` parsing + per-chunk match). Defer until a consumer surfaces; AP MVP typical patterns (`home/**` / `sensors/*/temp`) don't need it.

DECLARE codec (0x1E) — 9 declaration sub-types per zenoh-pico declarations.c, multi-round chain (~3 rounds like RESPONSE). Closure unblocks the mapping-id resolver on the registry so non-zero `wireexpr.id` Pushes route through resolved-base + suffix concatenation.

Symmetric dispatch for Reply / Err / Response — dispatch is Push-only. A future round adds the symmetric `NetworkMessage::Response` arm (`Response.body` peek-byte dispatches to reply / err; reply itself wraps a push_body so keyexpr matching passes through). Kind-filtered subscriptions (publish-only vs reply-also-accepted) are the textbook surface.

Layer 3 wire-interop tests — R90 / R91 carry. The wildcard matcher in R100 stays internally testable, but a wire-interop fixture against zenoh-pico's actual `_z_keyexpr_intersect_*` would prove cross-stack semantic compatibility. Estimate 1 round once the zenoh-pico-sys FFI surface exposes the keyexpr matcher symbols.

changes_bullets: crates/zenoh-pico-sys/wrapper.h: `#include "zenoh-pico/protocol/codec/network.h"` added alongside the existing transport/message/ext includes so bindgen can see the N-level (network-MID) encoders — same expansion pattern as previous Layer 3 rounds (the umbrella public header does not transitively pull in the internal codec headers; Layer 3 needs them explicitly).

crates/zenoh-pico-sys/build.rs allowlist: `_z_response_final_encode` + `_z_n_msg_response_final_t` added with an inline comment explaining why ResponseFinal was chosen as the first contact (smallest envelope post-R90: header + zsize request_id only).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_response_final.rs new — 3 byte-equivalence tests: (1) default ResponseFinal (request_id=0) emits the canonical [0x1A, 0x00] 2-byte wire, (2) single-byte VLE rid 0x42 emits [0x1A, 0x42], (3) multi-byte VLE rid 200 crosses the 7-bit boundary and emits [0x1A, 0xC8, 0x01]. Each test asserts wz_codecs::response_final::ResponseFinal encode() bytes match zenoh-pico's `_z_response_final_encode` output. Test layout mirrors the existing layer3_keep_alive.rs pattern (wbuf alloc → encode → wbuf_to_zbuf → raw slice copy → wbuf_clear).

Helper `zenoh_pico_encode_response_final(request_id: u64) -> Vec<u8>` widens the test's u64 input to the bindgen-surfaced `usize` zint_t via `as _` so the call site keeps the natural numeric type — zenoh-pico's `_z_zint_t` resolves to `size_t` on x86_64-linux which bindgen produces as `usize`. Comment explains the widen for future Layer 3 authors hitting the same surface.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_declare.rs new — 1 byte-equivalence test asserting `wz_codecs::declare::Declare::default().encode() == _z_declare_encode(default _z_n_msg_declare_t with 2 field patches)`. Wire bytes `[0x1E, 0x1A]` (envelope MID 0x1E with no flags + decl_final inner MID 0x1A).

Two-patch fixture: (1) `_ext_qos._val = 5` matches `_Z_N_QOS_DEFAULT._val` so `_z_declare_encode`'s `has_qos_ext` evaluates false and envelope Z stays clear; (2) `_decl._tag = 8 = _Z_DECL_FINAL` overrides zero-init's tag of 0 (= `_Z_DECL_KEXPR`) so the inner dispatch reaches `_z_decl_final_encode` (1 byte emit) instead of `_z_decl_kexpr_encode` (3 byte emit). The patch matches wz's R88 declared default arm `DeclareVariant default = CodecZenohDeclFinal`.

Tag-enum literal pinned to a `const Z_DECL_FINAL_TAG: u32 = 8;` rather than relying on bindgen's anonymous-enum surface naming. This keeps the test robust against bindgen pinning shifts (the `_Z_DECL_FINAL` ordinal is fixed by the upstream enum declaration order in declarations.h:97).

changes_bullets: vendor/sce submodule pointer 189bf7f4 → 4d1ef3f2 — absorbs the explicit-default-arm-marker + cross-doc wire-MID-default contract SCE upstream landed during the prior 3 weeks of drift. sources/codecs/ext_entry.scxml: `<sce:arm value="0x00" type="codec_zenoh_ext_unit"/>` → same arm + `default="true"`. The `<sce:default type="codec_zenoh_ext_unit"/>` catch-all line is kept (separate concept from the declared default arm — catch-all is a runtime fallback for unrecognized values, declared default arm is the compile-time pick for `Default::default()`).

sources/codecs/query.scxml header comment expanded — same shape: R88 mid `value="0x03"` baking + layer3_request.rs proof + SCE PR carry.

sources/codecs/request.scxml header comment expanded — three-divergence record: R108a mid `value="0x1C"` + R106 M=1 baking + R88 query-as-default-arm vs SCE fixture's msg_put-as-default-arm. Layer 3 proof at layer3_request.rs (R108b).

sources/codecs/msg_put.scxml header comment expanded — element-level identical to SCE upstream today but explicitly enrolled in the R88 family so a future SCE drift on msg_put is recognized as a regression. scripts/run-ci.sh `LAYER2_KNOWN_DIVERGENCE` array extended from `(init_body join)` to `(init_body join msg_del msg_put query request)`; per-entry rationale recorded in the comment block above the array.

scripts/run-ci.sh Layer B opens with a sce-codegen freshness check: compares vendor/sce HEAD `git log -1 --format=%ct` to the binary's `stat -c %Y`; if the binary is older, runs `scripts/build-sce.sh` automatically before continuing. The R112 -> R114 GitHub Actions failure traced exactly to this stale-binary path — binary mtime 2026-05-18 00:00 vs vendor pin checked out at R112 13:51. The gate eliminates that whole class of false-green pre-push results.

Freshness gate verified by code inspection rather than negative testing (would require destroying the binary mid-run, which the harness avoids). Root cause analysis end-to-end: R112 bumped vendor/sce 189bf7f4 → 4d1ef3f2 (15 commits including the variant-default-uniformity parse-time enforcement series). The bump's wz-side break (ext_entry default arm) was caught + fixed in R112. The wz-side audit-traced wire-correctness improvements in msg_del/query/request from R88/R106/R108a were ALREADY divergent from SCE fixtures at that pin — but local pre-push hit a sce-codegen binary built BEFORE R112 (5月 18 00:00, pre-R112), which silently matched both sides through pre-R112 semantics. CI built sce-codegen fresh against the R112 pin and detected the audit-traced divergences as Layer 2 MISMATCH. The freshness gate ensures local and CI see the same emit logic going forward; KNOWN_DIVERGENCE makes the expected MISMATCHes non-fatal as the R44 precedent prescribed.

When SCE merges, the corresponding entries can be removed from LAYER2_KNOWN_DIVERGENCE. Same lifecycle as the R44 init_body/join PR carry.

session_glue.rs imports wz_codecs::declare::Declare next to the existing 10 wz-codecs envelope codec imports, and adds NetworkMessage::Declare(Box<Declare>) as the 7th typed variant (sizing rationale mirrors Request/Push/Response — interest_id + ext vec + DeclareVariant inline form is larger than the Unknown variant).

parse_frame_payload gains a wire_const::N_MID_DECLARE => Declare::decode → NetworkMessage::Declare arm directly above the catch-all Unknown branch; the manual Debug impl on NetworkMessage gains a matching Declare(_) → "Declare(..)" formatter arm so DriverLoopOutcome's #[derive(Debug)] keeps compiling.

Round 116.decision_summary: R116 bumps the SCE vendor pin from 4d1ef3f2 to 122f851d, adopting upstream commit fa3a2fda ("fix: route scheduler clock through Hal trait under std builds") which the watching-zenoh R115 carry-verification surfaced as a blocker for deterministic timer-driven testing under host CI; with the routing fix in place, wz authors TestHal in wz-runtime-tokio-test-support (process-global AtomicU64 backing) and adds the hal_timer_routing.rs integration test that exercises the substrate against the 4 SCXML delay values session_fsm_unicast.scxml uses (link.open_timeout=5s / init_ack.timeout=2s / open_ack.timeout=2s / closing.timeout=100ms), proving the wz consumer can now drive the SCE scheduler clock from a synthetic Hal under std builds for the first time.
changes_bullets: vendor/sce submodule pointer 4d1ef3f2 -> 122f851d (6 commits drift: 5b069ff9 / 76b71756 / a81cc368 / 4d54811c / fa3a2fda / 122f851d — the load-bearing change is fa3a2fda which unifies SchedTimePoint to u64 ms and routes sched_now/sched_now_plus through <P::Hal as Hal>::now_ticks_ms on both std and no_std; StdHal's Instant::now-backed now_ticks_ms keeps std production behavior byte-identical).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio-test-support/src/lib.rs adds the TestHal zero-sized type plus the test_hal_set_ticks / test_hal_advance_ticks / test_hal_now_ticks helpers; the implementation mirrors SCE's own hal_clock_routing.rs MockHal but lives in the test-support sibling crate so wz consumer tests can author Hal-mocked policies without re-publishing the AtomicU64 backing inside each test binary.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/hal_timer_routing.rs (NEW, 6 tests) — declares an in-test TimerProbePolicy whose `type Hal = TestHal`, anchors a fresh epoch via the helper, schedules a delayed event matching one of the session-fsm SCXML delay values, advances TestHal across ready_at, and asserts has_ready_events flips false->true at the exact synthetic tick. Coverage: 5s link.open_timeout (advance 4999 -> still pending, advance +2 -> ready), 2s init_ack.timeout (exact-equal Hal tick satisfies <=), 2s+2s sibling schedules with distinct send_ids (both ready), 100ms closing.timeout (millisecond resolution), Hal clock reset-backward path (event re-pends), public helper-vs-trait observable consistency.

crates/wz-integration-tests/Cargo.toml dev-deps add sce-rust-runtime path dep — only the test surface reaches into Engine / Hal / StatePolicy directly; production wz crates remain on sce-forge-runtime + generated Policy code.

hal_timer_routing.rs adds a process-binary-local Mutex<()> HAL_LOCK guarding every test fn so the multi-thread default of cargo test cannot race on the process-global TestHal AtomicU64. Poison recovery via PoisonError::into_inner keeps subsequent tests runnable after a panicked test — each test re-anchors at entry so the poisoned tick value is overwritten before any assertion reads it. The lock is the textbook fix for the failure observed during R116b authoring: 5x consecutive multi-thread runs surfaced one race in test 2/5, single-threaded baseline was 5/5 green; post-lock 8x multi-thread runs are all green.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace: 159 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (was 153/0/1 in R115 baseline; +6 from hal_timer_routing.rs).

cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test hal_timer_routing: 6/6 green under both single-thread (--test-threads=1) and the multi-thread default; 8 consecutive multi-thread runs all 6/6 confirm the HAL_LOCK serialization removed the AtomicU64 sequence race.

Round 121e.decision_summary: R121e lands wz publisher → zenoh-pico z_sub reverse-direction round-trip; second integration test exercises the outbound Push path against a foreign subscriber, completing AP MVP bidirectional pub/sub interop.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — new imports (frame::Frame, msg_put::MsgPut, push::PushVariant, wireexpr::{Wireexpr,WireexprVariant}, wireexpr_local::WireexprLocal, std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64,Ordering}); new field SessionLinkActions.outbound_frame_sn: AtomicU64 seeded from params.initial_sn in new(); two free fns build_push_literal(keyexpr_suffix,&value) + encode_frame_with_push(sn,push,reliable) modelled on encode_init/encode_open; two methods on SessionLinkActions — next_outbound_frame_sn() (SeqCst fetch_add) and send_push_literal(keyexpr,&value,reliable) which composes Frame[Push(literal,Put)] and dispatches via self.driver.send_blocking. Wire shape: [parent_flags|T_MID_FRAME(0x05)] + VLE(sn) + Push.encode_bytes; Push.header = N_MID_PUSH(0x1D)|N(0x20), M flag derived at encode (push.rs:189 from WireexprLocal arm).

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs — CLI extension: --key now optional, new --publish <keyexpr> + --value <text> pair. Argv validation matrix (--key alone OR --publish+--value OR both; --publish without --value rejected; --value without --publish rejected; neither rejected). run_demo signature shifts to (listen, key: Option<String>, publisher_spec: Option<(String,String)>). New free async fn publisher_task(actions, keyexpr, value) — polls actions.trace_snapshot().send_open_ack > 0 every 50ms (5s timeout), then emits PUBLISHER_BURST_COUNT=5 Pushes spaced PUBLISHER_BURST_INTERVAL_MS=200ms apart via actions.send_push_literal. publisher_task spawned BEFORE drive_session loop; handle awaited with 200ms timeout in cleanup. PUBLISHER EMITTED stderr line per emission for diagnostic surface.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_publisher_to_zsub.rs new — R121e hard-gate test. Spawns wz-ap-demo --listen <free> --publish demo/test --value hello-from-wz with stderr tempfile capture; spawns z_sub via `stdbuf -oL -eL` (forces line buffering on glibc-piped stdout per R121d carry feedback_foreign_peer_crash_diagnosis) with -k demo/** -e tcp/127.0.0.1:<port> -m client and stdout tempfile capture; two-stage wait — 'Opening session' (5s) then '>> [Subscriber] Received' (10s) — followed by belt-and-suspenders assertions on publish_key + publish_value substring presence; teardown kills both children; full captured streams surfaced on any failure.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs tests module — 4 new unit tests: build_push_literal_shapes_struct_for_literal_keyexpr (asserts Push.header == 0x3D = N_MID_PUSH|N_flag with M deferred to encode, WireexprLocal arm with id=0+suffix=Some+suffix_len matched, MsgPut header 0x01 with no flags + payload_len/payload populated, no extensions on any layer); encode_frame_with_push_emits_transport_header_plus_frame_body (asserts reliable→FLAG_T_FRAME_R|T_MID_FRAME parent byte, best-effort→T_MID_FRAME only, body[0]=VLE(sn=0)=0x00, tail bytes == Push.encode() verbatim); encode_frame_with_push_carries_vle_sn_across_widths (round-trip 7-point sn corpus 0/1/127/128/16383/16384/1_000_000 through parse_inbound, asserts sn + reliable both recovered); next_outbound_frame_sn_seeds_at_initial_sn_then_increments (NullDriver harness, params.initial_sn=42 yields 42,43,44 across three calls). Total wz-runtime-tokio --lib lane = 32 passed (up from 28 pre-R121e).

scripts/run-ci.sh — Layer E lane comment + body extended. Header line tagged 'R121c z_put → wz subscriber + R121e wz publisher → z_sub; both directions in one lane'. layer_e_ap_demo_round_trip body adds `--test wz_publisher_to_zsub` alongside `--test ap_demo_round_trip` so the single cargo invocation runs both binary tests with one build/link pass. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs TcpDriver::send (lines 160-181): replaces the `len.to_le_bytes()` + two `write_all` pair with a single StreamEnvelope construction + encode + write_all. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs TcpDriver::poll_event (lines 191-224): two-step read pattern. First reads the 2-byte prefix raw (sized by the codec's min_frame_bytes), then sizes a frame buffer to `2 + payload_len` from the LE-decoded prefix, reads the payload tail into `frame[2..]`, and decodes the full frame through `StreamEnvelope::decode` for SSOT byte interpretation. The codec validates the structural decode; the manual prefix sniff is a bounded duplication of `min_frame_bytes=2` documented in the call-site comment.

Three small expected-wire helpers `expected_wire_255`/`256`/`300` build the reference byte sequences inline.

Round 121h-perf-bump-1-study.decision_summary: R121h-perf-bump-1 reduced to a study round: empirical impact survey shows the prior session's 3-phase carry is infeasible because partial SCXML migration breaks the build at every intermediate state, so the carry is revised from 3-phase to 2-phase (atomic bump+migrate, then TcpDriver hot path).
changes_bullets: No wz src or vendor changes this round. Study-only entry; the audit trail captures the revised migration plan so the next session can execute against a verified scope rather than the prior session's misdiagnosed 3-[REDACTED].

Empirical scope: 12 wz SCXML files use the legacy `<sce:requires-parent-flags>` element and/or `parent.X` predicate (prior session estimate was 11). The 12: init_body, open_body, hello, join, push, request, interest_body, timestamp, decl_kexpr, decl_subscriber, decl_queryable, decl_token, wireexpr, wireexpr_local, wireexpr_nonlocal (correction: actually 15 files surface in grep but decl_kexpr / decl_token / wireexpr / wireexpr_local / wireexpr_nonlocal grouping needs per-file checks during the migration round; the 12 = files with non-zero RPF blocks OR non-comment parent.X predicates).

Partial migration is infeasible. SCE Phase D2+D3+D4 (commit 19b0fcf0) deletes the legacy RPF mechanism + `<sce:requires-parent-flags>` XSD element entirely. The new grammar (`<sce:flag-inputs>` / `<sce:flag-bind>` from Phase A 36c0750e + Phase B 63daab97 codegen wire-up) is rejected by the current vendor pin 54d513af. There is no overlap window where both grammars parse; the bump and the 12-file migration must land in one commit.

Migration pattern reference (SCE Phase C bf41498c migrated 19 conformance fixtures with this exact pattern). Old form on a leaf consumer: `<sce:requires-parent-flags carrier="header"><sce:flag name="S" bit="6"/></sce:requires-parent-flags>` + `sce:present-if="parent.S"` on gated fields. New form: `<sce:flag-inputs><sce:flag-input name="S" width="1"/></sce:flag-inputs>` + `sce:present-if="S"` (no `parent.` prefix; SCE Phase B snake_cases the identifier for the typed encode/decode parameter so uppercase leaf flag names retain their literal form). Parent importers add `<sce:flag-bind input="S" source="S"/>` as a child of the `<sce:import>` element to wire each declared input to a source flag (dotted carrier.flag form or chain-forwarder bare-name form).

init_body.scxml-shaped example (the smallest migration in the 12): drop the RPF block declaring `S`(bit=6) and `A`(bit=5) on carrier=header; add `<sce:flag-inputs>` with `<sce:flag-input name="S" width="1"/>` and `<sce:flag-input name="A" width="1"/>`; rewrite the 4 `parent.S` predicates to `S` and the 2 `parent.A` predicates to `A`. init_body is NOT imported by any wz SCXML (wz constructs the transport envelope in Rust runtime), so no parent flag-bind is needed.

Variant-dispatcher cases (wireexpr.scxml + wireexpr_local.scxml + wireexpr_nonlocal.scxml): Phase D1 b8f86b46 added variant arm flag-bind threading codegen — the dispatcher's `<sce:import>` of each arm body now needs the same `<sce:flag-bind>` wire-up as a regular consumer. wireexpr.scxml has the variant-dispatch + RPF combination; the migration needs care to preserve the B5-ν chain-forwarding (parent.N gates the suffix in each arm body, threaded through the dispatcher's flag-bind to the arm's flag-inputs).

Encoder API impact after vendor bump (separate from SCXML grammar). SCE B1-α series (cb1b40b7 / 4eafcc7b / e01aac02 / 35998fd7 / 100a2ca0 / de5d5e9a) introduced `SceSink` trait + `SliceSink<&mut [u8]>` + `VecSink<&mut Vec<u8>>` + an `encode_to_vec()` feature-gated wrapper. The `*.encode()` zero-arg method that wz callers rely on is replaced. Mechanical drop-in: rename to `*.encode_to_vec()` (alloc feature on by default for std builds). Hot-path sink-based migration (TcpDriver) is a separate concern. ~10+ wz call-sites need the rename.
verification_bullets: Impact count gathered via `grep -l 'requires-parent-flags|parent\.[A-Za-z_]' sources/codecs/*.scxml` (15 files surfaced) and a follow-up per-file count of non-zero RPF blocks + non-comment `parent.X` predicates (12 files actually need migration; the 3 comment-only ones are not at risk).

SCE Phase C migration pattern verified by reading the diff at SCE commit bf41498c (tests/forge/resources/codec_init_syn_body.scxml + codec_zenoh_decl_subscriber.scxml). Both files showed the same RPF → flag-inputs / parent.X → X / import flag-bind addition pattern.

Coexistence-window check: SCE Phase A (36c0750e) commit body states `legacy RPF + parent.X predicate paths coexist during Phase A pending later atomic`. SCE Phase D2+D3+D4 (19b0fcf0) commit body states `Removes RequiresParentFlags struct + CodecModel field + PresentIfScope::Parent variant + ... XSD drops <sce:requires-parent-flags> element`. The current SCE main HEAD is post-D2 (de5d5e9a), so the coexistence window has closed. No vendor pin between A and D2 is reachable because SCE main is now past D2; the only safe target is HEAD (de5d5e9a).

No wz src changes → no test surface to verify. The next round's verification surface is `bash scripts/run-ci.sh` 8 lanes (especially Layer B verify-codegen.sh and Layer E ap_demo_round_trip 5-test bundle).
carry_forward_bullets: Revised R121h-perf-bump scope (replaces the 3-phase carry from R121h-perf-bump-attempt). Round 121h-perf-bump-2 (atomic): vendor pin 54d513af -> de5d5e9a + all 12 SCXML migrate (init_body + open_body + hello + join + push + request + interest_body + timestamp + decl_subscriber + decl_queryable + decl_token + wireexpr trio) + `*.encode()` -> `*.encode_to_vec()` mass rename + 8-lane CI pass + 14 byte-compare invariants preserved. Each wz SCXML migration needs the same narrowing audit — trust grep-confirmed predicate usage as the authoritative input list, not the RPF block's flag count.

changes_bullets: encode_init at crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs:1539-1547: pre-reserve Vec capacity = 1 (parent_flags | T_MID_INIT) + InitBody::MAX_ENCODED_BYTES + ext_bytes.len() instead of an ad-hoc body.zid.len() + cookie.len() + 12 estimate; wrap the wire Vec in VecSink after pushing the header byte and call body.encode(&mut sink, s, a) directly, eliminating the intermediate body.encode_to_vec(s, a) allocation. ext_bytes still extended at the end (encode_ext_chain is a separate concern not touched this round)

encode_open at session_glue.rs:1593-1600: same sink-based shape applied. Pre-reserve = 1 + OpenBody::MAX_ENCODED_BYTES + ext_bytes.len(); body.encode(&mut sink, a) replaces body.encode_to_vec(a) + extend_from_slice. Same ext_bytes extension at end

encode_close at session_glue.rs:1641-1648: pre-reserve = 1 + Close::MAX_ENCODED_BYTES (2 byte total worst-case); Close { reason }.encode(&mut sink) replaces the encode_to_vec + extend_from_slice pair. Most dramatic per-call ratio (2-byte wire was 2 allocs; now 1)

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs imports: add wz_codecs::decl_subscriber::DeclSubscriber.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs build_declare_subscriber(subscriber_id, keyexpr_mapping_id, keyexpr_suffix) builder added next to build_declare_kexpr. Inner DeclSubscriber.header carries author-supplied MID(0x02) + optional N(0x20) suffix gate; the M bit (0x40) is codegen-derived from the wireexpr import's variant-dispatch flag=header.M declaration in decl_subscriber.scxml under the R121h-pre B5-nu ownership invert. Wireexpr arm fixed to Local (default arm per wireexpr.scxml default=true); literal-vs-alias-vs-composite is driven by the (mapping_id, suffix) pair following the same convention as build_push_aliased and build_declare_kexpr.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs SessionLinkActions::send_declare_subscriber action added alongside send_declare_keyexpr. Hard-coded to the reliable channel for the same SN-window ordering reason as DECLARE-kexpr: the peer's subscriber table must be populated before any matching Push arrives, otherwise the peer drops it as unknown subscription.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs tests: two new unit tests. build_declare_subscriber_wraps_decl_subscriber_in_declare_envelope exercises the 3 semantic cases (pure alias, composite alias+suffix, literal id=0+suffix) at the struct-shape level. build_declare_subscriber_emits_zenoh_pico_compatible_wire_bytes is the wire-byte regression gate — 3-vector byte-for-byte compare against zenoh-pico declarations.c:65-84 reference encoder. The literal case validates the wireexpr local-sentinel id=0 + VLE(len) + suffix bytes shape; the alias case validates the M-bit codegen derivation (header = 0x42 = MID|M); the composite case validates the N|M co-set header (0x62) + wireexpr id-prefix + suffix-tail emit.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib build_declare_subscriber: both new tests pass. The byte-compare test confirms the 3 emit shapes match zenoh-pico's _z_decl_subscriber_encode + _z_decl_commons_encode byte-for-byte; any future codegen drift on either header derivation, wireexpr arm selection, or the parent.M dispatch path surfaces immediately.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_declare_subscriber_nonlocal` / `build_declare_queryable_nonlocal` / `build_declare_token_nonlocal` (post-R121i-b `build_declare_token`). Same `(id, mapping_id, suffix)` signature as the Local-arm builders; inner `Wireexpr` arm flipped to `WireexprNonlocal`; codegen-derived M bit (0x00 vs Local's 0x40 — verified at `wz-codecs-*/out/decl_subscriber.rs` line 134's `_derived_header` match). `build_declare_kexpr` deliberately has no Nonlocal companion — DeclKexpr's encoder-perspective locality is by construction Local (sender installs the (id, literal) pair into its OWN mapping table).

Each `_nonlocal` builder panics on `keyexpr_mapping_id == 0` mirroring `build_declare_kexpr_rejects_zero_mapping_id`. Rationale: zenoh-pico's `_Z_KEYEXPR_MAPPING_LOCAL` sentinel is `(uintptr_t)0` (core.h:151), so a remote-mapped id=0 refers to the peer's literal-sentinel slot which carries no table entry — the literal case is only representable in the Local arm via `build_declare_subscriber(_, 0, Some(s))`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added six unit tests in the `tests` mod (one byte-compare + one panic-rejection per builder). Each byte-compare locks alias (mapping_id=7, no suffix) / composite (mapping_id=7 + Some("abc")) / multi-byte VLE boundary (mapping_id=200, no suffix) — three vectors per builder. Locked wire bytes: 0x02 / 0x22 / 0x02 (Nonlocal subscriber header), 0x04 / 0x24 / 0x04 (queryable), 0x06 / 0x26 / 0x06 (token) — all with the M bit clear (Local-arm counterparts emit 0x42 / 0x62, 0x44 / 0x64, 0x46 / 0x66).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs imports: replace `use wz_codecs::request::Request;` with `use wz_codecs::request::{Request, RequestVariant};` (the variant enum is needed by the builder) and add `use wz_codecs::query::Query;` for the inner body type.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs build_request_query(rid, keyexpr_mapping_id, keyexpr_suffix) builder added next to build_declare_final. Emits the minimal AP MVP shape: Request.header = _Z_MID_N_REQUEST(0x1C) | optional N(0x20) suffix gate, with M(0x40) codegen-derived from the WireexprLocal arm via the same <sce:variant-dispatch flag=header.M> mechanism the DECLARE builders use. Inner Query.header = _Z_MID_Z_QUERY(0x03) only — no C(consolidation) / P(params) / Z(exts) flags. Doc comment enumerates the three layered follow-up helpers (build_request_query_with_consolidation / _with_parameters / _with_exts) that future rounds will add.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs encode_frame_with_request(sn, request, reliable) helper added: composes the one transport-envelope header byte that lives outside the body codec's scope (parent_flags | T_MID_FRAME) with Frame {sn, payload: request.encode()}.encode() body. Mirror of encode_frame_with_push (R121e) and encode_frame_with_declare (R121g); the reliable-channel default matches the DECLARE outbound contract (SN-window ordering ensures the peer sees the Query before any Response/ResponseFinal that depends on the rid).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs SessionLinkActions::send_request_query(rid, mapping_id, suffix) action added: build_request_query -> next_outbound_frame_sn -> encode_frame_with_request -> driver.send_blocking(Reliable). Same SN-window ordering reason as the DECLARE outbound path; unreliable Query is unsupported by this minimal builder because the local z_get future would hang on a dropped Query.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `pub enum ConsolidationMode { None, Monotonic, Latest }` mirroring zenoh-pico's `z_consolidation_mode_t` (constants.h:185-187) for the three transmitted values. `Z_CONSOLIDATION_MODE_AUTO = -1` is intentionally NOT representable since zenoh-pico's encoder treats AUTO as the `do not transmit` sentinel — callers wanting that case use plain `build_request_query`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `ConsolidationMode::wire_byte(self) -> u8` const fn returning 0/1/2 per the zenoh-pico enum integer values. Const-fn so the mapping is verifiable at compile time.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_consolidation(rid, mapping_id, suffix, consolidation)`. Built on top of `build_request_query` (calls it then mutates the inner `Query` body via the `RequestVariant::CodecZenohQuery` arm match): ORs Q_C(0x20) into `Query.header` and sets `Query.consolidation = Some(consolidation.wire_byte())`. The 1-byte consolidation field then emits at offset 4 of the Request wire shape (after the existing 4-byte minimal-shape prefix). No params, no exts — those are separate layered helpers (R121j-1b/c/d carry).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two unit tests. `build_request_query_with_consolidation_emits_zenoh_pico_compatible_wire_bytes` byte-compare-locks the three modes (alias case, mapping_id=7, no suffix): NONE → 0x5C 0x2A 0x07 0x23 0x00; MONOTONIC → ...0x23 0x01; LATEST → ...0x23 0x02. The 0x23 = MID(0x03) | Q_C(0x20) replaces the minimal-shape 0x03. `consolidation_mode_wire_byte_matches_zenoh_pico_enum_values` independently locks the enum-to-byte mapping so a refactor of the const fn without an encoder change still catches the regression.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `pub const REQUEST_QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_LEN: usize = 256` mirroring sources/codecs/query.scxml's `sce:max-size="256"` on the parameters field.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_request_query_with_parameters(rid, mapping_id, suffix, params)`. Built on top of `build_request_query` (same one-shot composition pattern as R121j-1a): ORs Q_P(0x40) into `Query.header`, sets `parameters_len = Some(params.len() as u64)` and `parameters = Some(params.to_vec())`. The codec gates both `parameters_len` and `parameters` fields on `header.P` (query.scxml line 79 / 81), so the flag + paired Optional fields stay byte-coherent.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two assertion gates. `assert!(!params.is_empty(), ...)` rejects the empty-slice case (zenoh-pico's `has_params` predicate at message.c:398 is `_z_slice_check && len > 0`, so an empty slice would silently clear Q_P and emit no params — the caller's intent is then `build_request_query` no-params). `assert!(params.len() <= REQUEST_QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_LEN, ...)` rejects oversize at the call site rather than at the peer's decoder.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added three unit tests in the `tests` mod. Byte-compare locks small-params (k=v) + multi-byte VLE boundary (params_len=128 → 0x80 0x01) + max-size (256-byte payload → VLE 0x80 0x02). Two `#[should_panic]` tests guard the empty-slice and over-max rejections.

Out of scope (audit-traced carry): `_implicit_anyke` selector convention (zenoh-pico message.c:414-425 prepends `_Z_QUERY_PARAMS_KEY_ANYKE` for `**` / `?` selectors). AP MVP simple `z_get` does not set it; a future helper `build_request_query_with_parameters_and_anyke` layers the anyke-prepend when needed.

One-shot pattern mirroring R121j-1a/1b/1c: calls `build_request_query` then mutates Request to set the Request-level N_Z flag (0x80, the network-message-layer extensions chain present bit at request.scxml's `<sce:flag name="Z" bit="7"/>`) and append a single ExtEntry with header=`ENC_ZINT(0x20)|id_timeout(0x06)=0x26` and ExtZint body. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — doc comment clarifies the two distinct Z bits at two layers (Request.header.Z gates Request-level tlv-chain; ExtEntry.header.Z is the per-entry chain-continuation marker). For single-ext, only the former is set; the latter stays clear. Same shape pattern applies to R121j-1c's Q-level ext chain (Query.header.Z + entry-Z).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — assertion gate: `timeout_ms != 0` rejected. zenoh-pico's encoder predicate at vendor/zenoh-pico/src/protocol/definitions/network.c:29 is `ext_timeout_ms = msg->_ext_timeout_ms != 0`, so a zero value silently clears the ext from the wire — the helper surfaces this as a panic at the call site rather than letting the caller think their timeout is being honored.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added two unit tests. Byte-compare locks single-byte VLE (timeout=50ms → 0x32), multi-byte VLE boundary (timeout=1000ms → 0xE8 0x07), and large VLE (timeout=2^32 ms → 5-byte VLE `0x80 0x80 0x80 0x80 0x10`). One panic-rejection test guards the timeout_ms=0 case. Inner-arm sanity verifies the Request-level Extensions vec, the ExtEntry.header byte, and the ExtZint.value independently — Query body stays minimal (no Q_C / Q_P / Q_Z).

Scope-deferred (audit-traced carry): four other Request-level exts. QoS (ext_id=0x01, ZINT u64, no M): priority + congestion-control + reliability packed into one zint per zenoh-pico session-level helper. Timestamp (ext_id=0x02, ZBUF, no M): timestamp_t struct (zid+time pair). Target (ext_id=0x04, ZINT, M=1!): query target enum (BestMatching / All / AllComplete). Budget (ext_id=0x05, ZINT u64, no M): max replies count. Each follows R121j-1d's pattern with appropriate ENC and ext_id; target's M=1 means the peer MUST handle it or fail the frame.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_response_reply_literal(request_id, keyexpr_suffix, payload)` for literal-keyexpr replies (id=0 + suffix). Wire shape: Response.header = MID(0x1B)|N(0x20)|M(0x40 codegen-derived), VLE(rid), wireexpr Local, Reply.header(0x04), MsgPut.header(0x01), VLE(payload_len), payload. No Response-level exts, no Reply consolidation, no Reply exts, no MsgPut T/E/Z gates. Empty suffix rejected (literal shape's purpose is inline keyexpr).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_response_reply_aliased(request_id, mapping_id, suffix: Option<&str>, payload)` for peer-declared-mapping replies. Convention matches the DECLARE/Request builders ((N,None) pure alias / (N,Some) compound). Panics on mapping_id=0 (literal-sentinel inversion); use the _literal variant for that case.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `encode_frame_with_response(sn, response, reliable)` mirroring the other `encode_frame_with_*` Frame-envelope wrappers (PUSH/DECLARE/REQUEST/RESPONSE_FINAL). Reliable channel is the default — a dropped Reply hangs the requester's `z_get` since the queryable thinks it sent the reply and won't re-emit.

Minimal Err shape (header=0x05 MID only, no E encoding, no Z exts, no payload prefix beyond payload_len + bytes).

Structural difference from Reply documented: Reply wraps a MsgPut which itself carries a MID byte (0x01) before its own payload_len/payload pair, so a literal Response(Reply) wire ends with `[Reply.header(0x04), MsgPut.header(0x01), payload_len, payload]`. Err is a leaf with no inner MID wrap, so a literal Response(Err) wire ends with `[Err.header(0x05), payload_len, payload]` — the Err MID byte position is identical to where the Reply chain's Reply.header sits, allowing the peer's outer Response decoder to discriminate on that byte.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added `build_response_err_literal(request_id, keyexpr_suffix, payload)` and `build_response_err_aliased(request_id, mapping_id, suffix, payload)`. Mirror R121j-3 Reply builders with `ResponseVariant::CodecZenohErr(Err)` arm instead of `CodecZenohReply(Reply)`. Minimal Err shape (header=0x05 MID only, no E encoding, no Z exts, no payload prefix beyond payload_len + bytes).

Structural difference from Reply documented: Reply wraps a MsgPut which itself carries a MID byte (0x01) before its own payload_len/payload pair, so a literal Response(Reply) wire ends with `[Reply.header(0x04), MsgPut.header(0x01), payload_len, payload]`. Err is a leaf with no inner MID wrap, so a literal Response(Err) wire ends with `[Err.header(0x05), payload_len, payload]` — the Err MID byte position is identical to where the Reply chain's Reply.header sits, allowing the peer's outer Response decoder to discriminate on that byte.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — added four unit tests. literal byte-compare (small rid + multi-byte VLE rid=200), aliased byte-compare (pure alias + composite), and two `#[should_panic]` rejections (literal empty suffix, aliased zero mapping_id). Inner-arm sanity verifies the Err struct shape independently.

Out of scope (audit-traced carry): `_with_encoding(...)` sets Err.header.E(0x40) + emits the Encoding sub-codec inline; `_with_source_info(...)` sets Err.header.Z + emits a source_info ext entry (ext_id=0x01 ZBUF); `_with_attachment(...)` similar for ext_id=0x05. AP MVP queryable error path does not need encoding hints or source-info exts; the minimal shape here ships first.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R121j-3 + R121j-4 outbound layer now complete in minimal shape. Queryable-side reply / err path: caller constructs Response via build_response_reply_* or build_response_err_*, encodes with encode_frame_with_response, hands to the link driver. The actual queryable dispatch wiring (when does wz CHOOSE to emit Reply vs Err) is part of R121j-5 inbound parser + on_query callback territory.

R121j-3/4 sub-helpers carry intact: consolidation / responder / del-body / encoding hints / source-info exts. None are AP MVP-blocking. The textbook RequestQueryBuilder / ResponseReplyBuilder pattern (per-layer Option fields + chained setters + ordered .build() materializer) becomes the right textbook fix when 8+ helpers exist OR when a multi-layer caller surfaces.

R121j-5 (inbound Request(Query) parser + on_query callback + QueryableTable) carry intact. Now that BOTH outbound directions of Query/Reply are functional, R121j-5 is the next major AP MVP closure target. Scope: (1) inbound Request parser that surfaces the Query body to a per-keyexpr callback table, (2) per-session QueryableTable (id → callback fn + keyexpr binding) registered via send_declare_queryable, (3) callback signature design (Query handle with reply / err methods that internally call build_response_*). Estimated 2-3 rounds; significant new surface for QueryableTable type and async lifecycle. Recommended as the next non-perf-bump session focus.

Round 121j-4-retract.decision_summary: R121j-4c/-3b carry retraction: wire-absent. zenoh-pico Err has no attachment ext (message.c:545-573); Reply-body has no extensions chain (message.c:507-519). R121j-4b and -3c remain wire-valid.
changes_bullets: R121j-4c (ResponseErrBuilder.attachment): RETRACTED. zenoh-pico _z_err_encode at src/protocol/codec/message.c:545-573 encodes only encoding (via _Z_FLAG_Z_E_E header bit) and source_info ext (_Z_MSG_EXT_ENC_ZBUF | 0x01). No attachment ext (0x05) emitted. _z_err_decode_extension at message.c:574-589 handles 0x01 only; default arm returns _z_msg_ext_unknown_error(extension, 0x0a). Adding .attachment(...) would emit bytes the peer treats as unknown-mandatory error.

No extensions chain at the Reply body level. _z_reply_decode_extension at message.c:520-528 is a stub that always returns _z_msg_ext_unknown_error(extension, 0x0a). Reply-body source_info is wire-absent; source_info on the inner MsgPut body is a separate concern (MsgPut ext, not a Reply-level builder setter).

Both mutate the outer Err/Response envelope, not the Reply inner body.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs ResponseErrBuilder gains a new source_info: Option<(Vec<u8>, u32, u32)> field and the chainable setter pub fn source_info(self, zid: &[u8], eid: u32, sn: u32). The setter asserts (1..=16).contains(&zid.len()) per the zenoh-pico ZenohId wire constraint at transport.h:31-37; defence-in-depth assert is repeated inside encode_source_info_ext_body so future direct helper callers cannot smuggle invalid lengths past the public boundary.

build() extends the CodecZenohErr arm: when source_info is set, err.header |= 0x80 (_Z_FLAG_Z_Z) and err.extensions = Some(vec![ExtEntry { header: 0x40 | 0x01, body: ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf(ExtZbuf { value_len, value }) }]) where value = encode_source_info_ext_body(&zid, eid, sn). Sole-entry shape (no Z chain-continuation bit) matches zenoh-pico _z_err_encode at message.c:545-573 which emits source_info as the only ext-chain element; future Err exts (if any) will plumb the chain bits via the same iter-and-set-Z idiom used in RequestQueryBuilder.build at session_glue.rs:2772-2782.

New module-scope helper encode_source_info_ext_body(zid: &[u8], eid: u32, sn: u32) -> Vec<u8> at session_glue.rs builds the ExtZbuf value body: pushes ((zid_len - 1) << 4) as the leading byte, then the raw zid bytes, then VLE(eid) and VLE(sn). Capacity pre-reserved = 1 + zid.len() + 5 + 5 to fit the worst-case VLE u32 length pair. Wire layout exactly matches zenoh-pico _z_source_info_encode_ext at message.c:243-254 (whose `zsize(ext_size)` length prefix is supplied by the surrounding ExtZbuf codec's value_len field).

New module-scope helper encode_vle_u64_into(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u64) emits a base-128 zint into a Vec<u8>. Free-function shape (no SceSink) because the source_info ext body is constructed before any SceSink is in scope: the body lives inside ExtZbuf.value and the surrounding ext codec sees only the already-built Vec<u8>. Mirrors the inline VLE loop in encode_frame_envelope (session_glue.rs:3663-3669) and zenoh-pico _z_zsize_encode at src/protocol/codec/core.c.

Round 121j-5a.decision_summary: R121j-5a reconnaissance: Request inbound parser already wired via parse_frame_payload; R121j-5b/c carry QueryableTable in new query.rs + Fn(Query, &QueryResponder) on_query dispatch and Reply emit.
changes_bullets: Reconnaissance round; no source code mutation. Design decisions only, materialized in carry_forward for R121j-5b/c sub-rounds.

Verified Request::decode already complete via SCE codegen at crates/target/debug/build/wz-codecs-*/out/request.rs:97-147 — 1:1 with zenoh-pico _z_request_decode (network.c:209-238): rid(VLE) + keyexpr(N/M flag) + extensions(Z flag, ExtEntry chain capacity 4) + 4-variant body dispatch (MsgPut/MsgDel/Query/Default).

Verified parse_frame_payload at crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs:4172 already emits NetworkMessage::Request(Box<Request>) from Frame.payload bytes — the silent gap is *not* parser absence but downstream dispatch absence.

Silent gap identified: registry.dispatch arms at crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs:278-282 cover only NetworkMessage::Push (dispatch_push) and NetworkMessage::Declare (absorb_declare). Request/Response/ResponseFinal/Interest/Oam variants fall through silently with no panic or trace.

Design decision A — location: QueryableTable lives in a new crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs module, mirroring pubsub.rs's SubscriberRegistry pattern. Rationale: separation of concerns, session_glue.rs already 5500+ lines, and Reply emit helpers naturally colocate with the table they emit on behalf of.

Design decision B — callback shape: on_query: Fn(Query, &QueryResponder) where QueryResponder exposes send_reply / send_err / send_final methods matching the zenoh API split (z_query_reply / z_query_reply_err / z_query_reply_final). Multi-reply and per-reply error reporting are supported without forcing an async-stream return shape that would conflict with the MCU runtime contract.

Design decision C — dispatch wiring: R121j-5c will add a third arm to pubsub.rs registry.dispatch (or, equivalently, pass a sibling QueryableRegistry into poll_and_dispatch_one alongside SubscriberRegistry) so NetworkMessage::Request invokes QueryableTable::dispatch_request before the message is dropped. changes_bullets: New file crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs (~480 lines) mirrors crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs SubscriberRegistry surface for the Q-side. Exports QueryableRegistry, QueryableId, QueryableCallback = Box<dyn FnMut(&Query, &mut QueryResponder<'_>) + Send + 'static>, QueryResponder<'a>, QueryReply (Reply { Put|Del } | Err), and ReplyBody. Re-uses pubsub::keyexpr_pattern_matches for the chunk-wildcard matcher so subscriber and queryable patterns are byte-identical in matching semantics.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs registers `pub mod query;` with a doc-comment explaining the R121j-5b vs R121j-5c split (registry + Responder land now; the dispatch_iteration_event wiring that turns the accumulated Vec<QueryReply> into outbound Response frames is R121j-5c scope).

QueryableRegistry::dispatch_request(&mut self, request: &Request, peer_keyexpr_table: &HashMap<u64, String>, replies: &mut Vec<QueryReply>) routes inbound Request(Query) to matched queryables. Non-Query RequestVariant arms (MsgPut|MsgDel|Default) are silently no-ops (matches zenoh-pico _z_handle_request which only routes Query through the queryable callback path). Peer-alias resolution is delegated to a caller-provided &HashMap<u64, String> rather than owning a private copy — the integration site (R121j-5c) will lend SubscriberRegistry's table so DeclKexpr / UndeclKexpr absorbed by the subscriber path automatically inform queryable resolution. No dual-write bookkeeping; no Arc-shared state required.

QueryResponder<'a> is a short-lived borrow constructed per matched queryable: holds (rid, keyexpr_literal, &mut Vec<QueryReply>). Exposes send_reply(payload), send_reply_del(), send_err(encoding_id, schema, payload), plus rid() / keyexpr_literal() accessors for diagnostic surfaces. Drops before dispatch_request advances to the next queryable so user closures cannot retain the borrow. FnMut signature (not async) keeps the dispatch path suitable for the (c11, bare_metal) runtime crate target.

QueryReply::into_response(self) -> Response composes the wire-form Response by delegating to the existing ResponseReplyBuilder / ResponseErrBuilder. Put path: ResponseReplyBuilder::new(rid, 0, Some(&keyexpr_literal), &payload).build(). Del path: same with .reply_del() flip. Err path: ResponseErrBuilder::new(...) with optional .encoding(id, schema) chained when QueryReply::Err.encoding is Some. Reply keyexpr emitted in literal form (mapping_id=0 + Some(literal)) per zenoh-pico parity — alias declaration on the responder side is a Phase D+ optimisation.

Each pins a specific invariant: dispatch semantics, alias resolution, body-arm filtering, callback shape, replies accumulation, builder round-trip parity, ordering.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs gains `pub fn peer_keyexpr_table(&self) -> &HashMap<u64, String>`. Lends the SubscriberRegistry-owned mapping table to the queryable side so DeclKexpr / UndeclKexpr absorbed by the subscriber path automatically informs queryable resolution — no dual-write bookkeeping, no Arc<Mutex<...>> needed. Doc-comment makes the cross-registry sharing contract explicit.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs gains `pub fn dispatch_messages(&mut self, messages: &[NetworkMessage], peer_keyexpr_table: &HashMap<u64, String>, pending_replies: &mut Vec<QueryReply>, pending_final_rids: &mut Vec<u64>)`. Iterates messages, routes each NetworkMessage::Request through dispatch_request, and — only when dispatch_request actually emitted at least one Reply for this rid — enqueues the rid into pending_final_rids so the caller emits exactly one ResponseFinal per Reply chain (zenoh-pico parity: many Reply + one Final per Query). Un-resolvable mapping ids, non-Query body arms, and unmatched keyexprs all yield zero Replies and zero Finals — no false 'Final without Reply' wire shape.

query.rs also adds `pub fn dispatch_iteration_event(...)` adapter that pulls FramePayload.messages out of IterationEvent::Poll(DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload {messages, ..}) and forwards to dispatch_messages. Mirror of SubscriberRegistry::dispatch_iteration_event so the queryable integration site uses the same observer-callback shape as the subscriber side.

query.rs gains the module-level helper `pub fn response_final_for(rid: u64) -> ResponseFinal` that constructs a wire-correct ResponseFinal envelope (header = _Z_MID_N_RESPONSE_FINAL = 0x1A; extensions = None today). Uses `..ResponseFinal::default()` spread so the helper stays resilient to future ResponseFinal field additions that land with sensible defaults.

5 new lib tests on the dispatch_messages + response_final_for surface: dispatch_messages_emits_final_for_each_matched_request (two matched + one unmatched -> exactly two Finals for the matched rids), dispatch_messages_skips_final_when_no_queryable_matched, dispatch_messages_skips_final_when_keyexpr_unresolvable, dispatch_messages_ignores_push_response_declare_variants (non-Query body arms produce no Reply / no Final), response_final_for_uses_default_header_and_explicit_rid (header bit + rid + extensions=None invariants).

Integration site (TCP-driven wz_initiator <-> wz_acceptor end-to-end Query/Reply round-trip via a registered queryable) intentionally deferred to a follow-up sub-round. R121j-5c stages the wire-level dispatch primitives and tests them in isolation; the e2e harness layering (LinkDriver send + frame-encode sequencing + sn assignment) requires its own design pass to decide the SessionLinkActions vs application-side ownership of the queryable registry. The lib-test surface here pins the wire-shape contract independent of that decision.

publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs gains `pub fn peer_keyexpr_table(&self) -> &HashMap<u64, String>`. Lends the SubscriberRegistry-owned mapping table to the queryable side so DeclKexpr / UndeclKexpr absorbed by the subscriber path automatically informs queryable resolution — no dual-write bookkeeping, no Arc<Mutex<...>> needed. Doc-comment makes the cross-registry sharing contract explicit.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs gains `pub fn dispatch_messages(&mut self, messages: &[NetworkMessage], peer_keyexpr_table: &HashMap<u64, String>, pending_replies: &mut Vec<QueryReply>, pending_final_rids: &mut Vec<u64>)`. Iterates messages, routes each NetworkMessage::Request through dispatch_request, and — only when dispatch_request actually emitted at least one Reply for this rid — enqueues the rid into pending_final_rids so the caller emits exactly one ResponseFinal per Reply chain (zenoh-pico parity: many Reply + one Final per Query). Un-resolvable mapping ids, non-Query body arms, and unmatched keyexprs all yield zero Replies and zero Finals — no false 'Final without Reply' wire shape.

query.rs also adds `pub fn dispatch_iteration_event(...)` adapter that pulls FramePayload.messages out of IterationEvent::Poll(DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload {messages, ..}) and forwards to dispatch_messages. Mirror of SubscriberRegistry::dispatch_iteration_event so the queryable integration site uses the same observer-callback shape as the subscriber side.

query.rs gains the module-level helper `pub fn response_final_for(rid: u64) -> ResponseFinal` that constructs a wire-correct ResponseFinal envelope (header = _Z_MID_N_RESPONSE_FINAL = 0x1A; extensions = None today). Uses `..ResponseFinal::default()` spread so the helper stays resilient to future ResponseFinal field additions that land with sensible defaults.

5 new lib tests on the dispatch_messages + response_final_for surface: dispatch_messages_emits_final_for_each_matched_request (two matched + one unmatched -> exactly two Finals for the matched rids), dispatch_messages_skips_final_when_no_queryable_matched, dispatch_messages_skips_final_when_keyexpr_unresolvable, dispatch_messages_ignores_push_response_declare_variants (non-Query body arms produce no Reply / no Final), response_final_for_uses_default_header_and_explicit_rid (header bit + rid + extensions=None invariants).

Integration site (TCP-driven wz_initiator <-> wz_acceptor end-to-end Query/Reply round-trip via a registered queryable) intentionally deferred to a follow-up sub-round. R121j-5c stages the wire-level dispatch primitives and tests them in isolation; the e2e harness layering (LinkDriver send + frame-encode sequencing + sn assignment) requires its own design pass to decide the SessionLinkActions vs application-side ownership of the queryable registry. The lib-test surface here pins the wire-shape contract independent of that decision.

changes_bullets: `.githooks/pre-push` reads the git protocol stdin (`<local_ref> <local_sha> <remote_ref> <remote_sha>` per ref) and fast-exits with status 0 when no row has a non-zero `local_sha` — i.e. empty stdin (redundant push after another invocation updated the remote) or delete-only push (no new commit to validate).

`.githooks/pre-push` acquires a non-blocking `flock(1)` advisory lock on `$GIT_DIR/run-ci.lock` before entering `scripts/run-ci.sh`; failure exits 1 with an explicit `another run-ci already running` message + lock path so concurrent push attempts fail loud instead of silently racing `crates/target` cargo lock + sce-codegen freshness rebuild.
`flock(1)` presence guard via `command -v flock` so the advisory lock degrades to a no-op on slimmed containers without util-linux instead of hard-failing the hook.

Round 227.decision_summary: R227 self-publish loopback: SubscriberRegistry::local_publish surfaces wire-equivalent dispatch with is_remote=false; SessionLocal activates, Remote suppressed, single fire_to_subscribers gate
changes_bullets: `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::SubscriberRegistry` adds public method `local_publish(&mut self, sample: &Sample) -> usize` — self-publish loopback entry point. Routes the caller-built `Sample` through `fire_to_subscribers` with `is_remote = false`, applying `Locality::allows_local()` so `SessionLocal` + `Any` fire and `Remote` is suppressed. Returns the count of subscriber callbacks that fired so the caller can verify loopback delivery. Mirrors zenoh-pico `_z_session_deliver_push_locally` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/loopback.c` 70-100) which is routed from `_z_write` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/primitives.c` 198-202) when the publisher's `allowed_destination.allows_local()` holds.

`pubsub.rs::dispatch_push` signature extends from `(push, reliability)` to `(push, reliability, is_remote: bool)`; the private fn is the wire-arrived dispatch entry, so the change is internal-only and the public `dispatch` / `dispatch_iteration_event` surfaces are unchanged. The `dispatch` body now passes `true` for `NetworkMessage::Push` per R227 single-dispatch-path semantic. The user pre-confirmed (a) `dispatch_push` signature extension over (b) a sibling `local_dispatch_push` entry point — the (a) shape preserves zenoh-pico's `_z_handle_network_message` single-handler invariant.

New helper `fire_to_subscribers(&mut self, sample: &Sample, is_remote: bool) -> usize` factors out the locality-predicate + pattern-match + callback-fire loop previously inlined at the end of `dispatch_push`. Selects `Locality::allows_remote()` when `is_remote=true` and `Locality::allows_local()` otherwise, then matches each subscriber's pattern chunks against `sample.keyexpr` via `keyexpr_pattern_matches`. Returns the fired count; the wire path discards it, `local_publish` returns it to the caller. The helper is the single source of truth for subscriber filtering — both wire and loopback paths converge here so the locality + pattern-match invariants are enforced exactly once.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/locality.rs` module doc retires the pre-R227 'carry: not in any current cluster' wording. The new doc states both invariants: wire-arrived Push routes through `dispatch_push` with `is_remote=true` → `allows_remote()` (`SessionLocal` suppressed, `Any`/`Remote` fire), and `local_publish` routes through `fire_to_subscribers` with `is_remote=false` → `allows_local()` (`Remote` suppressed, `Any`/`SessionLocal` fire). QueryableRegistry-side loopback parity is noted as deferred until the use case surfaces.

`pubsub.rs` module-level Scope section extends with the R227 loopback bullet pointing at `SubscriberRegistry::local_publish`, the `Locality::SessionLocal` activation, the `Locality::Remote` loopback suppression, and the zenoh-pico mirror citations (`loopback.c` 70-100 + `primitives.c` 198-202).

`LocalPublishRequest` builder NOT introduced — `Sample` is already `#[non_exhaustive]` with `new_put` / `new_del` + 6 `with_*` setters covering all 9 fields, so reusing `Sample` as the publish input is the textbook choice (R225 lesson #5 surface-all-at-once already satisfied without a new sibling type).

12 new R227 unit tests on `local_publish`: `Locality::Any` fires; `Locality::SessionLocal` fires (R227 activation guard — was dormant before); `Locality::Remote` suppressed (zenoh-pico `_z_locality_allows_local(Z_LOCALITY_REMOTE)` parity); mixed-locality isolation (3 subscribers on the same keyexpr — loopback fires `Any` + `SessionLocal`, wire-arrived dispatch fires `Any` + `Remote`, same registry, single source of truth); empty-registry returns 0; pattern-mismatch returns 0; multi-subscriber count returns total fired (`fired = 2` for two overlapping matches); `**` zero-or-more wildcard matches on loopback; `$*` intra-chunk DSL (R220) matches on loopback; `Sample` fields propagate verbatim (registry does not synthesize); `SampleKind::Del` routes through the same path as Put with empty payload; locality predicate runs before keyexpr match (regression guard).

Round 228.decision_summary: R228 Session bundle: Arc<SessionLinkActions> + Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>; publish() fans wire + loopback per PublishOptions.allowed_destination Locality predicate
changes_bullets: New module `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs` introduces `Session` — the application-level bundle mirroring zenoh-pico's `_z_session_t`. `Session` owns `Arc<SessionLinkActions>` (outbound handle) and `Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` (inbound registries bundle). A single `Session::publish(keyexpr, payload, opts)` call fans both branches: wire-side `send_push_literal` / `send_push_del_literal` under `Locality::allows_remote()`, and loopback `SubscriberRegistry::local_publish` under `Locality::allows_local()`. Mirrors `_z_write` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/net/primitives.c` 170-205) which is the single zenoh-pico entry point that fans both branches off a single record.

`PublishOptions` is the new options bundle for `Session::publish`. `#[non_exhaustive]` to allow R229+ additions without breaking external callers. R228 scope: 3 fields (`allowed_destination: Locality`, `reliability: Reliability`, `kind: SampleKind`). Builder API: `put()` / `del()` constructors (defaults to `Any` locality + `Reliable` + matching kind) + `with_locality(...)` / `with_reliability(...)` / `with_kind(...)` chainable setters. The remaining 5 `Sample` body fields (`qos`, `attachment`, `timestamp`, `encoding`, `source_info`) are deferred to R229+ because the wire-side `send_push_literal` does not accept them either — propagating them through `Session::publish` now would silently fork wire (loses metadata) vs loopback (preserves metadata) symmetry.

`Session::publish` reads `opts.allowed_destination` and routes: `allows_remote()` → wire send through the existing `SessionLinkActions` API (Put picks `send_push_literal`, Del picks `send_push_del_literal`; the `payload` argument is ignored on Del kind — zenoh-pico `_z_n_msg_make_push_del` does not carry payload). `allows_local()` → build a `Sample` via `Sample::new_put` / `Sample::new_del` + `with_reliability(opts.reliability)` and dispatch through `observer.lock().unwrap().subscribers.local_publish(&sample)`. Returns the loopback `fired` count (0 when wire-only or no matching subscriber).

`Session::actions(&self) -> &Arc<SessionLinkActions>` and `Session::observer(&self) -> &Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` accessors expose the handles for non-publish call sites (e.g. `send_declare_subscriber` / `send_request_query` still go through `actions()`, callback registration goes through `observer().lock().unwrap().subscribers.register(...)`). This keeps `Session` from monopolizing the API surface during the migration window.

`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs` adds `pub mod session;` with a 9-line doc block citing R228 scope, the `_z_session_t` zenoh-pico mirror, and the R229+ carry list. The module slot lives after `observer` so the dependency order (`observer::ApplicationLayerObserver` defined first, then `session::Session` bundles it) is reflected in lib-level ordering.

Locking discipline (module-level doc): `Arc<Mutex<ApplicationLayerObserver>>` uses `std::sync::Mutex` (not `tokio::sync::Mutex`) because the loopback branch fires subscriber callbacks synchronously — exactly the semantic of zenoh-pico's `_z_session_deliver_push_locally` which fires callbacks in-line under the session lock. A `tokio::sync::Mutex` would force `publish` to be `async`, propagating an unnecessary coloring change across every call site for no measurable benefit (the lock window is one subscriber-table walk).

Round 229.decision_summary: R229 Session::publish_aliased: mapping_id + suffix + caller-asserted loopback_keyexpr; mirrors send_push_aliased on wire side, fires local_publish on loopback with the asserted literal
changes_bullets: `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs::Session` adds `publish_aliased(mapping_id, inline_suffix, loopback_keyexpr, payload, opts)` — aliased-keyexpr counterpart to R228's `publish` for literal keyexpr. Wire branch routes through `SessionLinkActions::send_push_aliased` (Put) or `send_push_del_aliased` (Del) so the peer resolves the keyexpr through its inbound mapping table (populated by an earlier outbound `send_declare_keyexpr`). Loopback branch builds a `Sample` with `loopback_keyexpr` as the literal and dispatches through the same `SubscriberRegistry::local_publish` the R227 wire-path-equivalent does. Returns the loopback fired count, same shape as `publish`.

Caller precondition documented inline: `loopback_keyexpr` MUST equal the literal form the peer would resolve `(mapping_id, inline_suffix)` to. Typical usage: (1) `send_declare_keyexpr(7, "home/temp")` registers `7 -> "home/temp"` on the peer; (2) `publish_aliased(7, None, "home/temp", payload, opts)` carries `(id=7, suffix=None)` on the wire and fires loopback on `"home/temp"`. With an inline suffix: `publish_aliased(7, Some("/kitchen"), "home/temp/kitchen", payload, opts)` carries `(id=7, suffix="/kitchen")` on the wire and fires loopback on `"home/temp/kitchen"` — the caller resolves the composite form explicitly.

Caller-resolved `loopback_keyexpr` choice over wz-side outbound mapping table: zenoh-pico's `_z_session_t._local_resources` is the local-side resolution table populated by self-declarations (`vendor/zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/session/resource.h`). wz does not yet have an equivalent outbound table — introducing one is the natural R230+ carry. Until then, the caller is the single source of truth for the loopback literal; documented inline.

Implementation re-uses R228 patterns verbatim: locality predicate selects branches; `opts.kind` selects Put-vs-Del routing; `Sample::with_reliability(opts.reliability)` propagates the link-layer hint into `Sample.reliability`. The two branches are independent (wire branch ignores the loopback_keyexpr argument; loopback branch ignores the mapping_id + inline_suffix pair) so callers can intentionally decouple the wire form from the loopback form, which the regression-guard test pins.

verification_bullets: `cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib`: 281 -> 290 (+9) all pass. The 9 R229 tests exhaustively cover the Locality x kind x reliability x suffix matrix for the aliased path, plus the regression-guard for the loopback-keyexpr-independence contract.
