src/runtime.rs Runtime trait: type JoinHandle<T: Send + 'static>: Future<Output = Result<T, RuntimeError>> + Send + 'static GAT + spawn<F: Future + Send + 'static>(fut: F) -> Self::JoinHandle<F::Output>. Mirrors tokio JoinHandle as a Future contract so tokio impl can satisfy directly via JoinError -> RuntimeError::JoinFailed wrap.
src/time.rs TimeSource trait: now_monotonic_ms(&self) -> u64 + sleep(&self, ms: u64) -> impl Future<Output=()> + Send + '_ (RPITIT shape user-confirmed; Rust 1.75 stable).

src/allocator.rs Allocator trait: alloc(&self, Layout) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> + unsafe dealloc(&self, NonNull<u8>, Layout). Local trait (NOT core::alloc::Allocator which is nightly-only on MSRV 1.75) with explicit Option-on-OOM failure surface; buffer-pool / TLSF allocator pivot space preserved.

src/error.rs RuntimeError enum: JoinFailed + Shutdown variants, non_exhaustive. Display impl. core::error::Error impl deferred (requires MSRV 1.81); std::error::Error impl behind std feature deferred to R252+ AP integration round.
src/lib.rs cfg_attr no_std gate + alloc extern + module re-exports. deny(missing_docs) for trait-surface doc completeness.

Round 264.decision_summary: R264 closes the R263 verification debt by adding a Layer E fixture that spawns 2x wz-ap-demo (silent acceptor + initiator with --query-timeout-ms 500 --on-query-final-log) and asserts FINAL RECEIVED rid=1 fires within 400-2000 ms wall-time; the fixture surfaced an architectural gap where the R262 in-loop on_tick sweep could not fire sub-second because (a) the lease-bound sleep arm cadence is ~10 s on production AP params and (b) clamping the sleep arm with a sweep_tick_ms parameter inside drive_session_until_terminal cancels poll_and_dispatch_one mid-frame which is NOT cancel-safe for length-prefixed link drivers such as wz-ap-demo's InboundReadDriver; the R264 fix moves the sweep to a dedicated spawned task driven by TimeSource::sleep(100) so the drive_session loop's poll future runs to completion without competing select arms.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_ap_demo_query_timeout.rs: new Layer E fixture #[ignore]-gated. Spawns acceptor `wz-ap-demo --listen <port> --key demo/timeout` (subscriber declared, no queryable so the inbound Query has no responder and silently sinks at the peer), waits 5 s for 'listening on' witness, drops PortReservation, spawns initiator `wz-ap-demo --connect <port> --query demo/timeout --query-timeout-ms 500 --on-query-final-log`, waits 2 s for 'FINAL RECEIVED rid=1' stderr witness. Wall-time elapsed since initiator_start asserted 400 ms <= elapsed <= 2000 ms: 400 ms lower bound catches a deadline_ms=0 register-time regression; 2000 ms upper bound catches sweep cadence stall.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: new sweep_task spawned BEFORE drive_session_until_terminal. The task is an unbounded `loop { sweep_clock.sleep(100).await; <lock observer; sweep_timed_out(now_monotonic_ms()); drop lock> }` using the shared session_clock TokioTime (Copy + 'static). Implementation uses TimeSource::sleep only (no tokio::time::interval) so MCU profiles inherit the same code-shape via their concrete TimeSource impl. After drive_session_until_terminal returns the test calls sweep_task.abort(); abort() is sufficient because the task body holds no shared mutable state beyond the observer Arc<Mutex<>> (cleanly dropped on task join) and has no on-Drop cleanup requirements.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: drive_session on_tick closure becomes a no-op `|_now_ms| {}`. The R263 in-loop sweep call inside on_tick is removed because single-source sweep cadence in the dedicated task is cleaner than double-sourced (B' option chosen in R264 kickoff). The on_tick parameter is preserved on the drive_session API surface for future per-iteration observability uses.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: R260/R263 comment block above the drive_session call refreshed to reflect single-source sweep architecture; the R262/R263 reference to in-loop sweep removed; new R264 sweep_task comment block (~12 lines) documents the cancel-safety rationale + sweep cadence sizing + MCU-portability shape choice.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: drive_session_until_terminal doc-comment adds a 'R264 cancel-safety carry' note explaining that poll_and_dispatch_one is NOT cancel-safe for length-prefixed drivers (wz-ap-demo InboundReadDriver reads u16 length then payload via two read_exact calls; select! cancel between the two consumes the length bytes from the socket but drops the captured len, the next iteration's poll then mis-aligns by 2 bytes). carry_forward_bullets: R264 lesson: any architectural decision that adds select! arms to drive_session_until_terminal must FIRST audit poll_and_dispatch_one's cancel-safety against the concrete LinkDriver impls in scope (wz-ap-demo InboundReadDriver uses length-prefixed read_exact x2 — NOT cancel-safe). The original R264 attempt to add a sweep_tick_ms parameter that clamps the lease sleep arm tripped this hazard and broke wz_query_reply_round_trip. Future architectural changes touching the inner select! must include the cancel-safety audit in the design step.

R264 lesson: AskUserQuestion sequence (3 rounds of questions in one round of work) is the correct pattern when an architectural attempt surfaces a downstream regression mid-execution. Each AskUserQuestion presented previews of code shape so the user could evaluate the trade-off without reading source. The textbook beats 'silently revert and pick a different approach' because it leaves audit trace of the decision chain.

InboundReadDriver poll_event cancel-safety hazard (R264 surfaced): the function reads u16 length then variable-length payload via two read_exact calls. select! cancel between the calls drops the captured length and leaves the socket cursor 2 bytes ahead of where the next iteration expects. This was acceptable under R263 lease=10 s cadence (cancellation rare in steady-state traffic) but blocks any future sub-second sweep cadence work that would race poll_and_dispatch. Textbook fix: make poll_event truly cancel-safe by buffering partial-read state in InboundReadDriver. Scope estimate: 1-2 rounds (read state machine + matching changes in any other length-prefixed driver impl). Tag: cancel-safety carry, R265+.

R264 production-grade follow-ups (deferred to dedicated rounds): (a) FinalCallback FinalCause Normal vs TimedOut differentiation — wz-ap-demo's FINAL RECEIVED log line currently logs the same shape for both peer-final and timeout-sweep-final; if a deploy use case needs to differentiate, promote FinalCallback to FnMut(u64, FinalCause). YAGNI hold pending user inspection. (b) sweep cadence configurability via deploy.yaml — the 100 ms constant is currently a hardcoded literal in wz-ap-demo run_demo; production AP deploys may want to tune per topology. Topology-schema migration carry (R123b-pre) already tracks this surface.

R264 carry: sweep_task graceful shutdown is via abort() which is fine for current state (no async-cleanup-needed). If sweep_task ever owns external resources (open files, network sockets, etc.) abort() may bypass Drop guarantees; the textbook upgrade is a CancellationToken + select! { tick | cancel } shape. Not needed now; documented for the cancel-safety carry round.

R264 carry: drive_session_until_terminal's on_tick API parameter is now a no-op closure in wz-ap-demo (the only production caller). The R262 API surface is preserved for future per-iteration observability uses but currently has no consumer. YAGNI hold — if a future round confirms no consumer materializes by R270+, consider removing on_tick and the 11 caller sites (single revert via reverse-of-R262 commit shape).

Round 265.decision_summary: R265 closes the R264 cancel-safety carry by refactoring TcpDriver::poll_event (lib) and InboundReadDriver::poll_event (wz-ap-demo) from a read_exact-based shape (which dropped in-flight bytes on tokio::select! cancellation, leaving the next iteration's poll re-syncing from a mis-aligned socket cursor) into a ReadState state machine where each .await is a single .read() syscall (cancel-safe per tokio's documented contract) and the partial-read buffer survives cancellation in &mut self.read_state; the impl now matches the cancel-safety contract that drive_session_until_terminal's doc-comment had been claiming since R76b, and a new tcp_driver_cancel_safety.rs integration suite exercises the contract end-to-end against a real loopback TcpStream pair with 4 scenarios.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: new ReadState enum (Idle / Length{prefix: [u8; 2], offset: usize} / Payload{frame: Vec<u8>, offset: usize}) with Default derived on Idle. TcpDriver gains a read_state field; from_stream constructor initialises it to Idle. poll_event becomes `loop { match &mut self.read_state { ... } }` where each .await is a single stream.read(...) call. EOF (Ok(0)) and OS error branches reset read_state to Idle. The frame-complete branch takes the buffer out via std::mem::take, resets state, only then runs StreamEnvelope::decode.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: new InboundReadState enum (same Idle/Length/Payload shape, locally defined so the binary does not depend on a library-internal type). InboundReadDriver gains read_state; construction site passes InboundReadState::Idle. poll_event refactored to mirror TcpDriver. log::debug 'inbound frame' line moves into the frame-complete branch (only fires when a frame is reassembled).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/tcp_driver_cancel_safety.rs: new integration test file (4 scenarios). loopback_pair() helper builds a TcpListener-backed (writer: TcpStream, driver: TcpDriver) pair with TCP_NODELAY enabled on both sides so test write_all + flush sequences hit the wire promptly. envelope_bytes() helper encodes a payload through StreamEnvelope::encode_to_vec for byte-identical wire shape vs production. assert_rx_payload() re-encodes the received bytes back through StreamEnvelope::decode as a double-check.

tcp_driver_cancel_safety scenarios: (1) partial-length-prefix-survives-cancel: write 1 of 2 length-prefix bytes, race poll_event against 100 ms sleep (sleep wins), write remainder, verify Rx with full payload. (2) partial-payload-survives-cancel: write prefix + 5 of N payload bytes, race+sleep, write more, race+sleep again, write remainder, verify Rx — exercises multi-cancellation resilience. (3) eof-mid-frame-surfaces-PeerClosed: write partial frame + shutdown writer, verify Lost{PeerClosed}. (4) back-to-back-frames-with-intermediate-cancel: write entire first frame + second frame prefix only, first poll returns first frame, second poll parks (race+sleep wins), write second-frame payload, second poll returns second frame.

Round 266.decision_summary: R266 lands the panic_payload capture path on RuntimeError::JoinFailed under feature = "alloc": tokio's JoinError::into_panic() result is now propagated through to AP-profile callers as Box<dyn Any + Send + 'static>, accessible via a new RuntimeError::panic_payload() accessor + a Display impl that extracts String / &'static str payload bytes as a "panicked: <msg>" suffix; MCU no-alloc builds keep JoinFailed as a unit variant (no heap to box onto, no panic-infrastructure parity); R258's compile-time Send/Sync/Clone/Eq pin gates Sync/Clone/Eq on cfg(not(feature = "alloc")) because Box<dyn Any + Send> is not Sync (tokio surfaces Send-only payloads), not Clone (Any erases the concrete type's Clone) and not PartialEq; tokio test sites switch from assert_eq! against PartialEq-bound Result to matches! against variant shape (preserving R257 panic-vs-cancel split semantics) and unwrap-+-value-compare for Ok(value) checks.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: RuntimeError enum body cfg-gated. Under `feature = "alloc"` JoinFailed becomes struct-like with `payload: Option<Box<dyn core::any::Any + Send + 'static>>`; under !alloc it stays as a unit variant. `#[derive(Debug)]` only at the type-level; `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "alloc"), derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq))]` re-adds the no-alloc trait surface. JoinCancelled / Shutdown unchanged.

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: new smart constructors. `RuntimeError::join_failed()` available in both builds (None-payload under alloc; unit variant under no-alloc); `RuntimeError::join_failed_with_payload(Option<Box<dyn Any + Send + 'static>>)` available only under alloc. The constructor pair lets runtime impls produce the variant without `#[cfg]` switches at the call site (constructor itself dispatches the cfg internally).

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: new `RuntimeError::panic_payload(&self) -> Option<&(dyn Any + Send + 'static)>` accessor. Returns Some(&borrowed Box content) for JoinFailed-with-payload; None for JoinFailed-without-payload, JoinCancelled, Shutdown, or under no-alloc (where the slot does not exist). Doc-comment includes the textbook downcast snippet for the two common panic payload types (String / &'static str).

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: Display impl extended. Under alloc the JoinFailed arm tries `payload.downcast_ref::<String>()` first then `payload.downcast_ref::<&'static str>()`; on match Display emits `RuntimeError: spawned task panicked: <msg>`. Unknown payload type or no-payload falls back to the plain prefix string (preserves log-grep stability for callers that pattern-match on the prefix).

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: std::error::Error impl's source() chain stays None — the panic payload is type-erased Any (not dyn Error), so threading it through `source()` would mislead callers about what the chain carries. Doc-comment documents the rationale + points at panic_payload() as the explicit accessor.

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: compile_time_assertions module updated. _assert_send still pins Send (preserved in both builds; Result<T, RuntimeError> must cross thread boundaries via Future::Output). _assert_sync / _assert_clone / _assert_eq gated on `cfg(not(feature = "alloc"))`. The function calling them gates the alloc-mode assertions accordingly.

crates/wz-runtime-core/src/error.rs: 7 new tests under cfg(all(test, feature = "std")). Cover Box<dyn Error> compatibility (existing); source-chain-is-empty (extended to all variants); panic_payload accessor returns None for non-JoinFailed variants and for JoinFailed-no-payload; payload downcast to String (round-trip from Box<String>); payload downcast to &'static str; Display extracts String payload as suffix; Display extracts static str payload as suffix.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_impl.rs: TokioJoinHandle Future poll impl extracts the panic payload via `join_error.into_panic()` (only safe in the !is_cancelled branch where is_panic() is guaranteed true) and stuffs it into RuntimeError::join_failed_with_payload(Some(payload)). Doc-comment adds a R266 section explaining the capture path + downcast targets.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_impl.rs: existing 4 assert_eq! sites that relied on RuntimeError PartialEq for Err comparison switch to matches! against the variant shape. The R257 assert_ne! sanity check rewrites as two matches! negations (panic_outcome not JoinCancelled; cancel_outcome not JoinFailed).

R266 lesson: when adding a payload field to a non_exhaustive enum, audit downstream `assert_eq!` patterns that implicitly relied on the type's PartialEq impl. The Rust compiler surfaced 4 hit sites cleanly; matches! / expect+compare migration is mechanical. Future enum-payload additions should grep for `assert_eq!.*EnumName::` + `assert_ne!.*EnumName::` before designing the new variant.

R266 lesson: panic infrastructure produces Send-only payloads (Box<dyn Any + Send>), not Send + Sync. The pre-R266 R258 contract pinned Send + Sync at the RuntimeError level; adding the payload necessarily relaxes Sync under alloc. The relaxation is correct (no caller-site relied on shared-by-reference RuntimeError across threads) but it is a contract change worth documenting in the audit entry, not a silent reshape. The Send invariant is preserved (Result<T, RuntimeError> in Future::Output must be Send).

R266 follow-up (deferred): the std::error::Error::source() chain still returns None. An alternative design would wrap the panic payload in a dyn Error newtype that downcasts to the original Box<dyn Any> internally. The chosen design rejects this because (a) Any -> Error is an honest type erasure step that hides the downcast requirement from callers, and (b) the panic_payload() accessor is the textbook explicit-API shape. If a future round adds a richer source chain (e.g. wrapping a tokio-specific JoinError variant in JoinFailed) it should extend source() at that time.

R266 lesson: panic infrastructure produces Send-only payloads (Box<dyn Any + Send>), not Send + Sync. R266 follow-up (deferred): the std::error::Error::source() chain still returns None. An alternative design would wrap the panic payload in a dyn Error newtype that downcasts to the original Box<dyn Any> internally. The chosen design rejects this because (a) Any -> Error is an honest type erasure step that hides the downcast requirement from callers, and (b) the panic_payload() accessor is the textbook explicit-API shape. If a future round adds a richer source chain (e.g. wrapping a tokio-specific JoinError variant in JoinFailed) it should extend source() at that time.

Round 270.decision_summary: R270 adds --sweep-cadence-ms CLI flag to wz-ap-demo replacing the hardcoded 100 ms sweep_task sleep; default 100 preserves existing behaviour, 0 explicitly rejected. Closes R264 carry.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: --sweep-cadence-ms <ms> CLI parse added (lines ~663-687) following the --query-timeout-ms pattern; value 0 explicitly rejected with `wz-ap-demo: --sweep-cadence-ms must be > 0 (0 would busy-loop)` + ExitCode::from(2); non-numeric input rejected with `must be a u32`; default 100 preserves the pre-R270 hardcoded constant.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs ReplyConsumerSpec gains a `sweep_cadence_ms: u32` field with doc-comment explaining the wall-time bound + the parser-side 0-rejection invariant (the struct holds an unwrapped u32 because main's parse path guarantees > 0). The R121j-6-e2e-bundle approach keeps run_demo's clippy::too_many_arguments threshold satisfied — the new knob piggybacks on the existing reply-side spec struct (semantic grouping: sweep cadence is only meaningful when reply consumption is active).

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs run_demo sweep_task body (lines ~1456-1475): hardcoded `sweep_clock.sleep(100)` replaced with `sweep_clock.sleep(sweep_cadence_ms)` where `sweep_cadence_ms = u64::from(reply_log_spec.sweep_cadence_ms)`. The u32 -> u64 widening matches TimeSource::sleep's u64 milliseconds argument. R264 sweep_task preamble comment updated to reference --sweep-cadence-ms instead of the now-removed hardcoded 100.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/main.rs: --help / print_usage updated with the new flag listing in the USAGE summary + a 6-line OPTIONS block explaining the tick-period role + lower-is-tighter trade-off + R264 sweep_task reference. The OPTIONS block phrasing mirrors the --query-timeout-ms surrounding entry for consistency.

R264 carry `sweep cadence deploy.yaml knob (0.5R)` CLOSED via the CLI-flag path. Deploy.yaml schema integration is intentionally out of scope for wz-ap-demo today: wz-ap-demo's config surface is CLI flags (mirroring zenoh-cpp's z_get_options_t.timeout_ms pattern), and the existing deploy/*.yaml schema is centred on MCU/AP platform descriptors (cores, SRAM regions, link configs) rather than application-tunable knobs. A future production AP runtime that consumes deploy.yaml can reuse ReplyConsumerSpec.sweep_cadence_ms via a yaml -> struct deserializer; the field is already u32-typed.

Manual --help inspection: `--sweep-cadence-ms <ms>` appears in the USAGE summary + OPTIONS block; the OPTIONS prose matches the printed help with cargo run wz-ap-demo -- --help.

Manual rejection-path verification: `cargo run --bin wz-ap-demo -- --connect 127.0.0.1:9999 --query demo/test --sweep-cadence-ms 0` exits with code 2 + stderr `wz-ap-demo: --sweep-cadence-ms must be > 0 (0 would busy-loop)`; the same invocation with `--sweep-cadence-ms abc` exits with code 2 + stderr `wz-ap-demo: --sweep-cadence-ms must be a u32 (got "abc")`. Both error paths surface before any TCP connect attempt (parsing happens in main pre-runtime-spawn).

carry_forward_bullets: R264 carry `sweep cadence deploy.yaml knob (R264 carry, 0.5R)` CLOSED at R270 via CLI flag. Deploy.yaml schema integration deferred to a future production AP runtime round.

R270 carry: a future production AP runtime that consumes deploy.yaml can reuse ReplyConsumerSpec.sweep_cadence_ms via a yaml -> struct deserializer; the field is already u32-typed and the parser-side 0-rejection invariant is documented in the struct doc-comment. Phase W lwIP integration will inherit the same knob shape (MCU profile constant via deploy.yaml schema once the schema gains an application-knob section).

R270 lesson: when a `deploy.yaml knob` carry is small enough, the textbook scope respect is to first surface the knob at the existing application config layer (CLI flags here) and defer the deploy.yaml schema integration until the consuming production runtime exists. Reverse order (schema first, application later) would create dead schema fields that no code reads — same anti-pattern class as `feature = "std"` with no std-only code (closed at R269).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/teardown.rs (new, 196 lines) — six typestates (TeardownInitial -> TasksJoined -> TokenDropped -> CloseEmitted -> ActionsDropped -> WriterDrained) with consume-self transitions encode the canonical chain. Per-step doc-comments anchor each transition to its originating round: TeardownInitial::abort_sweep_join_tasks owns R264 sweep_task.abort + R121e 200ms publisher/query/declare task join; TasksJoined::drop_liveliness_token owns R277 token_rx receive + RAII drop that enqueues Declare(UndeclToken) on the writer channel; TokenDropped::emit_close_if_cancelled owns R284 graceful Close(Generic) emit gated on was_cancelled; CloseEmitted::drop_actions owns Arc<SessionLinkActions> drop so the writer-task mpsc sender clones drain; ActionsDropped::drain_writer owns the 50ms writer_handle drain. Reaching WriterDrained is the compile-time witness that all seven steps ran in order.

crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs — pre-R292 inline Step 2-7 body (sweep_task.abort + 3x 200ms task join + token_rx receive+drop + outcome.is_none() Close emit + drop(actions) + 50ms writer_handle drain, ~80 lines of doc-comment-anchored R264/R277/R284 invariants) replaced by the fluent typestate chain. The R292 call-site binding `let _: teardown::WriterDrained = TeardownInitial { ... }.abort_sweep_join_tasks().await.drop_liveliness_token().await.emit_close_if_cancelled().drop_actions().drain_writer().await;` makes the canonical-order witness explicit. run_demo's outer doc-comment redirects readers to crate::teardown for per-step rationale; module-level doc-comment updated to advertise R292 invariant promotion.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — SessionLinkActions struct: `last_inbound_keepalive_at` + `established_at` retyped from `Mutex<Option<Instant>>` to `Mutex<Option<u64>>` (storage is now u64 ms since the shared monotonic epoch); new `pub clock: TokioTime` field carries the shared epoch. `SessionLinkActions::new` signature gains a `clock: TokioTime` parameter so production callers (runner.rs) thread the same `TokioTime` value to actions + drive_session for R263 single-shared-epoch invariant. The two stamp-recording sites (`InboundFrame::KeepAlive` arm of `handle_inbound`, `record_established_at` Lua-bound action) read `self.clock.now_monotonic_ms()`. Doc-comments rewritten across both fields + the new field.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — `check_lease_deadline` signature: `now: Instant` -> `now_ms: u64`. Body rewritten as pure u64 arithmetic: `lease_ms` is the `lease` field times 1000 when `lease_in_seconds`, otherwise as-is; baseline is `max(established_ms, keepalive_ms)`; comparator is `now_ms.saturating_sub(stamp_ms) >= lease_ms`. The `Duration::from_secs/from_millis` calls retired.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — `drive_session_until_terminal` body: `lease_ms` + `lease_deadline_ms: Option<u64>` (`stamp_ms.map(|s| s.saturating_add(lease_ms))`), `remaining_ms = deadline_ms.saturating_sub(now_ms)` for the `clock.sleep(remaining_ms)` race arm, and the lease-branch `check_lease_deadline(actions, engine, clock.now_monotonic_ms())` call. Round 296.decision_summary: R296 closes R293-carry (b) two-side $* matcher — lead/trail anchor pair is exact (zenoh-pico intersects-mode equivalent), not an over-approximation; +8 verify tests + chunk_intersects doc-comment correction.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::chunk_intersects — the (true, true) branch's doc-comment and the surrounding `keyexpr_intersect_patterns` doc are rewritten. The previous text labelled the lead/trail anchor pair check as `R293 over-approximation for two-side `$*`` and pointed at zenoh-pico's `_z_chunk_intersect_left_with_right_substar_substar` as the carry refinement. R296 closure: the lead/trail anchor pair is the exact necessary-and-sufficient condition. Middle `$*`-separated sub-parts on both sides always admit a common chunk literal via alternating interleaving (any two ordered sub-part sequences `[A1..AN]` and `[B1..BM]` are realised by `A1 B1 A2 B2 …`, with each side independently `$*`-floating its own sub-parts). zenoh-pico's `chunk_special_intersects` reaches the same answer through the `right contains $*` over-approximation branch (line 156 of `keyexpr_match_template.h`); every (true, true) input lands there because by precondition both chunks carry at least one `$*`. So wz's algorithm and zenoh-pico's intersects-mode chunk matcher agree on every (true, true) input under canonical wire form.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/pubsub.rs::tests — 8 new verification tests pinning the exact algorithm boundary: `intersect_dsl_both_sides_lead_anchor_mismatch_rejects` (byte-distinct lead anchors `A` vs `B`), `..._trail_anchor_mismatch_rejects` (byte-distinct trail anchors), `..._lead_prefix_compatible_accepts` (lead `A` is a prefix of `AB`), `..._trail_suffix_compatible_accepts` (trail `C` is a suffix of `BC`), `..._middle_sub_parts_always_fit` ([A,B] vs [B,A] interleave in `BABA`), `..._distinct_middles_accept` (`$*ABC$*` ∩ `$*XYZ$*` shares `ABCXYZ`), `..._lead_prefix_with_trail_suffix_overlap` (combined prefix + suffix anchor checks), `..._byte_overlap_lead_rejects` (`AB` vs `AX` share first byte but diverge — neither is a prefix). The pre-existing `intersect_dsl_both_sides_over_approx_documented` is renamed to `intersect_dsl_both_sides_lead_trail_anchor` and its body retained as the trivial `pre$*` ∩ `$*post` case; net wz-runtime-tokio lib test growth 562 → 570 (+8).

changes_bullets: crates/zenoh-pico-sys/wrapper.h + build.rs — expose `_z_keyexpr_forward_intersects` (chunk-level forward-scan matcher that `_z_keyexpr_intersects` in session/keyexpr.c:581 dispatches into). Round 300.decision_summary: R300 closes R299 carry #1 (DoS mitigation): adds outbound DECLARE-side keyexpr gate that rejects R299 bug #3 SIGABRT pattern family pre-emit, plus argv eager-reject in wz-ap-demo.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/keyexpr_canon.rs — adds `OutboundKeyexprError` enum (NotCanonical(KeyexprCanonError) + PicoBugThreeFamily { keyexpr, offending_chunk }) and `check_outbound_keyexpr_pico_safe(input: &str) -> Result<(), OutboundKeyexprError>`. The gate first runs canonize_keyexpr for structural validity, then walks chunks with a 2-flag state machine (seen_double_star + seen_literal_after_double_star, reset on every fresh `**` chunk). Reject fires when both flags are set and the current chunk's canonical form is `*`-shape (single `*`, `**`, or any `$*`-only run via `chunk_canonizes_to_star_shape` private helper). Conservative scope: also rejects trailing `**` after a literal-after-`**` segment (`**/a/**` etc.) — R299 fixture empirically pins SIGABRT only for trailing `*`/`$*` (cannot cross-validate `**` trailing without process abort), but the underlying `in_big_wild` stale-state mechanism does not distinguish the closer's exact star-shape. False-positive zone documented; narrowing pending empirical fork-based pico abort probe.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs — adds `SendDeclareError` enum (Keyexpr(OutboundKeyexprError) + ReservedMappingIdZero + UnknownMappingId(u64) + MissingKeyexpr) with Display/Error/From impls. Adds private `SessionLinkActions::reconstruct_outbound_keyexpr(mapping_id, suffix) -> Result<String, SendDeclareError>` covering all four wire shapes ((0,None)=MissingKeyexpr / (0,Some(s))=literal / (id,None)=pure-alias prefix lookup / (id,Some(tail))=composite prefix||tail). Changes `send_declare_keyexpr`, `send_declare_subscriber`, `send_declare_queryable`, `send_declare_token` signatures from `()` to `Result<(), SendDeclareError>`. Each method gate-checks BEFORE wire emit or mapping-table side effect; send_declare_keyexpr also rejects mapping_id=0 (mirrors build_declare_kexpr's assertion as typed error). send_undeclare_kexpr unchanged (no keyexpr input). 9 new unit tests: reserved-id-zero / bug-three / structurally-invalid / missing-keyexpr / unknown-mapping / cross-boundary-bug-three / safe-alias-form / queryable+token gate inheritance / reconstruct shape table.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — `Session::declare_token` signature now `Result<LivelinessToken, OutboundKeyexprError>` (literal-mode, only Keyexpr variant reachable; unreachable! guards future refactors). `Session::declare_token_aliased` now also returns the existing `LivelinessAliasError` extended with `InvalidKeyexpr(OutboundKeyexprError)` variant + Display + Error::source impl. 13 declare_token test callsites updated to `.expect("hardcoded canonical literal keyexpr")`. 23 direct `send_declare_keyexpr` test callsites updated to chained `.expect()`.

No [dependencies] yet — features compile to no-op labels at R302a; downstream gating lands R302b+ as modules move into the facade.
144 atomic features named <domain>-<capability> kebab-case per R301 inventory. Identical id set, zero renames. Source of truth = inventory entries; Cargo.toml is the mechanical projection.

19 domain-aggregate features `domain-<name>` = union of each domain's atomic set. Granularity layer between hand-picking atomic and pick-a-preset. Used as `cargo add wz --features domain-pubsub` for whole-domain opt-in.

6 preset features as EXPLICIT per-preset atomic lists; no preset-extends-preset. Rationale: v0.1.0 is a frozen semver contract — atomic catalog growth cannot silently shift preset membership. Counts: preset-mcu-minimal=36 / preset-mcu-extended=59 / preset-ap-client=67 / preset-ap-router=80 / preset-ap-full=131 / preset-zenoh-cpp=118.

Implication edges encoded only where inventory reason field says 'requires X' / 'builds on X': attachment-encoding-aware→attachment-bytes; declare-keyexpr→keyexpr-mapping; pubsub-attachment→attachment-bytes; pubsub-priority→session-extqos; query-attachment→attachment-bytes; liveliness-get→query-get; liveliness-historical-samples→liveliness-history; codec-fragment→transport-fragmentation; codec-join→session-multicast; link-fragment→transport-fragmentation; locator-{quic,serial,tls,unixsock,vsock,ws}→transport-link-{same}; runtime-tokio-uring→runtime-tokio; scouting-gossip→routing-router; scouting-multicast→transport-link-udp; transport-link-tls→transport-link-tcp; access-extauth-{jwt,pubkey,usrpwd}→session-extauth; session-extcompression→transport-compression; session-extshm→transport-shm; routing-{failover,routes,static-routes}→routing-router; storage-{history,replication}→storage-backend.

default=[] (no-default). Composable-framework contract: user explicitly opts into a preset or hand-rolls atomic combos. Differs from batteries-included crates like tokio. Matches kconfig / NixOS USE / Buildroot semantics where the user authors the config.

Mutually-exclusive groups (platform-{bare-metal,linux,macos,windows,qnx,freertos,zephyr} / runtime-{tokio,lwip,no-std,async-std} / transport-fragmentation vs transport-lowlatency) NOT encoded as Cargo edges — Cargo features are monotone-additive. changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs: `pub fn read_captured(file: &mut File) -> String` rewritten. Old shape: `file.read_to_string(&mut s).expect("read captured output")` — panics on first non-UTF-8 byte the child wrote, surfacing the panic IN PLACE OF the captured content (caller sees the harness error, not the test's actual fail mode). New shape: `file.read_to_end(&mut bytes).expect("read captured bytes") + String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()` — non-UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD markers and the caller still sees the full captured snapshot.

Doc-comment expanded with the failure-mode background — child panic backtrace under tokio's worker-thread pool can interleave with a libc-side `abort(3)` message at byte granularity, producing mid-codepoint truncation. The strict-decode path masked this as a separate panic; lossy decode surfaces it as inline U+FFFD markers in the diagnostic output so the caller can see what the child actually wrote.
No source-level changes to wz-runtime-tokio / wz-codecs / wz-ap-demo — the flake was purely a test harness defect (R215 strict-decode legacy).
verification_bullets: Reproduction context — R302b push to origin/main triggered pre-push hook → scripts/run-ci.sh Layer E → `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --test wz_initiator_to_wz_acceptor --release -- --ignored` failed once with `read captured output: Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }`. Manual retry passed. User flagged: flaky-1-occurrence-is-still-flaky — retry-pass is NOT diagnosis exemption.

Root cause analysis — grepped `wait_for_substring` in src/lib.rs, found `read_captured` at line 151 using `.read_to_string(...).expect(...)`. Rust std `read_to_string` returns `io::Error { kind: InvalidData, message: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" }` on first invalid byte. Exact match for the observed panic. Mechanism: child stderr captured to tempfile via Stdio::from; child panic + abort interleave can write byte-granular non-UTF-8; harness reads + decodes strict → panic.
Fix applied: read_to_string → read_to_end + from_utf8_lossy.

Empirical confirmation: 30 consecutive iterations of `cargo test ... --ignored` post-fix. Result: pass=30 fail=0. With pre-fix flake rate observable in 1 of 2 push attempts (~50% per-push, lower per-iteration), 30 consecutive passes carries >99% confidence that root cause is mechanically removed — not chance.

Side-channel verification: /tmp/wz-flaky-1.log (one of 30 captured passes) contains 0 U+FFFD replacement characters. So in this measurement window the child stderr was actually valid UTF-8 — the pre-fix flake was driven by a child output mode that fires rarely; the lossy-decode fix protects against future occurrences regardless of frequency.
cargo check -p wz-integration-tests --tests → pass 1.63s. Build clean.

Round 305.decision_summary: R305 introduces ChildGuard RAII wrapper across 9 Layer E tests + 2 unit-test mechanical proofs, eliminating the orphan-subprocess class that caused the R302b push-time .git/run-ci.lock outage.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/src/lib.rs::common: new `ChildGuard` struct wrapping `std::process::Child`. `wrap(label, child)` constructs from an already-spawned Child; `child_mut()` returns `&mut Child` for the existing `.kill() / .wait()` call shape; `label()` exposes the spawn-time label for diagnostics. `impl Drop` runs `kill + wait` idempotently — explicit cleanup in the test body still works, and the guard's Drop is the safety net for any panic-unwind path.

9 Layer E tests refactored to wrap every `Command::spawn().expect(...)` in `ChildGuard::wrap(label, ...)` and change `child.kill() / .wait()` to `child.child_mut().kill() / .wait()`: ap_demo_round_trip.rs, wz_initiator_to_zsub.rs, wz_initiator_to_wz_acceptor.rs, wz_remote_declare_round_trip.rs, wz_publisher_to_zsub.rs, wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip.rs, wz_publisher_del_to_zsub.rs, wz_query_reply_round_trip.rs, wz_queryable_round_trip.rs. Each wrapped Child uses a short human label (e.g. `"wz-ap-demo acceptor (--listen --declare-token)"`) for forensic logs.

wz_remote_declare_round_trip.rs + wz_liveliness_subscriber_round_trip.rs: `graceful_terminate(&mut child, ...)` call sites updated to `graceful_terminate(child.child_mut(), ...)`. The helper signature stays `&mut std::process::Child`, so passing through the guard's `child_mut()` keeps SIGTERM-based graceful shutdown working alongside the panic safety net.

2 unit tests in src/lib.rs added: `child_guard_drop_kills_running_child_on_normal_exit` spawns `sleep 60`, wraps in ChildGuard, exits the inner scope, then verifies the PID is gone via `kill -0 <pid>` (exits non-zero on ESRCH). `child_guard_drop_kills_running_child_on_panic_unwind` spawns sleep 60, publishes its PID through `Arc<Mutex<Option<u32>>>`, wraps in ChildGuard inside a `std::panic::catch_unwind` closure, panics, then asserts the captured PID is dead post-unwind. Mechanical proof that the Drop runs on both exit shapes.
verification_bullets: cargo check -p wz-integration-tests --tests → pass 1.41s. All 9 refactored Layer E tests + the rest of the integration suite compile clean.

cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --lib → pass. Both new unit tests succeed: `kill: (PID): 그런 프로세스가 없음` (the `kill -0` ESRCH stderr from the post-Drop liveness check) appears in the test stdout, confirming the child was reaped after both the normal-exit and panic-unwind paths.

10 iterations of `cargo test -p wz-integration-tests --release --tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1` → pass=10 fail=0 across all 9 Layer E tests = 90 total e2e runs. Sequential `--test-threads=1` keeps PortReservation deterministic; no ChildGuard-related regression observable.
fuser .git/run-ci.lock during measurement → no PID held. No orphan wz-ap-demo / z_sub / stdbuf processes accumulated in `ps -p`.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs: 11 eprintln! sites converted to log::info!. Observer-callback closures (REMOTE SUBSCRIBER / QUERYABLE / TOKEN DECLARED + UNDECLARED, REPLY RECEIVED, FINAL RECEIVED, SUBSCRIBER FIRED, LIVELINESS SAMPLE, QUERYABLE FIRED) all route through env_logger's BufferWriter + io::stderr().lock() path. Pre-R308 the mixed eprintln! / log::info! writes serialised in theory (both acquire the same io::stderr() Mutex) but the empirical 30-trial measurement showed ~3-5% byte-interleave at the LIVELINESS SAMPLE callback fire site. R308 drops the duplicate eprintln! on error paths (log::warn! already covers them) and converts the success eprintln! to log::info!. Net: 5 eprintln! removed; 5 log::info! added (3 of those replace removed-eprintln on success paths; 0 net-add).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:Querier::get_matching_status (line 1945) loses its method-level `#[cfg(feature = "declare-queryable")]`. The signature is now always visible whenever `Querier` exists (i.e. whenever `feature = "query-get"` is enabled — the `impl Querier` block-level gate). The body branches: `#[cfg(feature = "declare-queryable")] let matching = { ... obs.remote_queryables.has_matching(&self.keyexpr) };` and `#[cfg(not(feature = "declare-queryable"))] let matching = false;`. The rustdoc records the R310.5c rationale (zenoh-cpp API parity, conservative-false default).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:QuerierAliased::get_matching_status (line 2082) loses its method-level cfg. The `UnknownMapping(id)` validation (resolve_outbound_mapping + ok_or) still always fires — callers see the declare-before-query invariant regardless of feature subset. Only the registry consult is gated; on the success path the method returns `Ok(MatchingStatus{matching:false})` when declare-queryable is off. The composed `_effective_keyexpr` binding takes a leading underscore so the unused-warning is silenced when the registry consult branch is elided.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:Publisher::get_matching_status (line 2195) loses its `#[cfg(feature = "declare-subscriber")]`. Same shape: signature always visible (Publisher itself has no cfg gate), body branches on declare-subscriber, conservative false-default when off. The rustdoc records the same R310.5c parity rationale.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs:PublisherAliased::get_matching_status (line 2287) loses its method-level cfg. UnknownMapping validation always fires; registry consult body-gated on declare-subscriber; `_effective_keyexpr` underscore-prefix for the elided-branch warning suppression.

Net effect: under `--no-default-features` (no declare-queryable, no declare-subscriber), `Publisher::get_matching_status` and `PublisherAliased::get_matching_status` are now callable (always returning `matching:false`); Querier/QuerierAliased::get_matching_status are callable iff `query-get` is enabled. This matches the zenoh-cpp shape where every Publisher / Publisher_alias / Querier / Querier_alias instance has a `get_matching_status()` method that always answers — whether the runtime actually tracks matching is a build-time question, not an API-surface question.

Round 311az-pre.decision_summary: R311az-pre ledger: wz-link-lwip 5.C UDP link 8 design decisions frozen (lwIP raw API, lwip-sys split, mpsc bridge, LwipRuntime sync site, trust placeholder); R311az implementation rationale baseline
changes_bullets: D1 link-class UDP-first: 5.C enum udp/tcp/serial/ws/raw_eth additive; R311az ships udp only; TCP stateful R311az-alpha cascade
D2 lwIP raw API not BSD socket: udp_new/bind/recv/sendto/remove/disconnect; LWIP_SOCKET=1 rejected (footprint, mandatory pbuf copy break of 5.E zero-copy invariant)
D3 lwip-sys FFI crate split: vendored lwIP 2.2.0 via cmake/bindgen/allowlist (mirror zenoh-pico-sys R41); allowlist starts at 6 udp_ fns plus pbuf and ip_addr types

Hidden-bug pattern guard for future deploy/* crates: (a) build.rs MUST emit `cargo:rustc-link-arg=-T<linker.x>` directly — never rely solely on `.cargo/config.toml::rustflags` because cargo's config lookup is CWD-based and scripts that build from the repo root will silently produce empty ELFs; (b) for embedded ClockSource impls, prefer architectural-standard surfaces (SysTick, generic timer) over implementation-defined ones (DWT CYCCNT on ARMv7-M) because QEMU + many silicon implementations stub the latter to 0; (c) when picking a QEMU `-machine`, cross-check `qemu-system-arm -machine help` for the machine's required CPU family — mps2-an385/386/505 each pin a distinct cortex-mN core and reject -kernel boot on a CPU mismatch.

Requires ARMv8-M Secure-state init in the demo (or a cortex-m-rt Secure-state setup feature) — SAU configuration to expose Non-secure region for the binary OR boot-via-Secure-only mode. changes_bullets: deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs SystickClock: TICKINT bit added (SYST_CSR_TICKINT = 1<<1) + RELOAD changed from 0xFFFFFF (~671ms wrap) to 24999 (1ms reload @ 25 MHz). `wraps` field now represents milliseconds since boot, incremented exclusively from the `SysTick` exception handler; `last_cvr` field + COUNTFLAG accumulation path removed (ISR is the single writer). `now_us` rewritten to a double-snap pattern (load wraps -> read CVR -> load wraps -> retry on mismatch) using Acquire ordering pairs with the handler's Release fetch_add — standard ISR-vs-thread lock-free read for an interrupt-incremented counter + an independently-decrementing hardware counter.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs new #[exception] handler: `#[exception] fn SysTick() { GLOBAL_CLOCK.wraps.fetch_add(1, Release); }` — sole side effect is the wraps increment so the ISR stays minimal (no allocation, no locks, no re-entrant work). cortex-m-rt 0.7's `exception` attribute is imported alongside `entry`.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs main loop: `cortex_m::asm::nop()` -> `cortex_m::asm::wfi()` + comment rewrite documenting the IRQ-driven idle pattern (textbook MCU: cycles only burn during work + tick ISR handling, not in a tight nop spin). R311be's contrary comment ('We deliberately do NOT call wfi() here — QEMU mps2-an386 has no SysTick configured') retired; R311bf's SystickClock was the prerequisite that makes wfi() safe (a SysTick wake source now exists).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs hprintln + PAYLOAD strings: 'R311bf' -> 'R311bi' (echo identity payload bytes change but the round-trip identity test is invariant of payload content; PAYLOAD const is still 29 bytes either side).

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs header doc: 'Why SysTick poll mode' section replaced with 'Why SysTick IRQ-driven ClockSource + wfi() main loop' — documents the R311bi reload-value choice (1 ms tick = one ISR per LwipTime::sleep iteration), the wfi() power-down semantics, and the double-snap lock-free read pattern.

Round 311di-pre-a.decision_summary: R311di-pre-a — wz-runtime-tokio adds hashbrown + portable-atomic deps; session_glue.rs HashMap + AtomicU64 imports route through them; first step toward wz-session-core no_std move-readiness.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: add `hashbrown = "0.15"` and `portable-atomic = "1"` to [dependencies]. Both crates resolve under default features — hashbrown ships foldhash + inline-more + allocator-api2 (match std::collections::HashMap behaviour on AP), portable-atomic forwards to core::sync::atomic when native u64 atomics exist (this crate, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and falls back via critical-section on MCU profiles (wz-runtime-lwip already pulls the same dep per R311bb). The version surface is the same one wz-session-core (R311di proper) will inherit when session_glue.rs / session.rs extract — pulling here first means the extraction is a file-move, not a dep-graph rewrite.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: lines 53-55 import surface lift. `use std::collections::HashMap;` → `use hashbrown::HashMap;` (hashbrown::HashMap is the upstream implementation of std::collections::HashMap — std re-exports it via the alloc crate's collections, so the API surface is byte-identical at the call sites: new() / insert() / remove() / get() / iter() / Entry API). `use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` → `use portable_atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};` (portable_atomic::AtomicU64 mirrors core::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 method-for-method; load() / store() / fetch_add() / Ordering enum identical). `use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};` retained for this round — Mutex<T> field types on SessionState route through Session<R>::Mutex<T> GAT at R311di proper (the GAT is already declared on the Runtime trait via R311ar, but the construction-side `Mutex::new(...)` calls on SessionState fields need a `Runtime::new_mutex<T>(t: T) -> Self::Mutex<T>` helper which is a separate ratify) and Arc is a zero-cost relabel (std::sync::Arc and alloc::sync::Arc are the same type) deferred to the same round.

Source-side effect: the 4 SessionState AtomicU64 fields (outbound_frame_sn, next_outbound_request_id, next_outbound_token_id, next_outbound_interest_id at session_glue.rs:865 / 900 / 924 / 949) and 1 HashMap field (outbound_mappings: Mutex<HashMap<u64, String>> at session_glue.rs:882) now hold portable_atomic / hashbrown types respectively. AP semantic unchanged — portable_atomic on x86_64 std forwards to native atomics and hashbrown is the same implementation std re-exports.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-core/src/runtime.rs: trait Runtime gains two construction-side methods. `fn new_mutex<T>(value: T) -> Self::Mutex<T> where T: Send + 'static` (complement of with_mutex_mut — generic-R code cannot invoke inherent methods on the GAT type Self::Mutex<T> since the trait declares the type as opaque; the trait method takes ownership and returns the GAT-typed value). `fn new_rwlock<T>(value: T) -> Self::RwLock<T> where T: Send + Sync + 'static` (one tighter bound than new_mutex because shared-read access lets &T cross threads, matching the type-level Self::RwLock bound). Doc comments record the per-profile binding discipline and the rationale for not exposing inherent methods on the GAT type.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_impl.rs: TokioRuntime impl gains `fn new_mutex<T>(value) -> Self::Mutex<T> { crate::sync::Mutex::new(value) }` and `fn new_rwlock<T>(value) -> Self::RwLock<T> { crate::sync::RwLock::new(value) }`. Both forward to the std primitive's `new` constructor (the crate::sync alias resolves to std::sync::Mutex / std::sync::RwLock). No poison state is materialised at construction time — std::sync::Mutex poisoning is a runtime side-effect, not a construction-time choice.

crates/wz-runtime-lwip/src/runtime_impl.rs: LwipRuntime<C: ClockSource> impl gains `fn new_mutex<T>(value) -> Self::Mutex<T> { Mutex::new(RefCell::new(value)) }` and `fn new_rwlock<T>(value) -> Self::RwLock<T> { Mutex::new(RefCell::new(value)) }`. RwLock collapses to the same critical_section::Mutex<RefCell<T>> shape per the single-core IRQ-safe model (see crate::sync module doc). Both constructors are infallible — critical_section::Mutex::new + RefCell::new are pure value-wrapping with no allocator or syscall dependency.

publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-core/src/runtime.rs: trait Runtime gains two construction-side methods. `fn new_mutex<T>(value: T) -> Self::Mutex<T> where T: Send + 'static` (complement of with_mutex_mut — generic-R code cannot invoke inherent methods on the GAT type Self::Mutex<T> since the trait declares the type as opaque; the trait method takes ownership and returns the GAT-typed value). `fn new_rwlock<T>(value: T) -> Self::RwLock<T> where T: Send + Sync + 'static` (one tighter bound than new_mutex because shared-read access lets &T cross threads, matching the type-level Self::RwLock bound). Doc comments record the per-profile binding discipline and the rationale for not exposing inherent methods on the GAT type.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/runtime_impl.rs: TokioRuntime impl gains `fn new_mutex<T>(value) -> Self::Mutex<T> { crate::sync::Mutex::new(value) }` and `fn new_rwlock<T>(value) -> Self::RwLock<T> { crate::sync::RwLock::new(value) }`. Both forward to the std primitive's `new` constructor (the crate::sync alias resolves to std::sync::Mutex / std::sync::RwLock). No poison state is materialised at construction time — std::sync::Mutex poisoning is a runtime side-effect, not a construction-time choice.

crates/wz-runtime-lwip/src/runtime_impl.rs: LwipRuntime<C: ClockSource> impl gains `fn new_mutex<T>(value) -> Self::Mutex<T> { Mutex::new(RefCell::new(value)) }` and `fn new_rwlock<T>(value) -> Self::RwLock<T> { Mutex::new(RefCell::new(value)) }`. RwLock collapses to the same critical_section::Mutex<RefCell<T>> shape per the single-core IRQ-safe model (see crate::sync module doc). Both constructors are infallible — critical_section::Mutex::new + RefCell::new are pure value-wrapping with no allocator or syscall dependency.

Round 311di-pre-f7.decision_summary: R311di-pre-f7 — decision-only round: 4 AtomicU64 fields keep `portable_atomic::AtomicU64` raw across profiles (option b ratified); Runtime trait stays at Mutex + RwLock abstractions only; portable_atomic IS the portable abstraction (option a R::Atomic GAT rejected as over-engineering).
changes_bullets: No source changes — decision-only round per the R311bp pattern (decision_summary records the ratification + atomic store ledger entry; no .rs file mutation). Mirrors the R311di-pre-f6 carry_forward question evaluation: option (a) Runtime trait extension with R::Atomic<u64> GAT + new_atomic + atomic_fetch_add* + atomic_load* methods (cleaner trait surface) vs (b) keep portable_atomic::AtomicU64 raw across profiles (zero added abstraction).

Ratification rationale: portable_atomic IS already the portable abstraction this problem domain needs. AP profile resolves to std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 (hardware atomic instructions on x86/ARM64); MCU profile via the unstable-portable-atomic-critical-section feature resolves to a critical_section-emulated atomic that gives correct semantics on single-core MCUs without hardware atomic ops. Wrapping it inside Runtime adds 4+ trait methods without expressivity gain — every binding would call back to portable_atomic verbatim. The Mutex abstraction earned its trait surface because std::sync::Mutex + critical_section::Mutex have genuinely different APIs (lock + PoisonError vs borrow + RefCell); atomic ops do not have that gap.

Inventory captured for future reviewers: 4 fields (outbound_frame_sn + next_outbound_request_id/token_id/interest_id; session_glue.rs:884/919/943/968) hold AtomicU64 directly. 4 fetch_add sites in the R-generic impl block (line 1343/1364/1383/1402). 4 AtomicU64::new construction sites in the concrete TokioRuntime impl block (line 1121-1125). 11 total portable_atomic references including the module-level import (line 72). All sites stay verbatim; portable_atomic is a workspace dep per R311di-pre-a + pre-b sweep so the dependency surface does not change.

Round 311ek.decision_summary: R311ek shuts the wz-runtime-tokio internal arbitrary-subset gap (north-star mechanism 1): observer ungated to alloc, sample + source_info encoders split out; 4 facade subsets build + new C4b lane.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: the `observer` module gate widened from `all(alloc, codec-declare)` to `alloc` so a codec-push-only subset can compose the bundle (it holds the always-compiled `subscribers` + `replies` registries that pub/sub dispatch needs); the `liveliness_subscribers` field + its import + its `new()` construction now gate on `liveliness-subscriber`, and the four declare consumer features (`declare-subscriber`/`declare-queryable`/`liveliness-token`/`liveliness-subscriber`) now imply `codec-declare` so each gated field's registry type is guaranteed to exist.

New `wz-session-core::source_info_ext` (alloc, no codec gate): `encode_source_info_ext_body` + the shared `pub(crate)` VLE primitive lifted out of the `codec-response`-gated `response_build` module so the `codec-push` body-extension path (`build_body_extensions`) reaches the encoder; `response_build`'s responder encoder re-imports the VLE helper.

New `wz-session-core::declare::liveliness_sample` (alloc): the codec-agnostic `LivelinessSample` / `LivelinessSampleKind` / `LivelinessSampleCallback` split out of the `codec-declare`-gated `liveliness_subscriber` module so the unconditional `Session::declare_liveliness_subscriber{_aliased}` Result-form signatures compile in a codec-declare-off subset; the registry stays gated and re-imports them.

wz-runtime-tokio: `declare.rs` re-exports retargeted (sample types unconditional from `liveliness_sample`, `LivelinessSubscriberRegistry` gated `liveliness-subscriber`, `encode_source_info_ext_body` under `any(codec-push, codec-response)`); the `LivelinessSubscriber` handle's `history_complete`/`undeclare`/`Drop` observer access gated `liveliness-subscriber` (signature-stable fallbacks); `Queryable.session` gated `query-queryable` with a PhantomData arm keeping `R`/`T` live; the `MsgPutOwned`/`MsgDelOwned`/`ExtZbufOwned` imports regated `codec-push` (their `codec-response`/`codec-request` arms were stale after R311dv/R311eh moved the response/request builders to session-core).

New Layer C4b facade arbitrary-incomplete-subset matrix in `scripts/run-ci.sh` + `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: cargo-builds the wz facade under four deliberately-incomplete coherent consumer subsets (pubsub-only / queryable-only / zget-reply-only / declare-observer) under deny-warnings — the facade-level analog of C1h that the named-preset C4 lane does not cover.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new scout_trace::ScoutTrace (4 u32 dispatch counters) + scout_params::ScoutParams (version/what/zid); pure value-type siblings of action_trace/session_init_params, kept out of the session bundle (scouting is a pre-session subsystem).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/scouting_glue.rs (new, scouting-active): ScoutingActions deps bundle + install_scouting_actions + register_scout_fns binding the four scouting.scxml actions as pure encode/decode+stash (scout_emit / record_hello_and_emit / emit_scout_timeout / diag_scout_tx_failed) + async drive_scouting_until_resolved loop (loop owns all socket IO; SCXML <send delay> serviced via Engine::tick) + new_scouting_engine.

Round 311er.decision_summary: R311er adds wz-session-core::locator parse_locator: the mode-agnostic seam turning active-discovered + static-synth locator strings into a typed ParsedLocator{Proto, SocketAddr} via core::net (MCU + AP).
changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new locator module — Proto{Tcp,Udp} + ParsedLocator{proto, addr: core::net::SocketAddr} + parse_locator(&str) -> Result<ParsedLocator, LocatorParseError{MissingProtoSeparator|UnknownProto(s)|BadAddress(s)}>.

The mode-agnostic seam: active mode's ScoutOutcome::Discovered(String) and static mode's synth_static_locators(..)->Vec<String> both produce zenoh locator strings; parse_locator turns either into the typed endpoint a link dial consumes, enforcing "a discovered locator is a discovered locator regardless of mode" in one runtime-agnostic place.

Pure core::net + alloc (no std, no socket, no FSM) so it cross-compiles on the MCU static-deploy profile; distinct from wz-codecs::locator (the wire codec). MVP scope = numeric tcp/udp SocketAddr (IPv4/IPv6); DNS / metadata-suffix / other transports surface as parse errors (deferred, not silently mis-parsed).
8 unit tests (tcp/udp ipv4, ipv6 bracketed, missing-separator, unknown-proto, DNS-as-BadAddress, metadata-as-BadAddress, out-of-range-port).

changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: TcpDriver::connect(addr) -> io::Result<Self> — TcpStream::connect then from_stream; the Initiator-side counterpart to the acceptor-side from_stream, fulfilling the standing open() doc note ('outbound dial flow lands when the Initiator path is wired').

Root cause: R311o's type-ungating made OutboundKeyexprError foundational (wrapped by the unconditional LivelinessAliasError::InvalidKeyexpr and imported unconditionally in session.rs:134), and the wz-session-core/alloc dep is unconditional, so the module + its consumers are always present — the gate was a phantom that broke every keyexpr-canon-OFF build.

Genuine exclusion is blocked by the signature-stability principle (cannot gate OutboundKeyexprError / LivelinessAliasError::InvalidKeyexpr).

Round 311fg.decision_summary: R311fg facade-subset BEHAVIOURAL e2e guard: new single-purpose wz-e2e-pubsub crate pins the pubsub-only foreign-interop subset and a new Layer E2 drives it against zenoh-pico; the e2e surfaced that transport-batching is load-bearing for the foreign handshake (build-coherent != interop-coherent).
changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-pubsub (Cargo.toml + src/main.rs): a minimal single-purpose e2e consumer binary that pins the pubsub-only foreign-interop facade subset (wz dep default-features off + explicit subset list). Acceptor + literal-keyexpr Put burst + drive-until-terminal/SIGTERM + minimal teardown, using ONLY the public facade pub/sub surface so it compiles under the subset with zero #[cfg]. Textbook single-responsibility — the alternative (cfg-gating the wz-ap-demo monolith for subset builds) is a ~70-site cfg-soup the project rejects. Registered as a workspace member in crates/Cargo.toml.

crates/wz-integration-tests: new wz_e2e_pubsub_to_zsub.rs e2e test (mirrors wz_publisher_to_zsub.rs but drives the subset binary against zenoh-pico z_sub) + wz_e2e_pubsub_binary() locator in the common lib.

scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer E2 (facade-subset behavioural e2e) drives the wz-e2e-* subset-pinned binaries vs zenoh-pico — the behavioural counterpart of the C4b facade BUILD subset matrix. Layer E now runs `--ignored --skip wz_e2e_` so the subset family runs ONLY in E2 (no test runs twice); header layer-list + run_layer dispatch updated.
.github/workflows/release.yml: build wz-e2e-pubsub (Layer E2 dep) + run Layer E2 steps added after the existing Layer E flow.
verification_bullets: Layer E2 e2e PASS 10/10 consecutive (no-flaky-ever sweep): the wz-e2e-pubsub acceptor's literal-keyexpr Put burst reaches zenoh-pico z_sub's subscriber callback (witnessed by ">> [Subscriber] Received" + the keyexpr + the value substrings).

FINDING — transport-batching is load-bearing for FOREIGN interop: with it off the pubsub subset BUILDS (C4b passes) and two wz peers interoperate (both force batch_size 65535) but zenoh-pico's z_sub rejects the InitAck (FSM closes SentInitAck -> Closed; z_sub logs "Unable to open session!"). Adding transport-batching to the pinned subset fixed the handshake. Only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces this; the build guard (C4b) and the in-process behavioural guard (C1j) both pass without it.
wz-e2e-pubsub builds clean (0 warnings under deny-warnings) under its isolated, feature-unification-free pinned subset (cargo build -p wz-e2e-pubsub).

full run-ci EXIT 0: all required lanes pass, including Layer E (full preset-ap-client demo suite, now run with --skip wz_e2e_) and the new Layer E2 (facade-subset e2e). fmt + clippy clean (the new crate + test; an earlier draft's fmt drift + a doc_lazy_continuation in the test doc were fixed before this run).
carry_forward_bullets: First facade-subset behavioural e2e guard lands (pubsub). Sibling subset binaries (wz-e2e-queryable / wz-e2e-liveliness) follow the same single-purpose-crate shape when their planes need foreign-interop coverage; each pins its own foreign-interop-coherent subset and adds a wz_e2e_* test that Layer E2 picks up.

FINDING generalisation: the foreign-interop-coherent subset is strictly larger than the build-coherent one (pubsub needs transport-batching for the zenoh-pico handshake). The other C4b/C4c/C1j build-coherent subsets may carry latent foreign-interop gaps that only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces — worth auditing as the wz-e2e-* family grows.

FOLLOW-UP (uncaught latent): an isolated `cargo clippy -p wz-e2e-pubsub` (the clippy analog of C3 for subset binaries) surfaces clippy::needless_return at session.rs:1181/1331/1433 — the signature-stability query-get methods whose `cfg(not(query-get))` arm's `return Err(FeatureDisabled)` becomes the function tail under the subset. No current CI lane clips wz-runtime-tokio under query-get OFF, so this is pre-existing + latent, not an R311fg regression. Adding a subset-isolated clippy guard requires resolving these per feedback_signature_stability (prefer cfg over #[allow]) first — coupled follow-up.

Open decision: whether C4b's pubsub-only BUILD subset should also list transport-batching for catalog consistency (build-coherent without it, interop-coherent only with it). Left as-is pending a ruling on whether C4b models build- or interop-coherence; the e2e binary pins the interop-coherent superset regardless.

Round 311fh.decision_summary: R311fh wz-e2e-queryable: second facade-subset e2e binary pins the queryable-only interop subset vs zenoh-pico z_get; codec-response-final surfaced as load-bearing for z_get's terminating Final.
changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-queryable (Cargo.toml + src/main.rs): single-purpose queryable-only facade-subset e2e binary (acceptor + queryable, ZERO #[cfg]); sibling of wz-e2e-pubsub. Registered as a workspace member in crates/Cargo.toml.

Pinned interop-coherent subset = the shared handshake core (transport-unicast/link-tcp/keepalive/batching + session open/accept + the init/open/close/keepalive/frame codec quintet + keyexpr-literal/-canon) PLUS query-queryable (implies codec-request + codec-response) PLUS codec-response-final; query-reply-err omitted because this binary emits only the Put-form reply.
crates/wz-integration-tests: new tests/wz_e2e_queryable_to_zget.rs e2e (wz queryable acceptor vs zenoh-pico z_get) + wz_e2e_queryable_binary() locator in src/lib.rs::common.

scripts/run-ci.sh Layer E2 extended: prereq guards now require z_sub + z_get and both subset binaries, and the lane runs both wz_e2e_pubsub_to_zsub + wz_e2e_queryable_to_zget; header doc updated. .github/workflows/release.yml adds a Build wz-e2e-queryable step before Layer E2.

The new test gates ONLY on z_get's ">> Received" witness, not its earlier "Opening session" line: z_get's main thread + reply-callback thread race on the shared non-O_APPEND tempfile offset and clobber the EARLIEST captured lines; the late witness lines survive. The two value/keyexpr substring asserts run on the full capture so line reordering is tolerated.
verification_bullets: e2e PASS: z_get logs ">> Received PUT ('demo/test': 'hello-from-wz-queryable-subset')" + ">> Received query final notification"; wz logs "QUERYABLE FIRED ... rid=1 keyexpr='demo/test'" — full inbound-Request(Query) -> QueryableRegistry -> Reply + ResponseFinal round-trip under the queryable-only subset against a foreign peer.

FINDING (queryable-plane analog of R311fg transport-batching): codec-response-final is load-bearing for FOREIGN interop. query-queryable implies only codec-request + codec-response (the Reply emit), so the C4b 'queryable-only' BUILD subset omits codec-response-final; without it the reply still arrives but z_get gets no terminating Final and falls back to its query timeout. The foreign-interop-coherent subset is strictly larger than the build-coherent one.

no-flaky-ever: 50/50 consecutive PASS after the capture-race fix. Mechanical root cause = z_get concurrent-thread tempfile-offset corruption of the earliest lines (1/30 reproduced, 'Opening session...' clobbered while '>> Received' survived); removed by gating on the corruption-resistant witness rather than the redundant early line.
cargo build -p wz-e2e-queryable clean (0 warnings under deny-warnings) in its isolated, feature-unification-free pinned subset.

full scripts/run-ci.sh EXIT 0: all required lanes pass incl. C0 ignore-discipline, clippy --workspace (default features), C1h/C1j/C4b/C4c subset matrices, Layer E (--skip wz_e2e_) and Layer E2 (both subset binaries). Layer G 7-MCU cross-compile OK (G.6 riscv SKIP env-only).
carry_forward_bullets: FOLLOW-UP (now confirmed on a 2nd plane): `cargo clippy -p wz-e2e-queryable` surfaces clippy::needless_return at session.rs:1181/1331/1433 — the signature-stability query-get methods whose cfg(not(query-get)) arm's `return Err(QueryAliasError::FeatureDisabled)` becomes the fn tail under any query-get-OFF subset. Pre-existing + latent (R311fg carry #3); full clippy --workspace runs with query-get ON (wz-ap-demo feature unification) so CI stays green. A subset-isolated clippy guard needs these resolved first per feedback_signature_stability (cfg tail-expr, not #[allow]); the blocker now gates BOTH the pubsub and queryable subset-clippy.

Next sibling: wz-e2e-liveliness (declare / liveliness plane) follows the same single-purpose-crate shape vs zenoh-pico's z_liveliness_* examples when that plane needs foreign-interop coverage; pins its own interop-coherent subset + a wz_e2e_* test Layer E2 picks up.

Two such deltas now recorded — worth a ruling on what C4b models.

FINDING generalisation holds: each consumer plane's foreign-interop-coherent subset can exceed its build-coherent one by a different feature; only an e2e-vs-foreign-peer guard surfaces which. Audit remaining build-coherent subsets as the wz-e2e-* family grows.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core: new declare/local_token.rs LocalTokenRegistry — the DECLARER-side registry of wz's own held LivelinessTokens (register/unregister + respond_to_interest). On an inbound non-final TOKENS Interest it stages an interest_id-tagged Declare(DeclToken) per held token whose keyexpr intersects the Interest pattern (keyexpr_intersect_patterns) + a terminating Declare(DeclFinal). Gated liveliness-token. 7 unit tests.

wz-session-core observer: new local_tokens field + pending_declares staging buffer (gated liveliness-token); dispatch_event fans the inbound Interest into local_tokens (two-phase stage), flush_pending drains pending_declares through the sink (two-phase drain, mirror of the queryable reply path). response_sink.rs: ResponseSink gains send_declare(DeclareOwned) (gated liveliness-token) + the &S / Arc<S> blanket impls.

wz-runtime-tokio: SessionLinkActions impls ResponseSink::send_declare (the inherent send_declare encodes via encode_frame_with_declare + send_blocking on the reliable channel). Session::declare_token registers (token_id, keyexpr) into observer.local_tokens; LivelinessToken::Drop + undeclare() unregister it. The interest_id-tagged response is the exact shape zenoh-pico's _z_liveliness_pending_query_reply / _z_liveliness_process_declare_final expect (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/liveliness.c:218-256). No SCXML / SCE change — the declare codec already carries the interest_id field + DeclFinal body variant.

DETERMINISTIC foreign proof: wz-e2e-liveliness-token vs zenoh-pico z_get_liveliness — z_get_liveliness's one-shot CURRENT liveliness query (NO future subscription) logs ">> Alive token ('group1/zenoh-pico')". That can ONLY come from R283's interest_id-tagged reply: zenoh-pico routes the proactive (interest_id-less) declare to _z_liveliness_process_remote_token_declare (subscriber callbacks, which a pure get has none of); the get resolves only via _z_liveliness_pending_query_reply on an interest_id-tagged declare. Earlier z_sub_liveliness attempts could not isolate R283 (its FUTURE subscription catches the proactive declare regardless), and wz-ap-demo's background declare raced the query — both ruled out before settling on the deterministic declarer-binary + z_get_liveliness pairing.

changes_bullets: New crate crates/wz-e2e-harness: shared acceptor scaffolding for the wz-e2e-* family — run_main (env_logger + multi-thread tokio runtime + block_on + ExitCode wrapper), run_acceptor_e2e (bind/accept/open/drive/teardown), OpenedE2e (the {session, clock} surface a setup registers into), AbortOnDrop (publish-task stop), session_init_params, shutdown_signal. Each binary now carries ONLY its CLI parse + a plane-specific setup closure (publish burst / declare_queryable / declare_liveliness_subscriber / declare_token). The 4 binaries' main.rs shrank 977 -> 379 lines (+239 harness); session_init_params + shutdown_signal had been byte-identical 4x.

Subset-pinning preserved: the harness pins ONLY the handshake-core intersection of all four binaries' subsets, so Cargo feature unification resolves each binary's wz to (core ∪ that binary's plane) — the harness adds nothing a binary did not already pin, and its source uses only core APIs so it compiles under the core alone. Each binary still builds + is clippy-clean (deny-warnings) under its isolated pinned subset.

Teardown ordering preserved in the harness: the setup's returned hold is dropped FIRST (RAII unregister / LivelinessToken Drop's UndeclToken emit / pubsub AbortOnDrop) before the action senders close the writer channel — so the R283 liveliness-token UndeclToken-before-writer-close and the pubsub burst-abort semantics are unchanged. The declarer's declare-before-drive-loop determinism is now a structural property of run_acceptor_e2e (setup runs before the loop).

wire_const SSOT: the inner declaration-body MIDs are centralised in wz_codecs::wire_const (gated codec-declare): D_MID_KEXPR/SUBSCRIBER/QUERYABLE/TOKEN (0x00/02/04/06), D_MID_UNDECL_* (01/03/05/07), D_MID_FINAL (0x1A), FLAG_D_N (inline-suffix N), FLAG_N_DECLARE_I (outer Declare interest_id-present I). The 12 session_glue build_declare_* / build_undeclare_* literals and the R283 wz-session-core::declare::local_token builders now reference them.

The context-dependent 0x20 N-flag COMPUTATIONS (wireexpr-N vs declare-N vs interest-C all share the bit) deliberately stay local — DRY applies to the disjoint MID enum, not to a coincidentally-shared bit; forcing them to one const would conflate distinct flags.

Builder unification (#3 of the review) deliberately NOT done: after the wire_const SSOT the proactive build_declare_token and the interest-response build_decl_token_reply share the constants; the two are legitimately different shapes (mapping-id + WireexprNonlocal sibling + interest_id None vs literal-only + interest_id Some), and collapsing them into one over-parameterised cross-crate function would be the wrong abstraction.

Comment rewritten to document the emergent-capability model.

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — the in-process queryable loopback fan in Session::query (observer.queryables.local_query -> QueryReply -> InboundReply) and Session::query_aliased is now wrapped in cfg(feature = query-queryable); the synthetic loopback Final (deliver_local_final) stays OUTSIDE that gate under query-get, so a wire-only getter (query-queryable OFF) finalises a SessionLocal/Any get immediately with zero local replies (semantically correct: no queryable capability => no local queryable to answer). query_aliased gains a cfg(not(query-queryable)) let _ = loopback_keyexpr since the wire branch routes by (mapping_id, inline_suffix).

wz-runtime-tokio/src/session.rs — the bare use wz_codecs::query::Query and use crate::query::QueryReply imports moved from cfg(query-get) to cfg(all(query-get, query-queryable)) to match their sole call site (the now-gated loopback fan).

The query-queryable-OFF behavioural twin is the now-genuinely-isolated wz-e2e-zget binary (Layer E2).

No preset change required: every wz facade preset that lists query-get already lists query-queryable explicitly (paired in wz/Cargo.toml), so dropping the implication only changes the arbitrary-subset zget-reply-only case — confirming the edge was redundant for presets and load-bearing only for the composability gap.

changes_bullets: session_glue.rs — 8 SessionLinkActions impl methods retrofit to signature-stable + body-cfg shape: send_declare_keyexpr / send_declare_subscriber / send_declare_queryable / send_declare_token (each Result<(), SendDeclareError>, body cfg-gated on the matching declare-* feature; when off the method returns Err(SendDeclareError::FeatureDisabled) — honest fail-fast typed reject); send_declare_final (() return, silent no-op body); send_interest_liveliness_subscriber + send_interest_final (() return, silent no-op body); send_response_final (() return, silent no-op body — body uses codec-response-final-gated build_response_final / encode_frame_with_response_final but signature args are unconditional). R311c → R311g1 close the SessionLinkActions cfg-on-signature anti-pattern that R311c first inflicted (send_close_with_reason was the precedent retrofit at R311g; this entry generalizes the pattern across all 8 carry-forward sites listed in R311g atomic entry).

SendDeclareError::FeatureDisabled enum variant + Display arm added (session_glue.rs:626 + L674). Variant ordering: appended at end so existing match arms surface a non-exhaustive-match warning on first compile post-bump rather than silently rebind a prior variant. session.rs declare_token_aliased match arm at L1545 gains an `unreachable!(\"declare-token must be ON whenever liveliness-token is ON per Cargo implication chain\")` arm — liveliness-token = [declare-token, declare-undeclare] in wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml ensures the FeatureDisabled variant is mechanically unreachable from this caller. declare_token literal-mode caller at L1469 already used a wildcard `other => unreachable!` arm so no source change required there.

parse_inbound — R311g #[allow(unused_variables)] / #[allow(unused_variables, unused_mut)] annotations on `has_ext` + `cursor` bindings replaced by explicit #[cfg(any(feature = \"codec-init-body\", feature = \"codec-open-body\", feature = \"codec-close\", feature = \"codec-keep-alive\", feature = \"codec-frame\"))] predicates. `flags` binding + wire_const::FLAG_T_Z constant gained the same cfg predicate (both now elide under minus-all-codecs). decode_ext_chain #[allow(dead_code)] annotation replaced by the same cfg(any(...)) predicate on the function definition. Verbose inline form per feedback_signature_stability MEMORY anchor (no alias macro — explicit features keep cargo-features intent visible).

session_glue.rs:64 — sce_forge_runtime::codec import split: CodecError + SceSink + VecSink remain unconditional (used by encode_frame_envelope + From<CodecError> for InboundParseError + outbound encode helpers that are still always-on pre-R311h..R311k), SceCursor split to a separate use line cfg-gated on the same union predicate (only consumed by parse_inbound / parse_frame_payload / decode_ext_chain — every caller behind a codec gate). The split is the minimal-change form that lets minus-all-codecs compile while preserving the future R311h..R311k path to fold CodecError / VecSink / SceSink under the same predicate once outbound encode_frame_* helpers are gated.

encode_init_with_role + encode_open_with_role (session_glue.rs L1056 / L1078) marked as principled exemption from this universal sweep — they are pure encoder helpers whose entire input type domain (InitBody / OpenBody construction) is feature-gated; the only consumer (wz-integration-tests/tests/layer3_ext_chain_outbound.rs) always has the feature ON via default-feature inheritance; Vec<u8> return type has no honest no-op semantic (Vec::new() = wire corruption; panic = fail-fast but unreachable in practice). Exemption is structurally distinct from per-cascade locality deferral (feedback_signature_stability MEMORY explicitly carves it out). Future retrofit path: type un-gating cascade (R267 reparam adjacent) or restructure as a typed trait so the feature gate appears at import site.

build_response_final / encode_frame_with_response_final / dispatch_response_final / session.rs API surface (declare_querier / declare_queryable / declare_token / declare_liveliness_subscriber + QueryOptions builder methods with_target / with_consolidation / with_timeout_ms) deferred to a separate type-ungating cascade — these signatures take or return feature-gated types (ResponseFinal / Querier / Queryable / Token / Subscriber / QueryOptions / QueryTarget / ConsolidationMode) so signature stability requires un-gating the type itself. R267 Session<R,T> reparam adjacent architectural concern; not eligible for body-only cfg.

observer.rs pending_reply_count / pending_final_count + reply.rs dispatch_response_final — kept cfg-on-signature for this round (diagnostic-only methods on observer side + type-gated ResponseFinal arg on reply side). Audited as not in Tier 1 in-scope; honest carry forward.

Captures the `#[allow]` as last resort rule + verbose inline cfg(any(...)) preference. Links to feedback_textbook_change_pattern / feedback_no_document_around_hack / feedback_no_flaky_ever. Round 311gj.decision_summary: R311gj corrects R311gi: the switchboard injects into the APP statechart engine (built in the app on_event closure), not the session FSM engine drive_session owns. drive_session UNCHANGED, no on_event ripple.
changes_bullets: R311gi Decision 2 conflated two engines: drive_session owns the SESSION FSM (LinkOpened/Close); the switchboard targets the APP SCXML statechart (temp_update), a distinct engine the app owns.
Correction: the app on_event closure captures &mut app_engine, builds EngineInjector, calls observer.dispatch_switchboard. drive_session keeps FnMut(IterationEvent) -- no signature change.
Unaffected: gc-2c-1 observer fan-out + dispatch_iteration_event + the gc-2b EngineInjector are correct as landed; only WHO builds the injector changes (the app, not the runtime loop).
