verification_bullets: Code read confirms the only AP engines threaded are SessionFsmUnicastPolicy (drive_session) + ScoutingPolicy; no application statechart engine exists in the current demo path.
raise_external_by_name graceful-ignores unknown names, so injecting an app event into the session FSM would silently no-op -- the latent wrong-target bug the correction avoids.
carry_forward_bullets: gc-2c-2 (corrected): wz-runtime-tokio switchboard feature forward + bridge dep + an Observer/EngineInjector real-engine test; wz facade + preset forward. drive_session untouched.
gc-3: generator + example app SCXML machine + live wz-ap-demo wiring (app on_event closure builds EngineInjector over the app engine).

Round 311gp.decision_summary: R311gp gc-3a: switchboard static generator foundation -- wz-switchboard-schema + wz-switchboard-codegen pure lib (forge-ast.v1 ingress events -> closed no-heap match, build-validated).
changes_bullets: New crate wz-switchboard-schema: no_std+alloc serde model of wz-switchboard.yaml (SwitchboardSpec{machine, bindings:[Binding{keyexpr,event}]}) -- the single shape both the AP dynamic SwitchboardRegistry loader and the MCU static generator bind to. Leaf data crate, no format backend pinned (YAML/JSON chosen at each consumer's I/O boundary), deny_unknown_fields.

New crate wz-switchboard-codegen: PURE transformation lib (no process/IO) -- generate(SwitchboardSpec, MachineFacts) -> Rust source for a closed no-heap dispatch_switchboard match; parse_machine_facts deserializes only the forge-ast.v1 statechart subset (v / kind / name / external_ingress_events) per docs/SCE_FORGE_AST.md + apis/forge-ast.v1.schema.json. Logic in a pure lib (not a build.rs) so validation + emission are unit+golden testable.

Validation = W3C SCXML 3.12.1 event-descriptor matching of each Binding.event against the machine's external_ingress_events (SCE's documented event-injection contract, drift-proof: SCE owns the reserved-family filter). Build errors: UnknownEvent, MachineMismatch, non-canonical Keyexpr, NotStatechart, UnsupportedAstVersion -- never a silent runtime no-op.

Emission reuses wz-session-core SSOT: canonize_keyexpr at build time (strict-reject where the runtime registry merely warns) + keyexpr_match::keyexpr_pattern_matches (no-alloc, BoundedVec-backed) over &'static str chunk literals. Mirrors SwitchboardRegistry::dispatch (every matching row fires in declaration order; signal path injects empty _event.data). No canonicalization/matching reimplemented.

Both crates added to crates/Cargo.toml workspace members (grouped with wz-statechart-bridge in the statechart domain). build.rs orchestration (shell-out sce-codegen --emit-ast + OUT_DIR include) and a real example machine deferred to gc-3c; the pure-lib boundary means that wiring -- and any future SCE in-process statechart API -- only changes the thin I/O layer, not the validated logic.
verification_bullets: wz-switchboard-codegen: 11 unit+golden tests pass -- parse_machine_facts (v1/kind/empty-ingress), W3C 3.12.1 descriptor matching (exact / token-boundary prefix / trailing .* / non-match / reverse), generate happy-path byte-exact golden, plus UnknownEvent / MachineMismatch / non-canonical-keyexpr rejects, prefix-descriptor accept, empty-switchboard constant-zero emit.
wz-switchboard-schema: 3 tests pass (serde round-trip, deny_unknown_fields reject of a typo'd key, keyexpr/event field-name contract).
cargo clippy --all-targets on both crates clean under workspace deny(warnings); cargo build --workspace green -- no regression to the existing 22 crates (purely additive members).

Empirically confirmed sce-codegen --emit-ast on a real statechart (sources/session/session_fsm_unicast.scxml) emits ast.document.external_ingress_events as an 18-event closed set with error.* filtered -- the generator's input contract is verified against SCE, not assumed.
validate_workspace: §5.20 caveat added; sections 257 unchanged, T1 orphan=0 (new=+0), round-trip 13/13, T3 warn 862 unchanged, GENERATED.md=sync.
carry_forward_bullets: gc-3b (next): value path -- extend wz-switchboard-schema with an optional payload-decode field + wz-switchboard-codegen to emit a typed EventSchema decode -> _event.data (forge-ast.v1 imported_event_schemas). This is the serialization SSOT deferred from gc-2; deserves its own round of design care.

gc-3c: wire the generator into a consumer build.rs (mcu-qemu-demo / wz-ap-demo) -- shell-out sce-codegen --emit-ast + OUT_DIR include -- against a real example SCXML application machine; this flips the §5.20 "MCU static match not yet generated" caveat.
A future AP dynamic loader (wz-runtime-tokio, std) deserializes wz-switchboard.yaml via wz-switchboard-schema to populate SwitchboardRegistry -- the schema crate is the shared SSOT, ready for it.

Long-term-ideal surfaced (non-blocking, SCE-owner decision): SCE exposing the statechart codegen+forge-ast pipeline in-process would remove the build.rs shell-out; the pure-lib boundary is designed so that change would touch only the I/O layer.

Round 311gs.decision_summary: R311gs: AP dynamic switchboard value path -- registry value rows route to a generated per-machine injector via a defaulted EventInjector::inject_value; one guard semantics across AP+MCU.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core `switchboard::EventInjector` gains a defaulted `inject_value(event_name, payload) -> bool` (the value shape of the same cohesive, SCE-free ingress port -- not a second port: a value injector necessarily owns the one `&mut Engine` borrow the signal path needs, so the borrow checker forbids splitting them). Signal-only impls inherit the `false` default, so the bridge `EngineInjector` and every gc-2c consumer ripple zero.

`SwitchboardEntry` gains a value/signal routing kind; `register_value()` mirrors a yaml `Binding` carrying a `codec`; `dispatch` routes value rows to `injector.inject_value(name, sample.payload())` (counting only on a successful decode -- byte-for-byte the static arm's `if let Ok(decoded)` semantics) and signal rows to `inject(name, "")`.

wz-switchboard-codegen refactors the value-arm decode+raise into a generated per-event `inject_<event>` helper (one decode body, deduped across keyexprs targeting the same event) shared by BOTH the static `dispatch_switchboard` arms (MCU) and a NEW generated `{Machine}Injector` newtype that impls `EventInjector` (signal via `raise_external_by_name`, `inject_value` matching `event_name` -> helper). The codec/payload-union mangling stays encapsulated in the generated injector (ACL); the static arm collapses to `if match && inject_<event>(payload, engine)`.

wz-switchboard-example enables `wz-session-core/switchboard` and adds 4 AP-dynamic smoke tests that drive the SAME machine through a runtime-populated `SwitchboardRegistry` + the generated `SensorMonitorInjector`, asserting state outcomes identical to the static `dispatch_switchboard` tests.

Structure note: the registry stays type-erased + non-generic (no `StatePolicy` leak into the SCE-free session-core tier); genericity over the machine lives behind the port in the generated injector. This refines R311gr's carry premise (which framed the registry itself decoding) -- the textbook split keeps the ACL/DIP boundary intact while the value path still reaches `raise_external_typed`.

Round 311ha.decision_summary: R311ha: gc-3 carry #2 CLOSED -- live switchboard value-path e2e: a real zenoh-pico z_put to demo/sensor/temp drives the demo's app machine idle->hot through the production session + observer + switchboard.
changes_bullets: New Layer E e2e test wz-integration-tests/tests/ap_demo_switchboard_inbound.rs: a REAL foreign peer (zenoh-pico z_put CLI) publishes a temperature sample to the demo's switchboard value keyexpr (demo/sensor/temp), and the demo's session inbound -> ApplicationLayerObserver switchboard fan-out -> generated SensorMonitorInjector decodes the wire payload into the typed _event.data and drives the application machine idle -> hot. Asserts the demo stderr line `APP SWITCHBOARD FIRED ... app_state=Hot`. Mirrors the ap_demo_round_trip harness (spawn demo --listen, wait "listening on", z_put -e tcp client, wait the marker, SIGTERM).

Test data note: zenoh-pico z_put -v takes a STRING value, so the wire payload is the literal ASCII bytes; temp_payload decodes a big-endian uint16 from the first two bytes, and every printable ASCII byte is >= 0x20, so any two-character value decodes to celsius_centi >= 8224 -- over the 3000 guard. The value "OK" (0x4F4B = 20299) therefore reaches Hot. SUB-threshold discrimination (a cold sample that must STAY idle) needs arbitrary wire bytes the CLI cannot express, so it stays covered by the in-process fan-out test (R311gz); this e2e owns the live-wire plumbing proof.

Layer-classification: named ap_demo_* (full preset-ap-client wz-ap-demo, Layer E) rather than wz_e2e_* (the facade-subset family Layer E2 drives against wz-e2e-* binaries). The #[ignore] + the non-wz_e2e_ test-fn name make run-ci Layer E (`--ignored --skip wz_e2e_`) pick it up automatically with no script edit.
verification_bullets: ap_demo_switchboard_inbound::switchboard_value_path_against_zenoh_pico_z_put passes: captured demo stderr shows the full live path -- "listening on" -> "accepted peer" -> "session Established" -> "switchboard registered" -> "APP SWITCHBOARD FIRED fired=1 app_state=Hot" -> "session ended: Terminated".

Full host run-ci (WZ_RUN_LAYER_G=1) all required layers pass incl Layer G MCU no_std cross-compile (thumbv7m + riscv32imac) and Layer E, which now runs BOTH binary-dep e2e tests (ap_demo_round_trip + the new switchboard inbound) against the live wz-ap-demo + zenoh-pico CLI.

Round 311i.decision_summary: R311i codec-declare wire-layer cascade — 9 declare-family wz-codecs modules gated + Cargo edges + session_glue.rs Declare wire surface body-cfg.
changes_bullets: wz-codecs/Cargo.toml — `codec-declare = []` feature added + appended to default list. Caveat documents the 9-sub-codec scope (declare envelope + 4 decl_* + 4 undecl_* + decl_final) + the wz-runtime-tokio side wire-emit surface gated by the matching forward + the declare-* high-level features implying codec-declare.

wz-codecs/build.rs — 10 declare-family stems (declare + decl_kexpr/subscriber/queryable/token/final + undecl_kexpr/subscriber/queryable/token) routed to `CARGO_FEATURE_CODEC_DECLARE` env-var check + matching `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed` line. Adding a single match-arm covers all 10 stems via `|` pattern.

wz-codecs/src/lib.rs — 9 `pub mod` blocks gated `#[cfg(feature = \"codec-declare\")]` (declare envelope + 4 decl_* + 4 undecl_*; decl_final is part of the same gate). codec-declare OFF elides the 9 modules entirely — SCXML codegen still emits the OUT_DIR artifacts under any default-on build but the lib.rs include disappears.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — `codec-declare = [\"codec-frame\"]` declares the second body-codec-implies-envelope edge (codec-push was the first at R311h). wz-codecs Cargo dep features list gains `\"codec-declare\"` alongside `\"alloc\"` + `\"codec-push\"` so the consumer modules (pubsub.rs absorb_declare + declare/ family) always have the declare types available regardless of wz-runtime-tokio's codec-declare gate state. `codec-declare` appended to the wz-runtime-tokio default feature list.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — 7 high-level declare features (declare-final / declare-interest / declare-keyexpr / declare-queryable / declare-subscriber / declare-token / declare-undeclare) gain `[\"codec-declare\"]` implication so toggling a high-level declare feature on automatically pulls codec-declare on. The R311g1 send_declare_* body-cfg branch (on `feature = \"declare-keyexpr\"` etc.) is now mechanically guaranteed to see codec-declare-on whenever the body branch is reachable.

wz/Cargo.toml — `codec-declare = [\"wz-runtime-tokio?/codec-declare\"]` facade forward replaces the previous placeholder. Caveat documents the same wire-layer scope as R311h: feature-off elides session_glue.rs Declare wire surface; consumer module (declare/, pubsub.rs absorb_declare) stays compiled — R311m architectural round for the consumer side.

session_glue.rs — 6 declare-family wz-codecs imports cfg-gated (decl_final / decl_kexpr / decl_queryable / decl_subscriber / decl_token + declare envelope). 4 undecl_* imports cfg-gated. 1 wireexpr_nonlocal import cfg-gated (sole user is the declare-side WireexprNonlocal-arm builders). `N_MID_DECLARE` const cfg-gated on codec-declare.

session_glue.rs — 8 `pub fn build_declare_*` builders cfg-gated (principled exemption: return type `Declare` is itself feature-gated): build_declare_kexpr / subscriber / queryable / token / subscriber_nonlocal / queryable_nonlocal / token_nonlocal / final. 4 `pub fn build_undeclare_*` builders cfg-gated: undeclare_kexpr / subscriber / queryable / token. 1 `pub fn encode_frame_with_declare` cfg-gated.

session_glue.rs — `NetworkMessage::Declare(Box<Declare>)` enum variant cfg-gated. `Self::Declare(_) => f.write_str(\"Declare(..)\")` Debug arm cfg-gated. `parse_frame_payload` `wire_const::N_MID_DECLARE => { ... }` match arm cfg-gated. The body-codec gate cascades cleanly through every wire-emit / decode site in session_glue.rs.

pubsub.rs — `use wz_codecs::declare::DeclareVariant;` cfg-gated. `use wz_codecs::wireexpr::WireexprVariant;` cfg-gated (only declare absorption uses it). `NetworkMessage::Declare(decl) => self.absorb_declare(&decl.body)` match arm cfg-gated. `fn absorb_declare(&mut self, body: &DeclareVariant)` cfg-gated. `fn resolve_wireexpr(&self, body: &WireexprVariant) -> Option<String>` cfg-gated. The pubsub-side declare absorption is wire-codec-coupled; without codec-declare the peer cannot emit DECLARE records so the absorption path elides.

send_declare_* method bodies (R311g1 SessionLinkActions retrofit) — no source change required this round: the bodies branch on `#[cfg(feature = \"declare-keyexpr\")]` etc.; the new Cargo implication `declare-keyexpr = [\"codec-declare\"]` mechanically guarantees the body's build_declare_kexpr / encode_frame_with_declare calls always see codec-declare on. The signature-stability contract from R311g1 carries through unchanged.
verification_bullets: cargo check matrix — default-features clean; --no-default-features (minus-all-codecs) clean; the explicit body-feature lanes (declare-keyexpr etc.) auto-pull codec-declare via the new Cargo implication so the body-cfg branch compiles correctly.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib: 589/589 pass — unit-test baseline preserved.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean — no new lint surface from the new gates.
cargo fmt --all --check: clean.

Round 311j.decision_summary: R311j codec-request wire-layer cascade — request envelope + Query inner body gated; query-* implies codec-request; send_request_query body-cfg.
changes_bullets: wz-codecs/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = []` feature added + appended to default. Caveat scopes the gate: SCXML codegen for request envelope + Query inner body + matching `pub mod` blocks; downstream wz-runtime-tokio session_glue.rs Request wire surface + 6 build_request_query_* + encode_frame_with_request + RequestQueryBuilder + NetworkMessage::Request variant + parse arm.

wz-codecs/build.rs — `request` and `query` stems routed to `CARGO_FEATURE_CODEC_REQUEST` env-var check + matching `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed` line. Single match arm via `|` pattern covers both stems.
wz-codecs/src/lib.rs — `pub mod query` and `pub mod request` blocks gated `#[cfg(feature = \"codec-request\")]`. Query is the Request body inner type so they share the codec-request gate.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = [\"codec-frame\"]` declares the third body-codec-implies-envelope edge (after R311h codec-push and R311i codec-declare). wz-codecs Cargo dep features gain `\"codec-request\"` so the consumer module (query.rs / reply.rs / session.rs Query/Queryable/Reply APIs) always have the request/query types available. `codec-request` appended to the default feature list.

wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml — query-get / query-queryable / query-reply features gain `[\"codec-request\"]` implication so toggling a high-level query feature on automatically pulls codec-request on (query-get retains its existing implications + adds codec-request).

wz/Cargo.toml — `codec-request = [\"wz-runtime-tokio?/codec-request\"]` facade forward replaces the previous placeholder. Same wire-layer scope as R311h/R311i; consumer module (query.rs/reply.rs/session.rs) stays compiled — R311m architectural round for the consumer side.

session_glue.rs — `use wz_codecs::query::Query;` cfg-gated. `use wz_codecs::request::{Request, RequestVariant};` cfg-gated. `wz_codecs::timestamp::Timestamp` import gated on `any(codec-request, codec-push)` (consumed by RequestQueryBuilder + push metadata setters). `N_MID_REQUEST` const gate broadened from `codec-frame` to `codec-request` (the request envelope is now its own atomic body codec).

session_glue.rs — 6 `pub fn build_request_query*` builders cfg-gated on codec-request (principled exemption: return type `Request` is itself feature-gated): build_request_query / build_request_query_with_consolidation / _with_parameters / _with_attachment / _with_timeout_ms / _with_target. 1 `pub fn encode_frame_with_request` cfg-gated. `RequestQueryBuilder` struct + impl block cfg-gated.

session_glue.rs — `NetworkMessage::Request(Box<Request>)` enum variant cfg-gated. `Self::Request(_) => f.write_str(\"Request(..)\")` Debug arm cfg-gated. `parse_frame_payload` `wire_const::N_MID_REQUEST => { ... }` match arm cfg-gated.

session_glue.rs — send_request_query + send_request_query_with_meta SessionLinkActions methods retrofit to signature-stable + body-cfg shape per R311g1 / `feedback_signature_stability` MEMORY note. Both `()` returning so body-cfg branch silently no-ops when codec-request off; matching peer's z_get future hangs until per-call timeout fires (documented minus-codec-request contract). `let _ = (args)` suppresses unused-variable warnings on the disabled branch.

Implication chain extended: codec-request = [codec-frame] is the third body-codec-implies-envelope edge after codec-push (R311h) and codec-declare (R311i). Handshake-only-deploy contract closure progresses: codec-frame OFF now requires codec-push + codec-declare + codec-request OFF; R311k will add codec-response = [codec-frame] to complete the closure.
verification_bullets: cargo check matrix — default-features clean; --no-default-features (minus-all-codecs) clean. The Cargo implication chain (query-* implies codec-request) auto-pulls codec-request when query features are on so the body-cfg branch of send_request_query is mechanically reachable.
cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib: 589/589 pass — unit-test baseline preserved.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: clean.
cargo fmt --all --check: clean.
Layer E lane — wz_publisher_to_zsub 30-trial flake-0 confirms the Request wire emit + parse path stays bit-identical under the cfg cascade (pure refactor).
validate_workspace: entries 328→329, sections 255, T1=0, RT 13/13, sync.
carry_forward_bullets: R311k codec-response cascade — wire-layer gates for Response/ResponseVariant/Reply/Err imports, N_MID_RESPONSE const, build_response + encode_frame_with_response + reply/err builders, NetworkMessage::Response variant, parse arm. send_response body cfg per R311g1 pattern. Also includes the deferred R311e signature-deletion retrofit on build_response_final / encode_frame_with_response_final / send_response_final per R311g1 signature-stability pattern. codec-response = [codec-frame] imply. After R311k codec-frame elision becomes coherent (every body codec implies codec-frame so codec-frame OFF → handshake-only deploy: Init / Open / Close + KeepAlive).

R311m consumer-module cascade — the deferred pub/sub / declare-consumer / query-consumer / reply-consumer module gates. session.rs Session::publish + declare_subscriber{_aliased} + Subscriber struct + Drop + observer.rs subscribers field + declare/ subscriber.rs/queryable.rs/liveliness.rs/liveliness_subscriber.rs equivalents + query.rs QueryableRegistry + reply.rs ReplyRegistry + observer.rs queryables/replies fields. Architectural cascade distinct from per-cascade locality deferral.

Type-ungating carry forward unchanged — session.rs API surface (declare_querier / declare_queryable / declare_token / declare_liveliness_subscriber + QueryOptions builder methods) + ResponseFinal-using helpers. Blocked on type-gate elimination; R267 Session<R,T> reparam architectural pivot is the natural carrier.

Tier 3 measurement automation carry forward — extend scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh + CI Layer F to auto-verify each codec-* feature has a non-trivial mechanical delta WHEN the dependent high-level features are ALSO turned off (the imply chain makes single-feature elision misleading at the catalog level). Multi-feature elision lanes (e.g. `minus-codec-request --features=no-query-*`) become the truthful measurement for body codecs after R311h..R311k cascade closure.

Architectural carries unchanged: R267 Session<R,T> reparam (MCU prerequisite + type-ungating carrier for declare-*/query-* signatures), R284 uniform Established gate, R283 peer-side Interest inbound bilateral, R301 §8 SCE cross-repo, Q_B / Q_E codec slots, Phase W full lwIP (north star MCU half), R299 carry #2 / #3, R300 narrow, R301 §7 cargo wz-config tool, R304 stderr non-UTF-8 source, keyexpr_canon proptest filter.

changes_bullets: wz-session-core `sn.rs` NEW: zenoh-pico `transport/utils.c` mirror (`mask_from_res` / `half` / `precedes` / `decrement` / `increment`), pure no_std unconditional; half-window SN ordering SSOT (first consumer = multicast data plane).

`multicast_dispatch.rs`: `PeerSlot` gains `sn_mask` + per-channel `rx_sn_reliable`/`rx_sn_best_effort`; `ingest_join` signature gains `JoinSnBaseline` (sn_res + next_sn pair) and seeds baselines via decrement (the §3.2 `init_rx_seq` effect point, realised; re-seeds on refresh JOIN per pico `_sn_rx_sns` copy); NEW `ingest_frame_by_src(src, reliable, sn, now)` -> `FrameIngest` (Admitted / OutOfOrder / UnknownPeer / SessionNotRunning) applying the half-window gate per channel; OutOfOrder still refreshes lease (pico sets `_received = true` BEFORE its SN gate - liveness independent of data validity).

`multicast_glue.rs` (wz-runtime-tokio): `decode_join` full-body decode (decode_join_zid now a thin projection); NEW `validate_join` (§3.2 rejection rules: version + sn_res compat, absent sn_res = own default); JOIN RX arm validates before `ingest_join`; `T_MID_FRAME` arm now decodes via `parse_inbound`, admits via `ingest_frame_by_src`, parses payload via `parse_frame_payload`, and fans `IterationEvent::Poll(DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload)` through the NEW `on_event: FnMut(IterationEvent)` parameter of `drive_multicast_session` (the unicast `drive_session_until_terminal` observer-fan mirror - one `ApplicationLayerObserver` serves both transports); malformed/unknown-peer/stale frames dropped without touching the session FSM.
`MulticastParams` gains `seq_num_res` (own 2-bit resolution; multicast has no negotiation, mismatched JOINs are ignored).
wz-runtime-tokio Cargo: `transport-multicast` forward gains `codec-frame` (kconfig select - the data plane is the point of a transport; consumer arms stay per-feature like unicast).

Round 311ka.decision_summary: R311ka session-review fixes: F-1 multicast_put_literal reliable=true (pico Z_RELIABILITY_DEFAULT falsified the best-effort claim), F-2 finalized-staging loss window closed (same-lock-window drain contract + debug_assert; false comment rewritten), F-3 GaveUp-resume e2e pin, F-4 multicast-declarations RX-half caveat.
changes_bullets: F-1 (parity falsified): `multicast_put_literal` defaulted best-effort with a doc claiming "the zenoh multicast default" — pico's put default is RELIABLE (`Z_RELIABILITY_DEFAULT = Z_RELIABILITY_RELIABLE`, api/constants.h:203, multicast included). Now `reliable: true` + honest doc (the flag selects the SN ring + R flag, not a delivery guarantee — neither impl retransmits); unit test asserts the R flag + reliable-ring JOIN advance.

F-2 (false comment + loss window): the F3 `finalized` staging overflow comments claimed a dropped marker "only delays the prune" — FALSE: this drain is a get entry's ONLY prune, a dropped marker is a permanent replay-leak. Closed the window structurally: every staging site now drains within its own lock window (dispatch -> flush_pending same call; sweep -> caller drain — the wz-ap-demo ticker drains `take_finalized` -> prune right after `sweep_timed_out` under the same observer lock), making one staged batch provably <= the pending table; `debug_assert` pins the invariant; comments rewritten to the airtight contract.

F-2 enabler: `prune_liveliness_get_interest` moved to an INHERENT method on `SessionLinkActions` (the `send_response` inherent-twin shape); the `ResponseSink` trait method delegates — sweep callers holding the actions handle need no trait import.

F-3 (doc claim unpinned): NEW e2e `gave_up_supervisor_resumes_on_re_drive` pins the F6 GaveUp-resume contract (endpoint dies -> drive #1 GaveUp{attempts:2} -> post-GaveUp send rejects SendDeclareError::TransportUnavailable (F2) -> endpoint rebinds same addr -> drive #2 re-handshakes + replays verbatim + reconnects()==1).
F-6 (doc drift): `response_sink` module intro now describes the full drain-effect set (reply emits + declarer interest-responses + the F3 cache prune), not just "wire emit".

Reply-before-Final restructure: the dispatch SSOT (dispatch_iteration_event_with) stages each matched request's ResponseFinal as a deferred-fire JOB contiguous with the handler jobs (same observer lock window) instead of flushing finals under the lock — a drainer executes a taken batch sequentially, so per-rid ordering is structural and drainer-identity-independent (an auxiliary query/publish-tail or sweep drainer stealing the batch preserves it); observer grows flush_pending_replies + take_pending_final_rids, the combined flush_pending stays the raw-registry / MCU drain

query/query_aliased local sequencing: the loopback Final is delivered AFTER the tail drain ran every deferred local handler (then a second drain fires on_final) — on_final after every local on_reply, the pico deliver-query-locally emit-final-at-tail ordering preserved across the deferred shape

changes_bullets: session review of the R311lf..li data-plane deferral cascade (lf ratify + lg/lh/li the 4-plane implementation): lf/lg/lh verdict textbook — no hack / doc-around-hack / workaround; SSOT axes hold (single DeferredFireQueue, owned-staging reuses Sample::from_view / InboundReply / QueryResponder / into_response with zero third structs, dispatch SSOT strengthened); li carried one real defect (Finding A below), closed in this same round

Finding A (real, li-introduced) CLOSED: the Reply-before-Final ordering li claimed as structural held only when a stealing drainer acquired the observer lock first; an auxiliary drainer taking the queue with the queue lock ALONE (drain_deferred_fires / publish / query / sweep tails) could mem::take a half-staged dispatch window — a queryable handler job staged before its trailing ResponseFinal job — and emit the Final ahead of the handler's last Reply on the wire

fix = observer-serialized batch take (NOT the FinalGuard the review floated): DeferredFireQueue::take_batch + Session::drain_deferred_fires wraps each take in the observer lock; since every stage() runs inside the staging site's observer-lock window, an observer-serialized take observes only whole numbers of complete windows, so [handler, final] always land in one batch on one drainer in FIFO order; jobs still RUN outside the lock (the lock is held only across the cheap Vec swap), preserving the lock-free callback invariant. Chosen over FinalGuard (pico query-rc-drop parity) because it is a localized lock-discipline fix with an obvious invariant vs a cross-layer per-request refcount threaded through sink->job + a raw-path double-emit interaction; FinalGuard is now unnecessary (the Final stays a staged job emitted by the existing send_response_final)

secondary cleanup: publish / publish_aliased drain only on the allows_local path — a Remote-only publish stages nothing, so its prior unconditional drain was gratuitous (ran drive-loop-staged callbacks on the publish thread); now a method drains iff it staged

self-contained DeferredFireQueue::drain_and_fire retained (queue lock only) for single-thread fixtures (the deferred_fire_infra unit tests) where no concurrent stager exists; its doc states the non-serialized caveat
verification_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio --lib 251 PASS (unchanged set — the fix is a lock-discipline change under the existing functional tests; the wire queryable test queryable_handler_runs_deferred_replies_then_final_on_wire pins Reply-frame-before-Final-frame), deferred_fire_infra 4 PASS, wz-session-core PASS

multicast_glue.rs: MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply { declare: DeclareOwned } variant (gated liveliness-token, the sole producer; it implies declare-token -> codec-declare) + loop TX arm (mint reliable SN -> encode_frame_with_declare -> multicast_frame_or_fragments, reliable).

MulticastReplySink intentionally does NOT impl LivelinessGetPrune: the get-prune concern is the session-reconnect declaration-cache prune, and the connectionless multicast transport (JOIN + lease, no re-dial) has no cache to prune. changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip session_drive.rs: introduce SessionDriveConfig { timeouts, role, max_iters } - the static parameterization of one run_session drive, separated from the loop's live collaborators (the runtime / link / driver / actions / clock handles + the on_event observer) via Introduce-Parameter-Object. run_session drops from 9 args to 7 (runtime, link, driver, actions, clock, config, on_event) and the #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] the prior signature carried is removed. The body destructures config into the local names at the top, mirroring how the two multicast loops handle MulticastDriveConfig.

All three fields are Copy (SessionTimeouts derives Copy, SessionRole is a Copy enum, max_iters is Option<usize>), so SessionDriveConfig owns them by value and carries no lifetime - unlike wz_session_core MulticastDriveConfig, which must borrow its non-Copy params (the Vec-bearing MulticastParams). The HandshakeDeadlineTracker::new(*timeouts) deref becomes a by-value pass.

Exported via the wz_session_lwip lib pub use; it reaches the facade through the existing pub use wz_session_lwip as session_lwip.

Round 311lx.decision_summary: R311lx Round A: multicast TX emit extracted to shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx SSOT (MulticastTxItem + multicast_tx_emit, the TX twin of multicast_rx); AP loop de-duplicated to call it.
changes_bullets: New wz_session_core::multicast_tx SSOT (the TX twin of R311lv's multicast_rx): MulticastTxItem (moved from wz-runtime-tokio) + MulticastTxFrames + multicast_tx_emit(item, &mut TxSn, &MulticastParams) -> MulticastTxFrames. The §3.1 TxData decision (item variant -> mint -> encode_frame_with_* -> multicast_frame_or_fragments) now has ONE home consumed by both transport profiles' loops, realising the engine-free contract for the egress half - it was inline-duplicated in the AP loop, the same smell R311lv removed for RX. Module gated all(session-multicast, codec-frame, alloc); the per-variant body codecs (codec-push/response/response-final/liveliness-token) gate the enum variants + emit arms; the emit fn is union-gated so it exists only when a body codec inhabits the item.

multicast_put_literal moved alongside MulticastTxItem (it composes the session-core build_push_literal SSOT, so it belongs with the shared item type). Both re-exported from wz_runtime_tokio::multicast_glue via pub use, so the AP loop's public TX API + its tests are unchanged by the move.

wz-runtime-tokio multicast_glue de-duplicated: the inline 4-arm outbound match (Push/Response/ResponseFinal/DeclareReply, ~110 LOC) replaced by a multicast_tx_emit call + a send loop, so the AP loop now owns only the IO (the mpsc recv + the async LinkDriver::send). The emit import + the outbound Some(item) arm are union-gated, with a not(union) `match item {}` arm preserving the uninhabited-item build (matching the prior per-codec import gating; no robustness regression). The encode_frame_with_* / multicast_frame_or_fragments / build_response_final / push_build imports retired from the loop (the SSOT owns them); build_token_reply / build_final_reply stay (the AP MulticastReplySink composes them before enqueuing).

ResponseFinal now routes through multicast_frame_or_fragments like the other three variants (one uniform egress path): byte-identical (a single tiny VLE rid never reaches the budget, so it returns its one frame with no follow-on mint) but it removes the special-case arm and keeps params + tx_sn used by every arm, so the union-gated emit fn has no unused-parameter edge in any single-codec config.

Round 311ly.decision_summary: R311ly Round B: MCU multicast TX seam - run_multicast_session next_tx pull-callback feeds the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT (z_put over the group); 8->7 args via clock-derivation, no #[allow].
changes_bullets: wz_session_lwip::multicast_drive::run_multicast_session gains the application TX publish seam (the R311lu/lv carry): a next_tx: FnMut() -> Option<MulticastTxItem> pull-callback, symmetric with the on_event push-callback - the MCU busy-poll mirror of the AP loop's tokio mpsc outbound receiver. Each iteration, right after the JOIN beacon and before the lwIP pump, the loop drains pending outbound items and frames each through the SAME shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx::multicast_tx_emit SSOT (R311lx) the AP loop calls, multicasting the datagrams via send_to_group so they ride that iteration's run_until_idle. The MCU multicast loop now emits app data, not only the JOIN beacon.

The TX emit + the mut tx_sn binding are gated on codec-push (wz-session-lwip's only forwarded TX body codec); a codec-free transport-multicast build leaves MulticastTxItem uninhabited, so the seam stays in the signature - next_tx is consumed by a not(codec-push) `if let Some(item) = next_tx() { match item {} }` - without an unused-parameter or unused-mut lint, so the RX-only multicast build is unchanged.

New wz-session-lwip `codec-push` feature forwards wz-session-core/codec-push (orthogonal to transport-multicast; a publishing multicast node enables both). build_push_literal needs only codec-push, so multicast_put_literal builds a literal-keyexpr Put with no extra pub/sub feature.

Adding next_tx took the loop to 8 args (clippy too_many_arguments 8/7). Resolved NOT with #[allow] (the hack R311lw just removed from run_session) but by dropping the redundant clock parameter: the multicast loop derives its monotonic clock from the runtime it already pumps (LwipTime::new(runtime)). Unlike the unicast run_session (R263 external clock to share the actions clock-clone epoch) or the AP loop (ambient tokio, no runtime param), the multicast loop has no actions bundle, so an external clock was a redundant re-derivation. 7 args, no #[allow].

Deterministic real-lwIP test run_multicast_session_publishes_a_put_over_loopback (codec-push): a queued Put is framed + multicast, echoed by multicast loopback, admitted at our own source via a pre-injected distinct-zid JOIN (the §3.2 source-keyed peer entry), and observed by on_event as a Push - a true TX -> loopback -> RX round trip, frozen-clock deterministic.

Round 311lz.decision_summary: R311lz: MCU multicast TX seam variant-complete - next_tx gate codec-push-only -> TX-codec union, so Response/ResponseFinal/DeclareReply route through multicast_tx_emit SSOT like Push.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip's multicast TX seam (run_multicast_session's next_tx pull) is now variant-complete: the loop's TX gate - the multicast_tx_emit import, the `mut tx_sn` binding, and the drain while-loop - generalised from `#[cfg(feature = "codec-push")]` to the `any(codec-push, codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token)` union, the SAME gate the shared wz_session_core::multicast_tx::multicast_tx_emit SSOT and the AP wz-runtime-tokio::multicast_glue loop already carry. A queued queryable Response / ResponseFinal or a liveliness DeclareReply now routes through the one SSOT exactly as Push did (R311ly); the drain stays variant-agnostic (the item carries which arm). Three new wz-session-lwip features forward the matching wz-session-core TX body codecs: codec-response + codec-response-final (the queryable reply chain - a reply payload + its terminating ResponseFinal, forwarded together because a reply needs both) and liveliness-token (the declarer-side interest-response; transitively pulls codec-declare so the loop can frame a held-token Declare reply over the group). Each is orthogonal to transport-multicast; a publishing node enables the variant(s) it emits. The application produces these reply items today (it builds + queues them on next_tx); the observer-staging auto-producer is the follow-on.

New deterministic real-lwIP test run_multicast_session_publishes_a_declare_reply_over_loopback (liveliness-token, NO codec-push): a DeclFinal reply (build_final_reply(9).try_into_owned()) queued on next_tx is framed by multicast_tx_emit, multicast to the group, echoed by loopback, admitted at our own pre-injected distinct-zid source, and observed by on_event as a Declare carrying interest id 9 - a true non-Push TX -> loopback -> RX round trip, frozen-clock deterministic. It exercises the union gate WITHOUT codec-push (the case the old codec-push-only gating mis-compiled to `match item {}` on an inhabited type). The variant-body check (DeclFinal vs DeclToken) is omitted: it needs wz-codecs, not an MCU-crate dep, and interest_id is the querier's correlation key while the only Declare emitted is the DeclFinal, so it suffices.

Round 311ma.decision_summary: R311ma: MCU multicast observer staging - MulticastReplyQueue (no_std DeclareReplySink, mirror of AP MulticastReplySink); observer flush_declare_replies -> queue -> next_tx auto-reply to Interest.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip gains MulticastReplyQueue (wz_session_lwip::multicast_drive), the no_std MCU mirror of the AP loop's MulticastReplySink: an Rc<RefCell<VecDeque<MulticastTxItem>>> (the single-task busy-poll analogue of the AP's tokio mpsc - on_event pushes, next_tx pops, same thread, so no cross-thread Send) implementing DeclareReplySink. The observer drains its staged liveliness interest-response replies into it (flush_declare_replies); the sink owns the encode by building the owned Declare via the shared build_token_reply / build_final_reply SSOT (the same wire shape the unicast SessionLinkActions: DeclareReplySink derives) and enqueues a MulticastTxItem::DeclareReply. Clone shares the backing store between the on_event + next_tx closures; pop() drains FIFO for the next_tx seam.

Per the R311lq interface segregation the queue implements ONLY DeclareReplySink - the concern a liveliness declarer drains. It does NOT implement LivelinessGetPrune (the connectionless multicast transport has no reconnect declaration cache to prune, same rationale as the AP MulticastReplySink). The queryable ResponseSink reply chain is deliberately NOT here: it names wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned, a codec type this MCU crate does not yet dep, and needs the query-queryable registry forward - carried as the follow-on.

New integration test run_multicast_session_stages_observer_declare_replies_into_next_tx (liveliness-token): an inbound liveliness Interest (CURRENT, interest id 9) for a held local token (build_interest_liveliness_get + encode_frame_with_interest, injected at the JOIN-advertised SN 0) is dispatched to the observer, which stages a DeclToken + terminating DeclFinal; the on_event closure flushes them through the queue's DeclareReplySink into the shared queue, and next_tx drains both - asserting exactly 2 DeclareReply items reached the seam (observer -> sink -> next_tx). The MCU mirror of the AP drive_loop_emits_liveliness_token_reply_over_multicast.

The test asserts on the DRAINED items, not a loopback echo: the injected Interest at SN 0 advances the shared source peer entry past our reply mints, so an echoed DeclToken at our tx SN 0 would be SN-stale-dropped (a loopback-observation artifact, not a bug). The wire emit of a queued DeclareReply is separately covered by the R311lz run_multicast_session_publishes_a_declare_reply_over_loopback round-trip. Round 311mb.decision_summary: R311mb: MCU queryable observer staging - MulticastReplyQueue impls ResponseSink (query-queryable + wz-codecs dep); box large MulticastTxItem variants to fix large_enum_variant + shrink MCU queue.
changes_bullets: wz-session-lwip's MulticastReplyQueue (R311ma) now also implements ResponseSink (the queryable reply chain), completing the MCU observer-staging mirror of the AP MulticastReplySink: the observer drains its staged query replies (flush_query_replies -> Response + terminating ResponseFinal, reply-before-final) into the queue, the loop's next_tx seam drains them out. So a registered queryable on the MCU now auto-replies to an inbound Query over the group, as the liveliness declarer (R311ma) does for an Interest. The type's gate widened from liveliness-token to the reply-variant union any(codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token); each producer-trait impl stays gated by its own codec family (ResponseSink any(codec-response, codec-response-final); DeclareReplySink liveliness-token).

New wz-session-lwip query-queryable feature forwards wz-session-core/query-queryable (the QueryableRegistry + codec-request for inbound Query decode + codec-response). codec-response now ALSO forwards wz-codecs/codec-response, and a wz-codecs direct dep (default-features=false, alloc) is added SOLELY so the ResponseSink::send_response signature can name wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned (the one wz_codecs type this MCU crate references; the declare / push arms use inferred owned types). Mirrors how wz-runtime-tokio deps wz-codecs for the AP reply path.

New integration test run_multicast_session_stages_observer_query_replies_into_next_tx (all(query-queryable, codec-response, codec-response-final)): an inbound Query (rid 7, at the JOIN-advertised SN 0) for a registered queryable is dispatched to the observer, whose handler stages a Response; flush_query_replies drains it + its terminating ResponseFinal through the queue's ResponseSink into the shared queue, and next_tx drains exactly one Response + one ResponseFinal. Asserts on the drained items (the injected Query at SN 0 advances the shared peer entry past our reply mints, so a loopback echo would SN-stale-drop - the same artifact the liveliness sibling avoids).

Boxed the large MulticastTxItem variants (R311mb): Push -> Box<PushOwned>, Response -> Box<ResponseOwned>, DeclareReply -> Box<DeclareOwned> (the small ResponseFinal, a bare rid, stays inline), mirroring NetworkMessage's own Box<PushOwned> / Box<ResponseOwned> / Box<DeclareOwned> in the same crate. This bounds the enum to a pointer (the owned payloads already heap-allocate, so the extra Box is marginal), shrinks the MCU MulticastReplyQueue's VecDeque slots from 700+ bytes to pointer-sized, AND fixes clippy large_enum_variant which the new codec-response/final-only run-ci clippy combo surfaced (the lint compares largest vs second-largest variant; without codec-push / liveliness-token, Response 784 bytes vs ResponseFinal 8 bytes tripped it). multicast_tx_emit derefs the Box per arm; the AP + MCU construction sites Box::new. The `use alloc::boxed::Box` import is gated on the boxed-variant union (codec-push / codec-response / liveliness-token; NOT codec-response-final, which stays inline), so a no-data-codec or ResponseFinal-only build does not import an unused Box under -D warnings.

Boxed the large MulticastTxItem variants (R311mb): Push -> Box<PushOwned>, Response -> Box<ResponseOwned>, DeclareReply -> Box<DeclareOwned> (the small ResponseFinal, a bare rid, stays inline), mirroring NetworkMessage's own Box<PushOwned> / Box<ResponseOwned> / Box<DeclareOwned> in the same crate. This bounds the enum to a pointer (the owned payloads already heap-allocate, so the extra Box is marginal), shrinks the MCU MulticastReplyQueue's VecDeque slots from 700+ bytes to pointer-sized, AND fixes clippy large_enum_variant which the new codec-response/final-only run-ci clippy combo surfaced (the lint compares largest vs second-largest variant; without codec-push / liveliness-token, Response 784 bytes vs ResponseFinal 8 bytes tripped it). multicast_tx_emit derefs the Box per arm; the AP + MCU construction sites Box::new. The `use alloc::boxed::Box` import is gated on the boxed-variant union (codec-push / codec-response / liveliness-token; NOT codec-response-final, which stays inline), so a no-data-codec or ResponseFinal-only build does not import an unused Box under -D warnings.

Round 311md.decision_summary: R311md: reply-sink SSOT - generic MulticastReplySink<Q> + MulticastReplyEnqueue in wz-session-core; AP/MCU give only a backing; dedups the sink impl + drops wz-session-lwip wz-codecs dep.
changes_bullets: New wz-session-core module multicast_reply_sink (gated all(session-multicast, codec-frame, alloc) - the multicast_tx gate): a generic MulticastReplySink<Q> + a MulticastReplyEnqueue trait. The "given a ResponseSink / DeclareReplySink call, which MulticastTxItem does it become" construction (the build_*_reply + try_into_owned + Box::new + variant choice) lives here ONCE - the TX-staging twin of the multicast_rx (RX dispatch) and multicast_tx (TX emit) SSOTs. ResponseSink (codec-response / codec-response-final) + DeclareReplySink (liveliness-token) are impl'd once for MulticastReplySink<Q: MulticastReplyEnqueue>; Q decides only HOW each constructed item is queued for the loop.

Before R311md the AP MulticastReplySink (wz-runtime-tokio) and the MCU MulticastReplyQueue (wz-session-lwip) duplicated those four trait methods byte-for-byte except the enqueue line (tx.send vs queue.push_back). Both collapse to a MulticastReplyEnqueue backing: AP TokioReplyBacking (wraps UnboundedSender, enqueue = send) + pub type MulticastReplySink = MulticastReplySink<TokioReplyBacking> (the public name is preserved); MCU MulticastReplyQueue becomes the Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>> backing (enqueue = push_back, keeps pop() for next_tx). The observer drains MulticastReplySink::new(backing.clone()); the loop pops the backing.

wz-session-lwip's wz-codecs DIRECT DEP (added R311mb only to name wz_codecs::response::ResponseOwned in its duplicated send_response signature) is REMOVED, and its codec-response feature no longer forwards wz-codecs/codec-response: the ResponseOwned-named send_response now lives in wz-session-core (which already deps wz-codecs), and the backing's enqueue takes the already-constructed MulticastTxItem. So the dep was a pure symptom of the duplication - folding the impl removed both. The MCU backing crate names no codec type.

Behaviour-identical: no wire / FSM / SN / construction change - only the home of the 4 trait methods moved from two crates to one generic. AP multicast_glue reply tests + MCU observer-staging tests updated to drain through MulticastReplySink::new(queue.clone()) instead of the queue directly (the queue is now the enqueue backing, not the sink). The R311lz DeclareReply loopback test fully-qualifies alloc::boxed::Box::new (the top-level Box import moved out of wz-session-lwip with the impls).

Round 311me.decision_summary: R311me: deferred_fire gate collapsed to `deferred-fire` alone; liveliness-token no longer drags Arc onto the M0 multicast profile, so thumbv6m liveliness cross-builds via the inline-fire path.
changes_bullets: lib.rs: the deferred_fire module #[cfg] collapses from all(feature="alloc", any(deferred-fire, session-matching, declare-subscriber, declare-queryable, liveliness-token, liveliness-subscriber, query-reply)) to feature="deferred-fire" alone (the feature implies alloc). The pre-R311lh plane arms were dead weight: no wz-session-core code instantiates a deferred type under them (only doc-links in decl_sink.rs / declare/matching.rs), and the only real consumer, AP wz-runtime-tokio, enables deferred-fire unconditionally on its wz-session-core dependency - so the module still compiles for the tier that uses it.

Root cause closed: liveliness-token in the gate forced `use alloc::sync::Arc;` (deferred_fire.rs:101) to compile on the MCU multicast profile; thumbv6m (ARMv6-M) has no target_has_atomic="ptr", so the otherwise-unused module failed to build (E0432 unresolved import alloc::sync). The MCU multicast liveliness / queryable reply is staged inline through the Rc<RefCell<VecDeque>>-backed MulticastReplyQueue (wz-session-lwip multicast_drive.rs), never the deferred seam - so dropping the module from that profile IS the inline-fire path the R311mc/md carry asked for, not a behaviour change.

Docs synced (non-store source files): the lib.rs deferred_fire module-decl comment, the deferred_fire.rs "## Gating" doc, and the wz-session-core Cargo.toml deferred-fire feature comment all rewritten to record the sole-gate structure and why the plane arms were removed (redundant post-R311lh + the thumbv6m Arc break).

After collapsing the gate the same thumbv6m build passes. AP unaffected: wz-runtime-tokio builds + the deferred_fire_infra integration test 5/5 pass; the host subset (liveliness-token WITHOUT deferred-fire) and the no-alloc decl lane (--no-default-features codec-declare,declare-subscriber,declare-queryable,liveliness-token,liveliness-subscriber) both build.

Round 311mf.decision_summary: R311mf: MCU multicast Fragment RX/TX - the AP R311kn/ko arms ported to run_multicast_session: reassembly RX wiring + a transport-fragmentation feature that splits TX via the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-lwip/src/multicast_drive.rs: run_multicast_session now wires the reassembly-divergent RX tail through the shared wz-session-core SSOT, the MCU twin of the AP loop's R311kn arm. Under `reassembly` a per-(slot,channel) Router (mcu_reassembly = ReassemblyDispatcher<4,4096>, the same run_session owns) is built before the loop; the FrameOutOfOrder arm aborts the channel's in-progress chain (reasm.abort_channel via peer_index_by_src), the Fragment arm parses the inbound T_MID_FRAGMENT (parse_inbound -> InboundFrame::Fragment) and reassembles via ingest_multicast_fragment (per-peer SN gate -> chain -> the completed message fans as the SAME FramePayload Poll a whole Frame does), and the Close arm aborts the departing peer's chains before close_by_src. The sweep arm becomes sweep_with(now, abort_peer_chains) + sweep_reporting under `reassembly`, the bare sweep otherwise. Without the feature the arms keep the prior drop-Fragment behaviour (pico fragmentation-off).

crates/wz-session-lwip/Cargo.toml: a new `transport-fragmentation` feature = [reassembly, wz-session-core/transport-fragmentation] forwards the core umbrella (reassembly + codec-fragment + alloc) and re-uses this crate's reassembly forward for the wz-runtime-lwip Router. No drive-loop code change for TX: run_multicast_session already frames its next_tx seam through the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT, which splits an oversize payload via multicast_frame_or_fragments once the feature is on - exactly as the AP loop. The MCU TX port was a feature forward; the fragmentation SSOT was already shared (R311ko).

Test run_multicast_session_reassembles_a_fragmented_put_over_loopback (gated transport-fragmentation,codec-push): the real-lwIP fragment leg. A 200-byte z_put at batch_size 64 is proven to fragment (>1 datagram via a direct multicast_tx_emit probe), multicast to the group, echoed back, and reassembled by the Fragment RX arm into one observed Push (no ReassemblyDropped). The pre-admitted peer JOIN advertises batch_size 64 to match self: validate_join admits only when the JOIN's batch_size equals the receiver's params, else the echoed fragments hit an UnknownPeer drop.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/multicast_rx.rs: two new SSOTs close the session-review Finding B (the dispatch CLASSIFY was already shared via dispatch_multicast_inbound, but the reassembly TAIL wiring was hand-mirrored byte-for-byte in the AP multicast_glue + MCU multicast_drive loops). dispatch_multicast_inbound_reassembling wraps the classify + applies the full tail (FrameOutOfOrder -> abort_channel, Fragment -> parse_inbound + ingest_multicast_fragment, Close -> abort_peer_chains + close_by_src) with the caller's Router; sweep_multicast_reassembling does the deadline-reclaim-report + evict-with-chain-abort pair. crates/wz-mcu-multicast-e2e/tests/host_multicast_e2e.rs: the RUNTIME PROOF the footprint bin cannot give via QEMU. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/reassembly.rs: NEW transport-agnostic shared module. Relocated TokioReassembly (the AP reassembly Router type alias) + reassembly_config() + the REASSEMBLY_SLOTS / REASSEMBLY_SLOT_SIZE consts out of session_glue.rs (the unicast handshake driver) into a neutral SSOT gated on the `reassembly` feature only. Both the unicast steady-state drive loop and the multicast drive loop (multicast_glue) run their own pool instance over the SAME SCE-sourced AP dims/knobs (one buffer-pool policy SSOT, two transports). Keeping them in session_glue made a transport-multicast-only build (no session_glue) unable to reach the pool config - the root of the facade composability gap.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs: `pub mod session_glue` + `pub mod session` are now `#[cfg(feature = "transport-unicast")]`. session_glue names the SessionFsmUnicast{Policy,Event} types and drives session_actions / session_timeouts / drive (all session-unicast-gated in wz-session-core); the Session handle owns a session_glue::SessionLinkActions bundle (the unicast action machinery) - so both are the unicast-session API surface. A transport-multicast-only build drives multicast through multicast_glue::drive_multicast_session over the shared ApplicationLayerObserver, not a Session handle. Added `#[cfg(feature = "reassembly")] pub mod reassembly`.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/{udp_pipeline,link_pipeline}.rs: import BoxedLinkDriver from its SSOT home wz_session_core::link (the shared link tier) instead of via the crate::session_glue re-export hop. The link pipeline is transport-agnostic (a multicast deploy binds a UDP multicast socket too), so it must not depend on the now-transport-unicast-gated session_glue. This also closed the pre-existing transport-link-udp / transport-link-tcp WITHOUT transport-unicast arbitrary-composition gaps as a bonus (the realistic transport-multicast,transport-link-udp deploy shape now builds).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multicast_glue.rs: the multicast reassembly Router is constructed from crate::reassembly (was crate::session_glue); the tx_sn TX-mint state carries a `#[cfg_attr(not(any(codec-push, codec-response, codec-response-final, liveliness-token)), allow(unused_mut))]` because a JOIN-only multicast build (transport-multicast with no data-plane body codecs, now reachable since the unicast decouple) reads tx_sn for the beacon (encode_join) but never mints (multicast_tx_emit is gated on those codecs).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: transport-multicast += codec-close. The shared multicast RX classify/dispatch SSOT wz_session_core::multicast_rx (consumed by multicast_glue) is gated on codec-close because it decodes T_MID_CLOSE and aborts the leaving peer's reassembly chains via dispatcher.close_by_src (multicast_rx.rs:147,209). A select edge in the same class as the existing codec-join / codec-frame - a multicast transport that cannot process a peer's Close is incomplete, not optional. Previously masked by the default codec set; the facade composability build (no default) exposed the unresolved multicast_rx import.

crates/wz/Cargo.toml: facade transport-multicast does NOT re-list codec-close - the crate forward self-selects it (wz-runtime-tokio/transport-multicast += codec-close; wz-session-lwip/transport-multicast already pulls wz-session-core/codec-close), mirroring how the facade does not re-list codec-join / codec-frame. An explicit facade codec-close forward would be redundant AND would perturb wz-runtime-lwip's feature set for the MCU multicast footprint bin (Q.5) for zero benefit, so it was deliberately omitted; a one-line comment records this.

scripts/run-ci.sh: NEW Layer C4e (transport-axis matrix). The consumer-plane matrices C4b/C4c/C1j/C4d vary the consumer plane on a transport-unicast base and cannot express the orthogonal transport axis; C4e builds the wz facade (the reported-gap shape) + clippy-checks the wz-runtime-tokio crate in isolation (deny-warnings) under 3 multicast-WITHOUT-unicast subsets (multicast-join-only, multicast-data, multicast-udp-deploy) so the decouple cannot silently regress. No cargo-test twin: a multicast-only crate has no unicast-handshake tests and the multicast behaviour is already covered with unicast on by C1p/C1q + the MCU e2e by C1r. The stale "transport-unicast is FOUNDATIONAL / transport-multicast reserved with no consumer" rationale in _wz_runtime_tokio_coherent_subsets was corrected (transport-multicast is now an independently-composable atom).

Decision rationale (why the structural decouple, not an implication edge): the cheap alternative transport-multicast => transport-unicast was rejected as a smell - it would weld two catalog atoms (violating the atomic-features north star), encode a wz implementation artifact as a protocol-level dependency that is FALSE (zenoh-pico builds multicast-only), and leave the real mis-placement (SessionLinkActions / reassembly / BoxedLinkDriver sitting in the unicast tier) unaddressed. The structural decouple is the SSOT-correct fix: each module in its correct tier, the catalog-atomic transport-multicast composes alone.
verification_bullets: Full run-ci with Layer G + Q (WZ_RUN_LAYER_G=1 WZ_RUN_LAYER_Q=1 --skip-codegen): exit code 0, "run-ci: all required layers pass", no FAIL lines. NEW Layer C4e pass (3 transport-axis subsets: multicast-join-only / multicast-data / multicast-udp-deploy, each facade build + wz-runtime-tokio crate clippy -D warnings). Existing multicast lanes C1p / C1q (with unicast on) + C1r (MCU multicast e2e) all pass - no regression on the with-unicast multicast path.

Q.5 MCU multicast footprint gate UNMOVED: footprint[multicast-e2e] thumbv7m-none-eabi text=50680 (+0) OK / data=4 (+0) OK / bss=270100 (+0) INFO, thumbv7em-none-eabihf text=50484 (+0) OK - identical to the R311mi baseline. Confirms the facade transport-multicast did NOT re-list codec-close (which would have forced wz-runtime-lwip/codec-close and perturbed the bin); the bin's feature set is unchanged. Layer G all MCU cross-compile lanes pass (G.1-G.11).

The reported facade gap is closed: `cargo build -p wz --no-default-features --features runtime-tokio,transport-multicast` now compiles (was 13 errors on session_glue's unconditional unicast imports + 1 on multicast_rx's codec-close gate). 10-config compile sweep PASS: runtime-tokio (bare), transport-unicast, transport-multicast (multicast-only), transport-multicast+codec-push, unicast+multicast, preset-ap-client / -ap-router / -ap-full, wz-runtime-tokio default + --all-features.

Behaviour-neutral for existing consumers: cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --features transport-multicast = 268 lib tests + all integration tests pass (0 failed). clippy --all-targets clean on the default crate + the facade multicast-only + both-transports configs. cargo fmt --all -- --check clean.

The `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` failure (sce-rust-runtime no_std + http-send mutually-exclusive compile_error) is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: reproduced identically on stashed HEAD - it is cargo's workspace-wide feature unification footgun, which is why the project gate is run-ci.sh (per-crate feature sets), not a blanket --workspace --all-targets.
carry_forward_bullets: R311lv facade composability carry CLOSED: AP runtime-tokio,transport-multicast WITHOUT transport-unicast now compiles (the structural decouple). transport-multicast is an independently-composable catalog atom; a multicast-only build exposes the standalone drive_multicast_session loop over a shared ApplicationLayerObserver. Guarded by Layer C4e (3 transport-axis subsets: build + clippy) so it cannot regress.

Level B (north-star, deferred separate cascade): unify multicast under the Session handle (the zenoh-cpp transport-agnostic-session shape, where one Session owns unicast + multicast transports). Today a multicast-only build drives multicast via the standalone drive_multicast_session loop, NOT a Session handle (the Session handle is the unicast API surface, owning SessionLinkActions). Making Session own a multicast transport is a much larger architectural evolution; doing it in this round would have been scope creep.

Banked collateral: the BoxedLinkDriver SSOT-home redirect (udp_pipeline / link_pipeline import from wz_session_core::link instead of the session_glue re-export hop) also closed the pre-existing transport-link-udp / transport-link-tcp WITHOUT transport-unicast arbitrary-composition gaps - a degenerate-but-now-coherent link-only shape that previously failed because session_glue was compiled unconditionally.

Out of scope (no consumer): `#[cfg(test)] test_fixtures` still names the unicast SessionLinkActions, so a `cargo test --no-default-features --features transport-multicast` (no unicast) would not compile it. C4e is build + clippy only (no test twin) and there is no multicast-only test consumer, so this is not exercised; gating test_fixtures on transport-unicast is a trivial future cleanup if a multicast-only test lane is ever wanted.

Deferred from R311mi/mj (unchanged): a slim multicast rx pool (the 32x1536 pool is slim-toggle-independent today) for nrf51-class 16 KB SRAM + a thumbv6m multicast .text footprint baseline; and a differential footprint gate (feature ON/OFF ROM delta) expressing the north-star ">=256B measurable when disabled" claim more directly than the absolute-baseline idiom.

Round 311mr.decision_summary: B5b-1 (Level B): the transport-dispatch send seam. Add Session::send_network_message (the _z_send_n_msg analogue) routing a built NetworkMessage to the owned transport send path; B5b-1 inhabits the multicast arm (Push-only, gated not(transport-unicast)) and migrates the multicast publish remote leg through it. changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: added Session::send_network_message (gated all(transport-multicast, not(transport-unicast), codec-push)) - the wz analogue of zenoh-pico _z_send_n_msg (src/transport/transport.c:29 switch over the transport tag, called by every put/get/declare primitive in src/net/primitives.c). Takes a built NetworkMessage (the transport-agnostic outbound currency = pico _z_network_message_t) and routes Push -> MulticastTxItem::Push -> the drive-loop TX channel. A non-Push reaching it (unreachable: a multicast Session originates only Push) returns SendWireError::FeatureDisabled, never a panic. The application API stays transport-agnostic; the transport split lives in the seam (pico shape), not a fallible actions() exposed at every call site (the Option-A design I rejected).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: migrated the multicast Session::publish remote leg through the seam - builds NetworkMessage::Push via build_push_literal then send_network_message, replacing the inline multicast_put_literal enqueue. Return type Result<(), CodecError> -> Result<usize, SendWireError>. SendWireError is the SAME error the unicast dispatch_* family returns, so B5b-2's unicast arm needs no error unification; it lives ungated in wz_session_core::send_wire_error, reachable in a multicast-only build that the transport-unicast-gated session_glue re-export is not.

Remaining B5b: the UNICAST arm (route a NetworkMessage to the SessionLinkActions dispatch_* family - those take a closure-encoded body via dispatch_network_message, not a NetworkMessage value, so the arm matches the variant and calls the matching dispatch_*), then drop the not(transport-unicast) gate so a both-transports build runtime-matches the transport - which forces actions() (33 call sites, all in transport-unicast-gated methods) to become transport-aware = the actions() dismantling.
The seam's error type (SendWireError) is already transport-uniform, so the unicast arm needs no error unification.
Multicast Session origination stays Push-only until a multicast query/declare API exists (a new-feature follow-on); the reply messages are emitted by the drive-loop MulticastReplySink, not this seam.
The unicast publish still sends via send_push_with_meta_literal (not yet migrated to the seam); it migrates when the unicast arm lands (B5b-2).

Round 311mz.decision_summary: Session-review follow-up: fix the declare_token_aliased liveliness-token registration asymmetry (a confirmed correctness bug, pico-divergent). The literal Session::declare_token registered the held token in the declarer-side LocalTokenRegistry (so an inbound non-final liveliness Interest replays it to peers that subscribe LATER), but Session::declare_token_aliased silently skipped that register - so an aliased-declared token was invisible to late subscribers, diverging from zenoh-pico (_z_declare_liveliness_token always inserts into _local_tokens, net/liveliness.c:77, regardless of literal/alias form). Fixed unrepresentably (not test-guarded) per feedback_unrepresentable_over_test: the LocalTokenRegistry registration moved into LivelinessToken::new_held, the now-SOLE constructor, and the struct fields made private - so neither declare path can build a held token without registering. Behaviour change: aliased tokens now replay to late subscribers (the fix); literal path byte-identical.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/liveliness.rs: made the LivelinessToken fields private (was pub(super)) and added LivelinessToken::new_held - the SOLE constructor - which registers the token in the declarer-side LocalTokenRegistry (observer.local_tokens.register, the R283 late-subscriber replay state) then builds the handle. With the fields sealed, a held token cannot be constructed without that registration, so the literal and aliased declare paths register identically by construction (the asymmetry is unrepresentable, not merely tested - feedback_unrepresentable_over_test). Doc cites pico parity (net/liveliness.c:77) + the late-subscriber replay consequence.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: declare_token (literal) now calls LivelinessToken::new_held(self.clone(), token_id, keyexpr_string, options) instead of an inline observer.local_tokens.register + a direct struct literal - the register moved into the constructor (byte-identical effect). declare_token_aliased now ALSO calls new_held(self.clone(), token_id, resolved, options) - it previously constructed the handle WITHOUT registering, so this ADDS the missing registration of the RESOLVED literal (the bug fix). cache_token_declaration ordering unchanged (cache before register, both paths).

Round 311n.decision_summary: R311n measurement automation — scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh + lib/feature_implies.py compute wz-facade implies-graph from cargo metadata; honest SKIP on compile-fail lanes.
changes_bullets: scripts/lib/feature_implies.py NEW — wz facade → wz-runtime-tokio implies-graph resolver. Reads `cargo metadata --format-version=1 --no-deps` JSON from stdin, computes wz-runtime-tokio transitive closure + wz facade activation map + invert to PULLERS-by-codec, emits shell-sourceable `PULLERS_codec_X="..."` assignments for every `codec-*` rt feature. Standalone module instead of inline heredoc because `cargo metadata | python3 - <<EOF` is ambiguous in bash (heredoc + pipe both target stdin).

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh — each minus-<codec> lane excludes the codec + its full transitive puller set (declare-* / query-* / liveliness-* / domain-* / presets). Pre-R311n the exclusion was the codec name only; cargo resolver silently re-enabled the codec via `declare-subscriber = [codec-declare]` etc. and the lane measured a fake near-zero delta. The puller-aware exclusion makes the lane honest.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh — `measure()` gracefully SKIPs lanes whose binary fails to compile under the puller-aware exclusion. Writes `SKIP` to the size cache; the report prints `SKIP` instead of a numeric delta. Honest semantics for `this binary unconditionally references the consumer features and cannot be elided down to handshake-only`.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh — handshake-only lane added. Start from preset-ap-client; exclude every consumer feature; only `Init` / `Open` / `Close` + `KeepAlive` + transport / runtime plumbing remain. Skips for wz-ap-demo today; the lane shape is the contract a future minimal handshake binary would satisfy.

scripts/measure-codec-footprint.sh — threshold-based regression gate (`WZ_FOOTPRINT_THRESHOLD_BYTES` default 1024). Codec lanes below threshold fail the script. wz-codecs-only codecs (scout/hello/join/fragment) soft-skip; compile-fail SKIPs are excluded from the gate. Opt-out via `WZ_FOOTPRINT_NO_THRESHOLD=1`.

scripts/run-ci.sh — Layer F added. Opt-in via `--layer F` or `WZ_RUN_LAYER_F=1`. Runs `measure-codec-footprint.sh` as a catalog-truthfulness regression gate. Stays off the default dispatch path because the bench is expensive (~5-10 min cold; multiple wz-ap-demo release builds).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs liveliness_get (Session-review Finding 1, the real defect): bind `let actions = self.actions()?` at the TOP of the method, BEFORE the `if !is_established()` gate, and reuse it for alloc_next_interest_id + cache_get_interest. On a multicast session, is_established() reads `false` (the R311nc is_established() -> unwrap_or(false) projection), so the establishment gate front-ran the transport check and returned LivelinessGetError::NotEstablished ("retry after the session re-establishes" - futile on multicast) instead of the honest RequiresUnicast the `actions()?` one line later would have produced. Reordering makes the transport projection win; the unicast path is byte-identical (actions() is always Ok there, then the same is_established gate runs).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs Session::new: read `actions.params.zid.clone()` from the constructor PARAMETER before moving `actions` into SessionTransport::Unicast, dropping the R311nc defensive `if let Ok(actions) = session.actions()` that re-projected a value this ctor builds as Unicast by construction. No behavior change; removes a known-Ok re-ask.

changes_bullets: session/transport.rs (REWRITTEN): sealed-trait typestate home. `sealed::Sealed` + `TransportState<R,T>` trait (associated `type Payload` + `fn send_network_message`). Unconditional `struct Unicast` / `struct Multicast` markers; `Sealed` impls cfg-gated per feature. Unicast payload = `Arc<SessionLinkActions<R,T>>`; Multicast payload = `MulticastPayload { #[cfg(codec-push)] tx }`. Deleted `SessionTransport<R,T>` enum + manual Clone.

session/mod.rs: `Session<R,T,Tp>` struct — `transport: <Tp as TransportState<R,T>>::Payload`; no `Tp` default (eagerly bound-checked at definition in multicast-only builds; aliases carry the default). Clone impl gated `where Tp::Payload: Clone`. `TokioSession = Session<_,_,Unicast>` + `TokioMulticastSession = Session<_,_,Multicast>` aliases. Three impl blocks: agnostic (`publish`, observer, clock, `declare_subscriber`, `send_network_message` forwarder), unicast-only (`new`, infallible `actions()`, `dispatch_iteration_event{,_with}`, `is_established`, `batch_*`, all alias/query/declare/liveliness surface), multicast-only (`new_multicast`, `dispatch_multicast_iteration_event`).

changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_reassembles_pico_fragment_tx.rs 재작성(공통 setup helper run_pico_put_against_wz_acceptor + 2 test): (d) `DriverLoopOutcome::Fragment` 카운트로 fragment chain을 직접 assert(>=2) — wz RX read는 negotiated batch로 안 bounded라 `negotiated_batch_mtu()==64`만으론 단일프레임도 수신 가능, 즉 fragment 발생을 증명 못 했음(리뷰 d). (e) 257B negative test 신규 `wz_acceptor_rejects_pico_put_over_payload_bound`: pico(payload bound 없음)가 257B fragment 송신 → wz reassemble → re-parse `TooManyElements` → deliveries==0; wz MsgPut 256 bound(msg_put.scxml:111 sce:max-size) vs pico 무제한 = parity divergence를 mechanically pin(리뷰 e). (c) payload 반복 "0123456789"*20 → 62-char alphabet × coprime stride 7(주기 62, 64 MTU와 서로소); z_put -v 가 C-string이라 sibling layer3_reassembly_tx 의 raw (i*13) 불가 → shell-safe alphanumeric(리뷰 c).

(b) 테스트 위치는 false-positive(wz-integration-tests가 binary-dep infra+Layer C0 scan+spawn helper home). (c)(d)(e) REAL→fix. (f) REAL→carry 정정.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_publisher_to_pico_multicast_zsub.rs (NEW): wz in-library 멀티캐스트 publisher(ephemeral TX-only `UdpDriver::from_socket` + `drive_multicast_session` + `multicast_put_literal`; mc_params version 0x09 / batch 2048 / sn-req-res 0x02 = vendored pico config 정확히 일치)가 JOIN beacon + framed Push를 실 UDP group(224.0.0.224:7457)에 송신 → 외부 `z_sub -m peer -l udp/...#iface=<default-route-dev>`가 admit + decode → stdout `>> [Subscriber] Received ('demo/mc/interop': '...')` byte-exact. 방향=wz->pico (pico->wz는 wz `bind_multicast_v4`가 SO_REUSEADDR 미설정이라 동일 host 동일 group port co-bind 시 EADDRINUSE; carry). JOIN admission은 transitive 증명: pico rx.c:373-396이 version/seq_num_res/req_id_res/batch_size 불일치 peer의 Frame을 admit 전 drop하므로 z_sub의 Received 발화 자체가 wz JOIN을 pico가 파싱·admit했다는 증거. JOIN-admission 윈도우 레이스는 100ms republish loop로 제거([[feedback-no-flaky-ever]]). default-route iface는 `ip route show default`로 런타임 발견(wz INADDR_ANY mcast egress가 고르는 그 iface) → 양 peer 동일 링크. stdbuf -oL로 z_sub stdout line-buffer.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_publisher_to_pico_multicast_zsub.rs: F6 개선 — `wz_mc_params()`의 magic number(version 0x09 / batch 2048 / seq_num+req_id res 0x02)를 명명 상수 PICO_PROTO_VERSION / PICO_SN_RESOLUTION / PICO_BATCH_MULTICAST_SIZE로 anchor(vendored pico 소스 file 인용). 핵심 NOTE: 이 값들은 pico CONFIG 값이지 wz PROTOCOL default가 아님 — wz PROTOCOL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=8192이면 pico가 reject하므로 wz 상수로 치환 금지. pico pin bump가 이 값을 바꾸면 명명 상수 사이트에서 명시적 edit으로 표면화(현재 bare literal은 silent admission-rejection으로만 표출). 행동 변화 없음(동일 값), 테스트 15/15 no-flaky 유지.

verification_bullets: load-bearing 주장 2개를 소스/실측으로 자가 확정(리뷰어 주장 독립 재검증): (J) pico `vendor/zenoh-pico/src/transport/multicast/rx.c:182-186` `_z_multicast_handle_frame`이 entry==NULL(미admit peer)이면 'Dropping _Z_FRAME from unknown peer'로 drop — entry는 src addr 조회로 호환 JOIN admit(rx.c:378-396) 시에만 생성. 따라서 z_sub의 Push 수신 = wz JOIN을 pico가 admit한 transitive 증명, 성립. (C) `cargo tree -e features -p wz-runtime-tokio` 실측: default workspace resolution에 transport-multicast/transport-fragmentation/reassembly 미포함(codec-*/transport-unicast/batching/keepalive/link-* 만). resolver=2가 wz-integration-tests dev-dep의 transport-multicast를 wz-runtime-tokio 자체 C1 빌드에서 격리 — Cargo.toml 주석+ledger 주장 정확 확정.

리뷰어 findings triage: F6(MED, magic number)=REAL→적용(이 라운드). F1(SSOT 하니스 중복)=FALSE POSITIVE(dev-dep cycle hazard가 test-support 추출 차단, [[feedback-test-support-dev-dep-cycle]]; 2-site YAGNI). F2(republish loop)=올바른 no-flaky 패턴(외부 receiver admission in-process 미관측). F5(방향 wz->pico)=정당 scope(SO_REUSEADDR 부재는 lib.rs:794-800에 이미 문서화된 프로덕션 경계; carry로 추적). F3/F4/F7=LOW/false-positive. HIGH 없음, hack/SSOT 위반/숨은-갭-우회 없음.

Round 311no.decision_summary: R311no: 멀티캐스트 pico->wz dial-in 완성(양방향 interop). wz bind_multicast_v4에 REUSEADDR/REUSEPORT 추가(socket2, pico parity)로 group port co-bind. 외부 pico z_pub JOIN을 wz admit(active_peers==1 직접단언)+Push byte-exact.
changes_bullets: scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh: TARGETS에 z_pub 추가(주기 publish CLI). pico->wz 멀티캐스트 publisher로 필요 — z_put one-shot은 JOIN-admission 윈도우를 레이스하므로 주기 publisher(z_pub -n)가 no-flaky 전제. 동일 스크립트가 7 binaries 빌드(z_sub 체크가 z_pub 커버).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio: socket2를 optional 프로덕션 dep로 승격(version 0.6, features=["all"]로 set_reuse_port 잠금해제, dep:socket2 게이트=scouting-active/transport-multicast). UdpDriver::bind_multicast_v4를 socket2 경유 재작성 — SO_REUSEADDR+SO_REUSEPORT를 bind 전 설정(Socket->std UdpSocket->tokio from_std; tokio는 pre-bind setsockopt 훅 없음). zenoh-pico parity(udp_multicast_posix.c:180/185 무조건 REUSE, INADDR_ANY:port bind line196). lib.rs 주석의 'single-receiver, socket2 회피' 결정을 multi-listener pico-interop 요구로 supersede — 그 주석이 명시적으로 예고한 socket2 진입 지점.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_subscriber_from_pico_multicast.rs: 신규 e2e — 외부 pico z_pub -m peer 멀티캐스트 publisher의 JOIN beacon+framed Push를 wz in-library mcast subscriber가 group port co-bind + admit + byte-exact decode. dispatcher.active_peers()==1 직접 단언(R311nm transitive 증명과 대비 — wz가 in-process admitter). wz mc_params를 pico CONFIG(version 0x09/seq_num_res 0x02/batch 2048)에 핀해 ingest_join §3.2 admit. payload byte-exact는 pico [%4d]<value> 템플릿(z_pub.c) 재구성으로 full 단언(idx는 pico 내부 카운터라 비결정적).
scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer M(opt-in, env-dependent)에 4번째 sub-step(wz_subscriber_from_pico_multicast) 등록. 기존 z_sub 존재 체크가 z_pub도 graceful-SKIP 커버.
verification_bullets: Phase 0 falsify: z_pub 빌드(7 binaries) 후 pico z_pub -m peer -> pico z_sub -m peer 같은 host co-bind '>> Received' 5/5 — OS 멀티캐스트 라우팅 + REUSE co-bind 동작을 wz 프로덕션 변경 전 사전 확인. 멀티캐스트 listener는 양쪽 INADDR_ANY:port + REUSEADDR+REUSEPORT라 SO_REUSEPORT 필수(socket2 features=["all"]로 잠금해제).

Phase 1 회귀: REUSE 추가 후 기존 Layer M scouting_multicast_loopback 2/2 + multicast_pubsub_loopback 2/2 통과(단일 binder에 REUSE 무해). cargo check --features transport-multicast,scouting-active EXIT=0(socket2 path 컴파일).
Phase 2: 신규 pico->wz e2e 15/15 연속 no-flaky. Layer M 전체 4 sub-step EXIT=0. keyexpr matching + cross-impl JOIN admission(active_peers==1 직접) + Push byte-exact 실측 통과.

Phase 3: full host run-ci(WZ_RUN_LAYER_M=1) EXIT=0 'all required layers pass'(파이프 없는 exit code 직접 캡처; 컴파일 error[/panicked 0, 589 매치는 전부 '0 failed' 노이즈). atomic ledger entries 722->723, orphan delta=0(T1 new=+0 유지), T3 warn 4 불변. resolver=2가 socket2 dev-dep 누수를 C1 격리(default workspace 빌드 무영향).
carry_forward_bullets: R311no로 멀티캐스트 wz<->pico 양방향 interop 완성: wz->pico(R311nm) + pico->wz(R311no) 모두 실소켓 JOIN admit + Push byte-exact. wz가 admitter인 역방향은 active_peers()==1로 JOIN admission을 직접 관측(R311nm은 pico Frame-drop 정책으로 transitive 증명만 가능했음).

NEXT 후보: ① 멀티캐스트 큰메시지 >256B — wz MsgPut payload codec bound 256(msg_put.scxml:111) 확장 선결(별건; R311nl negative test가 unicast로 pin). ② breadth: serial 링크 / gossip scouting interop 실소켓. ③ 양방향 동시(wz+pico 동일 group 양쪽 publish)는 reachable하나 YAGNI.
설계 메모: socket2가 wz-runtime-tokio 프로덕션 dep로 진입(feature-gated). pico parity(멀티캐스트 group port=multi-listener, REUSE 무조건)가 근거 — 테스트 워크어라운드가 아니라 실 프로덕션 interop 갭 청산. lib.rs 주석이 예고한 진입 지점이었음.
UNPUSHED 누적: R311nm(b6572ca+e3c2e73) + R311nn(67c5ac3+5e79be9) + R311no(이 라운드) = origin/main(a95338c) 대비. push=사용자 명시 동의 대기.
