changes_bullets: F-1(CRITICAL/MAJOR, architect+root-cause 2-에이전트 독립 적발=최강 신호): D2 deregister "delta provably always empty" 주장 반증. 비균일 가중치(zenohd transport_weights를 wz가 ingest+적용)서 self-link drop이 cheaper detour 제거→노드 re-home→self가 remote root tree서 새 자식 획득→non-empty delta→re-advertise 누락. zenoh는 link-down delta를 pubsub_tree_change에 무조건 공급(mod.rs:140-149). 수정: linkstate_forward.rs deregister가 compute_trees delta를 capture해 re_advertise_subscriptions에 공급(inbound forward() 경로와 동일; 균일 가중치선 empty=no-op, re-home시만 발화). Reverses the earlier 'defer D2c as YAGNI' stance on the user textbook-over-cost ruling, after a direct zenoh read confirmed zenoh has no inline mode (the worker is the only, always-on recompute path); wz is a faithful port plus a delay-knob superset.

Tracked debt (honest): the wz tick is a periodic poll + dirty-check (a cheap local Cell read, a no-op when idle) rather than zenoh's park-on-recv. Forced by the architecture: forward() runs INSIDE the per-face drive future, so the loop's only regular re-entry point is the timer. A one-shot debounce (Notify-driven re-arm) would zero the idle polls but add cross-task signaling into the forwarder seam; judged KISS/YAGNI over the negligible 100ms no-op (the wire still carries zero periodic traffic). Revisit only if idle-poll cost is ever measured to matter.

Round 311si.decision_summary: R311si: c3c-3 B1a data-plane keyexpr alias resolution. The linkstate-peer forwarder now resolves an aliased (id!=0) Push keyexpr via a per-face link-local alias table populated from sourced Declare(DeclKexpr), and NORMALIZES the forwarded keyexpr to a literal so a downstream link (no shared alias table) can resolve it. Ports the established routing-routes HAT pattern (resolve_wireexpr SSOT + peer_keyexpr_table + absorb_declare) into the linkstate HAT; 0 new codec types. Interop value: external zenoh/pico peers that alias keyexprs (wz itself originates literals). Control-plane (DeclareSubscriber alias, B1b) deferred.
changes_bullets: session-core push_build.rs: extract literal_wireexpr (the SSOT literal-Wireexpr constructor; build_push_literal now delegates to it) + add set_push_keyexpr_literal (sets a Push's keyexpr to a literal AND the header N/0x20 suffix-present bit a literal keyexpr requires -- a pure-aliased inbound Push has N clear, so re-expressing only the keyexpr without the header desyncs the wire and the peer decoder reads an offset-shifted MsgPut header).

linkstate_forward.rs: FaceState gains keyexpr_table: hashbrown::HashMap<u64,String> -- a per-face, LINK-LOCAL keyexpr-alias table (hashbrown to match resolve_wireexpr's table type). register() inits it empty.

absorb_keyexpr_declaration(face, declare): a sourced Declare(DeclKexpr) resolves the declared base via resolve_wireexpr then inserts id->literal into the INBOUND face's table; an UndeclKexpr removes it. Mirrors the routing-routes HAT's absorb_declare (pubsub.rs:917-932). NOT re-flooded onward -- keyexpr aliasing is a per-transport negotiation in zenoh (hop-by-hop, never across the mesh).

forward() Declare dispatch: a DeclKexpr/UndeclKexpr arm (before the subscriber arms) routes to absorb_keyexpr_declaration instead of mis-handling it as a subscription via the _ => forward_subscription fallthrough.

forward_push: resolves push.keyexpr against the inbound face's alias table (resolve_wireexpr) inside the existing scoped faces borrow -- id==0 is the suffix verbatim, id!=0 is table[id]+suffix, an unresolvable alias drops the Push (same drop a missing literal got). The outbound carrier is NORMALIZED to a literal (set_push_keyexpr_literal) so a downstream child (no shared alias table) can resolve it. Removed the now-dead literal-only push_keyexpr helper.

Tests: forwarded_keyexpr helper (decodes the forwarded Push's keyexpr, None if still aliased) + 3 B1a units: an aliased Push resolves via the face table and forwards a LITERAL (proving normalize on the wire); an undeclared (UndeclKexpr'd) alias no longer resolves so the Push drops; an unknown alias Push is dropped.

Ports the established routing-routes HAT alias machinery (resolve_wireexpr SSOT + peer_keyexpr_table + absorb_declare) into the linkstate-peer HAT, which previously had no alias table and dropped any id!=0 keyexpr (literal-only). New codec types: 0 (build_declare_kexpr / build_undeclare_kexpr / build_push_aliased already existed).
verification_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio (routing-peer) lib 353 PASS (+3 B1a; linkstate_forward module 57). clippy(runtime-tokio --tests, routing-peer) clean + clippy(session-core --tests, codec-push/codec-declare/alloc) clean. fmt --check clean (both crates).

Root cause caught + fixed: the first run failed an_aliased_push_resolves... because build_push_aliased(7, None, ..) leaves the header N bit (0x20, suffix-present) CLEAR (pure-aliased, no suffix), and re-expressing only carrier.keyexpr to a suffix-bearing literal desynced the wire (the peer decoded an offset-shifted MsgPut header). Fixed by set_push_keyexpr_literal setting header |= 0x20 in lockstep, matching build_push_literal's invariant. Re-run: 57/57 green.

E6 e2e 6/6 (wz_peer_mesh 1 + wz_peer_data_forward 3: forward 2-hop / withdraw / 4-peer selectivity) -- NO regression, NO flake. The demo originates literal Pushes, so the normalize path is literal->literal (identity wire); B1a leaves the literal data path byte-unchanged.

changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph: remove_detached_nodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Zid> -- a DFS from self over each visited node's ADVERTISED links (node.links.keys(), not the petgraph edges: reachability is over what nodes claim to link to), removing every unvisited node. tree_children_of / next_hop now use graph.node_weight (not the panicking index op) so a child/hop pruned since the last compute_trees -- possible because the recompute is COALESCED onto a later tick (D2c) -- resolves to None and is skipped rather than panicking on a removed StableGraph index. Round 311sm.decision_summary: R311sm: c3c-3 D4 Details split. The linkstate re-flood (propagate) now honours zenoh's full-for-new / links-only-for-updated Details split (network.rs:645-678): a node seen for the first time with full state re-floods FULL (zid + links), an already-mapped re-advertiser re-floods LINKS-ONLY (no zid -- the receiver resolves the omitted zid from the psid it learned when the node was new). Changes splits into new/updated/removed; process_linkstates classifies by oldsn==0; make_link_state gains a links_only variant that clears the P flag and omits the zid (0 codec changes); build_linkstate_for becomes build_linkstate_split.
changes_bullets: make_link_state(idx, links_only): the wz LinkState codec already gates the zid on the P flag (linkstate.scxml options.P -> zid_len/zid present-if), so links_only=true clears P and omits zid_len/zid while keeping psid/sn/whatami/links/weights -- zenoh's Details{zid:false, links:true}. Mirrors zenoh make_link_state's per-Details field gating (network.rs:330-334). 0 codec changes (the wire shape was already representable).

Changes { new, updated, removed }: new = a node whose full state the receiver does not yet have, so the re-flood must carry its zid (a fresh insert, OR an existing node whose sn was still 0 = a placeholder = zenoh oldsn==0, network.rs:717); updated = an already-mapped re-advertiser (oldsn>0); removed = the D3 prune set. process_linkstates classifies each ingested entry into new/updated and retains BOTH minus the pruned zids.

build_linkstate_for(zids) -> build_linkstate_split(new, updated): builds new nodes FULL (make_link_state false) then updated nodes LINKS-ONLY (make_link_state true). New nodes are listed FIRST so a links-only entry that happens to reference a brand-new node still resolves within the single list. Mirrors zenoh make_msg over propagate_link_states' per-link out list (network.rs:645-678).

propagate (driver): per face (excluding the source face and the node whose own state it is), build_linkstate_split(new, updated) into ONE OAM so both halves arrive atomically -- zenoh network.rs:643-644 "send all states at once for each face to avoid premature node deletion on the other side". Early-returns when new and updated are both empty (overall and per face).

Correctness invariant: a face holds full state for every node either from its JOIN BOOTSTRAP (register -> flood_self floods the WHOLE graph FULL via build_linkstate_list, not just self) or from when the node was new (propagated full), so a later links-only update always resolves against a prior psid->zid mapping (convert_to_local_link_states' zid:None branch). Honest: locators still deferred; propagate keeps wz's tighter source-face exclusion for new nodes too (zenoh echoes new to the source and relies on sn-drop -- wz omits the redundant echo).

Tests: graph +2 (build_linkstate_split_full_carries_the_zid_links_only_omits_it = P flag + zid presence per variant; a_links_only_reflood_resolves_against_the_prior_full_mapping = B ingests A full then A links-only, resolving the zid-less entry + applying the newer sn) + 1 assertion fixed (a fresh node lands in `new` not `updated`); driver +1 (propagate_re_floods_new_full_and_updated_links_only decodes the frame to a non-involved face C and asserts new=full/updated=links-only, not swapped) + propagated_link_states OAM-decode helper.

Round 311sn.decision_summary: R311sn: c3c-3 B2 wildcard keyexpr intersection. LinkstatepeerSubs lookups (interested / interested_remote) now match a published key against every registered subscription keyexpr by keyexpr INTERSECTION (keyexpr_intersect_patterns -- the SSOT the local SubscriberRegistry already uses, zenoh's Resource::get_matches route matching) instead of exact string equality, so a demo/** or demo/* subscription attracts a concrete demo/data Push. An EXTENSION of the flat by_key map's read path (a private matching_peers scan), NOT the resource-tree rewrite the roadmap feared; the prefix-tree fold for sublinear matching stays a tracked performance deferral. Contained in the lookup -- register/flood/data-route/codec unchanged.
changes_bullets: linkstate_subs.rs: new private matching_peers(target, exclude) -- splits the target (published key) and each registered subscription keyexpr on '/' and tests keyexpr INTERSECTION via keyexpr_intersect_patterns (the same SSOT + chunk-split idiom as declare.rs:110-113), deduping peers across all matching keys. interested(keyexpr) = matching_peers(keyexpr, None); interested_remote(keyexpr, self_zid) = matching_peers(keyexpr, Some(self_zid)). So a demo/** or demo/* subscription now attracts a concrete demo/data Push, while a literal subscription stays byte-exact (intersection of two literals = equality).

register / withdraw / remove_peer / subscriptions UNCHANGED: the keyexpr stored is the pattern as-declared; only the read-path lookup widened from exact get to intersection scan. The data route (forward_push / publish -> interested_remote -> directions_toward) and the control plane (forward_subscription register, re_advertise_subscriptions) are also UNCHANGED -- B2 is contained entirely in the lookup, so a wildcard subscription flows through register/flood as a literal pattern string and is matched at read time. 0 forwarder changes, 0 codec changes.

SCOPE: an EXTENSION of the existing flat by_key: HashMap<String, HashSet<Zid>> read path -- NOT the resource-tree rewrite the roadmap feared. The wildcard MATCHING is the feature (delivered here); zenoh additionally folds subscriptions into a prefix RESOURCE TREE for sublinear matching, which stays a tracked PERFORMANCE deferral (the O(subscriptions) scan is correct but linear; the tree is only needed for large subscription sets, not modelled).

Module + field docs rewritten: the exact-match MVP note is replaced with the intersection-matching contract (keyexpr_intersect_patterns SSOT, zenoh Resource::get_matches), the resource-tree fold named as the honest remaining deferral (performance, not correctness).

Round 311so.decision_summary: R311so: c3c-3 E2 drop observability. The linkstate ingest's silent drops -- an unresolvable psid/link/zid, an invalid whatami, a list from an unknown or no-link face, a build-time edge to an un-indexed node -- are now surfaced through the log facade (wz's logging SSOT; zenoh tracing::error!s the same sites). error! for an unresolvable reference (protocol inconsistency), warn! for a host-validation drop of malformed input, debug! for a GC prune and a no-link-face drop. wz-routing-graph gains a log dep (AP-only, never reaches the MCU); wz-runtime-tokio already had it.
changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph Cargo.toml: + log = "0.4" (the facade; AP-only since this crate is routing-peer-pulled, so it never reaches the MCU footprint). convert_to_local_link_states now logs the 3 zenoh error! drop sites -- unknown link (network.rs:470), unresolvable node psid / no zid mapping (:507), unresolvable link psid (:538) -- plus 2 wz host-validation warn! drops (oversized zid, invalid whatami; wz carries the raw byte where zenoh rejects at decode, so wz owns the validation drop). make_link_state error!s a link dest not in the graph (an internal inconsistency -- an edge to an un-indexable vertex; zenoh :317). remove_detached_nodes debug!s each pruned node (zenoh :1008 GC event).

wz-runtime-tokio linkstate_forward.rs (already had log): ingest_inbound_linkstate debug!s a linkstate dropped from a face with no graph link (held without a routing zid at the handshake). resolve_source's nid arm was restructured from a silent `?` to a debug! + drop when the source psid is unmapped on the inbound link, so a data/control message that fails to forward is diagnosable.

Translation: zenoh logs via tracing; wz's established logging facade is `log` (wz-runtime-tokio + the wz-ap-demo runner already use log::*), so the faithful port is tracing::error! -> log::error!, preserving zenoh's level where it corresponds (error! for an unresolvable reference) and choosing warn! for the wz-specific host-validation drops and debug! for GC / no-link-face events.

Module doc: the prior "observability for dropped entries ... wz drops silently -- no tracing dep yet" deferral note is replaced with the log-facade observability contract (error! = unresolvable reference / protocol inconsistency, warn! = malformed-input validation drop, debug! = GC prune; a no-op without a backend).

changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph: `pub type Zid = Vec<u8>` becomes a Copy `struct Zid { bytes: [u8;16], len: u8 }` (the zenoh ZenohIdProto fixed-buffer-plus-size mirror) with from_slice (truncate to 16 + canonical zero-pad), as_slice (the trimmed wire bytes), len/is_empty, le16 (the 16-byte buffer the edge-jitter hashes), MAX_SIZE, a hex Debug, and From<&[u8]> / From<Vec<u8>>. zid_to_le_16 is now a one-line wrapper over le16 so the update_edge hash sites read unchanged.

The derived Ord/Eq/Hash are correct BECAUSE of the canonical invariant (bytes[len..]==0): a shorter zid that is a zero-extended prefix of a longer one compares equal on bytes then orders BEFORE it on len -- exactly as Vec<u8> orders a prefix before its extension (proved case-by-case: a differing real byte decides identically; an all-zero tail falls through to the len tie-break). So the deterministic cross-implementation edge-jitter tie-break with a zenohd peer (update_edge orders the pair by Ord, then hashes le16) is byte-for-byte unchanged by the representation switch.

Round 311sq.decision_summary: R311sq: 4-agent adversarial session review of sl..sp (D3/D4/B2/E2/E1) + remediation. The review found the self-assessment OVERCONFIDENT: a real correctness transient (tree-index reuse aliasing -- StableUnGraph reuses freed indices and D2c defers the recompute, so a stale tree entry could alias a reused index and misforward), a load-bearing untested claim (the Zid Ord == Vec<u8> cross-impl jitter tie-break), a convergent faithfulness gap (reintroduced placeholders not re-flooded), and convergent SSOT smells. All remediated: remove_detached_nodes scrubs freed indices from the cached trees; the Zid Ord equivalence is now tested; placeholders re-flood via changes.new; vestigial zid_to_le_16 deleted; purge_detached_interest + into_list extracted; matching_peers HashSet dedup; the demo drops a needless zid clone; + the D4 unmapped-psid drop test and doc-honesty fixes.
changes_bullets: F1 (CORRECTNESS, root-cause MAJOR): remove_detached_nodes now scrubs every freed NodeIndex from the cached spanning trees + distances (new scrub_trees). StableUnGraph REUSES a freed index on the next add_node, and the recompute is COALESCED (D2c), so a stale `trees` entry holding a freed index would, after a reuse, resolve via node_weight to a DIFFERENT live node and MISFORWARD a Push during the window (the node_weight guard only catches a still-absent index, not a reused one). Scrubbing keeps the invariant "the trees never reference a freed index": affected routes resolve to None (drop) until the tick rebuild, never an aliased misroute. +unit a_reused_node_index_does_not_alias_a_stale_tree_entry (prune frees C's idx, D reuses it, next_hop(self,D) must be None not C's old hop A).

F2 (CRITICAL coverage, quality): the load-bearing Zid Ord == Vec<u8> equivalence (the cross-impl jitter tie-break) was prose-only. +unit zid_ord_matches_vec_u8_ord_including_zero_extended_prefixes (a full table incl [1]/[1,0]/[1,5] prefix cases) + zid_eq_hash_truncation_and_from_are_canonical (HashSet dedup, >16 truncation, From<&[u8]>/From<Vec<u8>>).

F3 (faithfulness, architect+root-cause convergent): rebuild_edges now returns the placeholders it introduced; process_linkstates pushes them into changes.new (deduped) so a reintroduced node re-floods onward (zenoh new_nodes.push, network.rs:763) -- the prune retain drops it if it is itself unreachable. +unit a_reintroduced_placeholder_re_floods_as_new.
F4 (SSOT, architect+refactoring convergent): deleted the vestigial zid_to_le_16 free fn (body was `zid.le16()`); the 6 update_edge / test hash sites call .le16() directly.
F5 (SSOT, refactoring): the byte-identical "purge each removed node's interest" loop at the two prune sites (deregister + the ingest OAM arm) is extracted to one purge_detached_interest(&[Zid]).

F6 (SSOT, refactoring): build_linkstate_list / build_linkstate_split shared their LinkStateList assembly tail (triplicated num_link_states=len); a free `into_list(Vec<LinkstateOwned>)` derives the count once.

F7 (smell/perf, refactoring): matching_peers dedup was O(matches^2) via out.contains on the DATA path (interested_remote per Push); now a HashSet<Zid> accumulator (Zid is Copy+Hash). Doc names the per-message keyexpr-intersection cost.
F8 (smell, refactoring): the demo dropped an unnecessary params.zid.clone() -- LinkstateForwarder::new takes impl Into<Zid>, so it now passes &params.zid[..] (From<&[u8]>, no Vec clone).

Coverage + honesty: +unit a_links_only_entry_for_an_unmapped_psid_is_dropped (the D4 unsafe boundary -- a zid-less entry for an unmapped psid MUST drop; also path-covers the E2 unresolvable-psid log); edge_pruned test now asserts A/B SURVIVE (edge_count==0 is the edge prune, not a node prune -- it could have passed for the wrong reason). Doc honesty: the Zid Ord docstring now states the equivalence is vs the OLD Vec<u8> and that the vs-ZENOH property holds only for canonical wire zids (zenoh trims trailing zeros, so the prefix corner is unreachable); flood_self doc admits the D4 Details split is applied to propagate ONLY -- the self-event flood still sends FULL topology (a tracked follow-on); propagate doc labels the whole-source-face skip a deliberate divergence from zenoh's finer new-to-source rule.
verification_bullets: wz-routing-graph 38 PASS (+5: a_reused_node_index_does_not_alias (F1), zid_ord_matches_vec_u8 + zid_eq_hash_truncation_and_from (F2), a_reintroduced_placeholder_re_floods (F3), a_links_only_entry_for_an_unmapped_psid_is_dropped (D4 boundary)). wz-runtime-tokio (routing-peer) lib 360 PASS (the F5 purge extract + F7 HashSet dedup + the doc edits regress nothing). clippy(both --tests) clean. fmt --check clean (graph + runtime-tokio + ap-demo). default (non-routing-peer) wz-ap-demo + wz-runtime-tokio build clean.

E6 e2e 5/5 across 3 runs, NO flake (wz_peer_mesh 1 + wz_peer_data_forward 4: forward 2-hop / wildcard 2-hop / withdraw / 4-peer selectivity). The F1 tree scrub + F3 placeholder re-flood are behaviour changes on the prune / propagate paths, so the real-TCP multi-hop convergence + selectivity are the meaningful gate: they hold.

Round 311sq.publishable_decision_summary: R311sq: 4-agent adversarial session review of sl..sp (D3/D4/B2/E2/E1) + remediation. The review found the self-assessment OVERCONFIDENT: a real correctness transient (tree-index reuse aliasing -- StableUnGraph reuses freed indices and D2c defers the recompute, so a stale tree entry could alias a reused index and misforward), a load-bearing untested claim (the Zid Ord == Vec<u8> cross-impl jitter tie-break), a convergent faithfulness gap (reintroduced placeholders not re-flooded), and convergent SSOT smells. All remediated: remove_detached_nodes scrubs freed indices from the cached trees; the Zid Ord equivalence is now tested; placeholders re-flood via changes.new; vestigial zid_to_le_16 deleted; purge_detached_interest + into_list extracted; matching_peers HashSet dedup; the demo drops a needless zid clone; + the D4 unmapped-psid drop test and doc-honesty fixes.
publishable_changes_bullets: F1 (CORRECTNESS, root-cause MAJOR): remove_detached_nodes now scrubs every freed NodeIndex from the cached spanning trees + distances (new scrub_trees). StableUnGraph REUSES a freed index on the next add_node, and the recompute is COALESCED (D2c), so a stale `trees` entry holding a freed index would, after a reuse, resolve via node_weight to a DIFFERENT live node and MISFORWARD a Push during the window (the node_weight guard only catches a still-absent index, not a reused one). Scrubbing keeps the invariant "the trees never reference a freed index": affected routes resolve to None (drop) until the tick rebuild, never an aliased misroute. +unit a_reused_node_index_does_not_alias_a_stale_tree_entry (prune frees C's idx, D reuses it, next_hop(self,D) must be None not C's old hop A).

F2 (CRITICAL coverage, quality): the load-bearing Zid Ord == Vec<u8> equivalence (the cross-impl jitter tie-break) was prose-only. +unit zid_ord_matches_vec_u8_ord_including_zero_extended_prefixes (a full table incl [1]/[1,0]/[1,5] prefix cases) + zid_eq_hash_truncation_and_from_are_canonical (HashSet dedup, >16 truncation, From<&[u8]>/From<Vec<u8>>).

F3 (faithfulness, architect+root-cause convergent): rebuild_edges now returns the placeholders it introduced; process_linkstates pushes them into changes.new (deduped) so a reintroduced node re-floods onward (zenoh new_nodes.push, network.rs:763) -- the prune retain drops it if it is itself unreachable. +unit a_reintroduced_placeholder_re_floods_as_new.
F4 (SSOT, architect+refactoring convergent): deleted the vestigial zid_to_le_16 free fn (body was `zid.le16()`); the 6 update_edge / test hash sites call .le16() directly.
F5 (SSOT, refactoring): the byte-identical "purge each removed node's interest" loop at the two prune sites (deregister + the ingest OAM arm) is extracted to one purge_detached_interest(&[Zid]).

F6 (SSOT, refactoring): build_linkstate_list / build_linkstate_split shared their LinkStateList assembly tail (triplicated num_link_states=len); a free `into_list(Vec<LinkstateOwned>)` derives the count once.

F7 (smell/perf, refactoring): matching_peers dedup was O(matches^2) via out.contains on the DATA path (interested_remote per Push); now a HashSet<Zid> accumulator (Zid is Copy+Hash). Doc names the per-message keyexpr-intersection cost.
F8 (smell, refactoring): the demo dropped an unnecessary params.zid.clone() -- LinkstateForwarder::new takes impl Into<Zid>, so it now passes &params.zid[..] (From<&[u8]>, no Vec clone).

Coverage + honesty: +unit a_links_only_entry_for_an_unmapped_psid_is_dropped (the D4 unsafe boundary -- a zid-less entry for an unmapped psid MUST drop; also path-covers the E2 unresolvable-psid log); edge_pruned test now asserts A/B SURVIVE (edge_count==0 is the edge prune, not a node prune -- it could have passed for the wrong reason). Doc honesty: the Zid Ord docstring now states the equivalence is vs the OLD Vec<u8> and that the vs-ZENOH property holds only for canonical wire zids (zenoh trims trailing zeros, so the prefix corner is unreachable); flood_self doc admits the D4 Details split is applied to propagate ONLY -- the self-event flood still sends FULL topology (a tracked follow-on); propagate doc labels the whole-source-face skip a deliberate divergence from zenoh's finer new-to-source rule.

Round 311ss.decision_summary: R311ss: c3c-3 D4 self-flood delta -- the SELF-event topology floods now send zenoh's minimal delta, not the full topology. register: FULL to the NEW face + a 2-entry [neighbour zid-only, self links-only] delta to existing faces (1-entry self links-only if the neighbour was known); deregister: 1-entry self links-only to all. make_link_state generalized from a links_only bool to the zenoh Details{zid,links} model (adds the zid-only combo). Closes the self-event half of D4 (the propagate half was sm).
changes_bullets: Graph: make_link_state(idx, links_only: bool) generalized to make_link_state(idx, Details{zid,links}) -- the wz mirror of zenoh `Details` (network.rs:49, 304-348), gating the links iteration on details.links (empty list when false, like zenoh) and the zid field + P flag on details.zid. The prior two combos are unchanged (full = {zid:true,links:true}; links-only = {zid:false,links:true}); the new {zid:true,links:false} ZID-ONLY combo is the one shape the bool could not express. build_linkstate_list / build_linkstate_split rewritten over Details (behaviour identical, the split tests still pass).

Graph: new pub build_link_added_delta(neighbour) -> the 2-entry delta zenoh add_link sends to existing links (network.rs:873-890): [neighbour ZID-ONLY, self LINKS-ONLY]. The neighbour is listed first so self's links-only entry (which references it by psid) resolves within the one list. The remove_link / add_link-to-a-known-peer 1-entry [self links-only] delta REUSES the existing build_linkstate_split(&[], &[self_zid]) -- no new builder for it.

Round 311st.decision_summary: R311st: c3c-3 tracked (b) -- migrate the driver's peer-zid plumbing from Option<&[u8]>/&[u8] to the routing Option<Zid>/Zid. The session-layer peer_zid (Vec<u8>) is converted to Zid ONCE at the fan_out read boundary (and the 3 forward read sites), so resolve_source / is_tree_forward_target / is_child / the propagate keep all work in Zid terms (Copy, Eq) instead of re-deriving from raw bytes. Pure behavior-preserving refactor enabled by the sr Zid type; cleans the peer-zid seam F builds on.
changes_bullets: fan_out: the per-face builder callback is now FnMut(FaceId, Option<Zid>) (was Option<&[u8]>); fan_out converts state.actions.peer_zid() (Vec<u8>) -> Option<Zid> via Zid::from_slice at the SINGLE read boundary, so each builder gets a Copy Zid instead of a borrowed byte slice it must re-derive from.

resolve_source(inbound_zid: Option<Zid>, ..) (was Option<&[u8]>): node_id 0 returns inbound_zid? directly (no per-call Zid::from_slice). The 3 forward read sites (forward_push / forward_subscription declare + undeclare) convert peer_zid() -> Option<Zid> at the destructure and pass it (Copy) to BOTH resolve_source and is_tree_forward_target -- the inbound_zid.as_deref() calls are gone.

is_tree_forward_target(zid: Option<Zid>, inbound_zid: Option<Zid>, ..) and is_child(children: &[Zid], zid: Zid) -> children.contains(&zid) (was &[u8] + iter().any(|c| c.as_slice() == zid)). The propagate `keep` closure compares Option<Zid> directly (zid != Some(**z)) instead of via as_slice. is_child is by-value (Zid is Copy), so its three call sites (is_tree_forward_target + the two flood closures) need no textual change.

The session boundary is UNCHANGED: SessionLinkActions::peer_zid() still returns Option<Vec<u8>> (session-core is no_std and routing-agnostic; Zid lives in wz-routing-graph, so the Vec<u8> -> Zid conversion stays in the driver, the correct layer). The only bytes->Zid conversions left are the trusted-handshake boundary reads (fan_out + the 3 forward destructures + register), each via the infallible from_slice; an UNTRUSTED wire zid still validates via try_from at the ingest (sr).

Net effect: the data + control forward paths (source resolution + tree-child selection + re-flood exclusion) work in the routing Zid type end to end -- no more scattered Zid::from_slice / as_slice / as_deref on those paths -- the seam the F discovery subsystem builds on is now Zid-typed. Enabled by sr's Zid (Copy / Eq / Hash / AsRef).

changes_bullets: keyexpr_match: new pub keyexpr_intersects_target(candidate: &str, target_chunks: &[&str]) -> bool -- splits the candidate into the bounded chunk buffer (BoundedVec<_, MAX_KEYEXPR_CHUNKS>, exactly as keyexpr_pattern_matches splits its target: the MCU no-alloc backing is bounded, the AP alloc backing GROWS past it -> AP matching is unbounded and behaviour-identical to the prior Vec split) and consults keyexpr_intersect_patterns. This is the per-candidate membership test every keyexpr SCAN shares.

declare.rs declared_intersects (the SHARED consult behind subscriber + queryable has_matching AND the matching-watch re-evaluation): now splits the published target ONCE into a Vec, then declared.values().any(|c| keyexpr_intersects_target(c, &target_chunks)) -- replacing the inline per-candidate split + keyexpr_intersect_patterns. So BOTH local registries (sub + queryable) route through the shared helper.

linkstate_subs.rs matching_peers (the remote linkstate-peer interest scan, called per Push via interested / interested_remote): same shape -- split the target once, scan by_key calling keyexpr_intersects_target per registered subscription, collect + HashSet-dedup the matching peers. The import switches keyexpr_intersect_patterns -> keyexpr_intersects_target; the module + matching_peers docs now name the shared SSOT and that it is the single resource-tree seam.

Resource-tree NOT built (deliberate scope split): zenoh's prefix Resource tree (get_matches) for SUBLINEAR matching is a large HAT-coupled data structure, and a realistic subscription set is small (an unmeasured perf concern -> measure-first / YAGNI). The value delivered here is the SSOT SEAM: a future tree is ONE reimplementation site (keyexpr_intersects_target, or both callers swapping their HashMap scan at that one seam) rather than two divergent scans. So (c)'s "with the resource-tree" is intentionally split -- the extraction lands now, the tree stays a tracked PERF deferral.

+2 keyexpr_match unit tests (intersects_target_literal; intersects_target_wildcard, gated on keyexpr-wildcard-double). No bound unit test: BoundedVec grows on the AP/alloc backing, so the bound is a profile-dependent MCU property already inherited from keyexpr_pattern_matches (which has no bound test either).

Round 311sw.decision_summary: R311sw: BUILD FIX for sr -- zid_hex (the router/peer face-log hex helper, cfg(any(routing-router, routing-peer))) imported the routing-peer-only linkstate_forward::Zid (sr's SSOT-via-Zid::Display), so the routing-ROUTER-only demo build (run-ci Layer E3/E5) failed with error[E0432] unresolved import (Zid is gated behind routing-peer). Reverted zid_hex to direct per-byte hex formatting -- byte-identical output, no coupling to the peer-only type. The per-atom demo gate built only routing-peer + default, never routing-router alone, so the break reached the pre-push full run-ci. Build errors are absolute priority.
changes_bullets: runner.rs zid_hex (the face-log hex helper, cfg(any(routing-router, routing-peer))): removed the `use wz::runtime_tokio::linkstate_forward::Zid` import + the Zid::Display delegation that sr added as an SSOT, and restored the direct per-byte `bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()` formatting. The bug: linkstate_forward (which re-exports Zid) is gated behind `routing-peer`, but zid_hex compiles under routing-router OR routing-peer -- so the routing-ROUTER-only demo build (run-ci Layer E3 / E5) could not resolve the import and failed to compile. zid_hex is a router/peer face-log display helper; it must not couple to the routing-peer-only Zid type. Output is byte-identical (the same wire-order lowercase hex Zid::Display produces), just formatted in place.

Gate gap that let it through: the sr per-atom demo gate built only `--features routing-peer` (where linkstate_forward exists) + default (where zid_hex is cfg'd out entirely), never routing-router ALONE -- so sr's break reached the pre-push full run-ci undetected.
verification_bullets: wz-ap-demo builds clean on ALL 4 routing feature axes now: routing-router (the axis that broke -- E3/E5), routing-routes, routing-peer (E6), and default. Previously only routing-peer + default were gated per-atom, which is exactly how sr's zid_hex break slipped past to the pre-push gate.

Root-cause provenance: the pre-push full run-ci reported Layer E3 FAIL + E5 FAIL, both `error[E0432]: unresolved import wz::runtime_tokio::linkstate_forward` at runner.rs:1108 (zid_hex), with the compiler note `the item is gated behind the routing-peer feature`. Deterministic build error, NOT a flake.

First-attempt mis-diagnosis (recorded for honesty): the FIRST push-reject ALSO failed E3/E5 (same build error) AND failed Q.2.mps2-an386 (mcu-qemu-demo, exit 124 / 10s QEMU timeout) due to a CONCURRENT `cargo test --workspace` on /home/coin/pinion (load 7.88); I over-focused on Q and missed the deterministic E3/E5. On the idle re-run Q passed (binary footprint was +0, confirming Q was pure contention), leaving E3/E5 as the real blocker fixed here.

The fix is demo-only (zid_hex formatting); the routing/keyexpr crates are unchanged, so the graph 45 / session-core 151 / routing-peer lib 361 / clippy / fmt / E6 gates from sv still hold. Full run-ci re-run via the pre-push gate.

Round 311tk.decision_summary: R311tk: gossip-policy A5a -- port the zenoh AutoConnect policy type (role WhatAmIMatcher + AutoConnectStrategy zid tie-break) to wz-routing-graph; the vocabulary the discovery->dial seam consumes next.
changes_bullets: wz-routing-graph: new module autoconnect.rs -- AutoConnect { zid, matcher, strategy } + AutoConnectStrategy { Always(default), GreaterZid }. Ported from zenoh net/common.rs AutoConnect.
should_autoconnect(to, what) = matcher.matches(what) && (Always => true | GreaterZid => self.zid > to). The GreaterZid arm is the double-dial avoidance: only the greater-zid end of a pair dials.
Placement mirrors zenoh: type in the graph crate (lowest crate with both Zid + WhatAmIMatcher = zenoh's net/common.rs leaf); the driver holds the instance in A5c (= zenoh Gossip.autoconnect).
Flattens zenoh ModeDependent<TargetDependent<..>> config to one matcher + one strategy (the gossip_target/A4a simplification); semantics identical for the single-strategy default deploy.
pub re-export from lib.rs; the graph deferred-note refreshed (autoconnect POLICY now exists, the dial wiring is the next atom). No driver field yet, so no dead field until A5c consumes it.
verification_bullets: wz-routing-graph 56 tests (the +5 autoconnect: disabled never dials, Always ignores zid, matcher gate excludes client, GreaterZid dials only the strictly-greater end, a GreaterZid pair has exactly one dialer).
clippy -D warnings clean (graph + downstream wz-runtime-tokio --features routing-peer); fmt clean. Pure Copy type, no MCU dep (the graph crate is absent from the MCU footprint).
Grounding (read): zenoh net/common.rs should_autoconnect = matcher.matches && (Always|GreaterZid self.zid>to); AutoConnectStrategy default Always, peer gossip.autoconnect default router|peer.
carry_forward_bullets: R311tk = gossip-policy A5a: the AutoConnect policy type (role matcher + GreaterZid zid tie-break) lands in wz-routing-graph. The vocabulary only; no production consumer yet (tested in isolation).
NEXT A5b: a forwarder->accept-loop dial-intent channel -- the discovery seam (sync forwarder ingest) must hand a dial future to the async accept_loop FuturesUnordered.
THEN A5c: dial+open+register wiring -- the driver holds an AutoConnect field (zenoh Gossip.autoconnect), calls should_autoconnect on a discovered (zid, whatami), dials via node_locators on pass.

changes_bullets: run-ci Layer E3/E5 caught the regression (RUNCI_EXIT=1, masked by a wrapper echo -- the 'judge by unpiped exit code' lesson): wz_router_holds_two_concurrent_peers + 2 wz_router_forward FAILED. Root cause: the establishment dedup was the WRONG LAYER -- in the shared face_drive_loop it applied to the pure acceptor/router (NoOpForwarder, no routing graph), which legitimately holds N faces. The two-faces-one-zid hazard is a ROUTING-GRAPH concern (add_link/remove_link key the self-edge on zid).

Reverted the Step::Opened zid-dedup; KEPT the held_zids->faces:BTreeMap single-source collapse (clean; the value is read by the dial-intent dedup) and the dial_decision dial-intent dedup (autoconnect-only, never touches the acceptor).

The two-faces-one-zid corruption re-tracks as a PRE-EXISTING graph-layer debt: make add_link/remove_link zid-aware (refcount links per zid, or remove the self-edge only when the last link to a zid drops) -- fixes it at the source without touching the transport-agnostic face loop.

changes_bullets: run-ci caught it AGAIN (RUNCI_EXIT=1, E6 wz_peer_mesh_withdraws_subscription_two_hops FAILED): the tr revert removed the establishment dedup, re-opening the corruption the mutual-`--connect` peer mesh hits (two faces to one neighbour zid -> remove_link prunes the live peer). The dedup was load-bearing for E6; the blanket version passed E6 but failed E3/E5 (router).

Fix = GATE the dedup, not revert it: new FaceForwarder::dedups_faces_by_zid() (default false). LinkstateForwarder (graph keys the self-edge on zid) returns true -> the loop drops a redundant second face to an already-held zid. RoutingForwarder/NoOpForwarder (FaceId-keyed) keep false -> hold N faces (the router's two same-fixture-zid clients).

This is the wz analog of zenoh's transport manager init_transport_unicast (one transport per zid) but scoped to the forwarders that key routing state on zid -- not blanket (broke the router) and not the graph layer (would diverge from zenoh's network.rs, which is sound only BECAUSE the layer above guarantees zid-uniqueness).
holds_zid/faces docs restored to note both uses (dial-intent dedup + the gated establishment dedup); the runner --autoconnect comment's establishment-dedup claim is true again for the peer mesh.

Full run-ci re-run before push.

Empirical proof the corruption is real + reachable in the COMMON peer mesh (not just an autoconnect race): E6 passes WITH the dedup, fails WITHOUT. Confirmed by direct read (lib.rs:803 remove_link by zid) + the adversarial review.

Process lesson re-confirmed (twice this push attempt): judge run-ci by the unpiped RUNCI_EXIT (a wrapper echo masked exit 1 both times); and a 'revert to unblock' can itself BE a regression -- the gated fix, not the revert, was right.

Round 311tv.decision_summary: R311tv: §5.16 access-control atom 3 — egress enforcement (the Mux twin of ingress). The forwarder runs the interceptor seam at BOTH the inbound forward() and outbound fan_out chokepoints, sharing one AclPolicy; egress closes the gap ingress cannot (a node's own originations cross only fan_out).
changes_bullets: Two interceptor chains now (ingress_interceptors + egress_interceptors), the wz analogue of zenoh's DeMux (ingress) / Mux (egress) split. set_acl_policy installs an AclInterceptor per flow — Ingress consulted at forward(), Egress at fan_out — sharing the SAME AclPolicy (the rule set is immutable; a rule's flow selects where it applies).

admit_outbound(state, msg): consulted in fan_out after the per-face message is built and before it is sent. A denied outbound is dropped for THAT face (not sent, not counted) and witnessed by acl_denied. The destination subject is the face's zid already resolved in the fan_out loop; the egress chain lives in a separate RefCell so it does not conflict with the held faces borrow.

IngressContext renamed FaceContext: it serves BOTH directions — the subject is the peer on the other end of the link whether the message is inbound (ingress) or outbound (egress), so one context type backs both admit_inbound and admit_outbound.

Why egress is not mere symmetry: it closes the gap ingress cannot. A node's OWN originations (a publish) cross only fan_out, never forward()/ingress — so without egress they were never ACL-checked. Egress also enforces per-destination "do not send keyexpr K to peer Z". An Oam (link-state / gossip) carries no governed action, so topology propagation is never blocked.
demo --acl-deny <keyexpr> now installs an ingress AND an egress deny rule (a rule per flow) for the keyexpr — blocking K completely in both directions through this node.
verification_bullets: routing-peer lib 383/383 incl an_egress_acl_deny_blocks_a_relay_but_not_reception (S allows ingress but denies egress on demo/**: a Put from A on demo/data is RECEIVED — data_seen++ — yet NOT relayed to the interested child B + acl_denied witness; the gap ingress cannot close). The atom-1/2 ingress tests (Put relay, DeclareSubscriber) still pass. wz-access-control 7/7 (unchanged — egress reuses the existing AclFlow::Egress + decision).

changes_bullets: Collapsed the three per-feature forwarder setters (set_acl_policy / set_downsampling / set_low_pass), each of which APPENDED to both interceptor chains, into ONE set_interceptors(config: InterceptorConfig) that REPLACES both chains — the wz mirror of zenoh's single interceptor_factories(config) funnel (net/routing/interceptor/mod.rs:122). InterceptorConfig { acl: Option<AclPolicy>, downsampling: Vec<DownsamplingRule>, low_pass: Vec<LowPassRule> } is the wz analogue of the config slices zenoh reads (config.downsampling()/access_control()/low_pass_filter()). Closes the R311tx-review footgun: re-calling a setter duplicated an interceptor, and the cross-setter order was unspecified.

build_chain(flow) assembles each flow's chain in zenoh's FIXED factory order — downsampling, then access-control, then low-pass (interceptor_factories mod.rs:133-136, minus the qos-overwrite wz does not implement) — so the order is deterministic regardless of which features a deploy enables, no longer dependent on setter call order. Per-flow instances preserved (each flow gets its own downsampling timer and an ACL enforcer bound to that flow), matching zenoh's separate per-flow enforcers. The demo (wz-ap-demo runner.rs) now assembles ONE InterceptorConfig from its --acl-deny/--downsample/--max-payload flags and installs it once; the 6 forwarder tests migrated to the single seam.

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (the recurring calibration discipline): a default-refute review of the diff. It UPHELD per-flow isolation, factory-order fidelity, the empty-config fast path, and footgun closure, but REFUTED the self-assessed "behavior-preserving" framing — and was correct (every claim re-verified by direct read of zenoh before acting).

CORRECTION from the review's CRITICAL finding: the collapse also re-aligned the interceptor ORDER. The old demo/test call order was ACL -> downsampling; the new fixed order is downsampling -> ACL (zenoh's). Because InterceptorChain::admit short-circuits (Iterator::all) and the downsampler records its rate timer only on the messages IT admits (downsampling.rs:92), the order is OBSERVABLE when an ACL selectively denies: in zenoh order the downsampler stamps a message the ACL then denies (consuming the rule's rate budget); in the old order an ACL-denied message short-circuited before the downsampler saw it. So this is behavior-ALIGNED-to-zenoh, not behavior-preserving — zenoh's downsampler likewise stamps a message its ACL later denies (zenoh downsampling.rs:242-244 updates the timestamp only on admit, and the factory runs downsampling before the ACL).

Added a test (downsampling_precedes_the_acl_and_accounts_a_denied_message) that LOCKS the new order: an allow-default ACL denying demo/secret + a demo/** 1s downsample rule; a denied demo/secret followed back-to-back by an allowed demo/data shows demo/data rate-limited (the denied demo/secret consumed the budget) — under the old ACL-first order demo/data would relay, so the test fails if the order regresses. Also fixed two stale doc comments still naming the removed set_acl_policy / set_downsampling.

Round 311tz.decision_summary: R311tz: §5.15/§5.16 query routing atom 1 — the QUERYABLE interest control plane (the query-plane twin of the subscriber one): generalized LinkstatepeerSubs into a reusable LinkstatepeerInterest (subs + qabls) and unified the declare-reflood + tree-change re-advertise into shared kind-parameterized seams, so DeclareQueryable now floods, registers, converges to late joiners, and purges on face-down; UndeclareQueryable + Request/Response routing + Query ACL are honestly deferred; a 3-agent adversarial review's 'codec lacks ext_keyexpr -> FALSE' CRITICAL was itself refuted by direct read (it read an SCE forge fixture, not the wz-codecs type).
changes_bullets: Generalized `LinkstatepeerSubs` -> `LinkstatepeerInterest` (renamed linkstate_subs.rs -> linkstate_interest.rs; `subscriptions()` -> `entries()`): ONE generic keyexpr->peer-set interest table, the forwarder now holds TWO instances — `subs` (DeclareSubscriber interest) and `qabls` (DeclareQueryable interest) — the wz mirror of zenoh's per-Resource linkstatepeer_subs + linkstatepeer_qabls (hat/linkstate_peer/mod.rs:515,517), both the same peer-keyed shape. Avoids a 145-line clone (the SSOT call the sb-review precedent demands).

Unified the proven subscriber declare re-flood + tree-change re-advertise into shared kind-parameterized seams: forward_interest_declaration(.., table, build) backs forward_subscription + the new forward_queryable, and re_advertise_interest(.., table, build) backs re_advertise_subscriptions + the new re_advertise_queryables. Each plane is a thin wrapper supplying its body extractor + interest table + carrier builder; source-resolve + register-gate + tree-children + fan_out live once. forward_unsubscription stays standalone (a different retraction shape).

forward() dispatch: CodecZenohDeclQueryable -> forward_queryable (register the source peer's queryable interest in qabls, re-flood a clean sourced literal DeclareQueryable along the source's tree on a NEW registration — zenoh declare_linkstatepeer_queryable / propagate_sourced_queryable, queries.rs). recompute_and_advertise now also calls re_advertise_queryables so a queryable converges to a late-joining child (queries_tree_change, queries.rs:663-697). purge_detached_interest purges BOTH tables on face-down + ingest-detach (queries_remove_node).

UndeclareQueryable DEFERRED (a codec limit, not a routing one): the wz-codecs UndeclQueryable body the dispatch matches is { header, id } — no keyexpr ext (its subscriber twin UndeclSubscriber carries `extensions`, which is exactly why forward_unsubscription can read an ext_keyexpr and this cannot; zenoh's UndeclareQueryable has ext_wire_expr, declare.rs:520-523). A faithful queryable undeclare needs a wz-codecs SCHEMA extension first (a separate codec atom). Dropped via an EXPLICIT no-op arm (not the subscriber catch-all); face-down purge is the safety net.

3-AGENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (the recurring textbook?/SSOT?/north-star? trigger): architecture + honesty UPHELD (accurate zenoh citations, sound generalization, clean atom boundary). The correctness agent's CRITICAL ("the codec HAS ext_keyexpr, the deferral is FALSE") was REFUTED by direct read — it cited vendor/sce/tests/forge/expected/..., an SCE forge fixture, not the wz-codecs generated UndeclQueryable the forwarder dispatches on (declare.rs:48,158; undecl_queryable.rs:25-28 = header+id only). Lesson re-confirmed: agents can be confidently wrong; direct read is the arbiter.

Remediation from the valid findings: sharpened the deferral comment to cite the authoritative wz-codecs type (preventing the SCE-fixture confusion); added a "declarations only" note to forward_interest_declaration; added a no-op-arm regression test (an UndeclareQueryable on a live face is inert — it neither withdraws the queryable interest nor mis-routes to the subscriber table). interested_queryables kept pub, the observer twin of interested.

changes_bullets: New forward_request in the linkstate forwarder + a NetworkMessage::Request dispatch arm: relay a routed Query toward the matching QUERYABLES along the QUERIER's spanning tree — resolve the source (querier) from the Request routing-context node_id (read_request_source, atom 2a), read qabls.interested_remote for the keyexpr, route via directions_toward, re-stamp the source + B1-normalize the keyexpr to a literal (set_request_keyexpr_literal), fan out with the shared is_tree_forward_target predicate. The structural twin of forward_push, differing only in qabls-vs-subs, the Request carrier, no hop-limit, and the rid carried verbatim.

SCOPE = the FORWARD half only: the rid is carried VERBATIM and no pending-query state is allocated. The RETURN path (the pending-query table + per-hop qid remapping so a Response/ResponseFinal routes back to the querier) is atom 3 — until it lands, Response/ResponseFinal still hit the dispatch drop. No hop-limit: zenoh bounds a Query by the per-query timeout (atom 3), not a hop count, and a converged source tree is acyclic; the forward-only relay allocates no state, so a transient-recompute loop floods harmlessly until convergence (verified vs zenoh — the Request carries no TTL).

routing-peer feature += codec-request: a routing peer now relays Requests, so the Request wire surface + the request_routing_context seam are part of its contract (the query-plane twin of the codec-declare interest plane). Round 311uc.decision_summary: R311uc: query-routing atom 3 — the Reply RETURN path. A routed Query's Response/ResponseFinal route BACK to the querier via a new PendingQueries table with per-hop query-id remapping: forward_request allocates a per-outbound-face qid + records (out qid -> (inbound, rid)), forward_response peeks+rewrites+unicasts back, forward_response_final takes (frees)+routes back; deregister purges. Also wired the Response/ResponseFinal arms into send_network_message (they hit the FeatureDisabled catch — the bug blocking the reply send). 2-agent adversarial review: no critical (qid lifecycle correct vs zenoh) + caught a stray debug eprintln (removed). Per-query timeout + multi-hop e2e deferred (tracked).
changes_bullets: New crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_pending.rs: PendingQueries — the per-outbound-face `out qid -> (inbound face, inbound rid)` return table, the wz analogue of zenoh's per-FaceState pending_queries + next_qid (dispatcher/face.rs, queries.rs). allocate (per-face monotonic qid + record, zenoh insert_pending_query), peek (Response — entry survives, zenoh route_send_response uses get), take (ResponseFinal — frees, route_send_response_final removes), remove_face (face-down), len. Unit-tested (monotonic per-face, peek-non-consuming, take-prunes, selective remove_face).

forward_request RETROFIT (atom-2b verbatim-rid -> atom-3 remapped-qid): build the re-stamped TEMPLATE once, then PER outbound face allocate a fresh local qid + record (out qid -> (inbound, src_rid)) and stamp it as the carrier's rid. The per-face qid is why each child gets its own carrier (zenoh route_query's insert_pending_query per target). Remapping is required for correctness: two queriers' identical rids would collide on a shared relay face without a per-face-unique local qid.

forward_response: resolve the reply keyexpr against the inbound (forward-out) face's table, peek the return mapping for (inbound, response.request_id), rewrite request_id back to the recorded upstream rid, B1-normalize the keyexpr (new set_response_keyexpr_literal, N bit 0x20 = zenoh response::flag::N), and unicast to the recorded inbound face (a back-hop via fan_out single-face, NOT a tree fan-out — the pending table IS the return route). forward_response_final: TAKE (free) + rewrite + route back (no keyexpr). Dispatch arms for Response + ResponseFinal; deregister purges a departed face's pending entries.

send_network_message (session_actions.rs) Response/ResponseFinal arms: these hit the `_ => Err(FeatureDisabled)` catch, so fan_out's send returned Err and NO reply routed — the bug the e2e test surfaced. Added arms routing to the PRE-EXISTING (previously orphaned) dispatch_response / dispatch_response_final; widened the fn-gate any(...) + the routing-peer feature with codec-response + codec-response-final (the reply twin of the codec-request forward). AP-only — no MCU footprint.

2-AGENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (correctness + architecture): NO CRITICAL. The qid lifecycle (per-face uniqueness, peek-vs-take, the remap key = the inbound face), borrow safety (pending vs faces distinct RefCells), the send-seam, the keyexpr N bit, and the face-down purge + orphaned-src-face self-heal were all verified correct vs zenoh by direct read. The architecture agent CAUGHT a stray debug eprintln left in forward_response's error path (removed) and flagged the multi-hop / multi-queryable e2e tests as deferred (integration-test layer).

Round 311ud.decision_summary: R311ud: query-routing atom 4 — the §5.16 Query/DeclareQueryable/Reply ACL (the north-star the whole query-routing track was the prerequisite for). Extended the mesh ACL action set to the query plane: AclMessage += Query/DeclareQueryable/Reply, acl_action maps Request-by-body + Response->Reply + Declare(DeclQueryable)->DeclareQueryable, FaceContext::full_keyexpr resolves the query-plane keyexprs; the decision logic is already action-generic. Both ingress (drops a denied Query/DeclareQueryable before routing) and egress (drops a denied Reply on relay-back) gate via the existing seams. Focused adversarial review: correctness/fidelity HIGH; added an egress Reply enforcement test per its gap finding.
changes_bullets: wz-access-control AclMessage += Query (a routed Request's Query body), DeclareQueryable (the query-plane twin of DeclareSubscriber), Reply (a Response) — the zenoh authorization.rs query-plane action set (minus the deferred liveliness actions). The AclPolicy::decision is action-GENERIC (rule.messages.contains(action)), so the new actions needed NO decision change — they slot into the existing deny-first -> default -> allow engine.

interceptor/access_control.rs acl_action: a Request maps BY ITS BODY (Query->Query, Put->Put, Del->Delete) — the faithful zenoh per-body dispatch, gating a Request-carried write rather than admitting it (wz emits only Request(Query) today, so the Put/Del arms are faithful-but-unexercised); a Response (Reply or Err body) -> Reply; a Declare(DeclQueryable) -> DeclareQueryable; the keyless ResponseFinal stays ungoverned (admits via the None-keyexpr path).

linkstate_forward.rs FaceContext::full_keyexpr extended: a Request / Response carries its keyexpr inline (resolved alias-aware against the face's table); a Declare resolves via declare_subscriber_wireexpr OR declare_queryable_wireexpr (a Declare is one or the other). This is the per-face keyexpr the ingress (inbound face) and egress (destination face) enforcers feed the policy.

Enforcement is at the EXISTING seams: admit_inbound (forward()) drops a denied inbound Query / DeclareQueryable BEFORE forward_request / forward_queryable registers/routes it; admit_outbound (fan_out) drops a denied outbound Reply when forward_response relays it back — the egress gate the §5.16 atoms already wired (admit_outbound was a forward-compatible hook). The empty-chain fast path keeps a no-ACL deploy unaffected. demo --acl-deny now denies Query/DeclareQueryable/Reply too, so `--acl-deny K` closes K across the data AND query planes.

FOCUSED ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (correctness + fidelity): HIGH on both — the acl_action body-mapping, full_keyexpr resolution, and per-hop ingress/egress gating were all verified faithful vs zenoh authorization.rs / access_control.rs. Remediation: added an_egress_acl_deny_blocks_a_relayed_reply (the review's egress / Reply-enforcement gap — the tests were ingress-only) and fixed an overclaiming unit-test comment. The flagged Request-uniform-routing 'inconsistency' is a non-issue (a Request(Put) IS a write-to-queryable, routed there + gated as Put; wz emits only Request(Query) regardless).

Round 311uf.decision_summary: R311uf: query-routing per-query TIMEOUT — the tick-loop sweep GC for pending-query return entries (zenoh's per-query QueryCleanup). A forwarded Query's pending entry now carries a deadline (allocate-time + a configurable query_timeout, default 10s = zenoh queries_default_timeout); the LinkstateForwarder tick sweeps expired entries each coalescing window and routes a synthesized ResponseFinal back to the querier (zenoh finalize_pending_query), freeing the entry — so a queryable that crashes without a final on a still-up face no longer leaks the entry nor hangs the querier. The Err('Timeout') reply body is honestly deferred (separate Err-response origination; relay correctness = the closing final alone).
changes_bullets: PendingQueries (linkstate_pending.rs): entries gain a per-entry deadline (PendingReturn { inbound, inbound_rid, deadline: Instant }); allocate(.., deadline) stamps it; new expired(now) -> Vec<ExpiredQuery> removes & returns entries past their deadline and prunes emptied faces (HashMap::retain) — the wz form of zenoh QueryCleanup. peek/take return shape unchanged.

LinkstateForwarder (linkstate_forward.rs): new query_timeout: Cell<Duration> (default DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT = 10s = zenoh queries_default_timeout) + set_query_timeout config seam (twin of set_gossip_target etc.); forward_request stamps deadline = Instant::now() + query_timeout on every allocated entry.

tick() now also calls reap_timed_out_queries(): sweep expired(Instant::now()) (borrow released before send), bump a timed_out witness, and for each reaped entry synthesize build_response_final(inbound_rid) (the SSOT builder) + fan_out it back to the inbound face — exactly zenoh QueryCleanup::run -> finalize_pending_query. Cadence = the existing trees_delay coalescing window, so a query is reaped within one tick of its deadline (a coarser, allocation-free GC vs zenoh's per-query sleep task).

pending_timed_out() accessor added (GC witness, the timed_out twin of recomputes); pending_len() + remove_face docs updated (the timeout is now the 2nd GC path beside face-down purge). Err('Timeout') reply body deferred: a synthetic Err Response is a separate codec-build atom; the relay-layer correctness (no leak, no hang) is the closing final alone.

New build_response_err_empty SSOT builder (the empty-keyexpr Err shape: id=0, no suffix, N clear). Single-relay-faithful; the multi-hop Err is graceful-degrade (an intermediate relay forwards the keyexpr-less final but may drop the empty-keyexpr Err at forward_response resolution; the query still terminates via the final).
publishable_changes_bullets: wz-session-core response_build.rs: new build_response_err_empty(request_id, payload) — the empty-keyexpr Response(Err) shape (header 0x1B = MID, no N; WireexprLocal{id:0, no suffix}; Err body), the wz form of zenoh's QueryCleanup timeout reply Response{ wire_expr: WireExpr::empty(), payload: Err('Timeout') } (dispatcher/queries.rs:312-330). The empty-keyexpr sibling of build_response_err_literal/_aliased (both assert a keyexpr; a timeout reply names no resource).

linkstate_forward.rs reap_timed_out_queries: now sends TWO messages per reaped entry, exactly zenoh QueryCleanup::run — first the Err('Timeout') reply (build_response_err_empty, rid rewritten to the upstream rid, fan_out to the inbound face), then the closing ResponseFinal (unchanged). The Err build is fallible (tiny payload, cannot overflow) — a build error skips just the Err, the load-bearing final still sends.

Multi-hop note (honest): the closing final (no keyexpr) forwards across relays unchanged; the empty-keyexpr Err may be dropped at an intermediate relay's forward_response keyexpr resolution, so the multi-hop Err is graceful-degrade until the multi-hop e2e path lands. Single-relay (the tested shape) is fully faithful: the querier gets Err('Timeout') + the final.
publishable_verification_bullets: wz-session-core: build_response_err_empty_emits_empty_keyexpr_wire_bytes (exact wire bytes 0x5B|VLE(rid)|0x00|0x05|len|payload = zenoh WireExpr::empty() Err; inner-arm Err payload + empty Local keyexpr id=0/no-suffix). response_build 29/29; session-core default lib 153/153 no regression.

routing-peer lib 412/412 (the a_pending_query_times_out test now asserts BOTH frames: frame 0 = Err('Timeout') reply with rid rewritten to 99 + payload 'Timeout', frame 1 = the closing final with rid 99). base lib 277/277 no regression.

clippy -D clean (runtime-tokio routing-peer --all-targets, --no-default-features --features routing-peer, base; wz-session-core codec-response,alloc); fmt clean. Host gate only per the run-ci-batch policy; full run-ci runs once before the batch push.
publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R311ug = query-timeout Err('Timeout') reply: completes R311uf's QueryCleanup port to full zenoh fidelity (Err reply + closing final, the two messages zenoh's run() sends). The relay query track's timeout path now matches zenoh: a queryable that dies without a final yields the querier an explicit Err('Timeout') + a clean query close, not a silent empty.

DEFERRED (carried, honest): (1) multi-hop Err forwarding — an intermediate relay's forward_response drops the empty-keyexpr Err at keyexpr resolution (the final still propagates, so the query terminates); pairs with the multi-hop e2e + Session-API client path. Round 311uh.decision_summary: R311uh: multi-hop (2-relay) query e2e test — the cross-instance composition the single-relay tests cannot cover, closing the R311ue honesty gap (the track was END-TO-END at the relay layer but single-relay-tested). A query crosses A-S1-S2-C through two independent LinkstateForwarder instances with the qid remapped at each hop, and the Reply + ResponseFinal unwind back through BOTH pending tables; frames are shuttled relay-to-relay through the real wire-decode + forward() inbound path. Test-only, no production change.
changes_bullets: linkstate_forward.rs test: a_query_routes_across_two_relays_and_the_reply_unwinds_both_hops — two LinkstateForwarder instances (S1=0x01, S2=0x02) wired A-S1-S2-C (line topology via crafted ingest_inbound_linkstate + advertise_link_back on each; C's queryable on both). A's Query feeds S1.forward(), its output frame is wire-decoded and replayed into S2.forward(), S2's output reaches C; the Reply + Final shuttle back the reverse way.

feed_message(fwd, face, msg) test helper: wraps an already-decoded NetworkMessage as one inbound DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload and drives fwd.forward() — the shuttle primitive replaying one relay's recorded wire frame into the next relay's real decode + dispatch path.

Verified the cross-instance qid chaining + reply unwind: S1 maps qid_a -> A's rid 99, S2 maps qid_b -> qid_a; the Reply rewrites qid_b -> qid_a at S2 then qid_a -> 99 at S1; the Final frees both pending tables. (qid_a == qid_b == 1 is CORRECT: per-(relay,face) counters are independent; the remap is per-relay STATE proven by the unwind, not by distinct qid values — a first-draft assertion to the contrary was corrected.)
verification_bullets: routing-peer lib 413/413 (was 412; +1: a_query_routes_across_two_relays_and_the_reply_unwinds_both_hops — query routes A->S1->S2->C through two real instances incl cross-hop source re-stamp + resolution + double B1 keyexpr normalize; Reply request_id qid_b->qid_a->99; Final frees S2 then S1). Test-only: no production code touched.

Round 311ui.decision_summary: R311ui: QueryTarget BestMatching track, atom 1/N — the DeclareQueryable codec now carries the QueryableInfo extension. Realized the documented-but-deferred Z-gated ext_entry chain on decl_queryable.scxml (the shape declare.scxml uses), so a DeclareQueryable can carry zenoh's QueryableInfoType (complete/distance) — the data BestMatching needs (route to the nearest COMPLETE queryable, else all). Codec capacity + a wire round-trip proven; the typed QueryableInfo packing + qabls ingest + the BestMatching routing select are the following atoms. Default (no ext) wire byte-identical (Z=0) = backward-compat.
changes_bullets: sources/codecs/decl_queryable.scxml: added the Z-gated generic ext_entry tlv-chain (import ext_entry.scxml + <sce:tlv-chain id=extensions present-if=header.Z terminate-on=entry-flag>), modeled on declare.scxml's qos/timestamp ext chain. The documented-but-deferred queryable-info ext (the file's own header comment) is now realized as wire capacity; the QueryableInfo SEMANTIC (ext_id 0x01, complete bit + distance) interpretation will live in the routing layer, not the codec.

Regenerated (SCE codegen via wz-codecs build.rs): DeclQueryable / DeclQueryableOwned gain `extensions: Option<...ExtEntry...>` mirroring the parent Declare. build_declare_queryable + build_declare_queryable_nonlocal get `extensions: None` (zenoh DEFAULT { complete:false, distance:0 } = no ext = Z clear = byte-identical no-ext wire); the test-support decl_queryable uses ..default() so it picks up None automatically.
Backward-compat: the default DeclareQueryable wire stays [0x44, 0x00, 0x00] (Z=0, no ext) — the existing zenoh-pico-parity wire-byte test still holds; only a Z=1 info-ext form is new coverage.
verification_bullets: wz-session-core lib 295/295 (was 294; +1: a_decl_queryable_carries_a_z64_info_ext_across_a_wire_round_trip — a Z64 ext on a DeclareQueryable body survives encode -> Declare::decode -> try_into_owned, read back via the shared read_z64_ext SSOT; the default builder carries no ext + body Z clear). wz-runtime-tokio routing-peer 413/413 + base 277/277 unchanged (the codec change is backward-compat; forward_queryable ingest unaffected).

clippy -D clean (wz-session-core codec-declare,codec-response,alloc; wz-runtime-tokio routing-peer); fmt clean. PUSH-TIME (full run-ci): the MCU footprint delta (the regenerated decl_queryable gains the ext field on every MCU target) + the zenohd Z interop lane — the default no-ext wire is byte-identical so interop is expected green; the footprint + Z lanes confirm at push.
carry_forward_bullets: R311ui = QueryTarget BestMatching atom 1/N: the DeclareQueryable codec carries the QueryableInfo ext (Z-gated ext_entry chain), the wire capacity for zenoh's complete/distance — the data BestMatching needs. NEXT: (2) a typed queryable_info module (thin projection over the ext_nodeid read_z64_ext/set_z64_ext SSOT, ext_id 0x01, zenoh-exact complete/distance packing — verify vs zenoh QueryableInfoType encode) + build_declare_queryable producing it + forward_queryable ingest storing per-(key,zid) completeness/distance in qabls (HashMap<String,HashSet<Zid>> -> HashMap<String,HashMap<Zid,QueryableInfo>>) + distance increment on re-flood. (3) forward_request BestMatching select (nearest complete, else All fallback = current behavior). (4) high-level queryable API setting complete + demo + Request ext_target override.

DESIGN (verified): zenoh BestMatching (dispatcher/queries.rs:243-266) = the first COMPLETE queryable in distance-order, else fall back to All; QueryableInfo.distance accumulates per hop. wz's read_z64_ext/set_z64_ext (ext_nodeid) already provide the ext-chain SSOT; the codec field added here is the missing wire carrier.

Round 311uj.decision_summary: R311uj: QueryTarget BestMatching, atom 2a/N — the typed QueryableInfo over the R311ui wire capacity. New wz-session-core::queryable_info module: QueryableInfo{complete, distance} + read/set over the shared ext_nodeid z64-chain SSOT, with zenoh's EXACT packing (complete @ bit 0, distance << 8, verified vs zenoh-codec network/declare.rs:553-576; omit-on-DEFAULT). set_declare_queryable_info producer stamps it onto a built Declare(DeclQueryable) (Z-bit synced). The qabls ingest storing it + the BestMatching routing select are the next atoms.
changes_bullets: New wz-session-core/src/queryable_info.rs: QueryableInfo { complete: bool, distance: u16 } (+ DEFAULT) + read_queryable_info / set_queryable_info — thin projections over the shared ext_nodeid read_z64_ext / set_z64_ext z64-chain SSOT (like read_source/set_source), ext_id 0x01. zenoh-EXACT packing: value = (complete) | (distance << 8) (verified vs zenoh-codec network/declare.rs:553-576); DEFAULT {false,0} packs to 0 and OMITS (no ext, Z clear). Header 0x21 = id 0x01 | ENC_Z64, NO FLAG_M (zenoh's zextz64!(0x01, FALSE) is non-mandatory, unlike the mandatory ext_nodeid 0x33).

declare_build.rs set_declare_queryable_info(&mut DeclareOwned, QueryableInfo): the producer seam — stamps the info onto a built Declare(DeclQueryable) body ext chain + syncs the body header Z bit (the post-build twin of set_declare_source, on the BODY chain not the envelope). omit-on-DEFAULT keeps the byte-identical no-info wire. lib.rs: pub mod queryable_info (gated alloc + codec-declare).

INTEROP NOTE: the packing + the non-mandatory M=0 header were verified against zenoh source, not guessed — an earlier guess (distance << 1, with M) would have broken zenohd interop. The default wire is unchanged (omit-on-DEFAULT), so a no-info DeclareQueryable stays byte-identical.

Round 311ul.decision_summary: R311ul: QueryTarget BestMatching, atom 2b/N — qabls is now VALUE-BEARING with a value-diff change-gate (the session-review HIGH finding). LinkstatepeerInterest<V> generic (HashMap<String, HashMap<Zid, V>>): V=() subscriptions / V=QueryableInfo queryables (zenoh's deliberate HashSet-vs-HashMap split, mod.rs:516-517). register returns true on a NEW peer OR a CHANGED value (zenoh queries.rs:268), so a queryable flipping complete RE-FLOODS instead of silently not. forward_queryable reads read_queryable_info from the DeclareQueryable body + stores it; the shared seam threads the per-kind value via an InterestRegistration param-object. Multi-hop re-flood carrying the info downstream is tracked.
changes_bullets: linkstate_interest.rs: LinkstatepeerInterest -> generic LinkstatepeerInterest<V> (by_key: HashMap<String, HashMap<Zid, V>>). register(keyexpr, peer, value: V) -> bool is now the VALUE-DIFF gate (V: PartialEq): true on a NEW peer OR a CHANGED value, false on a redundant same-value re-declare — zenoh's register_linkstatepeer_queryable gate (current.is_none() || != qabl_info, queries.rs:268), not the prior new-peer-only HashSet::insert. For V=() (subs) the value never differs, so the gate reduces to new-peer = the prior behaviour exactly. withdraw/remove_peer/entries/matching_peers/interested/interested_remote stay value-agnostic (HashSet dedup preserved).

linkstate_forward.rs: subs: LinkstatepeerInterest<()> / qabls: LinkstatepeerInterest<QueryableInfo> (zenoh's deliberate HashSet-vs-HashMap split, mod.rs:516-517). forward_queryable reads the QueryableInfo from the DeclareQueryable BODY ext (read_queryable_info; absent = DEFAULT) + registers it. The shared forward_interest_declaration seam is generic <V: PartialEq> + threads the per-kind value via an InterestRegistration<V> param-object (table + value, ties V; keeps the seam at the 7-arg budget — the R311lw param-object precedent, not a #[allow]). re_advertise_interest generic <V>.

Round 311um.decision_summary: R311um: QueryTarget BestMatching, atom 3/N — forward_request now SELECTS the single nearest COMPLETE queryable (select_best_matching over the value-bearing qabls + the GRAPH distance) instead of fanning out to All; with no complete queryable it falls back to QueryTarget::All (the prior fan-out). 'Complete for this query' = the queryable declared complete AND its declaration keyexpr includes the full query keyexpr (zenoh complete && qabl_info.complete); 'nearest' is net.distance_to (zenoh net.distances[qabl_idx], NOT the carried distance, so no per-hop arithmetic). Behaviour is unchanged until a complete-queryable producer (atom 4) exists — every queryable is DEFAULT incomplete today, so BestMatching always falls to All.
changes_bullets: linkstate_interest.rs: matching_entries(target, exclude) -> Vec<(&str, Zid, &V)>, the VALUE-BEARING twin of matching_peers — every (declaration-keyexpr, peer, value) whose declaration INTERSECTS the target, one tuple PER declaration (no peer dedup), pub(crate). BestMatching needs the per-peer QueryableInfo AND the matched declaration keyexpr (the includes-the-query input) that the value-agnostic matching_peers discards. Mirrors zenoh's per-(matched-resource, qabl) iteration in insert_target_for_qabls (hat/linkstate_peer/queries.rs:710).

linkstate_forward.rs select_best_matching(keyexpr, source, self, inbound) -> Option<Zid>: filter matching_entries to queryables COMPLETE for the query (stored complete && keyexpr_includes_target(decl, query) = zenoh complete && qabl_info.complete, queries.rs:723), resolve each to its tree direction next_hop(source, peer) + graph distance net.distance_to(peer), exclude the inbound direction (zenoh qabl.direction.0.id != src_face.id), take the min-distance hop (zenoh route.sort_by_key(distance) queries.rs:1050 + the first-complete find dispatcher/queries.rs:243-266). forward_request routes to the single selected hop, else falls back to the All directions_toward fan-out (the prior behaviour folded into the None arm).

GRAPH distance, NOT carried: net.distance_to(peer) is the shortest-path distance from THIS node (zenoh reads net.distances[qabl_idx], queries.rs:724), so there is no per-hop distance arithmetic — the carried QueryableInfo.distance stays a stored value-diff-gate input, unused by the select. keyexpr_includes_target is the existing wz SSOT analogue of zenoh's DEFAULT_INCLUDER.includes.
verification_bullets: routing-peer lib 418/418 (was 415; +3: matching_entries_yields_the_per_peer_value_for_best_matching [value carried per-declaration, self excluded, non-intersecting target empty]; forward_request_best_matching_routes_only_to_the_complete_queryable [B complete + C incomplete at equal distance -> ONLY B, contrast the All test where both incomplete -> both]; forward_request_best_matching_prefers_the_nearer_of_two_complete_queryables [B distance 1 + E distance 2 behind D, both complete -> nearest B, never D's direction]). The existing forward_request_fans_out_to_every_matching_queryable comment now documents the All FALLBACK (DEFAULT-incomplete -> no complete -> All). base default lib 277/277 unchanged.

The discovery that closed 4b cheaply: the generated Request codec ALREADY decodes the ext chain into RequestOwned.extensions and the target ext is a zint over the SAME Z64 body the ext_nodeid reader decodes, so read_request_target is a thin read_z64_ext projection — NO codec/SCXML change, NO MCU wire surface (contra the 4a-carry pessimism). changes_bullets: query_mode.rs: TARGET_EXT_ID = 0x04 (the SSOT target ext id, replacing the request_build writer's magic literal) + QueryTarget::from_wire_byte(u64) -> Option<Self> (the inverse of wire_byte; 1->All, 2->AllComplete, else None = the never-transmitted BEST_MATCHING wire default). request_build.rs writer's target ext header now references TARGET_EXT_ID, so the id is defined ONCE and shared by read + write.

request_routing_context.rs read_request_target(&RequestOwned) -> Option<QueryTarget>: read_z64_ext(extensions, TARGET_EXT_ID).and_then(from_wire_byte) — a thin projection of the shared chain reader (the target ext's zint body is the SAME Z64 the ext_nodeid reader matches), so an absent ext = None = BestMatching. KEY: the generated RequestOwned.extensions ALREADY carries the decoded ext chain (the write side build_request_query_with_target pushes the target ext; decode round-trips it), so NO codec / SCXML change was needed (contra the 4a-carry which assumed an MCU-footprint wire decode).

Round 311uq.decision_summary: R311uq: QueryTarget BestMatching, atom 4d/N — the DOWNSTREAM carry that completes MULTI-HOP BestMatching. Both queryable re-flood paths now CARRY the source's QueryableInfo, not a clean declaration: forward_queryable's inbound re-flood (captures the read info) AND re_advertise_queryables' tree-change re-flood (entries() is now value-bearing). So a relay N hops from a complete queryable learns its completeness and routes by GRAPH distance — the prior clean re-flood made a 2-hop relay store the queryable as incomplete, so its BestMatching fell back to All. zenoh propagate_sourced_queryable re-floods the registered QueryableInfo VERBATIM (no per-hop distance increment; BestMatching reads net.distances).

re_advertise_interest seam: build is now Fn(&str, &V) and consumes the value-bearing entries(), so the tree-change re-advertise carries the per-peer value too. re_advertise_queryables stamps the QueryableInfo (build_declare_queryable_with_info), re_advertise_subscriptions ignores V=(). linkstate_interest.rs entries() -> Vec<(String, Zid, V)> (V: Clone) — the value-agnostic deferral note is now CLOSED.

WHY no distance increment: wz qabls is keyed by the queryable's ORIGIN zid (resolve_source maps every hop's re-stamped node_id back to it), and select_best_matching reads net.distance_to(origin) — the GRAPH distance from THIS relay — so the carried distance is IRRELEVANT to wz routing. zenoh's insert_target_for_qabls likewise reads net.distances[qabl_idx], not qabl_info.distance, and propagate_sourced_queryable re-floods the registered qabl_info VERBATIM (queries.rs:278). Three per-module message-Z consts (REQUEST_FLAG_Z / PUSH_FLAG_Z / DECLARE_FLAG_Z, each 0x80) collapse to ONE ext_nodeid::MESSAGE_FLAG_Z (semantically distinguished from the per-entry EXT_FLAG_Z — same bit, different layer), and the FIVE copies of the 'if present { header |= Z } else { header &= !Z }' bit-twiddle (set_push_source, set_push_hoplimit, set_declare_source, set_request_source, set_declare_queryable_info) collapse to ONE ext_nodeid::sync_header_z helper. changes_bullets: ext_nodeid.rs: + MESSAGE_FLAG_Z (the message-level header Z bit, zenoh <msg>::flag::Z; SAME 0x80 bit as the per-entry EXT_FLAG_Z but a DISTINCT layer — for a 1-ext message the header Z is set while that ext's own Z is clear, so the two consts are semantically separate) + sync_header_z(header, chain_present) (the shared header-Z bit-twiddle SSOT).

The 4 routing-context setters (set_push_source, set_push_hoplimit, set_declare_source, set_request_source) + declare_build set_declare_queryable_info now call ext_nodeid::sync_header_z(&mut <header>, present) — each a two-liner. The 3 per-module *_FLAG_Z consts (REQUEST_FLAG_Z / PUSH_FLAG_Z / DECLARE_FLAG_Z) removed; their tests reference MESSAGE_FLAG_Z. declare_build's body sync switched from EXT_FLAG_Z (a value-coincidence misnomer for the body HEADER bit) to the correct MESSAGE_FLAG_Z via the helper.
EXT_FLAG_Z (the per-ext-entry chain-continuation bit, apply_chain_z_bits) is UNCHANGED — it is the other layer, correctly kept separate (not merged into MESSAGE_FLAG_Z despite the shared 0x80 value).

Round 311us.decision_summary: R311us: tracked-debt paydown — forwarder clock INJECTION (the uk session-review finding). LinkstateForwarder's two Instant::now() sites (the pending-query deadline stamp in forward_request + the timeout reap in reap_timed_out_queries) now read through an injected clock field (Box<dyn Fn() -> Instant>), defaulting to Instant::now in production (new / with_trees_delay) and injectable via the new with_clock constructor.
