Constructors funnel through a new private build(zid, whatami, trees_delay, clock) so the field initialiser lives once; new / with_trees_delay pass Box::new(Instant::now), the new pub with_clock passes a custom clock (DI for deterministic tests).

The deterministic test a_pending_query_is_reaped_only_after_its_non_zero_deadline_passes: a base+offset fake clock (Instant is opaque, so a fake returns base + a controllable offset; the base cancels in the deadline comparison, leaving offset as virtual time). forward_request stamps deadline = base + 0 + 100ms; a sweep at offset 99ms does NOT reap (survives, no premature final to the querier); a sweep at offset 100ms reaps + routes the Err(Timeout) + closing final back to A.

Round 311v.decision_summary: R311v QueryEvent.attachment extraction. Inbound Query extension chain (ext_id 0x05, ExtZbuf) decoded to Option<&[u8]> view threaded through fire_matching_queryables; R311r carry closed.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: new module-private free function `fn extract_query_attachment(query: &Query) -> Option<&[u8]>` walks `query.extensions.as_ref()` and matches each `ExtEntry` against the zenoh-pico query-attachment wire shape (`ext_id == 0x05` low-nibble of header + `body == ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf`). First matching entry's `zbuf.value.as_slice()` is returned; absent extensions vec or no-attachment chain yields `None`. The mandatory bit (`_Z_MSG_EXT_FLAG_M = 0x10`) is intentionally NOT required to match because zenoh-pico's `_z_query_decode_extensions` falls into the `default` arm silently when M is clear (no `_z_msg_ext_unknown_error`), which is the encode-side behaviour we mirror at decode-side.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: `fire_matching_queryables` body augmented — the existing `let parameters_view = query.parameters.as_deref();` line is followed by `let attachment_view = extract_query_attachment(query);` so the view is computed ONCE per inbound query (the chain walk is O(n) on ext count which the zenoh wire format caps at 8 per `Query::decode` line 109). The `QueryEvent { ..., attachment: None, ... }` literal inside the matched-queryable loop body becomes `QueryEvent { ..., attachment: attachment_view, ... }`. The closure body's R311r doc-comment carry note ("attachment extraction from the extensions chain is a future round") rewritten to record the R311v closure ("the attachment view is extracted from the inbound extensions chain at R311v").

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: imports gain `use wz_codecs::ext_entry::ExtEntryVariant;` (the helper pattern-matches on the variant; the `ExtEntry` struct itself reaches the helper transitively through `Query.extensions: Option<Vec<ExtEntry>>` so it does not need a separate import at the module-prologue level — only the variant constants need direct reference). No new cfg-gates introduced; the helper compiles in every consumer-feature subset because `wz_codecs::ext_entry` is unconditionally part of the wz-codecs surface.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: tests module gains 2 new tests + 1 helper. `request_query_with_attachment(rid, suffix, attachment)` constructs a `Request` whose body is a `Query` carrying a single `ExtEntry` shaped per the zenoh-pico encode path (`ext.set_ext_id(0x05); ext.set_enc(2); ext.body = ExtEntryVariant::CodecZenohExtZbuf(ExtZbuf { value_len: attachment.len() as u64, value: attachment.to_vec() })`), plus `query.header |= 0x80` so a hypothetical round-trip through `Query::decode` would re-surface the chain. `dispatch_threads_attachment_into_query_event_callback` registers a queryable on `home/temp`, dispatches an attachment-bearing Query, and asserts the captured `event.attachment.map(<[u8]>::to_vec)` equals `b"hello-att"[..]`. `dispatch_query_without_extensions_threads_none_attachment` initialises the capture slot non-None (`Some(b"dirty".to_vec())`) so an accidental skipped-write would surface as a false positive, then dispatches a no-extensions Query and asserts the slot is None.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/query.rs: tests-module imports expanded — `std::sync::Mutex` joins the existing `std::sync::Arc` import (the new tests' capture pattern needs interior mutability across the move-closure boundary). `wz_codecs::ext_entry::ExtEntry` + `wz_codecs::ext_zbuf::ExtZbuf` are imported for the helper's construction path (the variant import `ExtEntryVariant` reaches the helper through the `use super::*` at the test module head).

timestamp_strictly_newer now = timestamp_order_key(a) > timestamp_order_key(b); the prior a.zid > b.zid Vec lexicographic diverged from uhlc for a non-canonically-encoded zid (trailing zero not trimmed, or author-chosen local_zid).
storage_history.rs: order_key removed; binary_search_by now uses the shared timestamp_order_key — version-list sort + newer-wins gate single-source the uhlc ordering (comparator SSOT).

Round 311vc.decision_summary: R311vc: session-review remediation 2/3 — fallback timestamp is now a wall-clock NTP64, closing the silent-data-loss mode the 4-agent review found (honesty Q3 + bug #6). The prior monotonic counter (1,2,3) was dominated by any real NTP64 (~10^18), so under newer-wins one real-timestamped Put made every later un-timestamped Put silently lose as Outdated. wall_clock_ntp64() mints the uhlc NTP64 layout (secs<<32 | frac), comparable to real publisher timestamps. Plus honesty docs: corrected the off-by service.rs:584 citation (an error-log line) to the real reply chain :575-577/:609-611, documented the StoredData.encoding Option divergence. The fallback stays injectable at the apply_sample FnOnce seam (§5.18 HLC drop-in).
changes_bullets: storage_service.rs: wall_clock_ntp64() = (unix_secs<<32)|(subsec_nanos<<32/1e9) — the uhlc NTP64 layout. The driver's fallback for an un-timestamped sample now mints this instead of a monotonic counter (1,2,3); the counter was dominated by any real NTP64 (~10^18) so under newer-wins a real-ts Put silently dropped every later un-ts Put as Outdated (data loss). Wall-clock competes fairly by time.

Module doc rewritten: the data-loss mode is named explicitly + the residual limits (non-monotonic across NTP steps, sub-ns collisions) + §5.18 HLC as the proper source + the fallback is injectable at the apply_sample FnOnce seam (HLC drop-in).

changes_bullets: storage_replication.rs: Digest::diff(&self, mut other) -> Option<DigestDiff> (digest.rs:109-170): config-fp mismatch -> None; hot era retain other-subs NOT matching self then drop now-empty intervals; warm era retain other-intervals not matching self; if hot/warm leftover -> DigestDiff (cold flag folded in); else cold differ -> cold-only DigestDiff; else None.

DigestDiff{cold_eras_differ: bool, warm_eras_differences: BTreeSet<IntervalIdx>, hot_eras_differences: BTreeMap<IntervalIdx, BTreeSet<SubIntervalIdx>>} (digest.rs:93-98) + accessors. The typed work-list the aligner track consumes. BTreeSet/BTreeMap for no_std (zenoh HashSet/HashMap; wire-irrelevant since diff is local-only).

Asymmetric by design: local.diff(remote) surfaces only what remote has that local differs on or lacks; local's own extras are found when remote runs remote.diff(local). Each replica diffs the received digest, so every divergence is found once on the side that must pull.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_aligner.rs (NEW, storage-aligner feat): Action{Put,Delete} + EventMetadata{key,timestamp,action}, a faithful mirror of zenoh log.rs:43-49 (Action) / :98-128 (EventMetadata). EventMetadata::fingerprint delegates to storage_replication::event_fingerprint (the digest SSOT, Event::compute_fingerprint log.rs:232-244); the action is NOT hashed (log.rs:226-231), so an event and a peer's copy of it agree, which is what makes the digest buckets compare.

crates/wz-session-core/Cargo.toml: storage-aligner = ["storage-replication"] (the aligner consumes a DigestDiff and reuses Fingerprint / event_fingerprint, so an event's identity agrees between the digest and the aligner). lib.rs: pub mod storage_aligner gated on storage-aligner.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_aligner.rs: EventBuckets{intervals: BTreeMap<IntervalIdx, BTreeMap<SubIntervalIdx, Vec<EventMetadata>>>} + from_events (the SSOT bucketing -- classify + event_fingerprint shared with build_digest) + 4 answer methods mirroring the zenoh Aligner replies one-to-one: cold_era_fingerprints (reply_cold_era aligner_query.rs:187-210), sub_intervals_fingerprints (reply_sub_intervals :216-235 via Interval::sub_intervals_fingerprints classification.rs:161-167, zero-fp-filtered), events_in (reply_events_metadata :242-265), all_events (AlignmentQuery::All :103-135).

crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_state.rs: StorageState::replication_events() (storage-aligner gated) -- the snapshot->EventMetadata bridge; one entry per `latest` key, Put vs Delete via backend.get(key).is_some() (a key in `latest` but gone from the backend = a Delete tombstone). debug_assert latest_mode (History::Latest only, like replication_digest).

byte-faithful: a sub-interval fp = XOR of its event fingerprints (zenoh SubInterval.fingerprint classification.rs:183); an interval fp = XOR of its sub fingerprints (Interval.fingerprint :104-108); reply_sub_intervals drops zero-fp sub-intervals (:164 -- defensive: distinct-key events make a zero XOR effectively unreachable, but the filter keeps byte-parity with zenoh).

The SSOT cross-check proves, for a snapshot spanning all three eras, that EventBuckets' answers equal build_digest's: the hot per-sub map == digest.hot_era_fingerprints exactly; XOR of the cold per-interval fps == digest.cold_era_fingerprint; each warm interval's sub fps XOR to digest.warm_era_fingerprints[i].

changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/storage_aligner.rs: new `pub mod wire` (the twin of storage_replication::wire) -- pub encode_event_metadata / decode_event_metadata + AlignmentDecodeError, built on private push_*/Reader helpers the AlignmentQuery/Reply envelope codec (next atom) reuses.

Byte layout (verified by reading uhlc-0.8.1 Timestamp/NTP64/ID derived serde + zenoh OwnedKeyExpr Serialize = Arc<str> -> String): EventMetadata = stripped_key Option(u8 tag 1=Some, then String[u64 len + utf8]) + timestamp Timestamp(NTP64 u64 LE 8B + ID [u8;16] 16B via zid_to_le_array SSOT) + timestamp_last_non_wildcard_update Option<Timestamp> + action Action(u32 LE variant index). bincode Option = u8 tag (NOT u32); a plain enum index = u32.

wz emits stripped_key=Some(key) (no strip_prefix) + tlnwu=Some(timestamp) (re-supplies the field the kernel type omits) + action 0/1 (Put/Delete). decode discards tlnwu (wildcard-only), trims the 16-byte id back to wz's length-trimmed zid (inverse of zid_to_le_array, round-trip exact), and rejects an inbound wildcard action 2/3 (UnsupportedAction), a None stripped_key (MissingKey), bad UTF-8, trailing bytes, or a hostile length -- the named non-converging residuals until wz storage gains wildcard updates / strip_prefix.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-session-core --features storage-aligner: storage_aligner::wire 6/6 -- encode_event_metadata_is_byte_identical_to_bincode_1_3 (THE fidelity test: wz's hand-rolled bytes == the real bincode 1.3 the version + default config zenoh uses, for the equivalent EventMetadata, across Put + Delete + a full 16-byte zid) and wz_and_bincode_1_3_read_each_others_event_metadata (both directions), plus round-trip, wildcard-action-unsupported, trailing+truncation, none-stripped-key rejections. Feature total 228.

changes_bullets: query_sink.rs: ReplyOut trait gains reply_keyed_attached(keyexpr, payload, encoding, attachment) -- alloc-gated, defaulted to the reply_keyed fallback so impls predating the seam stay valid; the reply-plane twin of reply_keyed_stamped.

query.rs: QueryReply::Reply gains attachment: Option<Vec<u8>>; QueryResponder::send_reply_keyed_attached stages encoding + attachment with no T-flag (the aligner orders by the EventMetadata carried in the attachment, not a reply timestamp); impl ReplyOut for QueryResponder forwards it; into_response threads the attachment into ResponseReplyBuilder::attachment; the four existing send_reply* producers carry attachment: None.

response_build.rs: ResponseReplyBuilder gains the attachment field + .attachment(&[u8]) setter (no length cap -- under alloc the ext-zbuf carrier is unbounded) + gated_reply_attachment (the pubsub-attachment gate SSOT, reusing crate::attachment::encode_attachment_ext(ATTACHMENT_EXT_ID_PUSH) so the reply attachment is byte-identical to a pubsub Put's); build() stamps the single inner-MsgPut body attachment ext + the Z(0x80) header bit, Put-only (dropped on the .reply_del() arm, matching zenoh-pico has_attachment = _is_put && ..).
reply.rs: the loopback From<QueryReply> destructures the new attachment field, dropped on receive (the receive twin is A8b).
verification_bullets: Fidelity anchor: zenoh-pico _z_push_body_encode emits the attachment ext as _Z_MSG_EXT_ENC_ZBUF | 0x03 (message.c:296), and a Reply body is encoded by the SAME _z_push_body_encode (message.c:517) -- so a reply attachment IS the push-body attachment ext; wz reuses its encode_attachment_ext(ATTACHMENT_EXT_ID_PUSH=0x03) SSOT, so the bytes match a pubsub Put attachment verbatim.

6 new tests: 5 in response_build (body ext + Z flag set; on-wire 0x43 ext header + VLE len + value; a 200-byte aligner-sized attachment survives the owned copy -- proves the unbounded alloc carrier vs the 32-byte QUERY_EXT_ZBUF_MAX_LEN; composes with encoding(E)+timestamp(T) on distinct bits; dropped on the Del arm) + 1 end-to-end seam in query (ReplyOut::reply_keyed_attached -> QueryResponder staging -> QueryReply -> into_response wire carries the 0x03 ext).

changes_bullets: storage_aligner_service.rs ASK side: query_replica_aligner spawns a task running run_alignment -- issue an AlignmentQuery on the peer's aligner keyexpr (Session::query + with_attachment(encode_alignment_query) + consolidation_for + with_timeout_ms(10s)), collect each reply via on_reply and await on_final through a tokio oneshot (issue_and_collect), then process each reply through the kernel process_alignment_reply and follow every AlignmentFollowup via next_query (Query -> finer query to the same peer, DiscoveredReplica -> All on the derived aligner keyexpr, Done -> stop), draining a work queue until the request tree converges.

Pure testable helpers: consolidation_for (Discovery -> Monotonic, else None; zenoh core.rs:504-515), decode_reply (ReplyView -> (AlignmentReply, Option<RetrievedValue>): the AlignmentReply rides the reply attachment (A8b ReplyView::attachment), a value is built only for a Retrieval variant; no-attachment or undecodable -> None, zenoh core.rs:539-557), retrieved_value (payload + put_encoding -> EncodingHint), next_query (the followup -> next (ke, query) mapping), discovery_keyexpr (@zid/*/<config-fp>/aligner for the initial Discovery). DecodedReply type alias for the reply tuple.

Deliberate divergence: zenoh spawns a fresh task per followup (recursive, core.rs:559-572 + aligner_reply.rs:118-223); wz drains a work queue in ONE task -- the same request tree, no per-step spawn, since the wz answer + process_alignment_reply are synchronous over the locked state. The std Mutex guard is held only across the synchronous process_alignment_reply calls in a tight scope, never across a query await.

Feature storage-aligner += query-consolidation (implies query-get -> query-reply: the Session::query GET seam + the ReplyView attachment/put_encoding RX path, A8b) + query-timeout (bounds each query so the followup loop never hangs on an unreachable replica -- the session emits Err+Final on timeout, firing on_final).

The detached pull's JoinHandle is dropped; the subscriber's RAII lifetime gates whether NEW pulls are spawned. state is shared with the StorageService (shared_state) so the digest the subscriber diffs and the entries the pull lands both reflect the one live store. zenoh spawn_digest_subscriber -> spawn_query_replica_aligner (core.rs:331-399 + 484-577).

changes_bullets: (HIGH) issue_and_collect now wraps the on_final await in a tokio::time::timeout backstop (ALIGNER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS + ALIGNER_BACKSTOP_SLACK_MS) so a spawned alignment task is SELF-BOUNDED. The prior ALIGNER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS doc claimed the wire with_timeout_ms guarantees on_final fires when a replica is unreachable, but the reply-timeout sweep (ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out) is a SEPARATE task -- R268 relocated it OUT of drive_session_until_terminal -- so a session without an app-spawned sweep would hang final_rx.await forever on a silent peer, leaking the detached task + its Arc<Mutex<StorageState>> clone per divergence. The backstop resolves regardless; the doc is corrected to state this honestly.

(MEDIUM) digest_keyexpr_zid_hex now requires the zid chunk to be all ascii-hexdigit (exactly what zid_to_zenoh_hex emits, so a legit peer never fails) -- defense-in-depth: a crafted/non-conformant peer keyexpr like @-digest/a$*/<fp> would otherwise splice a keyexpr WILDCARD into the aligner query keyexpr (aligner_keyexpr_for_hex), fanning a targeted Diff pull (and this replica's DigestDiff) out to many replicas. +3 rejection asserts.

(MEDIUM) run_alignment now truncates a Discovery query's replies to the first (replies.truncate(1)): zenoh defensively stops after the FIRST Discovery reply (core.rs:567-572) because Monotonic may still deliver several; without the guard several Discovery replies fanned into several All pulls.

(LOW) run_alignment now bounds the followup queue with MAX_ALIGNMENT_QUERIES (100k). A conformant peer's refinement tree stays far below; a hostile peer answering ANY query with fresh Discovery replies can no longer grow the queue unbounded (zenoh has the same exposure via unbounded task spawns; wz's single-task drain makes a cheap cap natural). Hitting it abandons THIS pass -- the next digest tick re-triggers if still diverged, so a deep alignment still converges over ticks.

(LOW) decode_reply now derives value-presence from the event Action (a Delete Retrieval -> None, matching the answer side which emits value=None for a Delete Retrieval) instead of the Retrieval variant alone (was building Some(RetrievedValue{[],None}) for a Delete Retrieval -- inert because the kernel Delete arm ignores value, but now consistent across all three seam sites). EventMetadata::action() (pub accessor) + Action imported. Doc corrected.

(LOW) two wrong-side citations fixed: retrieved_value (was aligner_query.rs:300-302, the producer side -> aligner_reply.rs:367-369, the SampleFields consumer side it mirrors); consolidation_for None (core.rs:499-504 comment range -> :504 the assignment). The stale module-doc NON-goals (which still listed A8c-2c as "remaining") updated -- A8c-2c is done; the remaining leg is the A11 live two-replica e2e.

(LOW) run_alignment now bounds the followup queue with MAX_ALIGNMENT_QUERIES (100k). A conformant peer's refinement tree stays far below; a hostile peer answering ANY query with fresh Discovery replies can no longer grow the queue unbounded (zenoh has the same exposure via unbounded task spawns; wz's single-task drain makes a cheap cap natural). Hitting it abandons THIS pass -- the next digest tick re-triggers if still diverged, so a deep alignment still converges over ticks.

(LOW) decode_reply now derives value-presence from the event Action (a Delete Retrieval -> None, matching the answer side which emits value=None for a Delete Retrieval) instead of the Retrieval variant alone (was building Some(RetrievedValue{[],None}) for a Delete Retrieval -- inert because the kernel Delete arm ignores value, but now consistent across all three seam sites). changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/query_reply_e2e.rs (NEW): the FIRST in-process Session::query -> remote declare_queryable -> reply -> on_final e2e over a real loopback TCP link. DURABLE LESSONS: (1) the wz<->zenohd handshake needs INTEROP params (version 0x09, batch_size 65535, seq_num_res/req_id_res 2 -- wz-ap-demo's demo_session_init_params), NOT fixture_session_init_params (version 0x05 / batch 0, a wz-internal-test shape a strict zenohd rejects at InitSyn). (2) A wz CLIENT publish returns Ok(0) routing to nobody when it does not know a matching remote subscription -- so seeding a foreign router's storage needs a foreign client (pico z_pub), not a wz-side Put. (3) pico z_pub prepends "[ N] " to its value (assert CONTAINS, not exact); a single pico z_put races its close and does not land.

Round 311ws.decision_summary: R311ws: A12 -- the ANSWER-direction wz<->zenohd storage-replication cross-impl e2e (mirror of A10): an empty zenohd replica converges to an in-process wz replica that HOLDS an entry, exercising wz's AlignerService answer side against the REAL zenoh aligner ASK. Fixed to keyexpr INTERSECTION. Convergence 5/5 non-flaky; no regression (query 269, runtime 279, storage 315, A11/A10 green).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/query.rs: Queryable::matches now matches an inbound query by keyexpr INTERSECTION (keyexpr_intersects_target -- the seam declared_intersects already uses) instead of keyexpr_pattern_matches, which matched the queryable pattern against the query as a concrete LITERAL, so a wildcard query selector's `*` was matched character-literally and never reached a concrete queryable. For a concrete query the result is identical -- no regression. Removed the now-unused keyexpr_pattern_matches import.

crates/wz-session-core/src/query.rs: NEW unit test concrete_queryable_answers_wildcard_query_selector -- a concrete queryable answers an intersecting wildcard selector and does NOT answer a non-intersecting one (the regression guard for the fix).

The digest-diff path (wz DigestPublisher -> zenohd @-digest/* subscriber -> concrete Diff) is the fallback once the Discovery GET times out.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: session-extauth = ["wz-session-core/session-extauth"] (AP forward; no wz-runtime-lwip forward -- zenoh-pico has no auth).

zenoh-pico has no auth (0 hits) -> extauth is AP-only, no parity expectation.

NEXT R2 = the method-agnostic auth DISPATCH seam: the wz mirror of zenoh establishment/ext/auth/mod.rs OpenFsm/AcceptFsm -- read inbound auth ext -> produce outbound auth ext across recv_init_syn/send_init_ack/send_open_syn/recv_open_ack, in the handshake glue (handshake_encode + session_glue), NO new SCXML state (per OQ-W10). NEXT R4 = pubkey method (zenoh pubkey.rs: RSA challenge-response) -> access-extauth-pubkey active; needs an RSA crypto dep DECISION first (which crate; AP-only).

access-extauth-jwt = zenoh PHANTOM (no transport-establishment JWT method exists in zenoh). After R4, RECLASSIFY the catalog atom (correct its source / remove), do NOT build (port-don't-invent). Round 311xe.decision_summary: R4c: the wz<->zenohd pubkey WIRE interop proof, bounded by a zenoh UPSTREAM limitation discovered by direct-read. A real zenohd 1.5.0 DECODES wz's pubkey InitSyn ZPublicKey byte-for-byte (the two-LE-ZBuf {n,e} codec is canonical-router decodable) and rejects only at its lookup -- so wz's pubkey wire interoperates. But stock zenohd cannot complete a pubkey handshake with ANY client: AuthPubKey::new gives a Some(empty) lookup that rejects every key (pubkey.rs:566-570), known_keys_file is an unimplemented @TODO, and disable_lookup is pub(crate) unreachable from config -- so a success-path Established cross-impl is impossible upstream, NOT a wz defect. (This OVERTURNS the R4b dissection's 'empty lookup accepts all'; direct-read of the source is the arbiter.) The test asserts the achievable interop -- zenohd logs 'PubKey extension - Recv InitSyn. Unauthorized PubKey.' (past the decode, not a Decoding error) -- and is promotable to assert Established if a future zenoh implements known_keys_file. No inventory change (R4b flipped pubkey active).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pubkey_zenohd_interop.rs: NEW wz<->zenohd pubkey WIRE interop e2e. Spawns a pubkey-configured zenohd (a PKCS#1 keypair generated with `openssl genrsa -traditional`, passed via --cfg transport/auth/pubkey/{public,private}_key_file); wz dials IN-PROCESS with a PubKeyMethod::initiator(generate_keypair). Asserts the achievable interop: zenohd DECODES wz's InitSyn ZPublicKey and rejects only at its lookup (the captured zenohd trace log shows "PubKey extension - Recv InitSyn. Round 311xj.decision_summary: R311xj continues the transport-advanced track: an AF_VSOCK (VM<->host / VM<->VM) link backend (transport-link-vsock), the wz mirror of zenoh's vsock link, reusing the proven TCP/unixsock stream pipeline seam. vsock is a reliable byte STREAM (is_streamed/is_reliable true, MTU BatchSize::MAX), so it reuses the stream_link StreamEnvelope SSOT over a tokio_vsock::VsockStream, split via tokio::io::split (the TLS pattern -- VsockStream has no owned-half split). The vsock/<CID>:<PORT> locator leaf (CID = case-insensitive VMADDR_CID_* / -1 / u32; PORT = VMADDR_PORT_ANY / -1 / u32) is ungated, platform-independent and fully unit-tested -- the genuinely-new logic. The backend is Linux-only (#[cfg(all(transport-link-vsock, target_os=linux))]) over a new optional Linux-only dep tokio-vsock 0.5 (matching zenoh-link-vsock 1.5.0). HONEST verification limit: the wz<->wz e2e + the pipeline bind/accept round-trip are #[ignore] -- AF_VSOCK loopback (VMADDR_CID_LOCAL) needs the vsock_loopback kernel module, ABSENT in this sandbox (probed: no /dev/vsock, bind=EPERM), so the LIVE handshake is NOT run here; it runs --ignored on a vsock-capable host (the Layer Z environment-gated pattern). The data path it would exercise is already proven by the TCP/TLS/unixsock lanes. transport-link-vsock reserved->active (atom 84).

Round 311xk.decision_summary: R311xk completes the link-kind family (tcp/udp/tls/ws/serial/unixsock/vsock + quic): a QUIC link backend (transport-link-quic), the wz mirror of zenoh-link-quic. zenoh carries a zenoh batch over ONE bidirectional QUIC stream per connection (uni rejected, max_concurrent_bidi=1) with the SAME StreamEnvelope length-prefix as TCP/TLS (is_streamed=true, MTU BatchSize::MAX), so it reuses the stream_link SSOT UNCHANGED over a quinn SendStream/RecvStream pair -- which are ALREADY split (no into_split / tokio::io::split). NEW dep quinn 0.11 (default-features=false, ring+rustls+runtime-tokio) -- front-load-verified to share a single rustls 0.23.40 with the existing tokio-rustls 0.26 (no version conflict), so QuicClientConfig::try_from(rustls::ClientConfig) type-checks. Proto::Quic is IP-family (numeric host:port, like tls/ws -- NOT a new AnyLocator variant); the cert (TLS-1.3 + ALPN hq-29, built by quic_config reusing the tls_config PEM loaders) is threaded via DialConfig.quic, the tls pattern. UNLIKE vsock, QUIC loopback needs no special kernel support, so the wz<->wz e2e is FULLY RUNNABLE (self-signed rcgen, no #[ignore]) -- the fully-verified link round closing vsock's #[ignore] gap. transport-link-quic reserved->active (atom 85).

Round 311xm.decision_summary: R311xm activates transport-compression + session-extcompression (atoms 87+88): the wz mirror of zenoh's per-batch lz4 compression (batch.rs) + the Z_EXT_COMPRESSION (0x6) handshake. Both peers offer a 0x6 UNIT ext on Init (the &= merge -- the transport-lowlatency negotiation pattern reused); when negotiated, every post-establishment batch is lz4-wrapped at send_wire as [BatchHeader][payload] (the compressed form kept ONLY when smaller -- incompressible data ships raw, never growing, zenoh batch.rs:347) and un-wrapped at dispatch_link_event (the OUTERMOST wire layer, outside the lowlatency lean encode). Handshake + OpenAck stay uncompressed FOR FREE via the is_established gate (the acceptor is not yet established when it emits OpenAck, so zenoh's explicit OpenAck-uncompressed workaround needs no analogue). NEW dep lz4_flex 0.11 (the SAME crate zenoh uses; no_std+alloc via the safe-* block impls -- front-load-verified), so a compression-negotiated wz<->zenohd session is byte-compatible. wz<->wz e2e: negotiate + deliver a compressible Put byte-exact over real TCP + a deterministic wire-form proof; cross-impl deferred.

Round 311xt.decision_summary: R311xt implements the §5.18 time-hlc atom -- the ACTIVE Hybrid Logical Clock timestamp source, the wz mirror of zenoh's Option<Arc<uhlc::HLC>> on the Runtime (net/runtime/mod.rs:147, an HLC created when timestamping is enabled). DIRECT-READ CORRECTION (the front-loaded highest-risk unknown): zenoh's HLC WRAPS the physical/system clock (HLCBuilder default clock = system_time_clock), it is NOT an alternative to wall-clock, so the prior inventory framing ("HLC = opt-in alternative to wall-clock" / "system-clock mutually-exclusive-with-HLC") was wrong and is corrected. wz reuses the uhlc crate verbatim (the algorithm SSOT, zenoh's 0.8 pin, the same reuse stance as lz4_flex/memmap2) and injects wz's own wall_clock_ntp64 as the HLC physical clock via HLCBuilder::with_clock, so the HLC wraps wz's existing wall-clock SSOT and produces the same NTP64 magnitude the digest/aligner use. The HLC lives in wz-runtime-tokio (the AP runtime, where zenoh puts it + where its sole consumer + physical source live), gated behind the new non-default time-hlc feature, and is wired LIVE into the storage capture fallback (wz's only auto-stamp site) via a FallbackStamp source seam: time-hlc ON stamps an un-timestamped sample with the HLC (logical counter + monotonicity + drift over the wall clock), OFF uses the bare wall_clock_ntp64 (byte-identical to prior behavior). A3 verdict: time-hlc is a genuine cfg-toggle gating real BEHAVIOR (unlike encoding, where gating a name was a dead stub) -> reserved->ACTIVE (active 90->91); the other 3 §5.18 atoms are FOUNDATIONAL (time-ntp64 word+codec, time-system-clock the physical layer the HLC wraps, time-timestamp-source the FallbackStamp seam) with reasons updated to the FOUNDATIONAL prefix.

Round 311xx.decision_summary: R311xx -- liveliness-history correctness fix (small-track A3 read-first surfaced two real fidelity bugs the absent integrated proof had hidden, NOT a cfg flip). Bug #1 (subscriber): history_complete was wired to flip on an inbound Interest(Final) -- which the responder never sends -- so the snapshot-complete signal never fired on a real wz<->wz / wz<->pico exchange (Put samples arrived; only the completion signal was misrouted); the R281 wire-up had cited the no-op pico _z_interest_process_interest_final (interest.c:524) instead of the real terminator handler _z_interest_process_declare_final (interest.c:508). Fixed: dispatch_messages now flips history_complete on the responder's Declare(DeclFinal) whose interest_id echoes a history-subscriber slot (mirror of the liveliness-get registry's fire_final_for), and ignores inbound Interest (the responder's concern). Bug #2 (responder): respond_to_interest gated the current-token replay on non-final (C|F), so a FUTURE-only (history=false) subscriber wrongly received the current tokens as spurious Put samples; fixed to gate on the CURRENT bit (zenoh `if mode.current()`, hat/client/token.rs:354) -- a FUTURE-only interest now stages nothing (future updates ride the declarer's proactive declare). Both bugs confirmed diagnose-first with failing guards before the fix; an integrated responder->subscriber test now proves the current-token Put AND history_complete together (the integrated proof the §5.10 review flagged as absent). STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory UNCHANGED -- liveliness-history stays reserved (R311xx adds no cfg gate), the cfg-gate->active promotion (R311cl's "careful per-call cfg-gate, not field gate") + liveliness-historical-samples FOUNDATIONAL reclassification are the R2 follow-up. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/declare/liveliness_subscriber.rs: dispatch_messages now flips history_complete on an inbound Declare(DeclFinal) whose interest_id echoes a history-subscriber slot (mirror of the liveliness-get registry's fire_final_for + pico _z_interest_process_declare_final, vendor/zenoh-pico/src/session/interest.c:508) and IGNORES inbound Interest messages (the responder's concern; pico _z_interest_process_interest_final, interest.c:524, is a TODO no-op). The prior R281 wire-up flipped history_complete on an Interest(Final) the responder never sends, so the snapshot-complete signal never fired on a real wz<->wz / wz<->pico exchange (Put samples arrived; only the completion signal was misrouted). dispatch_messages doc-comment corrected.

crates/wz-session-core/src/declare/local_token.rs: respond_to_interest gates the current-token replay on the CURRENT bit (new INTEREST_CURRENT_MASK 0x20) instead of the prior non-final (C|F) mask; a FUTURE-only Interest (the history=false subscriber's declare) now stages nothing -- future updates are covered by the declarer's proactive Declare(DeclToken), not by replaying current state. Mirror of zenoh `if mode.current()` (hat/client/token.rs:354). The pre-fix gate wrongly replied to FUTURE-only interests, so a history=false subscriber received the current tokens as spurious Put samples.

The "session-hardening (3)" the roadmap listed as AP-full-remaining is, on direct read, 1 phantom + 2 beyond-pico-substantial -- NOT 3 quick LAYER-1 wins. session-resumable: reserved -> DEPRECATED -- a zenoh PHANTOM (grep `resum*` = 0 hits across the whole checkout; reconnect = a fresh InitSyn/InitAck/OpenSyn/OpenAck handshake, with only zid-keyed transport reuse + transport_multilink + lease-based link-swap as continuity, none of which is resumption; pico = auto-reconnect via fresh _z_open + app-layer declaration-cache replay), and the faithful reconnect behavior wz needs is ALREADY built (R267+ reconnect + replay_declarations); the prior 'OQ-Q14 resumable session' source was a mislabel (log Q14 is an unrelated SCE question); jwt-precedent (R311xf) phantom->deprecated, re-openable beyond-zenoh. session-extqos + session-stateless-accept: stay reserved, reasons corrected to the real zenoh mechanism + both marked BEYOND-PICO full-zenoh (P4 scope, deferred) -- extqos = a DUAL ext on Init only (unit ext_qos XOR z64 ext_qos_link, superset/subset containment) that splits the transport into Priority(8) x Reliability(2) = 16 per-channel SN streams (is_qos a runtime flag, not a cargo feature; pico has none on unicast; wz is pico-faithful 2-channel; pubsub-priority carries the field but is not per-priority-SN-isolated, a soft dep); stateless-accept = an AES-BlockCipher-encrypted SYN-cookie (per-manager key), NOT the HMAC the inventory/OQ-W15 framing assumed -- a fidelity correction -- with an always-stateless acceptor that buffers only a u64 nonce (pico acceptor sends an empty cookie + stays stateful). Round 311y106b.decision_summary: R311y106b -- SESSION-REVIEW correction of R311y106 (found committed-but-unpushed, the user's textbook/SSOT/north-star trigger). A 3-agent adversarial session review caught one MUST-FIX that 6 prior panels + the author missed: the LIVE DeclareKeyExpr alias DEFINITION (send_declare_keyexpr) shipped BARE past the egress arm, while its reconnect-replay twin shipped namespaced -- the same operation handled two ways (an SSOT violation, the un-namespaced branch being the live one), reachable from the high-level aliased API (publish_aliased/query_aliased require a prior send_declare_keyexpr) and leaking a namespaced session's aliased publish to the bare keyexpr. Fix: the live alias definition now namespaces on the wire via the generalized namespace_egress_declare helper (now the single SSOT shared by the live alias path AND the reconnect replay), keeping outbound_mappings bare for loopback (transparent namespace, the zenoh model). Plus a doc-precision fix: the namespace.rs forwarder-safety claim is corrected to the real invariant (a namespaced face is never a forwarder face) instead of the egress-only-precise structural argument. Added the load-bearing namespace_alias_e2e test + the declare-keyexpr CI combo; deferral (b) narrowed to the three helpers with no high-level dependency. 18 kernel + 10 e2e green, fmt/clippy clean.
changes_bullets: session_actions.rs send_declare_keyexpr: the LIVE DeclareKeyExpr alias DEFINITION now passes through the egress decorator (namespace_egress_declare) before its direct dispatch_declare, so the wire alias is baked WITH the namespace (peer registers id -> <ns>/<suffix>); the local outbound_mappings keeps the BARE suffix for loopback resolution (transparent namespace, the zenoh model). Closes the isolation hole where a namespaced session's aliased publish/query (publish_aliased / query_aliased / *_auto, which require a prior send_declare_keyexpr) leaked to the bare keyexpr.

session_actions.rs: generalized replay_namespace_declare -> namespace_egress_declare (the egress-decorate-a-direct-dispatched-Declare SSOT now shared by BOTH the live alias definition AND the reconnect replay), re-gated to the exact caller union all(routing-namespace, any(declare-keyexpr, all(session-reconnect, any(declare-subscriber, declare-queryable, declare-token)))) so it is neither dead-code nor missing-method in any combo; replay_namespace_interest -> namespace_egress_interest (reconnect-only, name parity).

namespace.rs module doc: corrected the forwarder-coexistence safety claim. The old "boundaries distinct -> relays untouched, correct by construction" was egress-precise but ingress-imprecise (the ingress strip runs BEFORE on_event, which feeds the forwarder, so a namespaced FORWARDING face would relay the stripped relative keyexpr). Now states the real invariant: a namespaced face is NEVER a forwarder face (set_namespace reachable only from the client-open helpers; the router/peer face path never installs one), and flags that the future multihat router must re-examine strip-vs-forward ordering.

Round 311y107b.decision_summary: R311y107b -- post-commit SESSION REVIEW remediation of R311y107 (user textbook/SSOT/north-star/cost trigger; independent 3-agent review + direct-read arbitration, NEVER self-assessed). The review caught a y106b-class WHOLE-SYSTEM lifecycle asymmetry the y107 design+impl panels missed: the per-peer namespace_ingress is reset on evict() (with a guard test) but NOT on the two IN-PLACE peer-identity-reset paths -- the multicast re-JOIN known-address branch (ingest_join resets the SN baselines via seed_from_join but left namespace_ingress) and its unicast twin reset_for_reopen (resets rx_sn but left namespace_ingress). A new peer reusing an address (multicast) / a re-handshaked peer after reopen (unicast) inherits a stale blocked-id set -> a re-declared id's id-only undeclare is wrongly dropped -> a phantom subscriber leak. FIX (textbook-complete, BOTH paths): NamespaceIngress::reset() clears the blocked-id/incomplete correlation while KEEPING the namespace prefix; the multicast reset is conditional on a zid CHANGE (a same-zid periodic JOIN beacon keeps the live correlation -- the inverse phantom-undeclare bug is guarded). Correctness fix only; inventory/sections unchanged.

Round 311y108.decision_summary: R311y108 -- §5.21 router-hat slice 1a (dual-net topology STATE). Built RouterForwarder, the 4th impl FaceForwarder (crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/router_forward.rs), the wz port of zenoh hat/router's DUAL link-state mesh (routers_net + linkstatepeers_net) distinct from the single-net LinkstateForwarder. Slice 1a is the control-plane TOPOLOGY half: register/deregister classify a face into a tier by handshake whatami (Router->routers_net, Peer->linkstatepeers_net, Client/zidless->held no net); forward ingests OAM_LINKSTATE into the inbound tier's net + propagates within that tier + coalesces the per-net spanning-tree recompute onto the tick; the flood is TIER-SCOPED (a routers_net change reaches only Router faces -- the two psid spaces never cross-inject, the one router-specific seam since the gossip_target matcher cannot separate the nets). Push is counted (witness) but routed nowhere; Declare/Request/Response left alone. Decided via a pre-code 3-lens DESIGN panel (faithfulness/SSOT-reuse/scope) + a post-build 3-lens IMPL panel (faithfulness found NO logic bug / coverage / SSOT-honesty). Reuse strategy B: own 2 nets + 4 tier tables, reuse the shared LinkstateNetwork + LinkstatepeerInterest crates, pub(crate) peer_zid_routing/peer_whatami_routing, thin per-net wrappers, LinkstateForwarder untouched -- the y107b 'DOUBLED ~6000 LOC' fear was falsified (most of linkstate_forward.rs is tests; the algorithm SSOT is in the shared crates; the slice's fresh surface is ~250 lines of thin glue). The new routing-router-hat cargo feature is a FOUNDATION feature (the routing-accept precedent: a partial capability that gates code WITHOUT being an inventory atom), NOT the router-hat-router atom -- slice 1a routes nothing, the exact analogue of routing-accept (accept-and-hold without forwarding), so router-hat-router stays RESERVED and flips active only when the HAT routes (the COMPUTE slice), mirroring routing-routes/routing-router flipping active on the routing-accept foundation. CORRECTS the router-hat-multihat inventory mis-spec: its reason frames the multi-hat seam as zenoh's Box<dyn Any> type-erasure, but wz realizes the SAME seam via the typed FaceForwarder trait (accept_loop.rs:194) -- no Box<dyn Any>, no new_hat factory; RouterForwarder is the 4th typed impl. The seam is DONE + class=foundational, so router-hat-multihat correctly stays reserved+FOUNDATIONAL; only the Box<dyn Any> reason framing is the mis-spec (no inventory mutation -- the correction lives in this ledger entry per the build plan). 14 unit tests, CI Layer C1ay, Layer A3 green (the foundation feature is not an atom id, so reserved router atoms keep 0 cfg sites).

Added subscription ingest to RouterForwarder (the 1a topology-STATE forwarder): forward's DeclareSubscriber registers the resolve_source_in-resolved SOURCE into the INBOUND face's tier subs table (Router face -> router_subs, Peer face -> linkstatepeer_subs) + a change-gated WITHIN-TIER re-flood along the source's spanning tree (the per-tier analogue of LinkstateForwarder::forward_subscription); UndeclareSubscriber withdraws + re-floods the retraction; DeclKexpr/UndeclKexpr records the per-face link-local keyexpr alias. KEY DESIGN (pre-code 2-agent DERIVE-vs-STORE panel): the cross-tier bubble is DERIVED at route-compute, NOT stored. zenoh STORES tables.zid into the other tier's set when a cross-tier source exists (register_router_subscription pubsub.rs:248/297/338) and carries FOUR reverse-forget teardown sites; wz stores ONLY native sources and derives the bubble at the COMPUTE slice (cross_tier_self_source(ke,tier) = tier natives UNION self-iff-the-other-tier-has-a-native-for-the-EXACT-ke, computed from NATIVES only to avoid circular inflation). The panel proved stored==derived in every subscription scenario (V=(), no info merge), so deriving is behaviorally faithful AND makes the teardown drift unrepresentable-by-construction -- the same filter/project-on-read normalization LinkstatepeerInterest already uses for self-exclusion (superset/normalize, not mirror). resolve_source EXTRACTED to a pub(crate) free fn resolve_source_in(net,..) the method now delegates to (4 call sites unchanged); peer_zid_routing / peer_whatami_routing / declare_subscriber_wireexpr / is_tree_forward_target widened to pub(crate) (seams the router reuses). DEFERRED (named): queryable dual-tier INGEST + the QueryableInfo merge bubble = 1c; the client/simple-sub (session_ctxs leaf) store = 1d; the bubble DERIVATION + route compute + master-election + tree-change re_advertise = the COMPUTE slice. router-hat-router atom STAYS reserved (1b's re-flood is control-plane interest spread, NOT data/query route -- routing-router-hat remains the FOUNDATION feature, the routing-accept precedent from R311y108). 28 unit tests, CI Layer C1ay (comment re-cut to 1a+1b), A3 green, 127 linkstate tests unregressed. Decided via a pre-code DERIVE-vs-STORE design panel + a post-build 3-lens IMPL panel (faithfulness: SHIP, no logic bug / no borrow panic / byte-faithful mirror; coverage: +5 tests; SSOT: fixed the stale C1ay lane comment).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/router_forward.rs: forward's Declare arm now handles subscriptions -- DeclKexpr/UndeclKexpr -> absorb_keyexpr_declaration (per-face link-local alias), DeclareSubscriber -> ingest_subscription, UndeclareSubscriber -> withdraw_subscription; the queryable + Request/Response arms stay deferred (_ => {}). New: ingest_subscription (register the resolved SOURCE into the inbound tier's subs table + change-gated re-flood), withdraw_subscription (withdraw + re-flood the retraction), reflool via reflood_declaration (within-tier SHARED re-forward for both subscribe + unsubscribe -- cleaner than the sibling which duplicates the tail inline), subs_table (tier selector), RouterFaceState.keyexpr_table (per-face alias table). NO cross-tier bubble stored (DERIVED at compute).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/router_forward.rs (docs): module doc re-cut to 1a+1b (added the "Slice 1b landed" section documenting the DERIVE-not-STORE bubble decision + naming the COMPUTE-slice cross_tier_self_source obligation), the deferred list re-cut (qabls=1c, client=1d, bubble-derivation+route-compute+re_advertise=COMPUTE), and the field / purge / tick / forward-arm doc comments updated to the new boundary.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: resolve_source body EXTRACTED to a pub(crate) free fn resolve_source_in(net: &LinkstateNetwork, inbound_zid, inbound_link, node_id) -> Option<(Zid,u16)> (the SSOT RouterForwarder calls per tier-net); the resolve_source METHOD is now a 1-line delegate, the 4 original call sites unchanged. peer_zid_routing / peer_whatami_routing / declare_subscriber_wireexpr / is_tree_forward_target widened fn -> pub(crate) (seams the router reuses).

scripts/run-ci.sh: Layer C1ay lane COMMENT re-cut to "router-hat 1a+1b: dual-net STATE + subs INGEST" and its unit list + boundary line updated (the lane already runs the 1b tests via --lib router_forward; comment-only, the SSOT-panel F1 stale-promise fix).
verification_bullets: 28 router_forward unit tests green (14 from 1a + 14 for 1b): router/peer/client-face declare tiering (client not ingested = 1d pin); DeclareQueryable ingests nothing (1c pin); undeclare withdraw; within-tier re-flood on BOTH tiers (declare + undeclare re-flood reach the source's tree child, never back to the inbound source, never the other tier); duplicate-declare change-gate (no re-flood); aliased declare resolves via the face keyexpr_table + UndeclKexpr removes the alias; transit-source declare (node_id != 0) keyed on the resolve_source_in-resolved zid not the inbound neighbour; unknown-keyexpr undeclare no-op; face-down purges the declared interest (no bubble to leak).

clippy 2 combos (--all-targets + --no-default-features --features routing-router-hat) + fmt clean; Layer A3 green (router-hat-router stays reserved -> 0 cfg(feature="router-hat-router") sites; routing-router-hat is the FOUNDATION feature, unchanged); 127 linkstate lib tests unregressed by the resolve_source extraction + the pub(crate) widenings (the method delegates + 4 call sites unchanged).
CI Layer C1ay runs all 28 via --lib router_forward under routing-router-hat; no new lane (the comment was re-cut to 1a+1b).

Pre-code DERIVE-vs-STORE design panel (2 agents): faithfulness proved stored==derived in every subscription scenario (peer/router/two-peer/wildcard/client, V=() so no info merge) + cited the LinkstatepeerInterest filter-on-read precedent; scope/lifecycle proved native-only is leak-SAFE (no self-bubble stored -> nothing purge_detached_interest_tier could miss), recommended INCLUDING the alias absorb + reusing resolve_source_in.

Post-build IMPL panel (3 agents): faithfulness = SHIP (no logic bug, no reachable borrow panic, byte-faithful mirror of forward_subscription/forward_unsubscription, DERIVE-not-STORE correctly implemented); coverage = FUNCTIONAL, drove +5 tests (transit-source, undeclare re-flood, peer-tier re-flood, unknown-keyexpr undeclare, UndeclKexpr removal); SSOT = fixed the stale C1ay lane comment (F1) + confirmed the module/field docs, zenoh cites, resolve_source_in SSOT, and DERIVE-not-STORE honesty all clean.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y109 = §5.21 router-hat slice 1b (subscription dual-tier INGEST) DONE. DeclareSubscriber -> inbound-tier subs table (router_subs / linkstatepeer_subs) keyed by the resolve_source_in-resolved source + change-gated within-tier re-flood; UndeclareSubscriber withdraw + re-flood; DeclKexpr/UndeclKexpr alias absorb. The cross-tier bubble is DERIVED at compute, NOT stored (the DERIVE-vs-STORE design-panel decision).

NEXT (pick one): 1c = queryable dual-tier INGEST (DeclareQueryable -> router_qabls / linkstatepeer_qabls) -- distinct from subs because the bubble self entry carries a MERGED QueryableInfo (zenoh local_router_qabl_info / local_peer_qabl_info, complete=OR / distance=min), which -- like the sub bubble -- the COMPUTE slice DERIVES; OR 1d = the client/simple-sub store (zenoh session_ctxs per-face leaf input; a Client DeclareSubscriber is NOT ingested in 1b); OR the COMPUTE slice.

COMPUTE-slice NAMED obligation (DO NOT DROP): cross_tier_self_source(ke, tier) -- for tier A the interested set = tier-A subs natives UNION self IFF the OTHER tier (or the 1d client store) has a NATIVE for the EXACT ke; derive from NATIVES ONLY (exclude the derived-self) to avoid circular inflation; this same derivation sources self's flood in propagate_sourced + self in admin get_subscriptions. PLUS the tree-change re_advertise (re_advertise_subscriptions to new tree children -- the router tick currently DISCARDS the new-children delta) + 2-mesh compute_data_route/compute_query_route + elect_router master-election + RouteCache source-dim + shared_nodes maintenance. router-hat-router flips ACTIVE at COMPUTE (extend routing-router-hat to the atom-id feature then -- the routing-routes-on-routing-accept pattern). Until then router-hat-router STAYS reserved (1b's re-flood is control-plane interest spread, NOT data/query route); routing-router-hat remains the FOUNDATION feature.
Plane-extraction (reuse strategy A) recommended as a SEPARATE extract-first round BEFORE COMPUTE so the route plane is single-sourced, not copy-pasted from LinkstateForwarder.

DEFERRED 1b tests (low risk, noted): re-flood CONTENT assertion (the re-stamped psid + literal keyexpr -- carrier is byte-faithful to the sibling + resolve_source_in is shared-tested, so frame_count coverage suffices; a decode helper would strengthen); still-reachable-source purge on a single face-down (two-path; shared purge_detached_interest_tier uses remove_link's detached set, linkstate-tested); self-sourced declare drop (resolve_source_in self-guard, linkstate-tested).

Round 311y11.decision_summary: R311y11 -- track 2 (macOS/Windows CI): added a `portability` job to .github/workflows/ci.yml -- a matrix [macos-latest, windows-latest] that NATIVELY cargo-checks the wz AP stack (GitHub provides real mac/win runners, not cross-compile). Catches the target_os-routed AP regressions the Linux `ci` job cannot reach -- chiefly the quic-datagram per-OS max_datagram MTU consts (linux/macos/windows arms). Scope = the portable feature surface (default tcp/udp set + transport-link-quic-datagram); deliberately does NOT enable transport-link-{unixpipe,vsock} off-Linux (those pull dep:libc / dep:tokio-vsock from the [target.linux] table, so enabling them on a non-Linux target is an invalid dep: reference by construction -- they are Linux-only backends by the R311y10/vsock design). cargo CHECK (not test), a build-sce.sh prefix (shell: bash for the Windows git-bash runner), the Linux-only Layer A-F deps (mnemosyne-cli/protoc/zenoh-pico) skipped. Locally verifiable + DONE: yaml syntax (python) + the cargo commands on Linux. The mac/win NATIVE result is verified by GH Actions on push (no local mac/win runner -- the user-accepted CI-verifies model; the [[feedback-ci-yaml-local-verify]] tension resolved -- local covers yaml+commands+Linux, CI covers mac/win-native). No Rust / run-ci.sh / inventory change.
changes_bullets: .github/workflows/ci.yml: + `portability` job (matrix macos-latest + windows-latest, fail-fast: false, timeout 30m). Steps: checkout (submodules recursive) + dtolnay/rust-toolchain stable + Swatinem/rust-cache + build-sce.sh (shell: bash) + cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio (default AP surface) + cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio --features transport-link-quic-datagram (per-OS MTU). All cargo/script steps shell: bash so they run on the Windows git-bash runner.

Job-level comment documents the scope rationale: portable surface only; transport-link-{unixpipe,vsock} NOT enabled off-Linux (the Linux-target-only dep:libc / dep:tokio-vsock would be an invalid dep: reference -- those are Linux-only backends verified by the Linux `ci` lanes C1al / vsock).
verification_bullets: yaml syntax: python yaml.safe_load OK; jobs = [ci, cross-mcu, portability].

cargo command soundness (Linux): cargo check -p wz-runtime-tokio (default) + --features transport-link-quic-datagram both Finished clean (exit 0) -- the commands the mac/win job runs are valid; only the mac/win NATIVE compile is the untested-locally variable (by nature -- macOS cannot run on a Linux host).

No Rust / run-ci.sh / inventory change: run-ci.sh's Linux lanes are unaffected (last green at R311y10), so full run-ci was NOT re-run for this CI-config + ledger-only round; the pre-commit validate-workspace gates the ledger append. The mac/win native verification is the GH Actions run on the next push (the user-accepted CI-verifies model; no local mac/win runner).

C5c proper: RouterForwarder gains forward_response (PendingQueries::peek -- more replies may follow -- rid rewritten to the recorded upstream rid, keyexpr B1-literalized, unicast to the recorded querier face via the tier-agnostic send_to_face) + forward_response_final (take frees the branch) + reap_timed_out_queries (tick-tail expired sweep synthesizing the Err("Timeout") + closing final per zenoh QueryCleanup) + Response/ResponseFinal dispatch arms + the timed_out witness -- a deliberate line-for-line MIRROR of the sibling LinkstateForwarder's proven return path (fidelity panel verified statement-identical + zenoh-faithful: peek==queries.rs:610 get, take==:643 remove, timeout Err+final==QueryCleanup::run :306-348). THE BLOCKER (correctness panel; CONFIRMED by direct read of zenoh dispatcher/queries.rs:189-201 + :667-682): BOTH forwarders forwarded EVERY branch's ResponseFinal upstream immediately, but zenoh clones ONE Arc<Query> into every branch's pending entry and finalize_pending_query propagates the upstream final ONLY when Arc::into_inner succeeds (the LAST branch) -- so a Query fanned to 2+ queryables (All / AllComplete / BestMatching's fall-back) had its querier's get() closed by the FASTEST branch's final, losing the other branches' replies (latent in the peer since the query atom -- every test used ONE queryable; made first-class by C5b's multi-leg fan). ROOT-CAUSE FIX in the shared PendingQueries SSOT: a per-logical-query Rc<QueryFan> (the single-task analog of the Arc<Query>) shared by every branch's entry; take/expired report `last` via Rc::into_inner (the last-out gate); remove_face returns the fans a face-down DRAINED so deregister synthesizes their closing finals (zenoh finalize_pending_queries -- previously a face-down of the last answering branch left the querier hanging to its own timeout, masked by the unaggregated-final bug). Both forwarders re-wired: forward_request/route_request allocate against one shared fan; forward_response_final + the reap forward the final only on `last` (Err stays per branch, zenoh runs one QueryCleanup per branch); deregister sends the drained-fan finals. Round 311y128.decision_summary: R311y128 -- ACTIVATION-4 (the last activation slice): the TWO-ROUTER DATA federation E2E. Two --router-hat nodes dial each other to form the router mesh, and a publisher behind R1 reaches a subscriber behind R2 over real loopback TCP (P1 -> R1 -> [router mesh] -> R2 -> P2) -- the R311y120 black-hole proof, composing the A2a cross-tier-native advertise + the master-gated cross-mesh bridge end to end. +2 tests on the existing Layer E7; a deterministic shutdown learned-subscriber-interest witness added to run_peer (E6 non-regressed). A FLAKE was caught + root-caused + fixed (the converge test terminated before the listener sampled its router-tier peak; fixed by awaiting BOTH routers' convergence; 12/12 clean post-fix), and the federation test's peak assertion was hardened to await convergence EXPLICITLY (impl-check fold). 2-agent DESIGN panel + a post-build IMPL check, all PASS. HONEST SCOPE: the DATA federation is E2E-proven; the QUERY-plane E2E is a NAMED follow-up (no mesh-mode query issuer + the single-session hardcoded-zid collision) while the query ROUTE is unit-proven (route_request/forward_response incl 2-router HRW); this does NOT claim master-vs-non-master ELECTION (each router is sole master of its own domain). Inventory UNCHANGED (router-hat-router stays reserved -- the run-mode active flip is a separate post-ACTIVATION decision).

verification_bullets: 2-agent PRE-CODE DESIGN panel (flake/no-vacuous / scope-fidelity-honesty): BOTH PASS. Panel A: all witnesses deterministic/self-healing/latched; transit pin airtight (BOTH routers forwarded + P2 received forces the full chain, cannot pass broken); MASTER DETERMINISM verified BY SOURCE — a Router neighbour joins routers_net ONLY, R2 never enters R1's linkstatepeers_net, so shared_nodes = {self} and each router is always master of its domain (no port/zid-derived election flip); flagged the P1-learned-interest witness lacked a shutdown latch (causally race-free but robustness-insurance) -> folded (added the shutdown latch). Panel B: the query-plane deferral is HONEST (verified no mesh query issuer in run_peer/run_router_hat + no forwarder query() issuer + the single-session hardcoded-zid 01020304 dedup collision); the query ROUTE is unit-proven (2-router HRW route_request tests); the data-federation test genuinely closes the named y120 cross-tier-bubble E2E obligation; 2 honesty guardrails (no master-ELECTION overclaim; state data-proven/query-deferred/route-unit-proven) -> folded into the doc + this ledger.

A FLAKE WAS CAUGHT + ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (no-flaky discipline; NOT a retry-pass): the converge test originally awaited only R1 (the dialer) then terminated, but R2 (the listener) registers R1 on ACCEPT and needs its next 250ms app-tick to sample peak_routers=2, so termination could beat R2's peak sample (2/5 runs failed). FIX: await BOTH routers routers-net converged (2) before terminating (the positive-edge guarantees the peak is latched). Round 311y14.decision_summary: R311y14 -- root-cause fix for the Layer Q qemu-load-flake that blocked the R311y12+y13 push (NOT a --no-verify bypass). The Q qemu runs are wall-clock-bounded by run_qemu_case's `timeout`; 10s was too tight -- under full-CI concurrent load (parallel cargo builds + several qemu instances) a ~2s-standalone MCU e2e slowed past 10s and Q.2.mps2-an500 flaked exit=124, aborting the pre-push hook. DIAGNOSED per [[feedback-layer-q-qemu-load-flake]] + [[feedback-no-flaky-ever]]: Layer Q PASSES standalone (Q_EXIT=0, every Q.0/Q.1/Q.2/Q.4 x mps2-an385/an500 lane incl the one that flaked), the R311y12/y13 changes are AP-only (quic/facade/unixpipe-doc/CI + inventory -- NOT in the MCU/mcu-qemu-demo build), and the R311y13 full run-ci had already passed Q -- so it is the documented load-flake, not a regression. Root-caused: raised the run_qemu_case wall-clock timeout 10s -> 30s (~15x the standalone runtime; absorbs CI-load slowdown while still bounding a genuine runaway loop -- a real hang runs the full 30s vs ~2s, distinguishable in the captured log). run-ci.sh only (the Q.0/Q.2/Q.4 shared helper); no code/inventory change.
changes_bullets: scripts/run-ci.sh run_qemu_case (the shared Q.0/Q.2/Q.4 qemu-run helper): `timeout 10` -> a named `local timeout_s=30` used by both the timeout call and the exit=124 why-message; 30s ~= 15x the ~2s standalone e2e, absorbing full-CI-load wall-clock slowdown while still bounding a genuine runaway.
scripts/run-ci.sh: updated the 3 stale '10s timeout' doc comments (the run_qemu_case header + the two Q.2 lane comments) to the 30s wall-clock timeout.
verification_bullets: DIAGNOSIS, not retry-until-green: `bash scripts/run-ci.sh --layer Q` standalone = PASS (Q_EXIT=0; Q.0/Q.1/Q.2/Q.4 x mps2-an385/an500 all PASS, incl the mps2-an500 that flaked under the pre-push load + 'all required layers pass'). The pre-push failure was a single layer -- Q.2.mps2-an500 exit=124 (10s wall-clock timeout) -- with C0..G + Z all passing. R311y12/y13 touch only AP/inventory (not the MCU build), and bcpe60xvr (the R311y13 full run-ci) had passed Q -> confirmed the documented Layer-Q-qemu-load-flake, not a regression.

ROOT CAUSE (spike + zenohd RUST_LOG=trace + pico direct-read): a zenoh(-pico) publisher/querier write-filter drops its own put/get LOCALLY until the router answers its declare-Interest with a matching DeclareSubscriber/DeclareQueryable, and wz dropped the Interest (_ => {}) so the filter never deactivated and the pico publisher behind wz never put data on the wire. FIX = respond_to_interest + dump_interest_{subs,qabls} replying per matching REMOTE decl + a DeclareFinal; aggregate keyed on the interest ke (pico equals-match), reply carries interest_id + FLAG_N_DECLARE_I, DeclareFinal carries interest_id (pico hard-errors without), queryable folds the merged complete bit. New reply builders in declare_build.rs (not the liveliness-gated local_token). Tier 1 only; FUTURE + Interest(Final) + peer forwarder + match-all + KEYEXPRS = round B. 3-agent DESIGN + 3-agent IMPL adversarial review, all arbitrated by direct-read; product code faithful+robust, 2 test-quality MAJORs fixed; one intentional divergence logged (aggregate qabl-info fold scope).

Round 311y15.decision_summary: R311y15 -- fix the 3 red CI jobs to green. (1) Layer A: the CI-pinned mnemosyne-cli (R415, schema <=9) could not read the current atomic store (schema_version 23), hard-failing 'schema version mismatch' on every push; bumped the pin to R584 (bb01cc6b, on mnemosyne origin/main), matching the locally-installed --path binary. (2) Layer Q: the mps2-an386/an500 qemu hang root-caused to a non-monotonic SystickClock::now_us() in mcu-qemu-demo -- on Cortex-M4F/M7 the SysTick exception is delayed past a wrap boundary so wraps lags and now_us steps backward, violating the ClockSource monotonic contract; the backward step makes a SleepFuture see now<deadline AFTER pop_expired consumed its timer entry, losing the wake and livelocking the cooperative loop (m3 softfloat never delays the ISR far enough). Fixed with a monotonic floor on the demo clock; corrected R311y14's wrong load-slowdown timeout justification. (3) portability/windows: sce-codegen's libxml crate needs native libxml2, absent on the windows runner -> vcpkg install libxml2:x64-windows-static-md + VCPKG_ROOT/VCPKGRS_TRIPLET. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh: MNEMOSYNE_REV 48117d24 (R415) -> bb01cc6b (R584). The R415 pin's CLI only read atomic-store schema <=9 while the store is now schema_version 23, so Layer A hard-failed "schema version mismatch: store=23 expected <= 9" on every push. The new pin matches the locally-installed --path binary (mnemosyne-cli 0.1.0 bb01cc6b, on mnemosyne origin/main); ci.yml + release.yml share this script so the one bump covers both.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs: SystickClock gains a last_us AtomicU64 monotonic floor; now_us() clamps its raw wraps-based reading up to the max previously returned. The raw reading steps BACKWARD when the SysTick exception is delayed past a wrap boundary on Cortex-M4F/M7 (lazy FP-context stacking + the cooperative executor's interrupt-disabling critical sections lengthen ISR latency), so `wraps` lags the hardware. The ClockSource trait REQUIRES monotonic now_us; the backward step is the root cause of the Layer Q hang.

scripts/run-ci.sh: corrected the run_qemu_case timeout comment. R311y14 misattributed the an386/an500 hang to CI load-slowdown and bumped the bound 10s->30s (a timeout never fixes a hang); the real cause was the non-monotonic clock above. 30s stays purely as a runaway/livelock backstop.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: the portability(windows) leg gains a vcpkg `libxml2:x64-windows-static-md` install + VCPKG_ROOT/VCPKGRS_TRIPLET export before build-sce.sh, so sce-codegen's libxml crate resolves its native libxml2 C dep on the windows-msvc runner (macOS + the Linux ci job find it via pkg-config). static-md = static libxml2 against the dynamic CRT, matching rustc-msvc /MD.

Round 311y15.publishable_decision_summary: R311y15 -- fix the 3 red CI jobs to green. (1) Layer A: the CI-pinned mnemosyne-cli (R415, schema <=9) could not read the current atomic store (schema_version 23), hard-failing 'schema version mismatch' on every push; bumped the pin to R584 (bb01cc6b, on mnemosyne origin/main), matching the locally-installed --path binary. (2) Layer Q: the mps2-an386/an500 qemu hang root-caused to a non-monotonic SystickClock::now_us() in mcu-qemu-demo -- on Cortex-M4F/M7 the SysTick exception is delayed past a wrap boundary so wraps lags and now_us steps backward, violating the ClockSource monotonic contract; the backward step makes a SleepFuture see now<deadline AFTER pop_expired consumed its timer entry, losing the wake and livelocking the cooperative loop (m3 softfloat never delays the ISR far enough). Fixed with a monotonic floor on the demo clock; corrected R311y14's wrong load-slowdown timeout justification. (3) portability/windows: sce-codegen's libxml crate needs native libxml2, absent on the windows runner -> vcpkg install libxml2:x64-windows-static-md + VCPKG_ROOT/VCPKGRS_TRIPLET. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
publishable_changes_bullets: scripts/install-mnemosyne-cli.sh: MNEMOSYNE_REV 48117d24 (R415) -> bb01cc6b (R584). The new pin matches the locally-installed --path binary (mnemosyne-cli 0.1.0 bb01cc6b, on mnemosyne origin/main); ci.yml + release.yml share this script so the one bump covers both.

deploy/mcu-qemu-demo/src/main.rs: SystickClock gains a last_us AtomicU64 monotonic floor; now_us() clamps its raw wraps-based reading up to the max previously returned. The raw reading steps BACKWARD when the SysTick exception is delayed past a wrap boundary on Cortex-M4F/M7 (lazy FP-context stacking + the cooperative executor's interrupt-disabling critical sections lengthen ISR latency), so `wraps` lags the hardware. The ClockSource trait REQUIRES monotonic now_us; the backward step is the root cause of the Layer Q hang.

scripts/run-ci.sh: corrected the run_qemu_case timeout comment. R311y14 misattributed the an386/an500 hang to CI load-slowdown and bumped the bound 10s->30s (a timeout never fixes a hang); the real cause was the non-monotonic clock above. 30s stays purely as a runaway/livelock backstop.

Round 311y150.decision_summary: R311y150 -- qabl FUTURE-push (part A of the "y146 push-family completion"): a STRUCTURE/correctness forwarder mechanism (inventory-neutral, NO cfg gate) that closes the QUERY-plane analog of the y146 pub-before-sub hole. (1) PRESENCE: a querier-BEFORE-queryable querier's write-filter now deactivates when a matching queryable is learned later (mesh / client / self-local). (2) VALUE: a Z_QUERY_TARGET_ALL_COMPLETE querier's filter deactivates only on a complete=true reply (pico filtering.c:206), so when the FOLDED completeness flips false->true wz RE-pushes the SAME interned decl id carrying the new merged info (zenoh propagate_simple_queryable, linkstate_peer/queries.rs:180-198) -- else the ALL_COMPLETE querier black-holes. The subscriber store was GENERALIZED to FutureInterestStore<V> (subs V=() presence-only, qabls V=QueryableInfo value-aware) -- the y144 emit_current_interest_replies<V> precedent; V=() -> the value-change arm is unreachable, so sub behavior is provably unchanged (the 13 sub tests re-run with (), 588 lib tests green). Three DESIGN-panel-caught holes fixed before code: HOLE 1 (the push carries the RE-FOLDED merged info via merged_qabl_info, NOT a single source's raw -- else a downgrade re-arms the filter = black-hole); HOLE 2 (a new UNSTAMPED non-zero-id builder for the unsolicited push); HOLE 3 (the CURRENT-dump FUTURE branch emits the interned non-zero id so wire==seed). Both forwarders wired symmetrically; the peer is counterless + has no client-qabl plane (client declares dropped in resolve_source -- confirmed by direct-read arbitration when two IMPL agents disagreed), so its self-local + mesh fires are complete. IMPL(3)+DESIGN(3) panels direct-read-arbitrated: the IMPL pass caught one router fold divergence (merged folded the querier's own co-hosted queryable while the current dump excludes it -> a benign monotone-up spurious re-push), fixed by threading the destination face into pushes_for_new's value_of so merged EXCLUDES it (seed==push by construction). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

Now each handler field is Rc<RefCell<Handler>>; dispatch snapshots the matching Rc::clones under a SHORT borrow(), DROPS it, then invokes via try_borrow_mut() -- the single-task analog of zenoh Arc<Callback> cloned out of the guarded map before cb.call. A re-entrant register lands after the snapshot (excluded from the in-flight batch); a re-entrant undeclare (incl. self, incl. a sibling) drops the Vec Rc while the snapshot clone keeps the mid-fire handler alive; the ONE irreducible case -- a handler synchronously re-entering ITS OWN dispatch -- is SKIPPED by try_borrow_mut (a running FnMut cannot be aliased; faithful async queue-and-redeliver is the named follow-up). Now each handler field is Rc<RefCell<Handler>>; dispatch snapshots the matching Rc::clones under a SHORT borrow(), DROPS it, then invokes via try_borrow_mut() -- the single-task analog of zenoh Arc<Callback> cloned out of the guarded map before cb.call. A re-entrant register lands after the snapshot (excluded from the in-flight batch); a re-entrant undeclare (incl. self, incl. a sibling) drops the Vec Rc while the snapshot clone keeps the mid-fire handler alive; the ONE irreducible case -- a handler synchronously re-entering ITS OWN dispatch -- is SKIPPED by try_borrow_mut (a running FnMut cannot be aliased; faithful async queue-and-redeliver is the named follow-up). Signature-stable (register pub sig unchanged, wrap internal; 12 callers incl 2 wz-ap-demo unchanged). 3-agent DESIGN panel converged pre-code (FAITHFUL-HARDENING, not YAGNI -- zenoh queryable callback REQUIRES re-entry via query.reply()); 3-agent IMPL panel post-build (borrow CONFIRMED-SOUND, regression NO-REGRESSION, test-rigor HOLES-FOUND both fixed). 6 new re-entrancy tests; diagnose-first neuter->all 6 RefCell-already-borrowed.
publishable_changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: LocalQueryable.handler + LocalSubscriber.handler changed Box<dyn FnMut> -> Rc<RefCell<Box<dyn FnMut>>> (the aliases LocalQueryHandler/LocalSubscriberHandler stay the RefCell inner type). register_local_queryable/register_local_subscriber wrap the caller's Box in Rc::new(RefCell::new(handler)) INTERNALLY -- the pub signatures (handler: LocalQueryHandler/LocalSubscriberHandler) are byte-for-byte unchanged, so all 12 callers (2 in wz-ap-demo/src/runner.rs + 10 tests) pass Box::new(...) unchanged.

dispatch_local_queryables + dispatch_local_subscribers rewritten collect-drop-invoke: snapshot the matching handlers' Rc::clones under a SHORT borrow(), DROP it, then invoke each via try_borrow_mut() + (**h)(...). The queryable AllComplete gate rewrote from a `continue`-skip to an equivalent .filter(|lq| !matches!(AllComplete) || lq.complete) (De Morgan, verified for all 4 combos); reply order + matched-but-silent-still-emits-ResponseFinal + return-true are preserved (matched.is_empty() == the old !matched). The undeclare_{subscription,queryable} retain paths are UNTOUCHED (they read .keyexpr only).

6 new re-entrancy tests (linkstate_forward): reentrant-register (sub + qabl; the snapshot EXCLUDES the newly-registered decl from the in-flight batch, fires on the NEXT), reentrant-self-undeclare (sub + qabl; the snapshot Rc keeps the mid-fire handler alive), self-echo-skip (a handler re-driving its own matching Put is SKIPPED by try_borrow_mut -- hardened with a 2nd subscriber B asserting B fires twice [inner+outer] and A once, distinguishing skip-exercised from an inner no-op), sibling-undeclare (A undeclares a not-yet-fired B; B STILL fires this batch via the snapshot Rc, gone the next -- isolates snapshot-Rc liveness).

Doc: the dispatch_local_queryables/_subscribers caveats rewrote the old "would PANIC / re-openable follow-up" to the new re-entrancy contract (register/undeclare/self-undeclare safe; synchronous self-echo skipped); a Cost note records the snapshot Vec allocs only on >=1 local match (Rust Vec lazy) with SmallVec/SingleOrVec as a re-openable micro-opt (off the mesh hot path). The struct handler fields carry the Rc<RefCell> rationale.
clippy fixes folded in: (&mut **h) -> (**h) x2 (needless borrow) and the AllComplete filter bool-simplify.
