Round 311y160.decision_summary: R311y160 -- §5.26 rest-http-bridge BUILT (the one genuine net-new atom the R311y159 A3-audit found in the P4 LAYER-3 breadth track; user chose #1 rest build first). New AP-only crate wz-rest: a HAND-ROLLED HTTP/1.1 server (ZERO external HTTP dep -- user chose hand-rolled over hyper/axum, an even-lighter superset) bridging HTTP to a wz TokioSession -- GET/POST->Session::query (JSON reply array or ?_raw), PUT/PATCH->publish Put, DELETE->publish Del, URL path->keyexpr (canonize + @/local->@/<zid> via SSOT zid_to_zenoh_hex). Compile-time-composed superset of zenoh's dlopen .so tide plugin (no plugin host-trait/ABI/lifecycle FSM); in its own crate so no_std/MCU builds never pull it. Trusted-localhost scope (127.0.0.1 bind = exposure-boundary NOT auth, documented). rest-http-bridge reserved->active (A3 cfg site = the wz facade `pub use wz_rest as rest`); the feature forwards the EXACT wz-runtime-tokio set the DESIGN panel found load-bearing (codec-push so PUT/DELETE emit -- else silent Ok(0); codec-response-final so a GET completes; query-timeout; query-get; pubsub-encoding; query-consolidation; query-selector-parameters). 3-agent DESIGN panel (concurrency/security/API-fidelity) caught the wire-broken feature set (pubsub-put/delete were the WRONG gates) + 5 blockers pre-code; 3-agent IMPL panel caught + fixed a real pending-query LEAK (ReplyHandle is inert Copy-u64, no sweep wired -> added Session::sweep_expired_queries + serve's sweep task) + 2 SSOT reinventions (zid hex, JSON escaper) + fidelity gaps. WIRE E2E proven over two TCP-linked sessions (diagnose-first neuter FAILs). full run-ci deferred to push; A3 PASS (active 115->116); validate orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: NEW crate crates/wz-rest/ (AP-only, SPDX LGPL/Commercial): src/lib.rs (serve/serve_on + the AbortOnDrop sweep task + handle_connection with a per-connection read/write timeout + the SECURITY doc-note), src/http.rs (hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 request reader + Response writer: bounded 8KiB head/8MiB body, the must-handle malformed set -> clean 400/413/431/501/505, the 411-fix [absent Content-Length = empty body], 204 omits Content-Length, CORS), src/json.rs (hand-rolled JSON output + base64, routing string-escape through the SSOT wz_session_core::json::escape_into), src/bridge.rs (dispatch GET/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS, path_to_keyexpr, the query reply-collection via oneshot).
crates/wz-rest/Cargo.toml: deps wz-runtime-tokio (the load-bearing feature set) + wz-session-core (encoding + keyexpr_canon + zid_hex + json SSOTs) + tokio; dev-dep wz-runtime-tokio-test-support.
crates/Cargo.toml: wz-rest added to workspace members (covered by Layer C1 `cargo test --workspace` + C2 clippy).

crates/wz/Cargo.toml: `wz-rest = { optional = true }` + `rest-http-bridge = [dep:wz-rest, runtime-tokio, wz-runtime-tokio?/{transport-unicast,query-get,codec-response-final,codec-push,query-timeout,pubsub-encoding,query-consolidation,query-selector-parameters}]`.
crates/wz/src/lib.rs: `#[cfg(feature=rest-http-bridge)] pub use wz_rest as rest;` -- the A3 active cfg site + the public bridge entry point.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs: NEW `#[cfg(feature=query-get)] Session::sweep_expired_queries(&self) -> usize` (reply-registry deadline sweep + deferred-fire drain via the session's own clock; a line-for-line mirror of the wz-ap-demo sweep task) -- serve spawns a 1s-cadence caller so a GET whose wire ResponseFinal never arrives cannot leak its pending entry.
docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json: rest-http-bridge reserved->active with the built reason (mechanism + feature forwards + trusted-localhost scope); rest-sse-subscribe stays reserved (next round).
verification_bullets: wz-rest tests: 6 unit (base64 vectors, value_string null/utf8/binary, sample_object shape, split_target, path_to_keyexpr strip+canonicalise + @/local SSOT hex) + 1 WIRE E2E (rest_bridge_put_get_delete_traverse_the_wire) all pass. The wire test drives PUT/GET/DELETE over a real TCP socket against a SEPARATE session (subscriber receives PUT+DELETE, queryable answers GET as JSON) -- proving codec-push emit + query + codec-response-final completion over the wire (a loopback-only test would pass with those features OFF).

Diagnose-first: neutering the PUT publish (return 200 without publishing) FAILED the wire test at the subscriber-received assertion after the full 12.7s retry budget -- the test genuinely validates wire delivery, not a false pass.

3-agent DESIGN panel (concurrency+crate-structure / security+HTTP-correctness / wz-zenoh API-fidelity), direct-read arbitrated: all SUPPORT the approach; caught pre-code the wire-broken feature set (codec-push not pubsub-put; codec-response-final for GET completion; query-timeout to bound a silent GET), the missing Session::zid() (-> serve takes zid explicitly), a mandatory per-connection read timeout, the RFC-wrong 411 rule, and the missing Content-Type response header.

3-agent IMPL panel (correctness+panic-safety / HTTP-parser-fidelity / wz-API-fidelity+SSOT), direct-read arbitrated: parser is panic-clean and implements the full must-handle set; CONFIRMED + FIXED a pending-query LEAK (ReplyHandle is a Copy u64 with no Drop -> the held-handle comment was false; no reply sweep was wired -> added Session::sweep_expired_queries + serve's sweep task), the zid_hex bug (naive per-byte != zenoh LE->u128->BE hex -> @/local missed the adminspace; now the SSOT zid_to_zenoh_hex), and the json_escape SSOT reinvention/desync (now wz_session_core::json::escape_into); folded fidelity fixes (consolidation None on _time, default encoding on absent Content-Type, empty payload -> JSON null, 204 omits Content-Length).
clippy -p wz-rest --all-targets -D warnings: clean. cargo fmt --check: clean (wz-rest + wz-runtime-tokio, exit 0). wz-runtime-tokio builds with the new sweep method (default features).

Composition: `cargo build -p wz --features rest-http-bridge` EXIT=0 (the facade re-export + feature forwards compose). Layer A3 audit-catalog-status.sh PASS (AUDIT_EXIT=0; active 115->116; no reserved-but-gated drift). validate_workspace: T1 orphan new=+0, style unchanged.
MCU-safe by construction: wz-rest is AP-only (std+tokio), in its own crate; no no_std/MCU crate depends on it, so the hand-rolled HTTP server never enters those builds.
carry_forward_bullets: R311y160 = §5.26 rest-http-bridge BUILT + active (the one genuine net-new atom the R311y159 A3-audit found). New AP-only crate wz-rest = a hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 -> wz Session bridge (GET->query/PUT->put/DELETE->delete), ZERO external HTTP dep, trusted-localhost scope, in its own crate (MCU-safe). Added Session::sweep_expired_queries (core) so serve is self-contained against the pending-query leak. WIRE E2E + diagnose-first proven. rest-http-bridge reserved->active; the DESIGN+IMPL panels caught a wire-broken feature set + a real leak + 2 SSOT reinventions before commit.

NEXT in the #1 track = rest-sse-subscribe (still reserved): the Accept: text/event-stream GET path -> Session::declare_subscriber streaming as SSE events (data: JSON sample per push). The bridge already returns 501 for text/event-stream (documented placeholder). Its own round: needs a streaming response body (chunked or connection-held) fed from the subscriber callback via a channel, + a WIRE E2E asserting streamed samples. Feature rest-sse-subscribe = [rest-http-bridge, ...declare-subscriber already in the deps].

DISCLOSED (deferred, trusted-localhost-acceptable, none requested): no `Expect: 100-continue` handling (a large PUT incurs ~1s curl delay); no concurrent-connection cap/semaphore in serve_on (each conn is 15s read-bounded); the reply fan-in Vec + JSON body are unbounded (a wildcard GET could accumulate large -- acceptable for trusted-localhost); JSON `value` is always a string not zenoh's nested-JSON embedding (documented); `timestamp` always null (ReplyView has no timestamp accessor); browser cross-origin PUT/DELETE preflight is answered (OPTIONS->204 + Allow-Methods). A dedicated silent-GET-reap test for the sweep is deferred (the sweep is a line-for-line mirror of the proven wz-ap-demo sweep over tested primitives; a real test would cost the 10s query timeout).
The #2 and #3 tracks remain queued (user: 1->2->3): #2 = §5.22/§5.27 out-of-scope confirm-only reason sweep; #3 = named router follow-ups (peer future-push cross-impl e2e / D4 / re-entrancy async).

Round 311y161.decision_summary:
R311y161 -- §5.26 rest-sse-subscribe BUILT (the SSE half of the wz-rest REST bridge; finishes the #1 rest track). A GET with Accept: text/event-stream becomes Session::declare_subscriber, each received sample streamed to the HTTP client as `event: <PUT|DELETE>
data: <json-sample>

` until the client disconnects (the Subscriber handle drops -> UndeclareSubscriber). The subscriber callback (drive-loop task) hands samples to the socket-writing task via a BOUNDED channel (drop-newest on overflow); a 15s SSE-comment keepalive doubles as the disconnect probe. Gated behind wz-rest's rest-sse-subscribe feature (independently toggleable from the request/response bridge -- feature off => a text/event-stream GET returns 501). dispatch now returns an Outcome { Response | Sse } so handle_connection can hand the SSE case the write half. reserved->active (A3 cfg site = `#[cfg(feature=rest-sse-subscribe)] mod sse` + the Outcome::Sse arm); the wz facade `rest-sse-subscribe = [rest-http-bridge, wz-rest?/rest-sse-subscribe]`, and wz-rest's feature pulls declare-subscriber + pubsub-put/delete. New CI Layer C1az drives the SSE feature (the sse unit + rest_sse_wire_e2e tests are feature-gated, invisible to the default Layer C1 workspace test). 2-agent IMPL panel (concurrency/lifecycle + SSE-protocol/fidelity), direct-read arbitrated: framing/headers/event-name(PUT/DELETE)/data-shape FAITHFUL + teardown-on-all-paths clean; FIXED an unbounded-channel memory risk (slow-but-progressing consumer -> bounded channel) + corrected an honest timestamp-null disclosure. §5.26 rest now 2/2 active; A3 PASS (active 116->117); validate orphan new=+0. full run-ci deferred to push.
changes_bullets:
crates/wz-rest/src/sse.rs (NEW, feature rest-sse-subscribe): the SSE streamer -- declare_subscriber whose callback try_sends each sample into a bounded mpsc; the socket task selects between rx.recv() and a 15s keepalive, writing `event: <PUT|DELETE>
data: <json>

` (flushed per event) until a write error tears the subscriber down; format_event + write_all_timed helpers + 2 unit tests.

crates/wz-rest/src/bridge.rs: dispatch now returns `Outcome { Response(Response) | #[cfg(rest-sse-subscribe)] Sse(String) }`; is_event_stream + a cfg-split sse_outcome (feature-on -> resolve keyexpr -> Sse; feature-off -> 501). Removed the old inline SSE-501 from handle_query.

crates/wz-rest/src/lib.rs: `#[cfg(feature=rest-sse-subscribe)] mod sse`; handle_connection matches Outcome and, for Sse, hands sse::stream the write half. SECURITY docs gained the SSE live-tap amplification + no-connection-cap note.

crates/wz-rest/src/json.rs: corrected the timestamp-null justification -- the GET path's ReplyView genuinely lacks a timestamp accessor, but the SSE path's SampleView carries one, so rendering it (zenoh's uhlc-datetime) is a disclosed follow-up, not a surface limitation.
crates/wz-rest/Cargo.toml: `[features] rest-sse-subscribe = [wz-runtime-tokio/declare-subscriber, /pubsub-put, /pubsub-delete]`.

crates/wz-rest/tests/rest_sse_wire_e2e.rs (NEW, gated): a remote publish over a real TCP link streamed to an HTTP client as an SSE event (the streaming twin of the request/response wire test).

scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer C1az (layer_c1az_cargo_test_rest_sse) runs `cargo test -p wz-rest --features rest-sse-subscribe` + SSE clippy (the feature-gated SSE tests are invisible to C1's `cargo test --workspace`).

verification_bullets: wz-rest tests WITH rest-sse-subscribe: 8 unit (json 3 + bridge 3 + sse 2: format_event PUT + Del-empty-null) + rest_bridge_wire_e2e + rest_sse_wire_e2e all pass. The SSE wire test drives GET Accept: text/event-stream against serve_on on one session while a SEPARATE TCP-linked session publishes -- a streamed `event: PUT` carrying the payload PROVES the subscriber declaration propagated over the wire AND the remote push routed back through the SSE subscriber (a loopback-only test could not).

Diagnose-first: neutering sse::stream to return before writing any event FAILED the SSE wire test fast (0.00s, the client reads EOF, no event) -- the test genuinely validates SSE streaming, not a false pass.

A forwarder-local subscriber that, mid-callback, re-drives a matching Put to its OWN pattern (self-echo) was DROPPED by the y156 try_borrow_mut skip; zenoh never drops a self-echo (its callback subscriber recurses, its default FifoChannel requeues). Now the busy handler Rc + an owned Sample::from_view copy are queued in a bounded sub_redelivery ring and REDELIVERED at the outermost forward() exit (a forward_depth re-entrancy guard), making the wz synchronous callback subscriber behave like zenoh DEFAULT channel handler; overflow is drop-OLDEST past SELF_ECHO_QUEUE_CAP=256 (a RingChannel) since single-task backpressure would self-deadlock, so an unconditional self-republisher spins bounded, never a hang/stack-overflow. undeclare_subscription purges a retracted handler pending echoes (IMPL-panel probes 4+5). 3-agent DESIGN panel (build-vs-defer, arbitrated to BUILD on the north-star faithfulness override) + 3-agent IMPL panel (borrow-panic CONFIRMED-SAFE, SSOT reuse-of-deferred_fire rejected on 3 blockers, faithfulness verified). SUB plane only -- the QUERY twin still drops (ResponseFinal is eager; redelivery there needs a Reply-before-Final hold, a named follow-up). Correctness-only; NO inventory flip. Diagnose-first + 3 tests; linkstate 181/192 green, clippy+fmt clean.

Round 311y170.decision_summary: R311y170 -- §5.21 routing-token-tables SLICE-1: the router liveliness-TOKEN dual-tier INGEST plane, the TOKEN TWIN of the router_subs/router_qabls declaration tables (zenoh hat/router/token.rs). A sourced DeclareToken on a MESH face registers the source in the inbound tier's token table (Router->router_tokens, Peer->linkstatepeer_tokens; both LinkstatepeerInterest<()> -- tokens carry NO value) + within-tier re-flood, reusing the shared ingest_interest<()> core DIRECTLY (NOT the ingest_subscription wrapper, whose cross-tier-bubble + future-push tail is a later slice). REGISTER-ONLY: the sourced UndeclareToken withdraw is deferred (wz UndeclToken codec = header+id only, no ext_wire_expr -- the qabl-plane-before-the-ext-codec pattern); an inbound sourced UndeclareToken from a peer router is dropped at forward()'s catch-all, and the face-down purge_detached_interest_tier (EXTENDED here to drain the token tables) is the departed-source safety net. routing-token-tables reserved->ACTIVE (real cfg site: #[cfg(feature=routing-token-tables)] fields+ingest+arm+purge). cfg composes routing-router-hat only (NOT liveliness-token: the DeclToken codec already rides routing-peer->codec-declare). Cross-tier bubble + client propagation + token-interest + topology-reconcile = later slices. 2-agent DESIGN (mirror-verifies-template caught the purge-leak + wrapper-tail traps pre-code) + 2-agent IMPL (both SHIP, no blocker). 648 lib + 6 token tests green; clippy ON/OFF/standalone; A3 active 117->118; fmt; orphan new=+0. full run-ci at push.

The self-delivery guard || dst.zid==tables.zid is a faithful NO-OP in the pure forwarder + documented. DEFERRED (NAMED, slice-4b): the withdraw->reader-notify twin of undeclare_push_subs (liveliness stale-live residual). Code+test only; inventory UNCHANGED. Round 311y175.decision_summary: R311y175 -- §5.21 routing-token-tables slice-5: topology-reconcile withdraw->reader-notify = the LAST slice (the token-tables 5-slice track is COMPLETE). SCOPE (verify-first, 2-agent DESIGN panel + direct read): the three zenoh reconcile fns map as -- token_tree_change ALREADY DONE (slice-2 recompute_and_advertise_tier), token_remove_node mesh-drain + self-cross-tier-withdraw ALREADY DONE (slice-1/2 purge_detached_interest_tier), token_linkstate_change OUT-OF-SCOPE (router_peers_failover_brokering-gated; wz has NO failover-brokering, and the SUB twin pubsub_linkstate_change is ALSO unbuilt -- a symmetric omission of a mechanism wz lacks). So the ONLY net-new is undeclare_push_token (+ any_token_matches) -- the client-forget half of token_remove_node (zenoh propagate_forget_simple_token arm 1) + the graceful withdraw-notify, the token twin of undeclare_push_subs. Wired at 5 removal sites: 3 mirror the sub sites (graceful mesh withdraw_token, graceful client withdraw_client_token, ungraceful purge_detached_interest_tier) + 2 token-SPECIFIC the sub plane lacks -- (a) ingest_client_token id-reuse displacement (client_subs is a HashSet that cannot displace, so the 3-sub-site enumeration structurally misses it, IMPL-panel F1 catch) and (b) deregister client-FACE-DOWN (subs leave this a benign over-deliver gap; a liveliness token's stale-live is NOT benign -- zenoh close_face retracts on face-down for BOTH planes, mod.rs:498/541). This CLOSES the liveliness stale-live residual (the deferred slice-4b): a future-push reader told a token appeared is now told when it withdraws by ANY path. Code+test only; inventory UNCHANGED. CI Layer C1ay green (169 router_forward tests + both clippy arms); 2-agent DESIGN (scope claim verified correct) + 2-agent IMPL (VERDICT ship/faithful) panels; diagnose-first confirmed the any_token_matches gate + the client-face-down 4th site are load-bearing.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/router_forward.rs: new `any_token_matches` (twin of any_sub_matches -- the GLOBAL post-withdrawal "still backed" existence check: both mesh tiers matching_entries + client_tokens VALUES intersect, no face exclusion) + `undeclare_push_token` (twin of undeclare_push_subs -- future_tokens.forgets_for_withdrawn + send build_undeclare_token(id) id-keyed no-ext, zenoh propagate_forget_simple_token arm 1). Both `#[cfg(feature="routing-token-tables")]`.

Wired undeclare_push_token at 5 token-removal sites: withdraw_token (graceful mesh), withdraw_client_token (graceful client, unconditional-on-removal), purge_detached_interest_tier token loop (ungraceful detach) -- these 3 mirror the sub undeclare_push_subs sites; PLUS 2 token-SPECIFIC sites the sub plane lacks: ingest_client_token id-reuse displacement (client_subs is a HashSet that cannot displace) + deregister client-face-down (subs leave a benign over-deliver gap; tokens close stale-live).

deregister RESTRUCTURED: the departed client_tokens keyexprs are HOISTED, future_tokens.purge_face(id) runs FIRST (so the departed face is not self-notified), THEN undeclare_push_token per departed ke -- before the `link == None` early-return so a Client face is covered. The "no undeclare is owed" comment corrected: the DEPARTED face owes itself none (pico clears its own filter), the SURVIVING readers ARE owed one.
Imported build_undeclare_token (id-keyed) into the router token declare_build import group.

Withdraw DOWNGRADES-or-undeclares via withdraw_mesh_qabl_if_unbacked (undeclare_queryable REWIRED through it so a self-native retract with a surviving client downgrades, not nukes). changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs: new `client_qabls: RefCell<HashMap<FaceId, HashMap<String, QueryableInfo>>>` field (the query-plane twin of D4a's client_subs) + `ingest_client_queryable` (self-source a client DeclareQueryable under self_zid carrying the MERGED info, value-diff-gated flood + push_future_queryable(Some(inbound)) self-echo exclude) + `derived_self_qabl_info` (ADVERTISE-side fold over self-native local_queryables + client_qabls; deliberately NOT the global `merged_qabl_info`, which would pollute the advert with a remote's completeness) + `withdraw_mesh_qabl_if_unbacked` (Some=DOWNGRADE re-advertise the surviving merged info / None=withdraw self from qabls + UndeclareQueryable + undeclare_push_qabls) + `withdraw_client_queryable`.

forward_request RESTRUCTURED (the crux): computes `client_candidates` (co-attached client queryables matching the query, distance-1) then selects `(children /*mesh*/, client_targets)` per QueryTarget -- a COMPLETE client wins BestMatching (suppresses the mesh best), else the mesh complete-best, else the All-fallback fans mesh + all clients; All/AllComplete fan mesh directions + all matching clients. The new `forward_request_to_client_queryables` fans the Request to each client face allocating a pending qid sharing the ONE QueryFan, so the reply routes back via the UNCHANGED forward_response + the closing final aggregates last-out across mesh AND client branches. UNCONDITIONAL (single-net peer, no master gate). The sync dispatch_local_queryables (self-hosted admin GETs) runs only when there is zero async branch.

declare_queryable REWIRED to register the DERIVED merge (not raw `local(complete)`) so a coexisting client queryable is not CLOBBERED (the single (ke,self_zid) qabls slot OVERWRITES); undeclare_queryable REWIRED through `withdraw_mesh_qabl_if_unbacked` (a self-native retract with a surviving client DOWNGRADES, not nukes; the None arm preserves the old full-undeclare + idempotent forget for the self-native-only case, byte-for-byte).

forward() Declare/Undecl(Queryable) arms gained `is_client_face` forks (pure-add: client -> ingest/withdraw_client_queryable, mesh -> forward_queryable{,_undeclare}); `deregister` drains client_qabls (per-ke withdraw_mesh_qabl_if_unbacked, same hoist as the client-sub drain); `client_qabls_seen` accessor (the client_subs_seen twin, consumed by the unit tests); the stale "no client-qabl plane / peer drops client declares" docstrings on merged_qabl_info / push_future_queryable / undeclare_push_qabls corrected (a client qabl now folds in via the self_zid aggregate slot).
verification_bullets: 7 unit tests, all pass (167 peer-lib tests total): U1 ingest->advert (client DeclareQueryable lands in client_qabls + advertised under self_zid carrying its completeness) / U2 composed delivery (a routed Query is forwarded to the co-attached client queryable + its Reply routes back to the querier with the querier's rid) / U2b a COMPLETE client wins BestMatching over a COEXISTING mesh queryable on the same ke -- the black-hole the restructure fixes / U3 upgrade-merge (a 2nd complete co-host UPGRADES the advert to complete) / U4 downgrade withdraw (the complete contributor leaves -> a DOWNGRADED DeclareQueryable re-flood, NOT an UndeclareQueryable) / U5+U7 deregister purge (client face down -> client_qabls drained + the last backer's mesh advert withdrawn via a sourced UndeclareQueryable) / U6 shared-slot rewire (a self-native undeclare_queryable with a surviving client queryable DOWNGRADES-not-nukes the shared self_zid advert).

Round 311y18.decision_summary: R311y18 -- bump vendor/sce pin ba65f7a1b -> a51b5e7e1 to pick up the SCE fix 'Make sce:template content model UPA-deterministic for libxml2 2.15', the FINAL Windows-portability blocker. vcpkg's libxml2 2.15.3 enforces XSD UPA strictly and rejected SCE's sce-forge-ext.xsd <sce:template> content model (an sce:param particle ahead of an xs:any ##any wildcard = non-deterministic), failing sce-codegen at schema-compile (exit 2) on every generate; Linux/macOS lenient libxml2 (<=2.11) tolerated it. Root-caused by direct SCE read + reported (not worked-around in wz per the SCE-readonly rule); SCE collapsed <sce:template> to a lone ##any wildcard (param ordering stays enforced by the template.rs expander SSOT) + added a determinism guard test. Bump-only, no wz code change. Layer B byte-golden PASS (codegen output unchanged); statechart codegen + workspace build clean locally; the libxml2-2.15 acceptance verifies on the Windows CI push. validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: vendor/sce: submodule pin ba65f7a1b -> a51b5e7e1 (SCE fix "Make sce:template content model UPA-deterministic for libxml2 2.15", one commit on SCE origin/main atop the prior pin). No other SCE delta; no wz-side text change (the two ba65f7a1b mentions are a HISTORICAL footprint comment in check-footprint.sh:134 and a `pin >= ba65f7a1b` lower-bound in wz-session-core/src/vle.rs:14 -- both still correct since a51b5e7e1 > ba65f7a1b).

SCE fix provenance (direct read, SCE pin a51b5e7e1): schemas/sce-forge-ext.xsd <sce:template> dropped the `<xs:element ref="sce:param" minOccurs=0 maxOccurs=unbounded>` particle, leaving the lone `<xs:any namespace="##any" lax>` wildcard. A named particle ahead of an ##any wildcard is a non-deterministic content model (XSD 1.0 UPA violation) that libxml2 >= 2.15 rejects at schema-compile; the param-ordering grammar stays enforced by the sce-build/src/template.rs expander (the structural SSOT), and SCE added sce-build/tests/xsd_content_model_determinism.rs as a regression guard. The other 8 ##any in the schema are lone wildcards (no preceding named particle) = already deterministic, untouched.

Mutex-poison → skip-this-sweep (deliberate divergence from DigestPublisher's .expect — a deferred GC is benign). Round 311y186.decision_summary: R311y186 -- wz<->zenohd ALIGN-path storage wildcard-update e2e: a wildcard-only cross-impl test caught + fixed a real wz driver bug where storage_aligner_service.rs::decode_reply extracted the retrieval value only for Action::Put, dropping it for Action::WildcardPut, so the kernel's align-path WildcardPut arm (materializes only when a value is present) never fired and a pulled zenohd wildcard-update EVENT never registered on the receiver (wildcard_registry_lens stuck at (0,0) cross-impl). Fix = value-extraction guard Put | WildcardPut(_), mirroring zenohd reply_event_retrieval. Completes the storage wildcard-updates track (4 build slices + LIVE pico leg y185 + ALIGN leg y186); no inventory/atom status change.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/storage_aligner_service.rs::decode_reply — the retrieval value-extraction guard widened from `Action::Put` to `Action::Put | Action::WildcardPut(_)`. A WildcardPut retrieval carries its value (zenohd `reply_event_retrieval` reads it from `wildcard_puts`, replication/core/aligner_query.rs:320-334); dropping it left `value=None`, so the kernel's align-path WildcardPut arm (storage_state.rs:1344, which materializes only `if let Some(value)`) never fired and a real zenohd wildcard-update EVENT never registered on the receiver. +11-line comment naming the strand and the zenohd Put+WildcardPut / Delete+WildcardDelete value symmetry.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/storage_aligner_service.rs (tests) — new driver regression unit test `decode_reply_wildcard_put_retrieval_carries_payload_and_encoding`: a WildcardPut `Retrieval` reply's payload+encoding must be extracted off the ReplyView (the guard above), mirroring the existing Put case; the Delete/WildcardDelete no-value cases already guard the negative.

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_zenohd_storage_replication.rs — new Layer E `--ignored` cross-impl e2e `wz_replica_registers_wildcard_event_from_zenohd_storage_manager`: a foreign pico `z_pub` seeds a WILDCARD-ONLY update (`data/test/wild/**`) into an empty zenohd storage-manager (no concrete key, so the only replicated event is the wildcard-keyed one); an empty in-process wz replica + `spawn_digest_aligner` pulls it off zenohd's aligner and must register it. Poll-on-condition `wildcard_registry_lens().0 >= 1` (monotonic, generous budget over the 1s digest interval, non-flaky). + `WC_KEYEXPR` / `WC_SEED_VALUE` consts.

No code path other than decode_reply changed; the answer/serve side is untouched (AV5 — wz emits no wildcard events; `retrieval_response` returns None for WildcardPut/WildcardDelete, storage_state.rs:1157). No inventory/atom status change.
verification_bullets: The new cross-impl e2e FAILED pre-fix (wildcard_registry_lens stayed empty ~20s) and PASSES post-fix 4x consecutively @ ~1.9s each (non-flaky; poll-on-condition, monotonic once the BTreeMap insert lands). This is the arbiter: value-convergence alone would have mis-passed the leg as "correct".

No regression on the shared decode_reply: the ASK + ANSWER sibling ignored tests (wz_replica_converges_to_zenohd_storage_manager, zenohd_converges_to_wz_replica) both pass (3 ignored tests total in the file, all green).

Driver unit tests: all 6 decode_reply tests pass, including the new decode_reply_wildcard_put_retrieval_carries_payload_and_encoding. Affected-crate suites: wz-runtime-tokio --features storage-aligner (19 storage_aligner tests) + wz-session-core --features storage-mgr-garbage-collection (46 storage tests) pass.

Root cause established by direct read of zenoh 49c8a53 (arbiter, not inference): EventMetadata field order + Action variant indices 0/1/2/3 match wz (log.rs:44-49/100-106); OwnedKeyExpr serde = self.0 (Arc<str>) = plain bincode String (owned.rs:34-40); the wildcard-keyed event is logged (service.rs:243-254), kept in the log (core.rs:219 update -> insert_event), in the digest (log.rs:557-590), and served (aligner_query.rs:256/320) — so the only defect was the wz-side decode_reply value-drop.

Round 311y187.decision_summary: R311y187 -- router-multicast-faces slice 1: the EGRESS-only multicast group plane on RouterForwarder (mcast_groups egress, McastMux-faithful). A routed Push is broadcast UNCONDITIONALLY to every attached multicast group at the route_push tail (zenoh flat mcast_groups append outside the sub-gated graph walk, hat/router/pubsub.rs:1334), echo-guarded against mcast->mcast re-broadcast (zenoh egress_filter, hat/router/mod.rs:813). Gated on the existing transport-multicast feature; the router-multicast-faces atom stays RESERVED (A3-safe, 0 cfg sites on the atom feature), reserved->active flip at the cross-impl S4 slice. DESIGN panel (3-agent adversarial + direct-read) re-scoped the atom EGRESS-first: egress needs only a cross-task Send UnboundedSender<MulticastTxItem>, so the mcast drive loop stays a SEPARATE task and the !Send RouterForwarder just enqueues -- no single-task loop fold (INGRESS milestone, deferred); B 3-collection model adopted, A face-egress enum refactor rejected.

broadcast_to_mcast_groups(reliable, push, inbound_is_mcast) enqueues a MulticastTxItem::Push per group, called UNCONDITIONALLY at the route_push tail (zenoh flat mcast_groups append OUTSIDE the sub-gated graph walk, hat/router/pubsub.rs:1334); echo guard inbound_is_mcast -> return (zenoh egress_filter both-multicast deny, hat/router/mod.rs:813).

Round 311y189.decision_summary: R311y189 -- router-multicast-faces reliteralization fix (IMPL-review CONFIRMED bug). broadcast_to_mcast_groups egressed the RAW inbound push, skipping the keyexpr reliteralization every sibling router egress leg performs (deliver_to_client_subscribers, compute_self_publish_forward). A multicast group is a downstream link with NO shared expr-id alias table, so an ALIASED (id-only) inbound push -- the wire bandwidth-efficient shape (DeclKexpr id->literal then id-only pushes) -- egressed an unresolvable wireexpr: a group blackhole. FIX: route_push threads its resolved keyexpr into broadcast_to_mcast_groups, which reliteralize_push(push, keyexpr) once before enqueuing (a literal push forwards verbatim). Surfaced by the 3-agent IMPL review test-adequacy lens; the literal-only slice-1/3 tests structurally could not catch it. Regression test asserts the egressed keyexpr resolves against an EMPTY table (the group leaf no-alias view) to the literal, not the aliased id 7; the slice-3 unit was also strengthened to assert the resolved keyexpr.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/router_forward.rs broadcast_to_mcast_groups: added a keyexpr: &str param + reliteralize_push(push, keyexpr) ONCE before the group fan-out (mirrors deliver_to_client_subscribers / compute_self_publish_forward) + a groups.is_empty() early return (skip the reliteralize clone on the no-group common path). route_push threads its resolved keyexpr into the call.

Regression test aliased_routed_push_is_reliteralized_for_the_mcast_group: DeclKexpr(7->"demo/data") on the inbound face + a pure-aliased push (build_push_aliased(7, None)) through route_push; asserts resolve_wireexpr(egressed keyexpr, EMPTY table) == Some("demo/data") -- the aliased id 7 resolves to None (blackhole) without the fix, modeling a group leaf's no-alias-table view.

Strengthened routed_push_broadcasts_to_attached_mcast_group: now asserts the egressed keyexpr resolves against an empty table to the literal (was matches! variant + reliable only -- a wrong/stale keyexpr passed silently).

Round 311y19.decision_summary: R311y19 -- link bcrypt.lib on windows-msvc (new repo-root .cargo/config.toml) to close the next Windows-portability blocker. With the R311y18 SCE UPA fix, sce-codegen runs clean on Windows and the crates compile, but the build-script links (sce-forge-runtime, wz-codecs, which pull libxml via SCE's sce-build) fail LNK2019 'unresolved external symbol BCryptGenRandom referenced in xmlInitRandom': vcpkg's libxml2 >= 2.13 uses BCryptGenRandom but the libxml crate's vcpkg link metadata omits bcrypt. Fix = a windows-msvc-scoped rustflags link-arg bcrypt.lib (inert on every other target). Round 311y190.decision_summary: R311y190 -- MCU multicast now RUNS on-target via config; the "MCU multicast is host-only, on-target evidence deferred" debt is CLOSED. A general MCU node built through the wz facade with transport-multicast + the new loopback-multicast/loopif-multicast toggle + a testmode lwIP port completes a REAL IGMP-join + multicast-loopback roundtrip on QEMU (Cortex-M3/M4/M7), not just build+footprint. Mechanism: (1) a new lwIP port cross-test-mcast (cross-test + LWIP_LOOPIF_MULTICAST + LWIP_TESTMODE + runtime pool sizing, via #include of the shared cross-test so it stays byte-identical); (2) a no_std deploy-callable seam LwipLink::route_multicast_over_loopback (the promotion of test-support ip4_set_default_multicast_netif(netif_get_loopif()) routing), feature-gated on loopif-multicast so the LWIP_TESTMODE-only FFI couples the feature to a testmode port BY CONSTRUCTION (mismatch = compile fail); (3) the facade forward chain link->session-lwip->wz->wz-mcu-multicast-e2e->deploy (mirrors buffer-pool-session-rx-slim); (4) deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e loopback-multicast: main() routes multicast over loopif + REQUIRES full_success -> semihost PASS, dropping the loopback-only SKIP concession; (5) run-ci Layer Q.6 boots it on mps2-an385/an386/an500 asserting PASS. 3-agent DESIGN panel arbitrated the home (mcu-multicast-e2e, NOT the link-tier mcu-qemu-demo), the new-port-not-shared-edit, and the seam-not-just-port-defines trap; verified empirically (M3/M4/M7 QEMU boot PASS). Default build byte-identical; shared cross-test port + 7 other lanes untouched. DEFERRED (named): slim pool for nrf51/M0 <=16KB SRAM; real ethernet-netif multicast (no NIC in CI). Honest scope: a loopback transport-plumbing on-target proof, not real-network multicast.

Round 311y196.decision_summary: R311y196 - I3a per-peer aliased multicast ingress (router-multicast-faces): the router-hat resolves each multicast peer's DeclKexpr-declared keyexpr aliases to literal IN the no_std dispatch SSOT (new apply_declared_aliases on MulticastDispatcher, the keyexpr-alias twin of apply_namespace_ingress, keyed per peer via src on PeerSlot.keyexpr_table) and rewrites its aliased Pushes to literal (set_push_keyexpr_literal SSOT, keyexpr+header N-bit in sync) BEFORE the observer fan - lifting the I1 literal-only restriction with NO src-threading to the !Send forwarder and NO per-peer FaceIds. Per-peer table capped at 256 aliases (unauthenticated-multicast DoS guard). absorb_keyexpr_into moved to wz-session-core as the shared unicast+multicast SSOT. Inventory-neutral (grows the existing router-multicast-faces atom). Full 3-agent DESIGN + 3-agent IMPL review, direct-read arbitrated: DESIGN chose dispatch-SSOT resolution (PeerSlot IS wz's mcast_faces; zenoh's mcast peer face is WhatAmI::Client/'Quick hack', federation deferred to I3b as a superset); IMPL caught a stale header-N-bit desync (fixed) + the table DoS (capped), refuted all other classes.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/multicast_dispatch.rs: PeerSlot gains a per-peer id->literal keyexpr_table (cfg multicast-declarations), cleared on evict(); new apply_declared_aliases(src, &mut outcome) absorbs the peer's DeclKexpr + rewrites its aliased Pushes to literal via the set_push_keyexpr_literal SSOT (keyexpr + header N-bit in sync) BEFORE the observer fan; const MAX_ALIASES_PER_PEER=256 caps the table (unauthenticated-multicast DoS guard, growth-only reject so removals/re-declares still flow).

crates/wz-session-core/src/multicast_rx.rs: apply_declared_aliases called in dispatch_multicast_inbound (whole-frame) + the fragment-completion path (ingest_multicast_fragment), both BEFORE apply_namespace_ingress (id->literal first, then prefix-strip).

crates/wz-session-core/src/wireexpr_resolve.rs: absorb_keyexpr_into MOVED here as the keyexpr-absorb SSOT (cfg codec-declare) from wz-runtime-tokio; crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/linkstate_forward.rs re-exports it (pub(crate) use) so both unicast forwarders + the new multicast plane share ONE definition.

Cargo: new wz-session-core feature multicast-declarations=[session-multicast,alloc,codec-declare,codec-push]; wz-runtime-tokio router-multicast-faces implies wz-session-core/multicast-declarations. Inventory-NEUTRAL: grows the existing router-multicast-faces atom's realized capability (literal->aliased ingress), no new 5.21 catalog atom (a composition feature like codec-declare/keyexpr-prefix; A3 audit is inventory->cargo only, so a non-inventoried feature does not trip it).

4 new session-core unit tests: declared_alias_resolves_inbound_push_to_literal (+ push.header & 0x20 assertion), undeclared_alias_stays_unresolved, evict_clears_peer_aliases, per_peer_alias_table_is_capped.
verification_bullets: 384 session-core lib tests pass (4 new); clippy clean (session-core multicast-declarations + runtime router-multicast-faces,codec-push); feature-off + narrow-combo builds compile (router-multicast-faces alone = host-elided, session-multicast alone = MCU-like, no-default-features session-multicast/reassembly/alloc = MCU no_std lane); wz-ap-demo --features router-multicast-faces + the S4/I1/I2 interop tests compile.

MCU RX SSOT byte-identical: the only multicast_rx.rs delta is the cfg(multicast-declarations)-gated apply_declared_aliases call; the MCU crates (wz-session-lwip, wz-mcu-multicast-e2e) never enable the feature, so the field/method/const/call are all elided.

3-agent DESIGN panel, direct-read arbitrated: per-peer aliasing resolves IN the dispatch SSOT on PeerSlot (mirroring apply_namespace_ingress) - no src threaded to the !Send forwarder, no per-peer FaceIds; direct read confirmed PeerSlot IS wz's mcast_faces + zenoh's mcast peer face = WhatAmI::Client/DummyPrimitives/"Quick hack" and mcast_faces is never in a linkstate net, so faithful federation is I3b (a superset over zenoh's rough two-router-shared-group loop, which egress_filter does NOT prevent).

3-agent IMPL panel: CONFIRMED must-fix caught + fixed pre-commit - stale header N-bit (apply_declared_aliases rewrote the keyexpr but not the header N (suffix-present) bit; reliteralize_push's already-literal shortcut forwards it verbatim + desyncs the subscriber decoder on the no-namespace router-hat, exactly the I3a deployment) via set_push_keyexpr_literal + a header assertion; + the per-peer table memory-exhaustion DoS via MAX_ALIASES_PER_PEER; all other adversarial classes REFUTED (self-echo via the self-zid gate, wrong-peer via one-slot-per-src all-or-nothing, recycle via evict, cyclic-alias via single-lookup resolve).
carry_forward_bullets: I3a DONE (per-peer aliased multicast ingress, LOCAL delivery): the router-hat resolves a mcast peer's DeclKexpr-aliased Pushes to literal per peer + delivers to LOCAL unicast subs; lifts I1 literal-only; inventory-neutral; DoS-capped (256/peer). NEXT = I3b (loop-safe mesh-federation, the deferred HARD half): forwarder-side origin attribution (SP#1 carrier decided there) + origin-tagged loop-prevention SUPERSET over zenoh's Quick-hack (two-federated-routers-sharing-a-group is UNSAFE today, documented in route_push); its own 3-agent DESIGN pass. Then I3c cross-impl proofs.

DEFERRED (named): I3c cross-impl ALIASED proof needs an aliasing publisher - stock pico is Z_FEATURE_MULTICAST_DECLARATIONS=0 (literal only), so it needs a pico rebuilt with declarations, zenohd-on-multicast, or a wz aliasing mcast publisher; the I2 literal pico lane stays as the literal regression.

DEFERRED (named): the namespace_ingress twin carries the SAME unbounded per-peer pattern (routing-namespace feature) - a follow-up unifies the per-peer-decorator bound across BOTH decorators (needs care for namespace undeclare-correlation semantics, so it was NOT bundled into I3a).

Proves over real sockets (Layer M, #[ignore], 26/26 no-flaky): (a) the JOIN-whatami->router_member_zids->snapshot-diff relay->set_mcast_group_members membership chain converges cross-process (the leg the I3b unit tests inject past), and (b) LOOP-SAFE - EXACTLY ONE router federates the group-ingress into the mesh (a deterministic 1-of-2 log partition; elect_router returns self on an empty set so it is satisfiable only if the relay populated each router set), so the two-router-shared-group echo zenoh WhatAmI::Client Quick-hack leaves undefended cannot occur; and (c) the federated copy reaches the off-group mesh subscriber. Test-only + observe-only witness counters (behavior-preserving, routing identical); MCU byte-identical; inventory-neutral. Full 3-agent DESIGN + adversarial IMPL/WHOLE-SESSION review (CLEAN), direct-read arbitrated: DESIGN chose a --peer (mesh) sub over a --key client (a client is locally master-delivered = proves nothing beyond I2; a peer is reached only via the DR-gated federation), the deterministic 1-of-2 witness over a packet count, and a membership barrier to kill the startup double-DR transient.

Round 311y206.decision_summary: R311y206 -- wz->pico TX-fragmentation cross-impl fidelity bug FIX. wz outbound fragment chains omitted the zenoh fragment FIRST marker (Z-ext 0x02 on the first fragment) that zenoh-pico requires on a protocol-patch>=1 session (wz always advertises patch=1), so pico silently dropped every wz >MTU Put ("First fragment received without the start marker"). A new interop test (wz_fragment_tx_to_pico_zsub) surfaced it (20B sub-MTU passes / 200B fragmenting drops). Fixed build_fragment_wire/fragment_body to emit the marker on the first fragment (shared by unicast + multicast) + a secondary unicast SN double-mint that left a 1-SN wire gap (emit_frame_or_fragments now reuses the minted sn + reserves count-1, matching zenoh pipeline.rs + the already-correct multicast twin). Correctness-only, transport-fragmentation stays active. 3-agent review SOUND/COMPLETE + test-rigor remediations; full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0, hand-composed so ZERO codegen drift.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/frame_encode.rs: build_fragment_wire gained a `first: bool` param -- the FIRST fragment of a chain now sets the header Z flag (FLAG_T_Z 0x80) and inserts the FRAGMENT_FIRST ext byte (new const FRAGMENT_FIRST_EXT_HEADER = 0x02, id 0x02 | enc unit) between VLE(sn) and the payload; subsequent fragments are byte-unchanged. fragment_body passes `off == 0` as `first`, so BOTH the unicast (emit_frame_or_fragments) and multicast (multicast_frame_or_fragments) chains -- its only two callers -- get the marker. zenoh `fragment::ext::First = zextunit!(0x2,false)` / zenoh-pico `_Z_MSG_EXT_ID_FRAGMENT_FIRST`. The VLE(sn) stays the codec SSOT (encode Fragment{sn, payload:&[]} for the VLE, then push the ext + real payload) -- symmetric with inbound.rs's hand-rolled fragment Z-gated ext-chain decode. FRAG_HEADER_BUDGET doc notes the 1-byte ext rides the reserved-max-VLE(10)-minus-real-width(<=9) slack, so the first fragment stays <= mtu.

crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: emit_frame_or_fragments SN fix -- the oversize frame's already-minted `sn` IS the first fragment's SN; reserve only the `count-1` follow-on SNs (`for _ in 1..count { outbound_frame_sn.fetch_add(1) }`) and pass `sn` (not a fresh fetch_add(count)) as the fragment_body base. The prior code re-minted a fresh block, discarding `sn` and leaving a 1-SN wire gap; now ring-consecutive from `sn`, matching zenoh pipeline.rs + the multicast_frame_or_fragments twin. Both the mint and the follow-on reserve execute under the one tx_mutex hold (session_actions.rs:2383), so the split reservation is concurrency-equivalent to the old single fetch_add (correctness review Axis 4). multicast_frame_or_fragments doc updated to note unicast now mirrors it (no skip).

The Cortex-M SysTick clock was pasted in 3 deploy mains and had DRIFTED: only deploy/mcu-qemu-demo carried the R311y15 monotonic floor; deploy/mcu-session-acceptor + deploy/mcu-multicast-e2e ran the floorless pre-R311y15 copy (latent -- they drive a sync busy-poll session loop, not a SleepFuture, so the wake-loss livelock had not surfaced there, but the wz_runtime_lwip::time::ClockSource monotonic contract was nonetheless violated). Footprint: the u64 widening routes the 64-bit atomic through critical-section on ARMv7-M, growing qemu-demo .text +~500 B (mps2/v8m; thumbv6m +8, already crit-section) and multicast-e2e +444/+560 B (it also gained the floor); BASELINE_TEXT + BASELINE_MC_TEXT (+ bss) rebased in scripts/check-footprint.sh and §6.7/§6.9 store caveats appended (the gate's table<->caveat co-maintenance rule). Round 311y210.decision_summary: R311y210 -- REVERSE cross-impl Put body-metadata decode (card (c) of the pico/MCU step-1 track): a real zenoh-pico z_pub_attachment client Puts attachment kv-pairs + zenoh/string;utf8 encoding + ntp64 timestamp on ONE sample, and a wz subscriber DECODES all three off the delivered Sample -- the reverse of the wz->pico emit legs y207 (encoding) / y208 (timestamp) / y209 (attachment). New wz-session-core deserialize_kv_attachment is the decode twin of serialize_kv_attachment: it reads VLE(pair_count) then count length-prefixed key/value strings via the crate::vle read_zbuf SSOT (the read inverse of write_zbuf), byte-faithful to pico ze_deserializer_deserialize_sequence_length + _string (serialization.c) and the z_sub_attachment.c decode loop, reading EXACTLY count pairs, ignoring trailing bytes, and returning None on truncation with no panic and no per-count pre-allocation (loop bounded by buffer, not by count -- safer than pico malloc(sizeof(kv)*count)). The e2e ROOT CAUSE was pico z_declare_publisher arming a write-filter (api.c:1423) that suppresses the Put (z_publisher_put gates on !_z_write_filter_active, api.c:1525) until pico observes a matching subscriber declaration (filtering.c:199-208); the fix declares the wz subscriber through the full TokioSession (emits Declare(DeclSubscriber) on the wire) instead of a local-only observer.subscribers.register, and a proactive/id-0 declare opens pico's aggregate CLIENT filter (interest.c:268-273) so wz needs NO Interest-response -- the empirical checkpoint resolved POSITIVE. Additive test + decoder only, no production wire change; inventory unchanged (attachment-bytes already active since R311fv, the reverse decode is additive proof not a status flip). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/attachment.rs: new pub fn deserialize_kv_attachment(blob) -> Option<Vec<(Vec<u8>,Vec<u8>)>>, the decode twin of serialize_kv_attachment. Reads VLE(pair_count) via SceCursor::read_vle_u64 then count length-prefixed key/value strings via the crate::vle read_zbuf SSOT (the read inverse of write_zbuf), byte-faithful to pico ze_deserializer_deserialize_sequence_length + ze_deserializer_deserialize_string (serialization.c) and the z_sub_attachment.c decode loop. Reads EXACTLY count pairs and ignores trailing bytes (pico does not check full consumption); returns None on a truncated/malformed blob with no panic and no per-count pre-allocation -- the loop is bounded by the buffer, not by count, so a bogus large count bails on the first read_zbuf that runs out (safer than pico malloc(sizeof(kv_pair)*count)).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_pub_attachment_to_wz_sub.rs: new #[ignore] binary-dep e2e (Layer E via --ignored). A real pico z_pub_attachment client (-n 1 -> idx=0, one Put then close) emits attachment [(source,C),(index,0)] + encoding zenoh/string;utf8 (pico encoding id 1 -> wz wire packed_id (1<<1)|1 = 3, schema utf8) + an ntp64 z_timestamp_new on ONE sample; the wz acceptor subscriber decodes attachment (deserialize_kv_attachment), encoding (EncodingHint), and timestamp (presence) off the delivered Sample. One sample proves the whole reverse metadata track (the wz-side field readback that a pico SUBSCRIBER cannot give).

crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_pub_attachment_to_wz_sub.rs: the subscriber is declared through the full TokioSession::declare_subscriber (emits Declare(DeclSubscriber) on the wire), NOT a local-only observer.subscribers.register. pico z_pub_attachment uses z_declare_publisher, which arms a write-filter (_z_write_filter_create, api.c:1423) that suppresses the Put (z_publisher_put gates on !_z_write_filter_active, api.c:1525) until pico observes a matching subscriber declaration (filtering.c:199-208); a local-only register emits no wire declaration, so pico filtered every Put and delivered nothing (correct zenoh matching-optimisation, not a wz bug -- z_put carries no such filter, which is why the sibling fragment-RX e2e needs none). Drive shape mirrors namespace_matching_e2e.rs. Two preconditions documented in the test (both hard-fail to fired=0, never a false pass): EXACT keyexpr (pico CLIENT interest is AGGREGATE, matches via _z_keyexpr_equals) and pico MULTI-THREAD (Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD default, so pico's read task opens the filter during the 1s pre-put sleep).

Round 311y211.decision_summary: R311y211 -- reconnect×multilink coherence slice-1 (S2 FOUNDATION; the user chose the full A-only arc after the 3-agent DESIGN review dropped Approach C as unnecessary+unsafe). The y205 transport-multilink × session-reconnect compile_error XOR is REMOVED, and its single real hazard -- reset_for_reopen zeroing the SHARED SessionCore rx_sn / outbound_frame_sn, which in a live aggregate corrupts the surviving link's per-channel SN gate -- becomes a RUNTIME guard: when transport-multilink is also compiled the shared-core reset is skipped while live_link_count() > 0, making reset_for_reopen a TOTAL function (preserving a live survivor is the correct output for that input, not a bug to assert away). Production reaches the skip only as a safety net -- a partial loss survives via del_link (SN intact, no reset), a whole-collapse is a fresh-core rebuild (the accept loop drops the aggregate at remaining==0, so the next dial is a fresh primary), and the single-link ReconnectingSession supervisor runs on an EMPTY link set (link_count==0) so the guard is transparent to it. beyond-pico / P4 (pico has no unicast multilink; zenoh-full is the sole reference). A coexistence unit test pins the guard mechanics (SN preserved with a live link; re-seeded once the set is empty) and CI Layer C1ba invocation 5 runs it on default + transport-multilink (the ex-XOR combo) with a count-assert (grep ' 1 passed') so a future cfg-out reddens the lane, plus a both-crate clippy floor. 3-agent DESIGN review (dropped C, scoped A) + 2-agent IMPL review (correctness CLEAN; the test is proven to FAIL if the guard is removed; CI is proven to actually run it). NO per-link auto-re-add yet -- that is slice-2 (y212, the dropped-link-comes-back value). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0.

Round 311y214.decision_summary: R311y214 -- extqos slice-0: unicast TX Frame SN split per reliability channel. wz's single shared outbound_frame_sn (one ring for reliable AND best_effort) diverged from BOTH zenoh (non-QoS TransportPriorityTx still holds reliable+best_effort generators) and zenoh-pico (_z_transport_tx_get_sn switches on reliability into _sn_tx_reliable/_sn_tx_best_effort, common/tx.c:52-59): a best-effort Frame bumped the reliable SN so each channel saw a gapped-but-forward cadence the peer's per-channel _z_sn_precedes gate merely tolerated. New AtomicTxSn{reliable,best_effort} (the atomic unicast twin of the plain-u64 multicast sn::TxSn) splits the counter; next_outbound_frame_sn gains a reliable arg selecting the channel; the fragment-reserve loop burns follow-on SNs on the same channel; reset_for_reopen re-seeds both. Pure fidelity fix isolated from the priority dimension -- the DESIGN-reviewed foundation for the per-(priority,reliability) SN conduits (extqos) that make multilink priority-select safe (R311y215 arrays this per Priority conduit behind transport-qos).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: new `AtomicTxSn { reliable, best_effort: AtomicU64 }` (the atomic unicast twin of the plain-u64 multicast `sn::TxSn`) with `new(initial)` / `mint(reliable, mask)` / `reserve_next(reliable)` / `reset(initial)`. Field `outbound_frame_sn: AtomicU64` -> `AtomicTxSn`; ctor seeds both channels from `params.initial_sn`. `next_outbound_frame_sn(sn_mask)` -> `next_outbound_frame_sn(reliable, sn_mask)` delegating to `mint`. The two mint sites (batch-open + immediate) thread the dispatch `reliable`. The fragment-reserve loop (`emit_frame_or_fragments`) burns follow-on SNs via `reserve_next(reliable)` on the same channel as the first fragment (R311y206 ring-consecutive chain preserved, now per channel). `reset_for_reopen` re-seeds BOTH channels via `reset()`.

Round 311y217.decision_summary: R311y217 -- multilink priority-select LIBRARY core (the qos x multilink intersection). y205 built reliability-routed multilink (select_link picks a link by traffic class); y215-216 built + activated the QoS per-priority transport. This atom joins them: select_link(reliability) is widened to select_link(reliability, priority) with zenoh's 3-tier match (universal/tx.rs select), so each (priority, reliability) conduit pins to ONE physical link -- the one-conduit=one-link invariant (session_actions.rs:300-304) that keeps priority-select SN-safe (the peer's per-conduit RX SN gate never sees a cross-link reorder). A new LinkPriorityRange type (the wz mirror of zenoh PriorityRange, an inclusive Priority band) + a per-link priority_range + set_link_priority_range carry each link's band; select_link is full (reliability match AND band contains priority, SMALLEST band wins via STRICT `>` = stable first-seen) -> partial (reliability match, no covering band) -> any (first alive). priority is threaded through send_wire to all 10 call sites, with the SN-safety-critical batch-flush arms routing by the FRAME's OWN pinned conduit (batch.priority), NOT the triggering message -- a mismatch would split one conduit across links and silently lose a stale-dropped reliable frame. LinkReliabilityPref::Any stays any-tier ONLY (backward-compat + zenoh concrete-reliability primacy); a non-qos build degrades byte-identically to the old reliability-only 2-tier. Three deterministic recording-driver segregation tests prove routing on the immediate AND batch-reopen-flush paths + the narrowest-band tie-break; the #3 batch guard was diagnose-first-verified (it FAILS on the trigger-priority bug). Demo/deploy activation (the --qos flag, FaceSources.qos, per-face e2e) is deferred to y218. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

LinkReliabilityPref::Any is any-tier ONLY (never == want), preserving the pre-y217 contract + zenoh concrete-reliability primacy; a non-qos build degrades to the old reliability-only 2-tier (byte-identical).

Round 311y219a.decision_summary: R311y219a -- deploy-path per-face priority-band segregation (the y217 select_link priority tier ACTIVATED over the production accept/dial path). y217 built select_link(reliability, priority) + LinkPriorityRange as a recording-driver LIBRARY; y218 activated qos negotiation over multilink. This atom assigns the per-face priority band in the deploy path so a QoS multilink aggregate segregates distinct-priority Puts onto distinct physical links, proven in-process over a real peer_loop. KEY DESIGN (3-agent DESIGN review + direct-read arbitration): select_link disqualifies a reliability-mismatched link BEFORE the priority band (faithful to zenoh universal/tx.rs select), so a 2-link aggregate segregates on ONE axis only; with QoS ON all links are UNIFORM Reliable (new multilink_pref_for) so the priority band is the live discriminant, with QoS OFF the y205 even/odd reliability spread is unchanged (mutually-exclusive 2-link modes). This is a DIRECT MIRROR of a real zenoh multilink-over-TCP deploy (a TCP link is always is_reliable, so zenoh's per-link priority ranges ride all-Reliable links, tx.rs:86-88). Round 311y219b.decision_summary: R311y219b -- joined-face DELIVERY fix (the load-bearing half of the y219 split). A joined (aggregated secondary) multilink link was never registered as a forwarder face, so the real LinkstateForwarder DROPPED any data/control the sender routed onto it (forward_push / dispatch_local_subscribers early-return on faces.get(inbound)=None). Latent since y205 (DEFAULT priority always routes to first_alive=primary, so the secondary carried no data), first EXPOSED by y219a's priority routing (a non-DEFAULT Put deliberately rides the secondary; also DEFAULT=Data(5) falls in the LOW band, so post-y219a even a plain DEFAULT publish on a qos aggregate rides the possibly-secondary LOW-band link). KEY DESIGN ARBITRATION (3-agent DESIGN + direct-read): the naive call-site re-attribution (drive_joined_face forwards the PRIMARY id) BREAKS the receiver-side per-face observation that MULTIPLE committed+PUSHED tests rely on (the y205 deploy_active_two_links reliability-segregation assert_ne! on faces, and the y219a priority-segregation faces.len()==2) -- the DESIGN agent's "no observer" claim was wrong, the test forwarders ARE observers. So the fix is FORWARDER-INTERNAL (option D'): drive_joined_face is UNCHANGED (forwards the physical id), and only the REAL LinkstateForwarder resolves a joined FaceId to the session's PRIMARY registered face at the TOP of forward() -- via a new joined_faces map populated by two new FaceForwarder default-no-op methods register_joined/deregister_joined the accept loop calls at the JOIN / secondary-death. Observation-only test forwarders keep seeing the physical id (per-face witnesses unaffected), while the routing forwarder presents ONE logical face per aggregate (the faithful zenoh model: an aggregated transport is one FaceState; also unifies the per-link keyexpr alias table). The delivery fix is proven directly by a LinkstateForwarder lib unit (a Put on the joined FaceId is DROPPED before register_joined, DELIVERED after, DROPPED after deregister_joined -- diagnose-first verified RED when register_joined is neutered), and the accept-loop WIRING (register_joined called with secondary-not-registered -> primary-registered) by an assertion in the y219a deploy e2e. SCOPE (deferred, named, user-approved split): the demo binary reachability (a prioritized forwarder publish_qos + --express-high/--low CLI + a 2-proc black-box e2e) is a separable follow-up -- the in-process proof is the clean deterministic one (a black-box demo delivery witness needs a local-sub on --subscribe + is convergence-coin-flip-prone). full run-ci pending the batch push; per-atom host lanes green (lib unit incl diagnose-first RED, deploy e2e 3/3 with the wiring assert + per-face preserved, e2e 5, readd 1, routing-routes 21, all clippy -D warnings, fmt).

Round 311y220.decision_summary: R311y220 -- demo-reachability prioritized publish (the y219b-deferred, user-approved follow-up). Threads an application QoS priority from the forwarder publish API down to the previously-clamped dispatch_push(Priority::DEFAULT) at session_actions.rs (~3145), making the y217 select_link band routing + y219a per-face band assignment reachable from the application -- before y220 the forwarder publish API hard-clamped DEFAULT, so an app could never originate a banded Put. Layered base-delegates twin, byte-identical on the DEFAULT path: send_network_message_qos (kernel) is fed by fan_out_qos which is fed by publish_qos (forwarder); the base send_network_message / fan_out / publish delegate at Priority::DEFAULT (the Push arm prior hard-coded DEFAULT is now the default arg; all non-Push arms are control-plane and ignore priority -- Declare/Oam self-specify Control, Request/Interest/Response take none). Demo `--express-high` / `--low` flags (a new PublishBand enum -> RealTime/HIGH-band + express-flush | Background/LOW-band + non-express) drive publish_qos over an aggregated qos multilink session; the `--put` config-write path stays plain publish (control-plane DEFAULT). New ungated `use wz_session_core::qos::Priority` in linkstate_forward.rs + `pub use wz_session_core::qos` in wz-runtime-tokio/lib.rs (so the demo names wz::runtime_tokio::qos::Priority). 3-agent DESIGN review (pre-code) + 3-agent IMPL review (post-build), direct-read arbitrated. HONEST SCOPE (arbitrated by review): the 2-proc e2e wz_peer_multilink_qos_reach proves publish_qos send-PATH REACHABILITY from the demo binary (a `--express-high` Put originated via publish_qos and DELIVERED over the aggregated qos session; the `originating ExpressHigh Put via publish_qos` once-witness proves the NEW branch was taken, not the DEFAULT fall-through). It does NOT prove band-SELECTION observation (a black-box subscriber cannot see which physical link carried a Put, and a green result does not distinguish qos-on from qos-off; band-selection correctness stays the y219a in-process session_multilink_deploy_e2e + select_link unit tests) and does NOT prove the y219b joined-secondary DELIVERY fix (the B-side received-mesh-data equals data_seen, incremented UPSTREAM of the faces.get(inbound)=None drop gate y219b fixed, so it fires with y219b reverted; the deterministic guard stays the library unit test joined_link_inbound_delivers_to_primary_face_local_subscriber_after_register_joined). NAMED BOUND (transit priority loss): publish_qos bands ONLY the ORIGIN first hop -- forward_push (transit re-forward) has no priority param and the inbound handler discards the Frame priority, so a relay re-bands to DEFAULT until the deferred FramePayload.priority (~48-site) work. cfg-skew guard `#[cfg(not(codec-push))] let _ = priority` covers the non-push fn-gate disjuncts (declare-* / codec-request / codec-linkstate / codec-response); verified across 20 clippy/check combos + full run-ci. Round 311y222.decision_summary: R311y222 -- TX batch frame pins its FULL (priority, reliability) conduit, not priority alone. The batch reopen/flush decision in dispatch_network_message keyed on batch.priority only, so a same-priority / different-reliability message was absorbed into a frame with the wrong R flag + SN ring (a reliability-MISLABEL: best-effort delivered on the reliable channel or vice versa -- both SN rings stay in-sync, no desync/reassembly corruption; small live blast radius since wz has no reliable retransmit today, high fidelity/forward-safety value). Fix: an UNGATED reliability predicate reading the open frame own R flag (frame_wire_reliability(&batch.buf), no new BatchTx field) OR-ed with the existing qos-gated priority predicate; the flush routes the prev frame by its own conduit (y217 #3). UNGATED because two reliability Frame-SN conduits (AtomicTxSn { reliable, best_effort }) exist even on a non-QoS session -- the old check was wholly transport-qos-gated, so a non-QoS batching build had NO conduit check at all. zenoh per-(priority,reliability) frame-boundary parity (zenoh-codec CurrentFrame/NewFrame); a deliberate divergence from vendored zenoh-pico, which blind-appends mixed-reliability. 3-DESIGN + 3-IMPL adversarial, direct-read arbitrated (all SHIP); 2 review cleanups landed (frame_wire_reliability double-read hoist, loop-comment staleness).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs: the TX batch reopen/flush decision in dispatch_network_message now keys on the FULL (priority, reliability) conduit, not priority alone. A message whose reliability differs from the open batch frame flushes+reopens instead of being absorbed into a frame with the wrong R flag + SN ring. The RELIABILITY predicate is UNGATED -- read from the open frame's own R flag via frame_wire_reliability(&batch.buf), so no new BatchTx field -- because two reliability Frame-SN conduits exist even on a non-QoS session (AtomicTxSn { reliable, best_effort }); the PRIORITY predicate stays transport-qos-gated (per-priority conduits are QoS-only). The flushed frame is routed by its OWN conduit (frame R flag + batch.priority pin, DEFAULT under non-qos), never the triggering message (y217 #3). The BatchTx.priority field doc is corrected: the reliability half is buf-derived + ungated, so a non-QoS batch is NOT single-conduit.

crates/wz-session-core/src/frame_encode.rs: frame_wire_reliability doc records its second caller (the y222 reopen check) and the deliberate divergence from zenoh-pico -- pico appends mixed-reliability into whatever frame is open (tx.c _z_transport_tx_send_n_msg_inner mints the header only on an empty buffer, then blind-appends); wz instead follows zenoh's per-(priority, reliability) frame boundary (zenoh-codec CurrentFrame/NewFrame).
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multilink.rs: the y217 reopen-flush test doc updated -- the pinned conduit is (batch.priority + the frame's own R flag) as of the y222 (priority, reliability) key.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: new unit batch_reliability_change_flushes_open_frame in the batch_tx_tests mod (gated transport-batching + codec-push + codec-frame, NOT transport-qos -- so it runs on a NON-QoS build, the ungating proof): a reliable Put opens the frame (frame_count 0), a best-effort Put forces the reliability-change flush (frame_count 1), batch_flush drains the best-effort frame (frame_count 2); frame 0 R-set carries only the reliable message, frame 1 R-clear only the best-effort, each SN=0 (independent rings -- a shared ring would read sn=1).

3-DESIGN + 3-IMPL adversarial passes (read-only Plan agents), direct-read arbitrated. DESIGN: a REAL reliability-MISLABEL bug (both SN rings stay in-sync; NOT an SN-desync/reassembly corruption), reachable in a batch window, WORSE without transport-qos (the old reopen check was wholly qos-gated). Fix = an UNGATED buf-derived reliability predicate, NOT a (priority,reliable) tuple -- a non-QoS build does not normalize priority to DEFAULT (send_push_literal_qos passes it through; the DEFAULT re-bind is itself qos-gated), so a tuple compare would spuriously flush same-reliability/different-priority messages that share one non-qos wire conduit.

Round 311y22f.decision_summary: R311y22f -- urgent CI fix + false-claim correction. The post-push GitHub CI for R311y22e (run 28165570791) went RED on the portability(windows) job -- the WATCH I had flagged -- falsifying R311y22's core "no libxml2" claim. ROOT CAUSE (direct read, `cargo tree -i libxml --target all`): `sce-forge-runtime` -- the RUNTIME support crate every generated codec links against (SceCursor / CodecError) -- has its OWN build.rs build-dependency on `sce-build`, which pulls the `libxml` crate -> native libxml2. So compiling wz-runtime-tokio (-> wz-codecs -> sce-forge-runtime) compiles sce-forge-runtime's build script, which needs libxml2 REGARDLESS of R311y22 committing wz's codegen. R311y22d wrongly removed the windows libxml2 vcpkg install assuming committed codegen removed all libxml2 need; my R311y22b "toolchain-compiled=0" verification was a FALSE NEGATIVE (it counted `Compiling` lines, absent for the Linux-CACHED libxml; the fresh windows-msvc build exposed it). FIX: re-added the libxml2 vcpkg install to the windows portability job. The `build sce-codegen` step STAYS removed -- the AP build runs no codegen + needs no binary; macOS passed without either via system pkg-config libxml2. Corrected the false claim in the ci.yml comment + the ARCHITECTURE.md R311y22 note: R311y22 removed wz's build-time CODEGEN + the sce-codegen BINARY requirement (real wins -- no per-build regen, no build-sce.sh on consumers), but NOT libxml2; full libxml2 removal needs an SCE-upstream change (sce-forge-runtime decoupled from sce-build). What R311y22 DID achieve, verified-green THIS run (28165570791): cross-mcu Layer G+Q (committed codegen on all MCU triples + QEMU), macOS portability, and -- critically -- the Linux validate+verify+test job ran the NEW Layer B2 step + PASSED (the SSOT regen-diff gate IS now server-enforced) + E6 did not flake. So R311y22a-e's committed-codegen + regen-diff + binary-removal STAND; only the over-claimed "no libxml2" is corrected. LESSON: [[feedback-windows-portability-libxml2]] + [[feedback-ci-yaml-local-verify]] AGAIN -- a local-CACHED build hid a transitive build-dep the fresh windows CI caught; the toolchain-compiled-by-Compiling-line-grep is a false-negative trap; the 4-agent review missed it too (checked wz-codegen-build, not sce-forge-runtime's build-dep). validate_workspace orphan new=+0. Could not find libxml2 ... panicked"). Discriminating by construction, not a tautology: a dropped priority yields the packed byte == QosLevel::DEFAULT(0x05), which build_push_outer_extensions SUPPRESSES, so pico falls back to its default sample priority 5 and the exact "with priority: 1" assertion fails-by-timeout. scripts/build-zenoh-pico-cli.sh gains a SECOND in-place example patch (alongside the R216 z_put.c BLOCK-congestion patch); the renamed shared trap reverts both files under one EXIT handler, and a marker hard-reject closes the comment-anchor double-insert hazard (unlike z_put, the // Check timestamp anchor survives the insert); THIRD_PARTY.md documents it. New Layer-E-auto-swept e2e wz_priority_to_pico_zsub.rs (#[ignore], no run-ci.sh edit needed). publish_common.rs: corrected 5 PublishOptions field docs + with_timestamp that still claimed wire propagation was pending ("current wire branch drops this field" / "R233 carry" / "lands in R233") -- STALE since R233; the corrected docs state built+per-field-gated reality plus the accurate per-field witness (encoding=y207, timestamp=y208, attachment=y209, priority=y240). NOT the last metadata gap (honesty): source_info has NO cross-impl witness (only a wz-internal encoder unit test; the layer3_msg_* FFI gates cover only the metadata-absent baseline), and congestion + express ride the same qos byte but pico exposes only z_sample_priority per-sample -- all three remain un-proven wz->pico. The prior `restore_z_put()` trap handler was renamed `restore_pico_example_patches()` and now git-checkout-reverts BOTH z_put.c AND z_sub_attachment.c under the SINGLE `trap ... Round 311y252.decision_summary: R311y252 -- query LOOPBACK body-metadata surfacing; closes the y250/y251 carry's named NEXT actionable. Before this round build_loopback_query (wz-runtime-tokio session/mod.rs) built the loopback Query with ONLY the selector parameters (Q_P, R311y94) and left extensions=None, so a SessionLocal queryable's QueryView::attachment() / source_info() / payload() / encoding() ALL returned None even when the querier set them via QueryOptions::with_attachment / with_source_info / with_payload / with_encoding -- the three ext-borne slots surfaced on the WIRE path only. The receive side was never the gap: fire_matching_queryables already extracted all four from query.extensions (wz-session-core/query.rs:1293-1341); the loopback simply never BUILT the chain. Fixed by REUSING the wire SSOT instead of duplicating the ext-chain assembly: build_loopback_query now derives a TRIMMED QueryMetadata (parameters / source_info / attachment / value) from opts.query_metadata(), calls build_request_query_with_meta(0, 0, None, &meta) -- the same builder the wire branch uses -- and lifts out the inner RequestOwnedVariant::CodecZenohQuery body. The value(0x03) -> source_info(0x01) -> attachment(0x05) emit order, the Q_Z header flag and the Z chain-continuation bits are therefore produced by the single RequestQueryBuilder::build() SSOT (request_build.rs:573-629), NOT re-derived at the loopback site; and each slot's threading is gated on exactly the feature its receive-side extractor is gated on (query-value / query-source-info / query-attachment / query-selector-parameters), so the loopback surface stays symmetric with the wire surface across every feature subset. target / consolidation / timeout_ms are deliberately EXCLUDED (QueryView exposes no accessor for them), so the loopback Query body differs from the wire body by exactly the unobservable Q_C byte and builds no discarded Request-level ext chain. STRUCTURE/fidelity-only: no wire-path change, no new cfg gate, inventory UNCHANGED (a fidelity fix inside the already-active query plane, not a new atom). One deliberate BEHAVIOR CHANGE is named in the caveats: reusing the wire builder also adopts its 256-byte selector assert, which only the SessionLocal-only path had been escaping. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

It now derives a TRIMMED `QueryMetadata` (parameters / source_info / attachment / value) from `opts.query_metadata()`, calls `wz_session_core::request_build::build_request_query_with_meta(0, 0, None, &meta)` -- the SAME builder the wire branch uses -- and lifts out the inner `RequestOwnedVariant::CodecZenohQuery` body. The value(0x03) -> source_info(0x01) -> attachment(0x05) emit order, the Q_Z header flag and the Z chain-continuation bits are therefore produced by the single `RequestQueryBuilder::build()` SSOT (request_build.rs:573-629) and are NOT re-derived at the loopback site. `target` / `consolidation` / `timeout_ms` are deliberately EXCLUDED from the trimmed meta (`QueryView` exposes no accessor for them; target/timeout are Request-level exts a single-host fan-out has no relay to honour, and consolidation folds duplicate replies a single-source loopback cannot produce), so the loopback also builds no discarded Request-level ext chain. The rid=0 / literal-id-0 envelope is discarded -- the loopback rid + resolved keyexpr ride the `local_query()` call arguments, not the Query body, so both call sites (`Session::query` and `Session::query_aliased`) get an identical body.

A SessionLocal queryable's `QueryView` now observes parameters / attachment / source_info / payload / encoding exactly as a wire queryable does. No wire-path change, no new cfg gate, inventory UNCHANGED (this is a fidelity fix inside the already-active query plane, not a new atom).

BEHAVIOR CHANGE (deliberate, named): reusing the wire builder also adopts its caller-error asserts. Exactly one is reachable from the trimmed meta -- `RequestQueryBuilder::parameters` panics on a selector longer than REQUEST_QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_LEN (256). A `Locality::Any` / `Remote` query ALREADY hit that assert before this round (its wire branch calls the same builder), so only the `SessionLocal`-only path changes: it used to accept an over-256-byte selector silently (the old `SceBytes<256>` copy is unbounded under `alloc`, `N` advisory) and now panics like every other locality. Intended: a selector exceeding the wire bound could never reach a real wire queryable, so letting it through on loopback alone was a latent wire/loopback divergence. Documented as an explicit panic contract on `build_loopback_query`. The other builder asserts are unreachable from the trimmed meta (attachment's empty-slice panic is guarded by `!attachment.is_empty()`; timeout's zero panic cannot fire because the trimmed meta pins timeout_ms to 0; query_value asserts nothing).

SCOPE NOTE: `target` / `consolidation` / `timeout_ms` are deliberately EXCLUDED from the loopback meta -- `QueryView` exposes no accessor for any of them, target/timeout are Request-level exts a single-host fan-out has no relay to honour, and consolidation folds duplicate replies a single-source loopback cannot produce. So the loopback Query body differs from the wire Query body by exactly the (unobservable) Q_C consolidation byte. If a future round gives `QueryView` a consolidation/target accessor, this trim is the site to revisit.

Z-chain proof: the guard sets ALL FOUR slots at once, so the loopback Query body carries a 3-entry ext chain (value 0x03 -> source_info 0x01 -> attachment 0x05) with the Z continuation bit set on the first two and clear on the last. All three decode back correctly through `extract_query_value` / `extract_query_source_info` / `extract_query_attachment`, so the receive-side extractors mask the Z bit correctly over a multi-entry chain -- the case a single-ext loopback would not have exercised.

publishable_carry_forward_bullets: R311y252 = the query LOOPBACK body-metadata surfacing, which CLOSES the "(2) LOOPBACK value surfacing" carry named by R311y250/y251 (attachment / source_info / value were ALL un-surfaced on loopback; the carry said to do them together, and this round does). `build_loopback_query` no longer hand-builds a parameters-only Query -- it reuses the wire SSOT `build_request_query_with_meta` and lifts out the inner `CodecZenohQuery` body, so the value(0x03) -> source_info(0x01) -> attachment(0x05) emit order, the Q_Z flag and the Z chain-continuation bits come from the single `RequestQueryBuilder::build()` SSOT and are NOT re-derived at the loopback site. A SessionLocal queryable's `QueryView` now observes parameters / attachment / source_info / payload / encoding exactly as a wire queryable does. No wire-path change, no new cfg gate, inventory UNCHANGED (this is a fidelity fix inside the already-active query plane, not a new atom).

BEHAVIOR CHANGE (deliberate, named): reusing the wire builder also adopts its caller-error asserts. Exactly one is reachable from the trimmed meta -- `RequestQueryBuilder::parameters` panics on a selector longer than REQUEST_QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_LEN (256). A `Locality::Any` / `Remote` query ALREADY hit that assert before this round (its wire branch calls the same builder), so only the `SessionLocal`-only path changes: it used to accept an over-256-byte selector silently (the old `SceBytes<256>` copy is unbounded under `alloc`, `N` advisory) and now panics like every other locality. Intended: a selector exceeding the wire bound could never reach a real wire queryable, so letting it through on loopback alone was a latent wire/loopback divergence. Documented as an explicit panic contract on `build_loopback_query`. The other builder asserts are unreachable from the trimmed meta (attachment's empty-slice panic is guarded by `!attachment.is_empty()`; timeout's zero panic cannot fire because the trimmed meta pins timeout_ms to 0; query_value asserts nothing).

SCOPE NOTE: `target` / `consolidation` / `timeout_ms` are deliberately EXCLUDED from the loopback meta -- `QueryView` exposes no accessor for any of them, target/timeout are Request-level exts a single-host fan-out has no relay to honour, and consolidation folds duplicate replies a single-source loopback cannot produce. So the loopback Query body differs from the wire Query body by exactly the (unobservable) Q_C consolidation byte. If a future round gives `QueryView` a consolidation/target accessor, this trim is the site to revisit.
