Round 311y253.decision_summary: R311y253 -- a REAL BUILD BREAK fixed at its root, surfaced as a side-finding of the R311y252 review and taken next under the CLAUDE.md absolute-priority rule (build errors preempt all other work). DialConfig (wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs) carries TWO #[cfg]-gated fields (tls @transport-link-tls, quic @transport-link-quic) and was the ONE options struct in the crate still constructed by exhaustive struct literal. Every literal in the tree named exactly ONE of the two fields, so each was missing the other's: SIX integration-test targets (quic_e2e, quic_datagram_e2e, scouting_multicast_loopback, session_reconnect_e2e, tls_e2e, tls_pem_mtls_e2e) failed E0063 under --all-features, in BOTH directions (missing field  on the tls-side literals, missing field  on the quic-side ones). The two directions are what proves this was structural, not a one-site typo: the shape itself was wrong, because an exhaustive literal over cfg-gated fields only compiles for the single feature combination its author happened to build with. Fixed structurally rather than per-site: DialConfig is now #[non_exhaustive] + with_tls / with_quic hard-gated builders -- the QueryOptions / PublishOptions / QueryableOptions idiom this struct was the lone exception to (QueryOptions' own docstring already says 'never struct-literal externally'), which makes the fragile form UNREPRESENTABLE for out-of-crate callers (tests/ are separate crates) so a future third cfg-gated transport field cannot break them either. All 5 literal sites converted. The DEEPER gap was the missing GATE: Layer C2 runs clippy --workspace --all-targets on the DEFAULT feature set only, so it never composes two optional features that each own a lane but are never enabled TOGETHER -- exactly how a six-target break shipped unseen. New Layer C1bf clippy-gates -p wz-runtime-tokio --all-targets --all-features. Scoped per-crate deliberately: a workspace-wide --all-features is structurally IMPOSSIBLE here (sce-rust-runtime declares no_std XOR http-send behind a compile_error!), which also explains why no such lane ever existed. Build-integrity + CI-gate only: no wire change, no cfg gate added, no atom flipped, inventory UNCHANGED. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 with C1bf passing; validate_workspace orphan new=+0.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_open.rs: `DialConfig` gains `#[non_exhaustive]` + two hard-gated `with_*` builders (`with_tls` @transport-link-tls, `with_quic` @transport-link-quic) -- the shape every other options struct in the crate already uses (`QueryOptions` / `PublishOptions` / `QueryableOptions`: "construct via `default` plus optional `with_*` setters -- never struct-literal externally"). Both setters are HARD-gated (the fn disappears when the feature is off) rather than ungated-no-op, because their parameter types (`TlsDialConfig` / `QuicDialConfig`) are themselves cfg-gated, so the signature cannot exist without the feature -- the same precedent as `QueryOptions::with_attachment` / `with_source_info`. `#[non_exhaustive]` makes the fragile exhaustive-literal form UNREPRESENTABLE for out-of-crate callers (integration tests under `tests/` are separate crates), so a future third cfg-gated transport field cannot silently break them either.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/{quic_e2e.rs, quic_datagram_e2e.rs, scouting_multicast_loopback.rs, tls_harness/mod.rs, session_reconnect_e2e.rs}: all 5 `DialConfig` struct literals converted to the builder form (`DialConfig::default().with_tls(..)` / `.with_quic(..)`). These 5 sites are the whole population -- there is no lib-internal literal.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/quic_e2e.rs: the old comment there had DOCUMENTED the fragile shape rather than fixing it ("the quic-only build has `quic` as the sole DialConfig field ... so no `..Default::default()` -- keeps clippy off `needless_update`"), i.e. it reasoned about ONE feature combo and rationalised the literal. The builder dissolves both horns of that dilemma at once: no omitted field, and no `needless_update` (there is no struct-update expression at all). Comment replaced with the real invariant.

scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer C1bf (`layer_c1bf_cargo_clippy_all_features`, registered after C1be) -- `cargo clippy -p wz-runtime-tokio --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. This is the gate that was MISSING: Layer C2 runs `clippy --workspace --all-targets` on the DEFAULT feature set only, so it never composes two optional features that each have their own lane but are never enabled together -- precisely the blind spot that let the DialConfig break ship. Scoped to `-p wz-runtime-tokio` deliberately: a workspace-wide `--all-features` is structurally IMPOSSIBLE here (sce-rust-runtime declares `no_std` and `http-send` mutually exclusive behind a compile_error! guard), so per-crate is the only form this check can take, and wz-runtime-tokio is the crate carrying the cfg-gated public struct fields.

The two directions are the proof that this was not a one-site typo but a structural defect: every literal named exactly one cfg-gated field, so the tls-side ones broke under transport-link-quic and the quic-side ones under transport-link-tls. Round 311y255.decision_summary: R311y255 -- closes the long-carried "publish_qos congestion knob" item, and does it by fixing the SSOT violation underneath rather than bolting a second setter onto it. The QoS wire byte packs three sub-fields (`priority` low 3 bits, `nodrop` bit 3, `express` bit 4, per `_z_n_qos_create` network.h:84-89), and all three already rode the wire and were FOREIGN-PROVEN -- R311y242 (`wz_qos_congestion_express_to_pico_zsub`) has a real zenoh-pico subscriber decode congestion + express. But only ONE had a typed entry point: `PublishOptions::with_priority` (y235). A caller wanting `Block` had to hand-assemble the whole byte via `with_qos(QosLevel::from_parts(..))`, which forces them to restate the priority and express they did not want to change. That asymmetry is the carry. The naive fix -- add two more setters doing their own bit surgery -- would have spread the bit layout across a THIRD site: `QosLevel::from_parts` documents itself as "the SOLE packer ... so the layout lives once (no drift)", yet `PublishOptions::with_priority` already open-coded `& !0x07`, quietly falsifying that claim. So the layout was consolidated into the type that owns it: `QosLevel` gains named bit constants, a `congestion()` unpacker (the missing third accessor beside `priority()` / `is_express()`), and three per-field MERGE setters (`with_priority` / `with_congestion` / `with_express`) that each touch only their own sub-field; `from_parts` is now COMPOSED from those three rather than restating the shifts, making "the layout lives once" structurally true instead of a comment asking to be believed. `PublishOptions::with_priority` now delegates (its `& !0x07` is gone) and gains its two siblings, `with_congestion_control` + `with_express`, each gated on its own `pubsub-*` feature exactly as `with_priority` is. Untouched sub-fields fall back to the wire-DEFAULT byte (0x05 = Data / Drop / no-express), NOT a zeroed `Control` byte -- the trap R311y226 named. Behaviour-preservation is proven by the PRE-EXISTING byte-compare guards, which still pass unchanged: `qos_level_from_parts_packs_zenoh_pico_layout` pins 0x11 / 0x0D across the `from_parts` rewrite, and `publish_options_with_priority_is_single_source_band` pins bit-preservation across the delegation. Also carries a doc-truth-up: a foreign-proof test still flagged a `publish_common.rs` comment as STALE, but that comment had since been corrected -- a stale claim ABOUT a stale claim -- so it was dropped. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0; no wire change, no new atom, inventory UNCHANGED (the wire bits were already active and foreign-proven; this is the typed API surface for them).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-session-core/src/sample.rs: `QosLevel` becomes the single home of the `_z_n_qos_create` bit layout. New private named constants (PRIORITY_MASK 0x07 / NODROP_BIT 1<<3 / EXPRESS_BIT 1<<4) replace every open-coded literal; new `congestion()` unpacker completes the accessor trio beside `priority()` and `is_express()` (both now const fn and expressed via the constants); new per-field MERGE setters `with_priority` / `with_congestion` / `with_express` each rewrite ONLY their own sub-field and preserve the siblings. `from_parts` is now COMPOSED from those three setters instead of restating `priority.wire_byte() | (congestion.wire_bit() << 3) | ((express as u8) << 4)`, so its own "the SOLE packer ... the layout lives once" doc claim is structurally true rather than aspirational.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/publish_common.rs: `PublishOptions` gains the two typed QoS knobs that `with_priority` had been missing -- `with_congestion_control(CongestionControl)` (gated `pubsub-congestion-control`) and `with_express(bool)` (gated `pubsub-express`) -- each gated on its own feature exactly as `with_priority` is on `pubsub-priority`. All three now delegate to the `QosLevel` merge setters through a shared private `qos_base()` helper, so `with_priority`'s open-coded `& !0x07` mask is gone and no consumer re-derives the layout. `qos_base()` returns the already-attached QoS else `QosLevel::DEFAULT` (0x05), so sub-fields the caller did not set match a DEFAULT publish rather than a zeroed `Control`-priority byte.

Round 311y256.decision_summary: R311y256 -- scope honesty pass on the inventory, triggered by the user asking the right question: "why is there an out-of-scope at all?" -- which is a fair challenge, because the north star is explicitly NO-DEFERRAL. Reading the actual `reason` fields (not memory) showed the "out-of-scope" bucket was THREE different things wearing ONE label, and that the label was hiding a real half-violation. (1) OBVIATED (5, now DEPRECATED): plugin-manager / plugin-host-trait / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-abi-compat / storage-mgr-dynamic-volume-loading. These exist in zenoh ONLY because it chose runtime dynamic loading -- a registry of loaded plugins, a uniform start seam for them, a Declared->Loaded FSM whose gap exists solely because dlopen can fail, a cross-binary ABI gate whose sole caller is the dynamic loader, and the storage twin that dlopens volume .so files. wz composes subsystems at BUILD time (cargo features + cfg), so there is no registry, no seam, no load step, and exactly one ABI by construction. There is nothing to build; building them would mean re-adding a design wz deliberately beat (feedback_north_star_superset_not_mirror). Leaving them `reserved` misread as permanent incompleteness, so `deprecated` is the honest class. (2) REAL BACKLOG (4, out-of-scope label REMOVED): api-compat-c, api-compat-pico, plugin-dynamic-loading, storage-backend-filesystem. Their reasons pleaded "separate-repo" -- but a separate repo is zenoh's PACKAGING choice, not an impossibility, and under NO-DEFERRAL a scoping choice belongs on the schedule, not on a shelf. api-compat-pico is the most glaring: the north star is literally "zenoh + zenoh-pico FULL". storage-backend-filesystem's own reason already conceded it is the "lowest-dep Durable candidate, std-only" -- zero third-party dependency, plugging into a volume seam that is already FOUNDATIONAL and built. These four are now genuinely-unbuilt work, ordered AFTER the cross-impl-proof push per the user-decided SEQUENCE. (3) GENUINELY OUT-OF-SCOPE (2, reason REWRITTEN): storage-backend-rocksdb, storage-backend-external-db. The "separate repos" pretext is dropped as dishonest -- it was the same pretext rejected for the four above. The real reason is that these are THIRD-PARTY SYSTEM ADAPTERS (heavy C++ / network-DB client dependencies), not protocol surface, and they prove nothing further about wz's protocol fidelity: the Durable-storage capability they would demonstrate is already carried by storage-backend-filesystem over the identical volume seam. Omitting them leaves NO part of the zenoh+pico protocol catalog unproven, so this is not a NO-DEFERRAL violation; re-openable on a concrete deployment demand. Round 311y257.decision_summary: R311y257 -- give the inventory an IMPLEMENTATION axis, so it can answer "what work remains" without grepping English. The user asked how many rounds are left to pico/AP-full; trying to answer surfaced a structural defect, not just a missing number. `status` (active / reserved / deprecated) answers "is there a cfg knob?" -- per the active-iff-cfg-toggle rule -- and does NOT answer "is this built?". Those are different questions, and `reserved` was silently lumping together four unrelated situations: already-built-but-always-on (FOUNDATIONAL), genuinely unbuilt, deliberately excluded, and built-under-a-different-atom's-cargo-feature. The only place that distinction lived was free prose in the `reason` field, so "what is left" degraded to grepping English -- and two different greps of mine disagreed (10 vs 27), which is how the defect was caught. The earlier "~11 remaining atoms" figure came from the unreliable grep and was RETRACTED rather than re-guessed. Fixed within the closed Mnemosyne schema, since adding a field is forbidden (anti-patterns #9): the FIRST token of every non-active atom's `reason` must now be a tag from a closed 8-set, and the tag must agree with `status`. FOUNDATIONAL (built, always-on, no knob) / PARTIAL (built, named residual) / UNVERIFIED (code portable by construction, no CI lane proves it -- work is a lane, not code) / UNBUILT (genuinely not implemented) / BEYOND-PICO (deferred by design) / OUT-OF-SCOPE (deliberately excluded) / OBVIATED (no wz analog by construction) / PHANTOM (does not exist in zenoh). `active` needs no tag: built AND gated is unambiguous. PARTIAL and UNVERIFIED were not invented for symmetry -- the data forced them: session-extqos is NOT unbuilt, it is BUILT under the differently-named `transport-qos` cargo feature with a named S4 residual (an error in my own earlier count, which had it as "beyond-pico deferred"); and platform-macos / platform-windows have NO code to write at all (std+tokio is portable by construction) -- what they lack is a CI lane. Forcing either into UNBUILT or FOUNDATIONAL would have made the inventory lie. All 218 atoms tagged, 51 by this round's prefixing pass and the rest already conformant, with ZERO original reason text lost (verified against the committed HEAD store). The invariant is enforced as #5 in scripts/audit-catalog-status.sh (Layer A3), which also now PRINTS the roll-up every run: "REMAINING WORK (UNBUILT + PARTIAL + UNVERIFIED) = 9". So the question that started this is now a gate output, not a grep. full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate_workspace orphan new=+0; active count UNCHANGED (no code touched).
changes_bullets: docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json (inventory only; no code touched): every non-active atom's `reason` now begins with a closed-set implementation tag. 51 entries were prefixed by this round via the typed `mnemosyne-cli set-inventory-status` primitive (looped, never a direct JSON edit); the remaining non-active entries already began with a conformant tag and were left untouched (the pass is idempotent). Legacy synonyms were NORMALIZED rather than double-prefixed (the "REAL BACKLOG" prefix introduced in R311y256 is exactly UNBUILT, so it was replaced, not stacked).

Six atoms had NO classifiable marker at all and were classified by direct read of their own reason text: platform-macos + platform-windows -> UNVERIFIED (their reasons already said "std+tokio host-portable but NO wz CI lane -> unverified host; cfg=0" -- there is no code to write, only a lane); platform-qnx -> OUT-OF-SCOPE (its reason: "neither zenoh nor zenoh-pico has a QNX port" -- outside the zenoh+pico catalog entirely, a 2nd-horizon candidate); routing-failover -> BEYOND-PICO ("pico none -> P4-deferred"); runtime-tokio-uring + runtime-zero-copy -> UNBUILT (genuinely unbuilt, but PERF concerns sourced from wz's own RFC/ARCHITECTURE, not protocol surface).

Two atoms were RECLASSIFIED against my own earlier count, which the tagging pass proved wrong: session-extqos -> PARTIAL, not "beyond-pico deferred" -- its reason records "IMPL R311y215: the wz per-priority QoS transport is now BUILT under the transport-qos CARGO FEATURE ... session-extqos stays RESERVED (0 cfg(feature=session-extqos) sites -- the wz feature is named transport-qos)", i.e. it is built under another atom's knob with a named S4 residual. session-stateless-accept -> BEYOND-PICO (its own reason says so, past the 250-char window my first survey scanned).

scripts/audit-catalog-status.sh: new invariant #5 (implementation axis), enforced inside the existing Layer A3 gate rather than as a new layer -- catalog-status truthfulness is the same concern, so it belongs in the same SSOT. It FAILS, naming the atom, when (a) a non-active atom's reason does not start with a closed-set tag, or (b) the tag disagrees with status (e.g. OBVIATED implies deprecated). The script's own header already claimed a "FOUNDATIONAL marker in its reason" convention -- it was documented but never enforced; this makes it real.

scripts/audit-catalog-status.sh: the audit now PRINTS the implementation roll-up on every run -- the per-tag tally plus the line "REMAINING WORK (UNBUILT + PARTIAL + UNVERIFIED) = N: <atom list>". Answering "what is left" is now reading one CI line.
verification_bullets: ZERO INFORMATION LOST -- the load-bearing check for a 51-entry prose rewrite. The only intentional edit is the "REAL BACKLOG" -> "UNBUILT" synonym normalization from R311y256, which is a rename of a prefix this project introduced one round earlier, not a loss of source-cited content.

The gate FAILS on drift, proven in BOTH classes against doctored inventory copies (the store itself was never touched): (a) stripping the tag from api-compat-pico's reason -- the "a new atom lands untagged" case -- makes the audit exit non-zero with "FAIL: non-active atom whose reason does not START with an implementation tag", naming it; (b) flipping plugin-manager from deprecated to reserved while its reason still says OBVIATED makes it exit non-zero with "FAIL: implementation tag disagrees with status", naming the atom, its tag, and the status the tag implies. A gate that cannot fail is not a gate; both arms are exercised.

NEAR-MISS worth recording: the first attempt to prove drift-arm (b) reported a non-zero exit and was very nearly written up as 'caught'. It was not -- the fixture file had never been created (the command building it hit a 2-minute timeout mid-way), so the audit had died on a FileNotFoundError. A non-zero exit is NOT evidence a gate fired; the FAIL MESSAGE is. The arm was then re-run against a real fixture and produced the named failure quoted above. Judge a gate by what it PRINTS, not merely by its exit code.

The sidecar JSON was NEVER edited directly (anti-patterns #6). Reasons were passed via `--reason "$(cat FILE)"` so backticked identifiers survive (feedback_ledger_decision_backtick_shell_eval).

There is no dry-run on a mutate primitive. Repaired immediately from the committed HEAD store, and the repair verified by diffing ALL 218 inventory entries against HEAD (0 differences) BEFORE proceeding with the round. Lesson recorded: never aim a mutate primitive at a live entry to discover its flags.

Measured first (PRINCIPLES: base optimization on measurement, not assumption): a full run is 93 layers / 1349s / 22.5 min, and the top costs are Layer F 115s (MCU footprint), Layer A3 106s, C1ay 86s, C1j 67s, G 61s. Round 311y26.decision_summary: R311y26 -- FreeRTOS integration Round 2: crates/wz-runtime-freertos, the cooperative single-task PROFILE. Does NOT reimplement the executor or impl Runtime -- FreertosRuntime is a type alias for CoopRuntime<FreertosClock> (the audited wz-runtime-coop executor SSOT -- task pool/waker/timer queue -- reused verbatim, parameterised by the clock). Supplies ONLY the FreeRTOS seams: FreertosClock<TICK_HZ> (ClockSource over xTaskGetTickCount, const-generic over configTICK_RATE_HZ, mirrors SystickClock<CYCLES_PER_US>) + FreertosAllocator (GlobalAlloc over heap_4 pvPortMalloc/vPortFree, over-align-safe; deploy declares #[global_allocator]). Sync needs nothing (CoopRuntime uses critical_section; deploy supplies impl); net reuses NO_SYS lwip. Per the R311y25 lesson the CI lane (Layer G G.15, thumbv7m + WZ_FREERTOS_CONFIG) lands THIS round. Verified: cross-compile thumbv7m EXIT=0 + Layer G pass (G.14 + G.15 OK) + clippy(deny) + fmt + validate orphan new=+0. NEXT Round 3: boot + deploy/mcu-freertos-demo + QEMU mps2 e2e.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-freertos (new crate): Cargo.toml (full workspace inheritance + [lints] workspace=true + [lib]; deps freertos-sys + wz-runtime-coop[alloc]) + src/lib.rs (#![no_std]). The FreeRTOS cooperative single-task PROFILE.

FreertosRuntime<const TICK_HZ: u32> = type alias for CoopRuntime<FreertosClock<TICK_HZ>> — the executor is NOT reimplemented; the audited wz-runtime-coop task pool / waker / cancel / timer queue (the SSOT) is reused verbatim, parameterised only by the clock seam. = zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=0 ST mode (one task hosts run_until_idle).

FreertosClock<const TICK_HZ: u32>: impl wz_runtime_coop::ClockSource; now_us() = xTaskGetTickCount() as u64 * 1_000_000 / TICK_HZ (multiply-before-divide = exact for any tick rate; ticks*1e6 < 2^52 so no u64 overflow). Const-generic over configTICK_RATE_HZ — mirrors the bare-metal wz_mcu_clock::SystickClock<CYCLES_PER_US> const-generic timebase shape. ZST + Copy.

FreertosAllocator: unsafe impl GlobalAlloc over freertos-sys pvPortMalloc/vPortFree (heap_4). Direct for align<=8 (heap_4's portBYTE_ALIGNMENT on ARMv7-M); over-aligned requests over-allocate (size+align+usize), align up, and stash the heap_4 base pointer in the usize slot below the returned address so dealloc recovers it. Lives in the profile crate (not the deploy) because the FreeRTOS heap IS the kernel's — unlike the bare-metal profile's free embedded_alloc choice; the deploy declares #[global_allocator] static = FreertosAllocator.

Seams NOT needed here: sync (CoopRuntime already uses critical_section::Mutex; the deploy supplies the critical-section impl), net (reuses NO_SYS=1 lwip via wz-link-lwip, no FreeRTOS sys_arch — the executor polls lwIP single-threaded).

Round 311y28.decision_summary: R311y28 -- FreeRTOS integration Round 4 (the LAST FreeRTOS round): platform-freertos ACTIVE flip. The reserved platform-freertos atom is promoted to active by a GENUINE cfg(feature = "platform-freertos") site in crates/wz/src/lib.rs (`pub use wz_runtime_freertos as runtime_freertos`) -- the ONE platform-* that gates real code, because target_os CANNOT distinguish a FreeRTOS deploy from bare-metal (both are target_os = "none" on thumbv7m-none-eabi); so unlike platform-bare-metal (target-triple+no_std-selected = FOUNDATIONAL) the RTOS is an opt-in cfg knob (A3 active<=>cfg). The wz facade gains an optional wz-runtime-freertos dep pulled by `platform-freertos = ["dep:wz-runtime-freertos"]` (the runtime axis stays orthogonal -- the deploy composes runtime-coop); deploy/mcu-freertos-demo is rewired to drop its direct wz-runtime-freertos dep and consume the gate via wz::runtime_freertos, making it the real consumer the existing Layer Q.frt lane exercises (compile+link+boot under deny-warnings). HONESTY (R311y13 obligation): labelled the cooperative single-task profile (ONE FreeRTOS task hosts the reused wz-runtime-coop executor = zenoh-pico Z_FEATURE_MULTI_THREAD=0); native multi-task (xTaskCreate per read/lease thread, the pico default) recorded as a re-openable FUTURE profile, NOT shipped. Verified by EXECUTION: the rewired demo cross-builds (221360-byte ELF) + boots QEMU mps2-an385 PASS SYS_EXIT=0; cargo tree confirms the dep is genuinely toggled (absent OFF, present ON); Layer A3 active 95->96; validate orphan new=+0, T3 warn=4 unchanged. The FreeRTOS cooperative single-task profile is now COMPLETE end-to-end; Zephyr is the remaining RTOS port. A deploy preset (preset-freertos-*) is deferred as re-openable (the demo composes features directly; no consumer yet).

Round 311y30.decision_summary: R311y30 -- session-review remediation (the textbook/SSOT/north-star/cost-irrelevant trigger correctly forced a 4-agent INDEPENDENT adversarial review, direct-read arbitrated, over my session-end self-assessment which rated the work clean; the pattern is now PROVEN 4x -- R311y13/y20/y25/y30). The review caught a real HIGH soundness bug self-review MISSED. FIXES: (1) HIGH ZephyrAllocator alignment UB -- wz-runtime-zephyr copied FreeRTOS's HEAP_ALIGN=8, but Zephyr's k_malloc (kernel/mempool.c:107 = z_alloc_helper with sys_heap_noalign_alloc) only guarantees the sys_heap BASE alignment = sizeof(void*)=4 on a SMALL heap (the MCU default CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_SMALL_ONLY; heap.c:84 asserts ret & (big_heap?7:3)==0), so an align-8 allocation (any u64-bearing struct, incl wz-runtime-coop's OWN timer-queue Box entries) took the direct k_malloc branch and got a 4-aligned pointer = misalignment UB; fixed HEAP_ALIGN 8->4 so align>4 routes through the already-correct over-aligned stash branch. FreeRTOS heap_4 genuinely guarantees 8 (portBYTE_ALIGNMENT + a runtime assert), so FreertosAllocator's 8 stays correct -- the bug was the unverified copy of a constant across platforms. (2) MED the wz facade had NO compile_error for runtime-tokio + platform-freertos (two incompatible runtime profiles silently co-linked; the existing XOR guards only runtime-tokio+runtime-coop); added a dedicated gate making the illegal combo unrepresentable, keeping the runtime(§5.13)/platform(§5.14) axes orthogonal -- platform-freertos does NOT imply runtime-coop (deploys compose both explicitly, exactly as the MCU presets do for platform-bare-metal+runtime-coop). (3) honesty: the memory plan's "PROVEN end-to-end" scoped to "build-shape/toolchain proven via a scratch toy, NOT the wz Zephyr port (unbuilt/unbooted)". OVER-FLAGS arbitrated away by direct-read (agents over-flag): R311y29 having no ledger entry = NOT a violation (pure-code rounds y24/y26/y27/y29 did not append; review-remediation rounds y13/y20/y25/y30 do; the platform-zephyr inventory flip at Z3 will capture the track in the SSOT); the lib-check-only G.16/G.17 CI = an honestly-labeled staged limitation (Z2's deploy brings the real link+boot lane); the stale R311y27 strings in the demo = a harmless NIT (Q.frt judges by the semihost exit code, not a PASS-string grep). Verified: the guard fires on runtime-tokio+platform-freertos (compile_error) while valid runtime-coop+platform-freertos still builds; wz-runtime-zephyr host clippy(deny-warnings) + cross thumbv7m clean; full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; validate orphan new=+0; A3 active=96 UNCHANGED (code-only fixes, no inventory flip). Round 311y38.decision_summary: R311y38 -- adminspace §5.23 self-sufficiency round (the carry's #2 self-sufficiency track): made adminspace-core honestly buildable + functional under --no-default-features by fixing two latent defects the default-set-only C1am lane masked, declaring two genuine-but-undeclared deps, and adding the standalone CI lane C1an that locks them. (1) session/mod.rs carried a `use ResponseSink as _` that went UNUSED under --all-targets deny-warnings dev-dep feature-unification (the trait send_response_final is a pure forward to the always-present inherent SessionLinkActions::send_response_final, so on the concrete Arc<SessionLinkActions> the import only re-routed resolution to the same fn) -- removed it, behavior identical. TWO honesty/framing defects in y43 were fixed: (1) the composition test's headline assertion was a TAUTOLOGY -- config.to_admin_json() == WzConfig::from_init_params(&params).to_admin_json() holds by construction (to_admin_json omits interceptor state, both sides derive from the same params), so it would pass even if the drive were broken; replaced with a CONCRETE falsifiable expected JSON and the comment re-scoped from "refutes the y42 finding at the composition level" to the honest "binding-level foundation; the node-level/wire composition is the deferred Phase-2 step". (2) the run_peer "RETAINED for its whole lifetime / no longer DROPPED / shutdown-echo load-bearing, not dead scaffolding" framing OVER-CLAIMED: in committed y42 wz_config was ALREADY a function-scoped owned binding (never moved -> dropped at function end, not after install), so y43 made NO lifetime change; the only real run_peer delta was a shutdown log line with no consumer. Withdrawn: the shutdown echo removed, the comment rewritten to the honest scope (a build-time install+log view, NOT yet a live-mutate target; the install now routes through the InterceptorSink trait seam; the combined node deferred). R311y43's REAL substance stands: the InterceptorSink trait seam (config decoupled from the concrete forwarder) + the binding-level composition test. Inventory unchanged (A3 active=101). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0 (re-run post-remediation); validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

Round 311y44.decision_summary: R311y44 -- §5.23 Phase 2a: forwarder self-query dispatch bridge (de-risk the routing mechanism before hosting the admin handler). The blocker (verified by direct read): the LinkstateForwarder EXCLUDES self from query routing and its declare_queryable is interest-advertisement only (no handler) -- so a routing peer cannot answer its OWN queryable today; reply-production lived only at the Session level. This round adds a LOCAL-queryable-with-handler seam: register_local_queryable(keyexpr, complete, handler) stores a reply-producing FnMut(&dyn QueryView, &mut dyn ReplyOut) (the Session declare_queryable shape MINUS Send -- single-task, so a handler may capture an Rc, enabling Phase 2b's shared WzConfig), reusing declare_queryable for the interest flood. forward_request's empty-route branch (where a self-only match lands, since self is excluded from routing -- and each node's admin keyexpr is self-unique) now dispatches a matching local queryable: builds a LocalQueryView over the Request, runs the handler against a ForwarderReplyOut accumulator (the same pure response_build builders the Session path uses), then emits the Response(s) + closing ResponseFinal on the inbound face with rid = the inbound request rid -- the existing per-hop return path unwinds it (single- AND multi-hop; the mesh return routing is already live). User chose 2a-first (de-risk); the admin handler host + shared WzConfig + wire config GET are Phase 2b, the PUT is Phase 3. Adversarial review (2 independent agents): NO soundness/build defect (multi-hop unwind traced CORRECT; borrow-discipline sound -- handlers run under the local_queryables borrow, send_to_face after release; rid correct; empty-route scoping correct; byte-identical no-match fall-through). Test-strength remediation applied per the review: added a reply_keyed_encoded test (the Phase-2b admin production path -- replies under a DIFFERENT concrete key than the wildcard query) + an AllComplete-skips-incomplete test, and softened two doc-comments (the "faithfully" mirror claim + the build-error note). full run-ci RUNCI_EXIT=0; A3 active=101 unchanged (routing plumbing under existing routing-peer/query-queryable gates, no new atom); validate_workspace orphan new=+0.

Round 311y45.decision_summary: R311y45 -- §5.23 Phase 2b: a routing peer hosts its adminspace on the forwarder and answers its OWN config GET over the wire, reading its forwarder-bound WzConfig -- the runtime composition the R311y42 review found missing, now STRUCTURALLY closed (ONE Rc<RefCell<WzConfig>> both drives the forwarder AND answers the GET). Built on the y44 self-dispatch bridge. Changes: (1) EXTRACTED the Session admin handler's match+reply logic into a Session-INDEPENDENT SSOT wz_session_core::adminspace::answer_admin_query(view, out, ctx, sessions, config_json) + AdminAnswerCtx (root local_data / metrics / config + the read gate, now carried in ctx.read so it is feature-toggle-independent); (2) REFACTORED Session::declare_adminspace to call it (6 existing adminspace tests pass UNCHANGED -- parity); (3) run_peer promotes wz_config to a SHARED Rc<RefCell<WzConfig>> (the Phase-1 deferred sharing primitive, with the admin handler as its 2nd holder) and, under the new --config-queryable flag, register_local_queryable's the admin handler reading the shared config via answer_admin_query; (4) wz-runtime-tokio re-exports adminspace (cfg adminspace-core) + zid_hex; the demo's routing-peer feature pulls wz/adminspace-core; (5) a WIRE e2e (wz_peer_adminspace_config.rs, Layer E6): peer A --config-queryable hosts the admin, client B --connect A --query @/<A_zid>/peer/config gets A's config JSON over TCP (asserted: keyexpr + body=Put + the typed read-at-open fields). User chose the wire e2e as the proof. SCOPE/HONESTY (2-agent adversarial review, NO correctness/soundness/build/parity/flakiness defect found): the e2e proves config-GET-over-the-wire WORKS + the single shared instance serves both surfaces BY CONSTRUCTION; the served JSON is the READ-AT-OPEN mirror (handshake-fixed), so it cannot OBSERVE a runtime change -- live-reconfigure-over-wire visibility (interceptor config in the JSON) is a deferred §5.23 layer, and sessions[] for the forwarder host is empty (live-faces enumeration deferred). Both honesty findings remediated (the "LIVE" framing qualified to read-at-open / structural composition; the session/mod.rs sessions[] comment corrected to empty/deferred). changes_bullets: [SSOT] hoist the JSON string escaper to wz-session-core ungated json::escape_into (alloc-only, no adminspace-core dep): adminspace::push_json_str now delegates, config.rs drops its push_json_string twin and calls the shared one. The 18-line correctness-bearing escaper lives in ONE place (+ 2 escaper unit tests).

[never-run, R311y25 class] run-ci C1ao += `cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --features config-mutate-runtime,access-acl --lib to_admin_json`, so the cfg(all(routing-peer,access-acl)) acl_default/acl_deny branch of to_admin_json_is_typed_alphabetical actually EXECUTES in CI (every unfiltered full-lib lane builds routing-peer OFF, so that assert was never run).

[honesty] to_admin_json now emits acl_default ("allow"/"deny" base verdict) alongside acl_deny -> a default-deny policy is no longer mis-read as "open" (a bare acl_deny:[] inverts the truth). Refactored to_admin_json to an ordered (key, value-json) builder; the prior trailing-comma-prepend only worked for one leading optional key and broke for the deferred mid-object fields (downsampling/sessions). String values go through the shared escaper. 3 byte-exact tests updated.

[zenoh fidelity] admin_config_write_key doc corrected: only the key PATTERN (@/<zid>/<whatami>/config/**) matches zenoh; the acl-deny sub-key + bare-keyexpr payload is a deliberate MVP affordance, NOT a json-pointer/json5 subset (the prior doc over-claimed insert_json5 equivalence).

[strengthen] new 3-process GET-flip e2e wz_peer_config_write_acl_deny_is_get_observable_over_the_wire: A hosts BOTH --config-queryable + --config-writable off ONE shared WzConfig; B PUTs A's config/acl-deny; C (connect client) GETs A's config AFTER the reconfigure and observes acl_deny []->["mesh/data"] over the wire -- the headline GET-observable claim end-to-end (vs the prior composition-only argument), and a direct guard on the y42 two-instance gap. Rides the existing E6 registration (same test file).

Round 311y86.decision_summary: R311y86 -- the startup history query: ext-pubsub-advanced-history (§5.25) flipped ACTIVE. A history-enabled AdvancedSubscriber issues a GET over `<ke>/@adv/**` (with a `_max=N` cap) on declare, recovering the publishers' cached samples so a LATE JOINER gets the history (zenoh advanced_subscriber.rs:763-811); a `history_pending` gate buffers live samples until the GET completes so the older history delivers first (zenoh :504-516). Proven by a composed late-joiner e2e + a gating unit. The `_time` age filter + detect_late_publishers liveliness are documented follow-ons.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: HistoryConfig (sample_depth: Option<usize>) + new/max_samples builders. RecoveryConfig gains a cfg-history `history: Option<HistoryConfig>` field + with_history (the subscriber config carries both recovery + history). State gains a cfg-history `history_pending: bool`. issue_history_query GETs `<base>/@adv/**` (+ `_max=N` when sample_depth is set), feeding replies through the shared recovered_sample_from_reply -> handle_recovered; on the terminal Final, finish_history clears history_pending + flushes EVERY source's buffer oldest-first (zenoh InitialRepliesHandler::drop).

ingest_sequenced None-case: while history_pending, BUFFER the first sample (live or recovered) instead of delivering (zenoh :504-516) + skip the recovery trigger (the history GET is recovering it). declare_impl issues the history GET AFTER the live subscriber is declared (so a live sample during the GET is gated); in loopback it completes synchronously on declare.

Refactor: extracted recovered_sample_from_reply (the reply -> (key, sn, Sample) re-key, reading source_info + rebuilding the Put) shared by the recovery + history GETs (DRY -- issue_recovery_query now calls it too). The 6 unit-test State literals gained the cfg-history history_pending field.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml + crates/wz/Cargo.toml: ext-pubsub-advanced-history composes ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery (it reuses the reorder buffer + recovered-reply ordering + query plane); the facade forwards it. scripts/run-ci.sh: new Layer C1av co-enables history + advanced-publisher + pubsub-allow-loop -> the composed late-joiner e2e + the gating unit + clippy + facade build. inventory: ext-pubsub-advanced-history reserved -> active.
verification_bullets: cargo test -p wz-runtime-tokio --features ext-pubsub-advanced-history,ext-pubsub-advanced-publisher,pubsub-allow-loop --lib advanced_subscriber: 13 pass, incl composed_history_recovers_cache_for_late_joiner (cache holds 0,1,2; a history-enabled subscriber's declare GETs demo/data/@adv/** -> the cache answers -> the history_pending gate buffers -> the terminal Final flushes -> delivered [0,1,2] on declare) + history_pending_buffers_then_flushes_in_order (samples buffer while history pending, flush oldest-first on completion).

Regression: recovery (no history) 11 pass + non-recovery 3 pass -> the cfg-history field + the None-case gating gate out cleanly. clippy -D warnings clean; facade `cargo build -p wz --features ext-pubsub-advanced-history` exit 0; default `cargo build -p wz-runtime-tokio --lib` exit 0; fmt clean.

The `_max` cap is built (issue_history_query emits `_max=N`) + the cache filters it (advanced_cache answer_from_ring `_max` unit); the composed test uses the uncapped GET (recover all). DEFERRED (documented): the `_time` age filter (HistoryConfig::max_age consumer + the cache `_time`-range filter still IGNORED in advanced_cache.rs -> over-returns on an age-bounded history query) + detect_late_publishers liveliness.

changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_cache.rs cache_sample (review C1): `while ring.len() >= max_samples { pop_front }` -> `if`. crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs finish_recovery (review C2): gate the buffer flush on `!history_pending`. advanced_subscriber.rs (periodic spawn) + advanced_publisher.rs (heartbeat spawn) (review C4): `(period.as_millis() as u64).max(1)`. A sub-ms Duration truncated to period_ms=0 -> clock.sleep(0) busy spin (a GET / beacon storm). Clamped to >=1ms.

Round 311y88.decision_summary: R311y88 -- session-review remediation, the HIGH (H1 signature-stability): AdvancedSubscriber::declare no longer routes through the spawning declare_impl. It now builds a NON-spawning subscriber whose callback only orders (handle_live with retransmission off never returns a RecoveryRequest, so it neither captures the session nor tokio::spawns), giving it bounds IDENTICAL to the recovery-OFF build (T: TimeSource + 'static; no Send+Sync+'static / Session: Send / R: 'static). Toggling the additive ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery feature can therefore no longer tighten declare's signature and break a downstream non-recovery caller's compile -- the project's signature-stability invariant restored. The spawn-requiring bounds now live ONLY on declare_with_recovery.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: the recovery-build `declare` gets its own non-spawning body (was `Self::declare_impl(.., None)`, which unconditionally tokio::spawns + whose callback captures session.clone()). Its where-bounds drop from {R:'static, T: TimeSource+Send+Sync+'static, Session<R,T,Unicast>: Send+'static} to {T: TimeSource+'static} -- character-identical to the recovery-OFF `declare`. The callback calls handle_live and ignores the always-None (retransmission=false) result -> no session capture, no spawn; _periodic/_heartbeat_sub set to None.

declare_with_recovery + declare_impl unchanged: they legitimately spawn (periodic/heartbeat), so they keep the tight Send+Sync+'static bounds -- but that signature is additive (a cfg-gated method that simply does not exist with the feature off), not a toggle-unstable change to an existing signature, so it does not violate signature-stability.

Root-cause fix per the review: the H1 break was structural (plain declare reusing the spawning declare_impl + the session-capturing shared callback), not cosmetic; isolating the spawn/GET path to declare_with_recovery is the textbook separation.

Round 311y89.decision_summary: R311y89 -- review C3 remediation: the advanced-subscriber recovery/history GETs now carry a query timeout so a no-answerer GET cannot wedge the subscriber forever. issue_recovery_query / issue_history_query were building QueryOptions with timeout_ms=0 (the never-expire sentinel: the pending reply entry registers with deadline_ms=None, which ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out skips on every pass) and swallowing the Session::query Result. With Locality::Any a no-cache history GET gets only the loopback Final (1 of 2 expected) and the peer Final never arrives, so finish_history never runs -> history_pending stays set -> EVERY live sample buffers undelivered (the subscriber delivers nothing). Fix: a RecoveryConfig::query_timeout field (default Duration::from_secs(10) = zenoh-ext RecoveryConfig::query_timeout default + zenoh-pico Z_GET_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT), converted by recovery_query_timeout_ms (clamped to [1,u32::MAX] so a 0/sub-ms Duration cannot re-open the never-expire sentinel) and threaded via with_timeout_ms onto every recovery + history GET; ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery now composes query-timeout (else with_timeout_ms no-ops). Plus an Err-rollback: a GET that fails to issue calls finish_recovery / finish_history directly so pending_queries / history_pending do not wedge. STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory unchanged (ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery/-history stay active).
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: RecoveryConfig gained an always-present `query_timeout: Duration` field (default Duration::from_secs(10), zenoh's shared recovery/history GET timeout) + a with_query_timeout builder (signature-stable).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: new pure recovery_query_timeout_ms(Duration)->u32 clamps to [1,u32::MAX] -- the LOWER clamp is the correctness bite (a 0/sub-ms Duration is the timeout_ms==0 never-expire sentinel that registers the GET with deadline_ms=None, which ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out skips on every pass).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: issue_recovery_query + issue_history_query take a timeout_ms param set via QueryOptions::with_timeout_ms; run_periodic_tick threads it; declare_impl computes timeout_ms once and threads it to all 4 GET call sites (sample-driven / periodic / heartbeat / startup-history).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs: issue_recovery_query / issue_history_query now inspect the Session::query Result and roll back on Err (finish_recovery / finish_history) -- a GET that never registered (Session::query rolled its pending entry back on a wire-emit error) can be released by neither its on_final nor the deadline sweep, so pending_queries / history_pending would wedge otherwise.
crates/wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml: ext-pubsub-advanced-recovery now composes query-timeout (with_timeout_ms is a silent no-op without it, which would leave the wedge in place).

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs tests: +recovery_query_timeout_ms_clamps_to_a_live_deadline (pure clamp/cap unit) + history_get_with_no_answerer_is_rescued_by_the_timeout_sweep (composed: a no-answerer Locality::Any history GET buffers a live sample undelivered; driving observer.replies.sweep_timed_out past the deadline + drain_deferred_fires fires finish_history and the buffer flushes); the composed_periodic_tick test call updated for the new arg.

STRUCTURE-only, no wire/behavior change for the existing combos; inventory unchanged.

Round 311y92.decision_summary: R311y92 -- review S1 remediation: the @adv key-expr namespace SSOT. The advanced publisher CONSTRUCTS the @adv/pub/<zid>/<disc>/_ KE (cache queryable + liveliness token + heartbeat beacon) while the advanced subscriber MATCHES it (the recovery @adv/*/<zid>/<eid>/** + history @adv/** + heartbeat-sub @adv/pub/** GETs + the parse_heartbeat_source beacon parser). Previously the publisher held KE_ADV_PREFIX/KE_EMPTY consts (with pub still inline) while the subscriber hand-wrote @adv/pub inline x4, so the namespace had no single source of truth -- a drift on either side would silently break the recovery round-trip. Fix: a new pub(crate) advanced_ke module (the @adv/pub/_ consts + the publisher_adv_ke / recovery_get_ke / history_get_ke / heartbeat_sub_ke builders, each cfg-gated to its consumer feature so no combo dead-codes) that BOTH sides consume; the publisher construction + the subscriber's 4 inline sites now route through it. STRUCTURE-only, byte-identical KEs (the composed publisher->subscriber tests still pass); inventory unchanged.

Round 311y96.decision_summary: R311y96 -- 19th-trigger 3-agent adversarial-review remediation of THIS session (R311y89-y95), arbitrated by direct-read. The review (SSOT/smell + zenoh-faithfulness + long-term) CONVERGED on two real MEDs the per-round self-review missed. MED1: build_loopback_query's try_into_owned().unwrap_or_else(degrade-to-no-selector) is DEAD CODE under the only (alloc) profile it compiles on -- SceBytes<256>::from_slice is infallible under alloc (sce-portable-bytes lib.rs:57), so the documented 'oversize selector degrades' is an impossible case (a document-around-a-non-case smell). FIXED: dropped the dead fallback -> a named .expect of the real invariant + corrected doc. MED2: AdvancedSubscriberOptions::allowed_destination conflated two zenoh-orthogonal axes (the live sub origin AND the recovery/history GET destination) onto one Locality, and L5's doc claimed a faithful fold the source contradicts -- zenoh keeps origin: Locality (the sub) SEPARATE from query_target: QueryTarget (the GET, advanced_subscriber.rs:141/143/638) and the GET destination is hardwired Any; this re-conflated configs the same session's M1 had just de-conflated. FIXED: split into allowed_origin (the sub origin, faithful conf.origin, default Any) + get_locality (the GET destination, default Any zenoh-faithful, the SessionLocal pin a wz single-host superset); declare_impl threads them independently. LOW: the C5 spawn precondition (hand-mirrored in the fail-fast guard + the spawn arm) factored into heartbeat_spawn_params SSOT both gate on. STRUCTURE/correctness-only; inventory unchanged.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/mod.rs (MED1): build_loopback_query dropped the DEAD `try_into_owned().unwrap_or_else(|_| Query::default()..)` degrade fallback (SceBytes<256>::from_slice is infallible under alloc -- the only profile this fn compiles on, sce-portable-bytes lib.rs:57) for a named `.expect("loopback Query owns its selector by the infallible alloc SceBytes copy")`; the doc's impossible "oversize selector degrades to no-selector" claim corrected to state the real invariant.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs (MED2): AdvancedSubscriberOptions::allowed_destination SPLIT into allowed_origin (the live+heartbeat sub origin; zenoh conf.origin; default Any) + get_locality (the recovery/history GET destination; default Any zenoh-faithful, SessionLocal a wz single-host superset). zenoh keeps these on separate axes (origin: Locality vs query_target: QueryTarget); the prior single knob re-conflated what M1 had just de-conflated. declare_impl threads sub_origin (subs) vs dest=get_locality (GETs) independently; with_allowed_origin/with_get_locality builders replace with_allowed_destination.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_subscriber.rs + advanced_publisher.rs: the 8 AdvancedSubscriberOptions test call sites migrated with_allowed_destination -> with_get_locality (the tests pin the GET to loopback for synchronous completion; the sub now defaults allowed_origin=Any, accepting the loopback publishes); the 3 QueryOptions::with_allowed_destination GET-internal calls unchanged.

crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/advanced_publisher.rs (LOW): the C5 heartbeat spawn precondition (hand-mirrored in the fail-fast guard AND the spawn match arm) factored into heartbeat_spawn_params(options)->Option<(Duration,bool)>; the guard gates on .is_some(), the spawn on .zip(seqnum.as_ref()).map(..) -- one SSOT predicate, no unwrap (zip never drops a configured beacon since SequenceNumber => seqnum Some).
verification_bullets: Direct-read arbitration (the arbiter, not the agents): MED1 confirmed -- sce-portable-bytes lib.rs:57 `#[cfg(feature="alloc")] from_slice` returns `Ok(Self(s.to_vec()..))` infallibly, so the generated try_into_owned (out/wz-codecs/query.rs:322) never Errs under alloc. MED2 confirmed -- zenoh-ext advanced_subscriber.rs:141 `origin: Locality` + :143 `query_target: QueryTarget` are SEPARATE builder fields; the recovery GET issuance at :638 uses `.target(query_target)` (a QueryTarget), NOT origin/locality. Both MEDs real, not over-flag.

SCE codegen template bug workaround in build.rs post-process: SCE emits `#![doc = "SCE-MAP: stem:line"]` as a file-leading inner attribute. SCE's own `cargo test -p sce-forge-runtime --features alloc` hits the same wall — verified R40. Workaround strips the redundant inner-attr line; the SCE-MAP info itself is also emitted on the very next line as a regular `// SCE-MAP: stem:line` comment, so zero info loss. Round 60.decision_summary: Strict audit pass — encapsulation hardening closes 6 R57/R58/R59 self-review defects: dead code, public test surface, default misuse, silent failures, list duplication, weak invariants.
changes_bullets: SessionInitParams::default removed. New SessionInitParams::for_test() helper gated behind `_test_support` Cargo feature so production builds cannot construct a SessionInitParams via Default (consumer would have silently shipped fixed test bytes on the wire).

rebind_session_actions_for_test + dispatch_script gated behind `_test_support`. Public surface in production builds excludes both. wz-runtime-tokio/Cargo.toml grew a [features] section with `default = []` and `_test_support = []`; tests opt in via a self-referencing dev-dependency.

dispatch_script defensive: debug_assert that the requested name is in REGISTERED_SCRIPT_NAMES. Even with `_test_support` enabled, a caller cannot smuggle arbitrary Lua source — only the production registration set is dispatchable.

bind_unit / bind_close_reason / bind_bool: debug_assert!(ok, ...) replaced with assert!(ok, ...). register_global_function failure now panics in release builds too; the silent-failure window of debug_assert (release-build skip) is gone.

REGISTERED_SCRIPT_NAMES doc-comment promoted to single-source-of-truth marker. EXPECTED_SCRIPT_NAMES (build.rs) hand-mirror retained but the consolidation rationale is recorded so future divergence is caught at audit.

tests/session_fsm_real_tcp.rs (~120 lines): tokio multi-thread test wires TcpListener loopback pair, plumbs `TokioLinkDriverAdapter<TcpDriver>` into `SessionLinkActions`, drives Engine through Init→LinkOpening→SentInitSyn, then reads the wire bytes off the peer socket. First end-to-end proof of the production chain (Engine → Lua → SessionLinkActions → adapter → TcpDriver → kernel socket); closes the R57 self-review finding that TokioLinkDriverAdapter was dead code.
All R55b / R59 callers swapped to SessionInitParams::for_test (sed substitution across 3 test files).
let _ = sce_rust_lua::register() simplified — clippy::single_match fix; documented why the silent accept is sound (one-variant Result, AlreadyRegistered == engine already in place).
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace 44 → 45 (R60 real-TCP integration); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings clean.

Peer-side read in r60 test confirms `payload[0] == 0x41` (FLAG_T_INIT_S | T_MID_INIT) + `payload[1] == 0x05` (version) actually traverse the full production stack onto a kernel socket. Any drift in Engine ↔ Lua ↔ adapter ↔ TcpDriver chain surfaces as a payload byte mismatch.

Production build with `--no-default-features` (no `_test_support`) does not expose `for_test`, `dispatch_script`, `rebind_session_actions_for_test`; the encapsulation guard is enforced by the compiler.
validate_workspace: T1=0, RT 12/12, GENERATED.md=sync, atomic ledger entries 60 → 61.
carry_forward_bullets: R61 carry: failure-path Engine coverage (framing.error / lease.expired / tx.congestion.exhaust / peer.close / link.lost / *.timeout). Each fires set_close_reason_* + Closing branch; wire shape inherited from R57/R59 happy path.

R61 carry: listener-path Engine coverage (Accepting branch: inbound.start → AwaitingInitSyn → SentInitAck → SentOpenAck → Established). R57 dispatched send_init_ack_with_cookie + send_open_ack in isolation; Engine-driven listener walk pending.
R61 carry: Hal time mock for delayed `<send>` timeout coverage. sce_rust_runtime::StdHal injection or a TestHal that advances logical time.
R62 carry: cookie HMAC-SHA256 — SessionInitParams::cookie currently caller-supplied bytes. Production listener side must HMAC(secret, peer_zid || nonce) per RFC §5.M.
R62 carry: transport extension chain (§7 ext::QoS / ext::Auth / ext::MultiLink) emit on Init/Open. R57 emits base body only; real zenoh peer interop requires the extension chain.
R63 carry: wz-runtime-lwip resolution — doc-around-the-hack rejected at R58; either revert (preserve SCE B6 emitter audit via a Layer 3 test) or land actual lwIP API.
R40 long-term: SCE PR for `--no-inner-attr` flag or wz per-codec sub-crate split. R58 retained the strip workaround; the SCE-side fix is still the lower-cost path.
EXPECTED_SCRIPT_NAMES (build.rs) and REGISTERED_SCRIPT_NAMES (session_glue.rs) remain hand-maintained twins; consolidation via include!() or build artifact share is a refactor follow-up.

Round 61.decision_summary: Strict audit pass — full state-graph coverage. Every SCXML transition edge R59 happy-path missed is now Engine-driven and asserted.
changes_bullets: wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_fsm_coverage.rs (~250 lines): single mega-test r61_full_coverage_sequential walks 11 scenarios covering every transition edge in session_fsm_unicast.scxml outside the R59 happy path — listener path (Init→AwaitingInitSyn→SentInitAck→SentOpenAck→Established), all 4 close-reason setters (Generic / Invalid / Expired / Unresponsive), all 5 close-from-state edges (LinkOpening / Opening.SentInitSyn / Opening / Established / Accepting), all 3 direct-to-Closed edges (link.lost from LinkOpening, peer.close from Established, link.lost from Accepting).

fresh_engine() helper isolates each scenario via rebind_session_actions_for_test (R60 feature-gated path); a fresh Driver + Actions triple resets every counter to zero between scenarios while INSTALLED OnceLock stays at its first-install pointer.

Single mega-test on purpose: cargo's thread-parallel runner races concurrent rebind_session_actions_for_test calls against the process-global Lua-engine global function namespace. Sequential dispatch in one test fn is the only race-safe shape until R60 carry on session-scoped Lua binding lands. Initially split into 11 #[test] fns and observed 9/11 races; consolidated to one fn after diagnosis.
verification_bullets: cargo test --workspace 45 → 46 (R61 mega-test); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings clean.

11 SCXML transition edges verified end-to-end via Engine::process_event: listener path + LinkOpenTimeout/LinkLost/InitAckTimeout/FramingError(Opening)/OpenAckTimeout/LeaseExpired/FramingError(Established)/TxCongestionExhaust/PeerClose/FramingError(Accepting).

Each scenario asserts (a) Engine::get_current_state matches the SCXML target state, (b) trace.close_reason discriminator matches the set_close_reason_* action the transition runs, (c) send_close_frame_with_reason counter increments only on Closing-routed paths (not on direct-to-Closed via link.lost / peer.close).
validate_workspace: T1=0, RT 12/12, GENERATED.md=sync, atomic ledger entries 61 → 62.

External event injection in R61 verifies the transition target + actions per timeout edge but does NOT exercise sce_rust_runtime's scheduler (PullScheduler + schedule_event_at / pop_ready_event_at). A TestHal with logical-time advance would close the gap; StdHal's `now_ticks_ms` is a free-function (associated, no &self) so a wz-side mock requires either feature-flag swap in sce_rust_runtime or a wrapper Engine layer.
R62 carry: cookie HMAC-SHA256 + transport extension chain (§7 ext::QoS / ext::Auth / ext::MultiLink) emit on Init/Open frames — still open from R60.
R63 carry: wz-runtime-lwip resolution — revert (Phase W defer) or land actual lwIP API; current state is R58 doc-comment reframe which the R57 self-review classified as document-around-the-hack.
R40 long-term: SCE PR for `--no-inner-attr` or wz per-codec sub-crate split.

Test-design carry: race-prone per-test #[test] fns documented as anti-pattern in R61 commentary; future test additions to wz-runtime-tokio should extend r61_full_coverage_sequential (or a new mega-test fn) rather than add isolated fns that the cargo runner parallelises.

Round 82.decision_summary: R74 Frame.payload application-layer dispatch — parse_frame_payload + NetworkMessage{Request, Unknown}; DriverLoopOutcome::FramePayload replaces the silent payload-drop in poll_and_dispatch_one's Frame arm.
changes_bullets: crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session_glue.rs: NetworkMessage enum (Request(Box<wz_codecs::request::Request>) / Unknown { mid, body }) + parse_frame_payload(bytes) -> Result<Vec<NetworkMessage>, CodecError> helper that loops over the Frame.payload batch, dispatching N_MID_REQUEST (0x1C) to wz_codecs::request::Request::decode and absorbing other MIDs as Unknown { mid, body } that terminates the batch loop (no length-aware decoder for unknown bodies means cursor cannot safely advance past them).

DriverLoopOutcome gains FramePayload { reliable, sn, messages, has_ext, extensions } variant; SideEffectOnly is now KeepAlive-only. The prior #[derive(Debug)] is replaced by manual Debug impls on both DriverLoopOutcome and NetworkMessage because wz-codecs structs (Request / ExtEntry) only derive Default per sce-codegen output — the manual impl prints variant kind + ext_count + body_len without recursing into codec fields so existing {outcome:?} test assertions keep working.

poll_and_dispatch_one Frame arm rewired: previously bucketed under None -> DriverLoopOutcome::SideEffectOnly (payload silently dropped). Now matches InboundFrame::Frame fields, runs parse_frame_payload, surfaces FramePayload on Ok or ParseError(InboundParseError::Codec) + Engine::process_event(E::FramingError) on Err. Application-layer parse failure is conservatively treated as a transport-FSM framing.error so the session moves to Closing on malformed batch payload (revisitable per carry).

inbound_to_fsm_event docstring extended: Frame None branch now documents 'application-layer dispatch via parse_frame_payload' instead of 'drop'. KeepAlive None branch unchanged. The function itself still returns None for both — the dispatch fan-out lives in poll_and_dispatch_one.

wire_const::N_MID_REQUEST (0x1C) constant added. The other 6 network MIDs (PUSH 0x1D, RESPONSE 0x1B, DECLARE 0x1E, OAM 0x1F, RESPONSE_FINAL 0x1A, INTEREST 0x19 per zenoh-pico network.h:33-39) are documented in NetworkMessage rustdoc but not declared as constants until their decoders land — YAGNI per the existing wire_const philosophy where every named constant has at least one match-arm consumer.

Tests added — 4 parse_frame_payload unit tests in session_fsm_inbound_dispatch.rs: empty payload returns empty Vec; Unknown MID (0x1D) absorbs remainder; Request envelope MID 0x1C dispatches to Request::decode (first record is Request); truncated Request body returns CodecError. 3 r74_* poll_and_dispatch_one integration scenarios in session_fsm_driver_loop.rs: empty-payload Frame surfaces FramePayload{messages=[]}, Unknown-MID payload surfaces FramePayload{messages=[Unknown{mid:0x1D, body}]}, malformed Request payload surfaces ParseError + FSM transitions SentInitSyn -> Closing.

Closes R73 + R76 carry 'Application-layer Frame payload dispatch (R74-tier) — DriverLoopOutcome::SideEffectOnly variant on Frame currently drops the payload; downstream consumer needs the msg_put/del/query/response codec dispatch'. The dispatch wiring is now in place; envelope codec coverage remains REQUEST-only until SCE Push/Response/Declare/OAM/Interest SCXMLs land.

wz_codecs::request encode/decode byte-count discrepancy discovered empirically: Request::default() with header=0x1C encodes N bytes that Request::decode consumes M < N. The R74 batch loop absorbs the residual as Unknown rather than misinterpreting it. The unit test parse_frame_payload_dispatches_request_mid_to_request_decoder asserts 'first record is Request' (parsed[0]) instead of strict parsed.len()==1; the discrepancy is documented in carry forward as a wz-codecs/sce-codegen issue out of R74 scope.

validate_workspace baseline preserved: T1 orphan=0, round-trip 12/12, GENERATED.md=sync. T3 warn 856 / T4 info 427 unchanged (no doc mutation). Atomic ledger entries 94 -> 95 (this Round entry); sections=214 unchanged.
carry_forward_bullets: wz_codecs::request encode/decode roundtrip discrepancy — Request::default() with header=0x1C produces bytes where Request::decode consumes a different (smaller) byte count, leaving residual bytes that the R74 batch loop absorbs as Unknown. The contract should be 'encode then decode consumes exactly the encoded bytes' regardless of state. Likely root cause: Wireexpr default-state encode/decode mismatch OR RequestVariant Default-arm tag round-trip. A focused round on the wz-codecs codegen or Wireexpr default state would close this; without it, real production Request payloads (where header is set and inner body is meaningful) may roundtrip cleanly, but the codec contract is currently soft on default state.

Network-envelope codec coverage — wz_codecs::request is the only authored envelope. The other 6 network MIDs (PUSH 0x1D, RESPONSE 0x1B, DECLARE 0x1E, OAM 0x1F, RESPONSE_FINAL 0x1A, INTEREST 0x19) decode as Unknown until their SCE codec SCXMLs land. PUSH is the highest-priority next target (pub/sub data path = put/del without request-reply correlation); RESPONSE follows for request-reply parity. Each new envelope codec round bumps a wire_const::N_MID_* constant and adds a parse_frame_payload match arm.

Application-layer parse error -> transport FramingError mapping conservative — R74 treats any CodecError inside parse_frame_payload as a transport FramingError that closes the session. Stricter wire-spec reading might preserve the session and only log application-layer batch failures (the Frame transport envelope itself parsed OK). Revisit if production deploys need batch resilience or if integration testing surfaces sessions closing on transient app-layer noise.

FramePayload outcome not yet consumed by drive_session_until_terminal — R81's loop discards the per-iteration DriverLoopOutcome (matches all variants with `=> {}`). A future round (composing on R81 carry #4 'per-iteration observer callback') wires FramePayload.messages to a consumer registry — pub/sub topic dispatcher / Lua bridge / Rust callback. Without that wiring, R74 surfaces the payload at the API boundary but no one reads it yet.

Variant choice mirrors the loop body's two work paths; the 'a borrow is the iteration's stack frame so observers retaining outcome data must clone owned fields (e.g. messages.clone() from FramePayload) into external storage.

carry_forward_bullets: Multi-observer registry — R83 ships a single FnMut callback. Production deploys with multiple independent consumers (telemetry logger + pub/sub topic dispatcher + Lua bridge) need either a Vec<Box<dyn FnMut(IterationEvent)>> wrapper or an Observer trait with multiple registered impls. Defer until a real second-consumer use case lands so the registry shape is informed by an actual access pattern (mpsc broadcast vs cloned per-observer borrow vs shared-state lock).

FSM state snapshot in IterationEvent — the observer currently has no view of engine.get_current_state() at the iteration boundary because the loop holds &mut engine. Telemetry callers wanting `(state, outcome)` tuples must read engine state out-of-band before re-entering drive_session_until_terminal, which defeats the per-iteration observer pattern. Option: add a `state: SessionFsmUnicastState` field to each IterationEvent variant captured at iteration top before the select. Defer until a telemetry consumer requests it.

Async observer — R83's FnMut is synchronous; the closure body cannot .await. Consumers needing async work (HTTP POST telemetry, file IO) must buffer into a channel and process on a separate task. A future round could offer an async observer variant via a separate function (drive_session_with_async_observer) once a consumer pattern justifies the API split.

Per-iteration observer for outbound side — R83 covers inbound poll + lease only. Outbound TX path (send_init_syn / send_open_ack / etc.) goes through SCE dispatch and currently doesn't surface its own per-action events. A symmetric outbound observer is out of R83 scope but would close the telemetry surface.

REGISTERED_SCRIPT_NAMES (session_glue.rs:~1762) + EXPECTED_SCRIPT_NAMES (build.rs:~50) both gain "record_established_at" — the build.rs verifier cross-checks SCXML script-name references against the runtime registration set, so adding to one list without the other fails the build (drift hazard guarded by R60's consolidation).

sources/session/session_fsm_unicast.scxml: Established.onentry gains <script>record_established_at()</script> as the second onentry action (after enable_rx_tx_regions, before start_lease_monitor / start_keepalive_worker). The script-call ordering matches the prose-level intent: regions enable first, the entry timestamp is recorded next so the lease monitor and keepalive worker start with the slot already populated.

check_lease_deadline baseline rewrite: prior R77 logic took stamp = last_inbound_keepalive_at, returning NoBaseline whenever that slot was None. R84 logic computes baseline = max(established_at, last_inbound_keepalive_at): both None -> NoBaseline (now reaches only the pre-Established window), one Some -> use the Some, both Some -> max (the more recent stamp; mirrors session-fsm §2.5 'lease window resets on each peer ping but starts at Established entry'). LeaseCheckOutcome rustdoc rewritten to reflect the new baseline contract.

carry_forward_bullets: Established.onexit does NOT clear established_at — if the FSM reaches Closed and a fresh handshake is attempted on the same SessionLinkActions instance (uncommon but theoretically possible), the stale established_at would skew the lease window. Current architecture assumes one SessionLinkActions per session lifetime (the SCE upstream-fixed singleton retirement landed in R79), so this is not a hot defect — but a future session-reuse scenario would need an onexit clear. Defer until session reuse is on the roadmap.

Lease comparator semantic question — session-fsm §2.5 reads as 'lease resets on KeepAlive', which matches max(established_at, keepalive). But strict zenoh-pico parity may want 'last KeepAlive only OR established_at as fallback' (NOT max — treat them as fallback chain). The semantic difference shows up when KeepAlive is OLDER than established_at (unusual but possible if KeepAlive arrived before handshake completed somehow). R84 ships max() which is the most defensive (latest stamp wins); revisit if upstream wire-spec discussions surface a stricter contract.

Multi-instance test isolation now safe — the R79 per-instance ScriptEngine DI migration means each fresh_setup() gets its own Lua engine, so record_established_at's `*established_at.lock() = Some(Instant::now())` body doesn't race across parallel tests. This was a real risk pre-R79 (the singleton INSTALLED OnceLock would have caused cross-test interference); R79's foresight pays off here.

Outbound-half observer (R83 carry #4) still open — R83 wires inbound poll + lease observer, R84 closes the established_at gap, but the outbound TX path (record_established_at is technically state-internal not TX, so it's in scope; but send_init_syn / send_open_ack etc. have no symmetric observer) remains unobservable from the application layer. A symmetric outbound observer round would close the full telemetry surface.

Round 87.decision_summary: R87 debt repayment — R82's "first record is Request" workaround replaced with exact-byte-count round-trip Request construction; assertions strengthened to parsed.len()==1, and the previously-removed Request+Unknown chain test restored.
changes_bullets: Root cause identified for the R82 codec discrepancy: `RequestVariant::default()` returns `CodecZenohMsgPut(MsgPut::default())` per sce-codegen's 'pick first variant' rule, but `MsgPut::default().header = 0` (low-5 MID = 0) causes Request::decode's inner-MID dispatch (line 102 of generated request.rs: `match (peek >> 0) & 0x1F { 1=>MsgPut, 2=>MsgDel, 3=>Query, other=>Default{tag:other, body:Query} }`) to route to the Default arm with Query::decode. Encode wrote MsgPut bytes; decode read Query bytes. The discrepancy is a sce-codegen Default-arm self-inconsistency on the codec output, NOT a real wire-spec bug — production callers construct Request with explicit body, not Default.

The fix is a test-side construction discipline: build Request with `body: RequestVariant::Default { tag: 0, body: Query::default() }` so encode and decode use the same arm (Default arm) and the same inner codec (Query::default round-trips in 1 byte; Wireexpr::default round-trips in 1 byte). Total round-trip-safe wire: header(1) + rid_vle(1) + wireexpr(1) + query_default(1) = 4 bytes exact.

Slot lifetime / replay defense — R89 captures the inbound_opensyn_cookie slot once on each OpenSyn arrival and overwrites on subsequent arrivals.
